  every launch.** On a machine whose session bus has a portal that cannot start (a CI runner, a
  container, a bare window manager), only the first launch after login waits the portal's 300 ms
  before it starts without the bus. Later launches in the same session start straight away. The
  portal is asked again at the next login, or at the next launch once it has answered (ADR 0026,
  #2432).
- **A skill can't take a built-in skill's name** (Skill studio preview, #3680). Making, renaming, moving or sharing a skill, and accepting a chat's draft of a new one, are refused for the name of a skill purlis ships, such as `secrets` or `browser`, with "That name belongs to a built-in skill; pick another, or make a copy." The window and `purlis skill` refuse it alike. Restoring a deleted skill, installing one from a source, and an update that brings along a skill under such a name are refused too. A skill already in the project under such a name stays where it is, and no chat gets it.
- **A skill's History and Grades follow it across a rename and a move** (#3918). History lists
  the versions from before, read from the folder and name the skill had then, with their runs
  and grades, and the version that renamed or moved it shows that as its diff. Its Grades and
  each grade's scorecard read the grades recorded under its earlier name or level, and the
  chats this machine kept of its grades go with a rename. The Rename and Move dialogs say its
  history and grades move with it.
- **A grant never names the system's name lookup.** Allowing one of its sockets, or the Mac's
  own name lookup service, is refused at every level on a block's Notice, the centralized Ask
  and Settings, which say why. The Granted list and Doctor say one kept on this machine reaches
  no chat (#2657).
- **A squash-landed branch goes when its folder does.** `purlis worktree remove --delete-branch`
  and a task's Discard now delete a branch whose change landed by a squash merge, where before
  git's own check kept it because it does not find a squashed branch merged. Only the local
  branch goes, and a branch whose base has changed its files since stays (ADR 0110, #5168).
- **A chat started on an idle cluster runner waits for it.** The start used to be refused while the
  runner came back, and had to be started again. It now runs once the cluster operator vouches for
  the runner, for up to the pool's longest wait for that (#4403).
- **A cluster pool's retention holds at two hours at least, with an hour's notice at least.** A Pool
  that says less is read as those times, so a volume is not lost on a typed `30s`. Time spent stopped
  while an upstream object is in the way no longer counts toward a Claim's retention (#4405).
- **A task you stop or close names its branch** to the chat that asked, where it worked on a
  branch of its own, as its report would have (#1472).
- **Branch-folder work from a harness subagent goes to a purlis task.** A subagent's
  `purlis worktree add`, `commit` and `push` are refused at the hook with one line: this work
  is a purlis task, so ask your chat to dispatch it. The chat's own calls, and a subagent's
  reads, searches and reviews, run as before, in Claude Code and in Codex. A chat's briefing
  now says which work is a task's (anything that writes, commits, needs its own branch folder
  or runs long) and which a subagent's (#4773).
- **A table's row check looks like every other checkbox.** The box that chooses a row, and the one
  that chooses them all, are the same checkbox the rest of the window draws, so they follow a
  theme's checkbox settings. They take a press across the same 24px square as before (#3362).
- **A task can be started fresh where purlis can hand it its brief again.** The core no longer
  refuses Start fresh for a task whose brief it confirms as the one its dispatch was sent: the
  task starts with no conversation, is handed that brief under purlis's stamp, and is still its
  asker's task, owing its report. Where the brief cannot be confirmed (a dispatch from before
  purlis was started again, a record changed since, or none kept), Start fresh is still refused
  with the same sentence (#1609, #1489).
- **A task ends at its report.** When a task reports, the report is delivered to the chat
  that asked and then purlis ends the task's program: after the turn that sent the report is
  over, or after a bounded wait on a harness purlis cannot hear. A finished task no longer
  stays open holding memory until somebody closes it. Its row stays under the chat that asked,
  as a finished entry whose outcome and report can be read. `purlis dispatch list` keeps
  listing it until its row is cleared or the asking chat closes, and `wait` still answers with
  its report; a cancel, a follow-up or an answer to one says it has finished (#1485).
- **What is never ended.** A task you type into after its report, or begin a Smart close of,
  is yours from then and stays open. A task you have in front of you is ended only when you
  move to another chat. A task that reported itself blocked stays open, and so does a persona
  chat you started yourself with Ask from a tab. A task reading the report of a task of its own
  is ended when that turn is over, never during it (#1485).
- **A task that had reported when you quit is a finished row at the next launch**, and is not
  started again (#1485).
- **A session's tab still lists a task that has a tab or a pane of its own.** Its chip counts
  it and its menu marks it "in its own tab" or "beside it"; picking it there brings that tab or
  pane forward. While a task in its own tab waits for you and that tab is not in front, the
  session's chip wears the hand and names it (#1489, #1601).
- **The close button on a session's tab is the only close on the strip.** It closes the session
  and asks once about the tasks still working, as before. The dialog now says how many of the
  session's tasks have a tab of their own: those tabs close with the session's, and a task you
  keep running stays in the Chats list. A task beside its session is not ended by the
  session's close either (#1489).
- **Whenever a session's pane goes, its tasks' own tabs go back to the list.** The tab's close,
  a close of the session's pane, a Smart close and the session ending all do the same: a task
  the session leaves running has no tab left, a task beside it included, and is in the Chats
  list. None is ended by that (#1489).
- **A task is not started fresh.** A fresh start is a new conversation, and a task's brief is in
  the one it has. Its tab draws no Start fresh mark, the row in its tab's menu says why it
  cannot run, and purlis refuses it from anywhere else. Restart chat keeps the conversation,
  and on a task it asks first (#1489).
- **A task you are reading is not ended under you in any pane.** A task that has reported is
  held while it is on screen in the tab in front: inside its session's tab, beside its session,
  or in a tab of its own. It is ended once you look away. No system notification is sent about
  a chat that is on screen in any pane of the tab in front (#1489).
- **A task opened beside its session, and a task in a tab of its own, come back after a
  relaunch** where they were. A task whose session did not come back is in the Chats list
  (#1489).
- **A task asked for from a chat that works in a worktree is cut from that chat's branch.** With
  `--in worktree` (or a persona's `dispatch-isolation: worktree`), the task's new branch now
  starts from the branch the asking chat's own worktree is on, so the task sees its commits, and
  Merge lands it back into that branch, in that worktree. A chat in the clone itself gets a task
  cut from the clone's current commit, as before (#1472).
- **A Discard refused for a change says what changed.** It names the paths new to, or gone from,
  what would be lost, a commit made, or a folder switched to another branch. Where nothing new
  would be lost and a file was only written again, or a file went away while purlis read the
  folder, it says something is still writing there and to stop it first (#1472).
- **A task opens inside its session's tab.** Pressing a task in the Chats list, the explorer,
  the title bar's needs-you list or the palette brings forward the tab of the session that
  asked for it and switches that tab to the task. No tab is added. The pane's top line then
  says where you are, `steward 4 › talk · working`, with the whole path for a task of a task
  and `in <workspace>` for a task that works in another workspace. Pressing a name in it goes
  to that chat. The tab reads `steward 4 › talk`, and pressing it while it is in front goes
  back to the session's own chat. Each tab remembers the chat it shows, across a reload and a
  relaunch too (#1486).
- **A pane never changes what it shows by itself.** A task you are reading that ends stays on
  screen as ended, with how it ended and one button back to its session's chat. A pane never
  draws a task without the line that says which chat it is, and nothing typed reaches a task
  the pane cannot say the path to (#1486).
- **A chat of a tab that is waiting for you and is not on screen puts the hand on that tab.**
  That is a task that needs you, the session's own chat while the tab shows a task, and a chat
  with a dispatch held for your answer, a vault it was refused, a sandbox block or a restart
  it is owed. Going to it switches the tab to that chat. After you answer, the tab stays where
  it is (#1486).
- **What a chat of a tab has to ask you is on that tab's pane, whichever chat the tab shows.**
  A Notice of a chat that is not the one on screen says whose it is first and has **Go to
  it**. Its answers are that chat's (#1486).
- **A tab's close button closes the session, whatever the tab shows.** While a tab shows a
  task, the pane draws no close of its own, so nothing on screen reads as ending the task, and
  the close dialog says the session is what ends (#1486).
- **A task that needs you is counted on the workspace of the tab it lives in.** It was counted
  on the workspace it works in, where no tab wears it (#1486).
- **A file dropped on a tab goes to the chat the tab shows** (#1486).
- **A task starts in auto mode when the chat that asked for it runs in auto.** A Claude Code
  chat in auto mode, or with its permission prompts off, now starts its tasks in auto mode, so
  they no longer stop on tool prompts in tabs nobody is watching. A chat that asks starts tasks
  that ask. A profile that names its own permission mode keeps it. Codex and opencode tasks
  start in their default mode, as before (#3787).
- **A task that did not start is a failed row under its session, not a banner.** A task that
  was let through and then started no chat (the profile's program is missing or does not
  answer as its harness, the sandbox will not wrap it, there is no terminal to give it, its
  folder is gone, its worktree could not be cut, or a limit filled after you pressed Allow)
  is now a finished row under the chat that asked: failed, with the reason shown in full
  under it. It never folds into "Finished (n)", it is cleared like any finished row, and it
  is there after the app is quit and reopened. A task the chat tried several times is one
  row that says how often. Where you pressed Allow, the chat that asked is told as it is told
  a task's report, failed and in purlis's own words ("it did not start: <reason>"), so a
  command waiting on the task returns at once. A start refused while the asking command is
  still on the line is answered there, as before, and is not said twice. `purlis dispatch
  list` says "did not start" for such a task (#1497).
- **A task a launch could not start again is drawn under the chat that asked, and is not
  ended.** It stays recorded and is tried again at the next launch, as before. Its row gives
  the reason and offers Try to start again, Review and approve… where its profile waits on
  your approval, and End task. Only End task ends it: the chat that asked is then told it
  failed, and Reopen carries its conversation on as an ordinary chat. Until then that chat is
  told nothing, and a wait on the task answers that it is waiting on you (#1497).
- **The line across the window is kept for chats nobody asked for.** "<chat> did not start" is
  now drawn only for a chat you opened yourself, a handoff's chat, and a task whose asking
  chat did not come back either. A long reason in it wraps inside the window.
- **A task's dispatch question on its session's tab says "it".** It used to say "This chat",
  which read as the chat on screen; the task's path already says which chat asks (#1538).
- **A task's own branch folder is merged and discarded from its Changes tab, not from the
  explorer.** The explorer's **Merge** and **Remove** on a branch folder purlis cut for a task
  now say whose it is and point to that task's **Review changes**, where the merge shows what
  would land and waits until the task has ended. The Dispatches tab's row of such a task has
  **Review changes** too. Where purlis runs no git in a repo (its own git settings name a
  program), an ended task's folder is still removed from the explorer (#1534).
- **A task's Changes list marks every other chat that wrote a file**, not only a task of the
  same chat: the asking chat's edits and any other chat's are marked with its name too.
- **Tasks sharing a folder are named whichever chat asked for them**, and **Ask a persona…**
  names the tasks already working in the folder you pick before it starts one there.
- **A task's record lists the files it changed.** Once a task reports, purlis reads what it
  changed from the folder it worked in and keeps the list beside its report
  (`report.changed.files`). The Activity tab's "also changed by" mark reads that list, and
  reads file names out of a report's words only for a record that lists none (#1457).
- **A test server on a port the system picks runs in a sandboxed chat on Linux.** A Codex or
  opencode chat on Linux may start a TCP server on port 0 of 127.0.0.1, as Go's `httptest`, a
  Node test server started on 127.0.0.1 and Python's `HTTPServer(("127.0.0.1", 0))` do, with
  nothing to allow, and reach it there. It reaches no other port of this machine that way: only
  those its own servers hold. On every other address, and on macOS, the Notice that says what to
  do stays, and on Linux it now says to start the server on 127.0.0.1 (#3396).
- **A theme with a value purlis cannot read is refused whole** (#2322, ADR 0097 §2), whichever
  format it is in and wherever it comes from: purlis draws its own theme and the Notice names
  each value, instead of drawing the theme with that value replaced. A token a theme does not
  name is still purlis's, silently, and a token name purlis does not know is said and left out.
- **A workspace's colour keeps the accent apart from the danger colour, and Allow and Keep
  blocked stay apart under every tint, custom colours included.** Where a tint would bring
  either pair too near, it keeps the workspace's hue and gives it less colour. In Purlis
  Classic's light appearance this softens the accent of red, orange and pink workspaces.
- **The terminal is drawn in the theme's terminal font**, which for Purlis Classic is the
  family it always had.
- **A persona's tool is refused where the program it runs, as found and as its links resolve,
  is a shell, an interpreter or another program that runs what it is told**, with the same
  sentence as a tool named after one: Settings › Sandbox and the Notice say why, no Allow is of
  it, and a chat gets no script for it. A tool runs the program its links resolve to, and every
  link on the way to it is in a folder no chat writes.
- **A vault's status says why its program is not run, not that it is "not on PATH".** purlis
  looks for `op` and `vault` well beyond `PATH`, so `purlis vault list`, `purlis persona list`
  and the vault's tab now say "op CLI not found", or "op CLI found only where a chat can write"
  where the only copy is one a chat could have written. A reference vault names each CLI under
  the same two reasons (#1517).
- **A window with no project open shows a welcome with three doors.** **Create a project**,
  **Get a project from your forge** and **Open a folder on this machine…**, with **Sign in to
  GitHub or GitLab** under them and your recent projects below, with Locate… and Forget beside
  any that moved. It shows on every machine, including one that remembers a project from an old
  Mac or a launch from a terminal, where the bare opener used to hide the first run. Create a
  project is the first run's page, with its stack template. Getting a project from a forge and
  signing in from purlis itself say plainly that they come in a later update (#1812).
- A tool that gets no token in the cluster and hangs up while you are being asked now waits before
  it asks again, as one you refused does, so repeated runs don't raise and withdraw Asks.
- **A workspace's chats move together.** Moving a chat to a pool's runner, or back here, moves
  every chat of its workspace running where it runs, since they share its clones; its tab's row
  names them. Each keeps working until it is at a pause, none starts where it moved before all of
  their work is there, and if one cannot move, none does (#3453).
- **A chat never writes a workspace's `workspace.json`** (#2046). The app keeps a workspace's
  repos and settings there, so a chat's sandbox holds it, as it holds the project's manifests. A
  chat's `purlis clone` and `purlis workspace snapshot` are still recorded there, by the app.
  `purlis workspace rename` and `fork`, and `purlis skill grant --on/--off`, say inside a
  sandboxed chat that they are the person's to run, and change nothing.
- **About's licences open in a tab.** *Their licences* in About opens them as a tab of the
  project in front, where they can be read at length; with no project open they are shown in
  About as before (#1719).
- **What a chosen item says in the accent all draws from `accent.text`.** A chosen option card's
  check and icon, a chosen chip's check, a pinned switcher row's pin and the current explorer row's
  icon join the activity bars and page marks. A theme or a colour of yours that sets `accent.base`
  alone now reaches all of them, over Purlis too, and a workspace's colour turns them with the
  accent, except where that would bring them near the waiting or danger colour: there they keep
  the theme's colour (#3100).
- **The app leaves the terminal it was started from.** Started from a shell, the app no longer
  keeps that terminal as its controlling terminal, so no agent a chat runs can open it. Started
  straight from a shell, it runs again as its own child: the first process waits for it and
  ends as it ends, and if the first process is killed, the app ends with it. An app launched
  from a terminal now also ends when whatever launched it there exits, as Ctrl-C or closing the
  terminal ended it before (HP-2, #669).
- **What an action answered is a notice you can close.** Creating a workspace now says
  "Workspace git-ci-cd is ready" and one plain sentence, with Open and a Details disclosure
  holding what purlis said in full, instead of a full-width line of command-line text. × or Esc
  closes it, and the result stays in the Inbox's Notices under Results. Lines purlis writes for
  an agent ("ask the developer…") are never shown (#3344).
- **A chat's Activity keeps less, and says what it leaves out.** A message between two chats
  whose text reads like a credential keeps its line and not its text, and the Activity tab
  says the text was left out. Clear finished, and closing the chat that asked, forget what the
  cleared tasks and that chat said to each other, including a task that ends after the chat
  that asked has closed; removing a workspace forgets what the tasks
  that worked in it said, and says how many of their records stay. A file two tasks' reports
  both name is marked only where the two tasks ran at the same time. A long-lived chat's
  Activity lists the newest 200 tasks it dispatched, each with the tasks under it, and says how
  many older ones it does not (#1520).
- **Add a grant says when a name it picks waits for Give back.** Where the asking persona or
  the target is a name an earlier persona had, Settings › Project › Dispatch says under the
  form that a grant added for it is not in force until Give back, and says it again once the
  grant is added (#1586).
- **Add to a chat's context on a picked row hands every picked row.** In the explorer, the row
  menu of a row you picked with others reads *Add N picked to a chat's context* and hands them
  all as one paste, in the order the tree draws them. On a row outside the picks it still hands
  that row alone (#1151).
- **Add to memory is drawn as plainly as Not now.** The repository-instructions tab saves a
  repository's own instruction text into memory, so its answer is a trust decision and no longer
  stands out as the suggested one (#2591).
- **Advice about a purlis variable names it under both of its names.** The nested-plane alert
  says to unset `PURLIS_ROOT` and `CHARTER_ROOT`, and an unattended run with no workspace is told
  to re-launch with `PURLIS_WORKSPACE=<name> CHARTER_WORKSPACE=<name>`, since either name still
  decides while the rename's window is open (#1284).
- **Each row of the Alerts drawer has its way out, in place of a command to type.** A version
  pin and a front door naming no persona open the project's General settings, where the version
  lock, the update channel and the default persona's picker are. Workspaces behind the layout
  have Reinit, the doctor's new `workspace-reinit` fix. A nested project offers Open the outer
  project, and a project root being worked in or a save that is blocked offers Go to Saving. A
  broken editor or text-size setting links to Settings › You, and a theme file charter could
  not use whole offers Use built-in…, which asks first and then moves the file aside to
  `theme.aside.json` (or the next free name), never over another file. The rest can be
  dismissed (NO-6, #1238).
- **The doctor's `version lock` and `front door` rows link to Settings › General** when they
  warn, as the Alerts drawer's rows for the same problems do (NO-6, #1238).
- **Allow and Keep blocked are told apart at a glance.** On every ask that offers the two, they
  carry equal weight: each Allow is edged in the accent and led by an open lock, Keep blocked is
  the plain button, and the consent floors keep the two apart in any theme (#2503).
- **The needs-you mark is readable on a hovered control.** Purlis Classic dark's needs-you colour
  is a step lighter, so the title bar's hand clears 3:1 on its button under the pointer, and the
  consent floors hold that pair for every theme (#2504).
- **The cluster holds the operator to a runner's shape.** A new admission policy refuses its
  service account a template outside purlis's pod shape, and any upstream object outside a runner
  namespace (#3754). A policy made again under its binding, or a binding changed since it was
  made, now counts as made again for Claims and runner namespaces (#3854).
- **An answer given on a pane is listed under Recently answered.** The Inbox's look back listed
  only what was answered in the Inbox itself. An Allow, Keep blocked or Never pressed on a
  chat's dispatch or sandbox block Notice in its pane is now listed there too, with the words
  pressed, once its ask stops waiting (#1700).
- **An approved MCP server's environment values come from the person's approval.** In a
  sandboxed chat, a persona's credentialed MCP server approved with `purlis persona approve-mcp`
  starts with each variable its entry's `env` writes out, at the value its approved line shows.
  A value the harness fills in (`${VAR}`) is not on the line, so the server starts without it,
  and `approve-mcp` says so under the line, with what to write instead (#3441).
- **A question a chat asks you through purlis shows in its own words.** The waiting strip, the
  Inbox card and the quiz now show what `ask_operator` asks, where they said only "a form to
  fill". A later turn doesn't replace it, and it goes once you answer (#4710).
- **A chat is told your answer to what its sandbox refused, in one line.** Allow says
  "Allowed for this chat — retry" (or the scope you chose), and Keep blocked says "Kept
  blocked by the person — don't retry or work around it", with your reason if you gave one,
  for a host, a folder, a socket, a system service or a service on this Mac by its port, and a
  vault alike. The Inbox's row of a sandbox ask has a box for the reason (#1987).
- **An automatic save pushes only to the remote you saved to.** The window remembers the remote
  each clone pushes to, in your own config folder. When a clone's remote changes, an automatic
  save commits locally and asks you to confirm the new remote by saving from the window, which
  records it.
- **An edit of a file with CRLF line endings can be allowed from the Inbox.** Its change is drawn
  with `␍` at the end of each line that ends in CRLF, and says so, where before it was left to
  the chat's pane. A carriage return anywhere else still sends the edit to its pane (#1146).
- **An extension's manifest is `purlis-extension.json`.** purlis read only the old name,
  `charter-extension.json`, and ignored a manifest under the new one. It now reads
  `purlis-extension.json` first, and the built-in extensions ship under that name. A folder with
  only `charter-extension.json` is still read, for one release: rename the file before then. An
  approved extension whose manifest you rename is asked about again, because its files changed
  (#1802).
- **An interrupted grade's spend gives the next grade's estimate.** A grade's marker now
  records how many chats the grade asked for so far, whether they ran or not. When purlis
  stops during a grade, its row still says what those chats spent. The next plan shares that
  spend over those chats and says the estimate comes from an interrupted grade. Before this, a
  skill whose only grades were interrupted showed "ran no chat" in its plan. An interrupted
  grade recorded before this version still gives no estimate (#3602).
- **The dispatch question offers no box the decision would refuse.** A persona the person
  said never to for a chat above the asking one is not offered under the question's answers
  (#1548).
- **A task whose asking chat has closed ends at its report.** Its report is kept on its record,
  where the Dispatches tab shows it, and for the workspace, as before. The task's chat is then
  ended once its turn is over, the same as a task whose report reached its chat, and it no
  longer waits in your needs-you list. A task you started yourself from a tab, and a blocked
  task, still stay open for you (#1510).
- **A memory no index lists is a Notice under the strip.** When the doctor finds a memory its
  `MEMORY.md` does not link, which no chat would ever read, the project now says so beside the
  git identity Notice, and its Fix adds the missing links. The doctor's other fixable findings
  stay in the Doctor dialog, each for a reason written beside the list in the code (#1301).
- **An update's review says when it brings along a skill under a built-in skill's name** (Skill studio preview, #3728). Before, such an update was refused only once accepted. Now its review says "This update brings along secrets, whose name belongs to a built-in skill, so it can't be taken until the source renames it.", and Accept update stays unavailable with that reason. `purlis skill update` marks the skill where it lists what comes along, prints the line, and asks nothing.
- **A task's line in a tab's menu shows its buttons to the keyboard too**, and a screen reader
  hears what the task is doing when it asks for the line's description (#1551).
- **purlis is now licensed under the Apache License 2.0 (was MIT); copyright Purlis.** The
  licence and its NOTICE ship with the app and show under About › Licences. Releases up to and
  including v0.4.1 remain under MIT.
- **Curation actions, Start a chat here and theme chats refused for an unapproved profile offer Approve and start in place** (#3968). These start their chats on the project's default profile without the new-chat picker, and purlis refuses a profile nobody has approved on this machine. That refusal now has an Approve and start… button, as the Skill studio's starts have. It asks the picker's own question, showing the command the profile would run, and once you approve it starts the same chat with its prompt or reference typed and not sent. Before, you had to open a new tab, approve the profile there and come back.
- **A dispatched task's first line writes the asking chat's name in a code span**:
  ``⟨task from `steward 3` · workspace alpha · …⟩``. A chat's name is something a chat can
  choose, and the line around it is purlis's own (#1438).
- **Several chats asking together are one notification.** "3 chats need you" names them, and
  clicking it opens the Inbox at the first one still waiting. A chat that asks while that
  notification is still fresh is named in one more a few seconds later, if it still waits. A
  notification is still only for something a chat asks you, never for an update.
- **Only what waits on your decision raises a system notification, and a click opens the Inbox
  at it.** A permission prompt, a dispatch grant, a sandbox host, a prompt in a harness's
  terminal and a chat whose turn ended on you each notify, titled by who is asking
  (`steward 12 › #3046 drill`) and saying what kind of ask it is, never a command line or a
  host. A task that failed, a refused commit and other information no longer do. One chat's
  asks a few seconds apart share one notification. Nothing is sent while the Inbox is open in
  the window in front, or the chat is on screen. A click brings purlis forward and opens the
  Inbox at that chat's group (#1694).
- **A Claude Code chat's commits name its model.** Once the harness has said which model its
  session runs on, an agent's commit says `Assisted-by: claude-code:<model>` instead of
  `Assisted-by: claude-code`. Until it has, the trailer names the harness alone, as before
  (#1021).
- **The light editor opens the files of a repo's own folder too**, with the same checks as a
  branch's (#948), and when it will not open a file it now says so in terms of the branch's
  folder (FM-1, #1104).
- **A chat in a branch folder has a Branch ▸ on its list**: Merge its branch and Remove its
  branch folder, on its pane's ⋯, its sidebar row's ⋯ and right-click, and in the palette as
  "Merge <chat>'s branch into its clone" and "Remove <chat>'s branch folder". They act on that
  chat's own folder, any chat's and not only the one in front's, shells' and tasks' too. Discard
  and remove anyway appears there only after a removal was refused (#4851).
- **A branch's changed-file marks come back about three times sooner on a large repo.** The
  explorer reads what a branch changed after every write an agent makes. That read now compares
  the working tree on every core and looks for new files at the same time, as `git status` does:
  at 100,000 files it takes about 0.45 s instead of 1.4 s, close to `git status`'s 0.3 s, and it
  still starts no git process (#1153).
- **Remembering and todos work from a sandboxed chat, one in a clone included.** In a chat purlis
  started, `purlis persona remember` (the persona's own memory and `--shared`), `purlis workspace
  remember`, `purlis workspace note` and `purlis workspace todo "<text>"` hand the write to purlis
  over the chat's own connection, and print what they always printed. purlis writes it in the
  chat's own workspace or persona, credits it to the chat, and holds each chat to 60 such writes a
  minute. One such write holds at most 12 KiB, and its title is one line. No such write touches
  git's, a hook manager's, a harness's or an editor's folders, an ignore file, or the sandbox
  settings (#1333).
- **A memory title is always one line.** A newline in a title no longer reaches the memory's
  heading or its index line, whichever command wrote it (#1333).
- **Tidying memory and closing todos work from a sandboxed chat.** In a chat purlis started,
  `purlis persona forget`, `edit-memory`, `archive-memory`, `unarchive-memory`, `move-memory`
  and `optimize --apply`, and `purlis workspace forget`, `edit`, `archive`, `unarchive`,
  `move-memory`, `optimize --apply` and `todo done|forget`, hand the change to purlis over the
  chat's own connection and print what they always printed. purlis makes it only in the chat's
  own workspace, the persona it runs as and shared memory, credits it to the chat and counts it
  toward the chat's 60 writes a minute. Recording a todo from such a chat now also finishes the
  closes an interrupted `todo promote` left behind, as it does in a terminal (#1408).
- **A sandboxed chat is told, not left to fail, where purlis does not write for it.**
  `purlis persona remember --ephemeral` and `persona forget --ephemeral` (scratch in purlis's
  state folder), a memory command naming a persona other than the one the chat runs as, and a
  curation or move that reaches another workspace are refused with a sentence that names the
  way round (#1408).
- **`purlis workspace create` works from a sandboxed chat.** In a chat purlis started,
  `purlis workspace create <name> [--vision "…"]` hands the create to purlis, which makes the
  new workspace as a terminal's `create` does and prints what it always printed. It makes only a
  workspace that is not there yet. `--live`, `--use` and repos to clone still run in the chat
  (#1408).
- **`--workspace <its own workspace>` in a chat is the same as no `--workspace`.** In a chat purlis
  started, `purlis workspace remember`, `note`, `todo`, `todo done|forget`, `vision`, `forget`,
  `edit`, `archive` and `unarchive` hand their write to purlis when `-w` names the chat's own
  workspace, as they did with no `-w`. A sandboxed chat naming another workspace is refused
  with a sentence that names the way round (#1408).
- **A browser login stays in the browser you're watching.** `browser_login` now fills the browser the
  chat names or is using, instead of opening a new one each time. A browser that already holds the
  login answers "already logged in" and fills nothing. A new browser opens only for a login kept for
  later reuse, and the chat and the browser's timeline say why and offer to close the one left behind
  (#5121, #5096).
- **A persona's browser login is performed by purlis in the chat's own browser.** A chat calls
  `browser_login` with the login's name; purlis fills it from the vault on the declared origin
  alone, submits it and hands the browser back logged in, and that browser then reaches the
  login's site alone. The values never reach the chat, and no session file is written. Running
  the login as a command now does nothing and names `browser_login` (#2016).
- **A chat's browser asks you once, not at every tool.** In a Claude Code chat, the browser
  tools no longer stop on Claude Code's own permission prompt. Your answer to the chat's browser
  Ask (this project's sites, also the open web, or Keep off) is what lets them run, as your
  answer to a dispatch is for a dispatch. Your own `ask` or `deny` rules for these tools still
  win, and a browser still reaches only what you allowed (#2245).
- **A sandboxed chat no longer offers its harness's own browser.** A Claude Code chat purlis
  sandboxes is denied its Chrome integration; the browser a chat drives is purlis's (#2013).
- **purlis's own skills are named `purlis-<name>` on every harness.** `handoff` is now `purlis-handoff`, and on Claude Code `/purlis:purlis-handoff`. Old names keep working where purlis reads them: `purlis:handoff` in a persona's `skills:` list, a skill's text or `skill_load` reads as the new name, so no project has to change. A bare `handoff` is now an ordinary skill name, so a project's skill named `handoff` loads. A bare `/smart-close` no longer starts purlis's smart close (#4524).
- **The window-building skill is now `purlis-building-ui`.** It was `building-purlis-ui`, and `purlis-building-purlis-ui` for a short while. Both old names keep working where purlis reads them (#4524).
- **A command typed in Claude Code needs the new name.** Claude Code knows a skill only by the name it has now, so type `/purlis:purlis-handoff`, not `/purlis:handoff`, and `/purlis:purlis-building-ui`, not `/purlis:building-purlis-ui` (#4524).
- **The `purlis-` prefix is reserved.** New, rename, install and share refuse it for any skill but a built-in one. A project's skill already named so stays on disk and is left out of chats, saying why, until it is renamed (#4524).
- **Built-in skills fold away in the Library, and you can make your own copy of one** (Skill studio preview, #3686). The skills purlis ships sit in one quiet line at the end of the Library, which unfolds them in place; the Built-in chip lists them alone. A built-in skill still shows on its own when it needs you, when a skill of yours has its name, or when your search finds it. Make my own copy, on a built-in skill's page or under the folded line, copies it to a skill level you pick under a new name and a description of its own, as a skill you can edit, and opens it. The description starts as the built-in's with "(your copy of …)" after it, so a chat that gets both can tell them apart; the built-in skill stays as it is, and chats keep getting it beside your copy.
- **Many busy chats no longer crowd the window.** What the chats are doing, their moves, the
  files they touch and their skill runs reach the window as one update about every 100 ms,
  however many chats are working, and it is drawn in one go (#4746).
- **Cards, Notices, badges, counts and separators each have one look.** An ask in the Inbox, a
  task's question in a chat and a block's report under its Notice are one card: in Purlis on the
  window's fill with corners 10 and no hairline, and an ask keeps its waiting edge in every
  theme. Every badge and count is a pill in 11px words, and Settings › Sandbox › Your hosts says
  each host's status: "Waiting for you" on the amber wash until you confirm it, then
  "Confirmed". The line between two groups (a menu's sections, a dialog's footer, the rows of the
  Inbox's Notices) is its own part, as thick as the theme's `separator.width`, 0 for none, and in
  Purlis a plain or primary button and a field draw no border at any size; Allow and a
  destructive answer keep theirs. A theme sets these
  through `card.*`, `notice.*`, `badge.*`, `count.*` and `separator.*` parts, and `purlis theme
  parts` lists them; a card's or a Notice's fill is held to a ground an Allow on it is measured on
  (#2912).
- **Certificate checks are on by default in every sandboxed chat.** `gh`, `glab` and other Go
  tools verify a host's certificate through a macOS system service, and a sandboxed chat was
  refused it until each person allowed it on each machine, so those tools failed with
  `x509: OSStatus -26276`, or with an error that hid the cause (`gh auth status` said the token
  was invalid). Now every sandboxed chat has it, on Claude Code, Codex and opencode, with
  nothing to allow:
  - Settings › Sandbox has one switch, **Certificate checks**, on unless the project turns it
    off. The separate "on this machine" row is gone;
  - `[sandbox] certificate-checks = false` turns it off for everyone in a project. `true` says
    what leaving the key out says. **A project that never set the key now has the check**;
    nothing in your files changes;
  - an administrator's `sandbox.socket-grants: false` turns it off on that machine, and
    Settings says who set it;
  - a chat that was already running when you updated keeps the sandbox it started with: the
    Sandbox changed Notice lists it with Restart, and a block in it says the same;
  - a chat that has the check and whose tool still fails a certificate check is told so, and
    is not told to restart.
  What this leaves open, by decision: that system service makes its own requests, for revoked
  certificates and for the certificates a certificate names, and those do not go through the
  sandbox's proxy. Turn the switch off in a project where that matters more than those tools.
- **Changes is in the Panel's left half, after Repos**, and the left sidebar keeps Chats,
  Explorer and Search. ⌃⇧G and _Show the Changes view_ open it there, bringing the half back if
  it was away. Every view's key opens the view wherever it lives (spec #1736, #1739).
- **Many busy chats no longer flood the window with redraws.** What chats report about moving,
  what they are doing and which skill they run is now drawn once per frame, so a burst from many
  agents is one redraw instead of one for each event (#4731, part of #4724).
- **A chat moving redraws only that chat's mark.** What every chat is doing is held in a store
  outside the project view, and each tab, explorer row and pane reads its own chat from it. A
  chat's move used to redraw every tab and pane in the project, twice; now it redraws that
  chat's mark. When the needs-you queue changes with it, as most moves between running and
  waiting do, the pane in front is redrawn once as well (#1034) (SC-3, #681).
- **Start fresh says when it interrupts a turn.** The question now says when the chat is
  mid-turn, or when its harness reports nothing so charter cannot tell. A chat started fresh also
  keeps its place in the strip at the next launch, not only in the window (#1246).
- **Chat settings files are held as integrity paths.** A Claude Code chat whose settings are too
  long for its command line gets them from a file in the project's state folder. That folder is
  now held as purlis's own, like its other records, so no sandboxed chat writes it. Each file is
  named by the digest of what purlis wrote, and purlis reads one back only while it still holds
  that.
- **Chat settings live in the app's data folder.** A Claude Code chat whose settings are too long
  for its command line now gets them from a file in purlis's data folder, outside the project,
  instead of in the project's state folder. Older files in the project are cleaned up and never
  read.
- **The project's state folder is held whole** for Codex and opencode chats on macOS: a chat
  never renames, moves or removes it.
- **The chat tabs sit at the top of the centre column, directly above the chat they show.**
  The workspace tabs stay where they were. Tab reaches the chat tabs after the left sidebar,
  and F6 into the editor lands on the pane, not on its tabs. At 1024 px with both sidebars open,
  the strip still shows the selected tab, the overflow count and the `+` (#1836).
- **The Chats list puts the sessions that need you first**, then the ones at work, then the
  idle. The tasks under a session stay in the order they were started. While the pointer is
  over the list or the keyboard is in it, no row is moved: the order, the folds the list makes
  and the chats that arrive wait until you leave. A chat that ends is the exception: its row
  goes at once, and the rows below it move up (#1499).
- **A session folds by itself when every task under it is over**, and its row then counts how
  they ended. It opens again when one of them works or needs you. A fold you set yourself is
  kept (#1499).
- **A row of the Chats list is two lines**: the name and the state, then where the chat works,
  how long it has been in that state where the window saw it change, and its own branch. In a
  narrow sidebar the name is cut short, with the whole of it on hover, and the state never is:
  it goes under the name, and wraps where the sidebar is narrower than the state. A finished
  task's row follows the same rule. A task says its workspace only when it is not the asking
  session's. The "no tab" badge is gone (#1499).
- **The left region is never narrower than 11rem**, so a nested row of the Chats list keeps
  room for its state at any text size (#1499).
- **The Chats list is tidier.** A top-level chat's name now starts where the filter's text does,
  not about 53px to its right. A row without chats under it no longer draws an empty fold, the
  empty line under the filter is gone (what the filter hides is said beside the view's title),
  and every row is one compact height. The state's mark stays first on a row; the persona's mark
  now stands at the row's end, one size on every row (DS-11, #1843).
- **The Chats list's words are sized by what they are.** A chat's name is 13px (it was 11.9px),
  what is said under a row or about a finished task is 12px in the secondary colour, a count is
  11px, and a workspace's heading is the same small capitals as the list's title. No line of
  words under a row is under 11px any more: the task limit line and a restart's answer were
  10px. A row's card follows: its name, then its facts in the secondary colour. Rows are the
  height they were, a file's row's in the Explorer (#1920).
- **Opening a chat's tab no longer reads every chat's skills again.** Whether each open chat runs
  on instructions or skills that changed since it started is worked out off the window's thread,
  and each chat's skills are read again only when the project's instructions change (#4738).
- **Chats run in the session host by default.** Every chat now runs in purlis's session host
  rather than in the app's own process, so a crash of the app no longer ends it. Nothing you see
  or do with a chat changes. Upgrading loses nothing: each chat that was open reopens on its own
  conversation, on its own profile, in its own folder and branch, and your session records and
  the profiles you declared yourself work as they did, with nothing to set up or approve again.
  Opening a project writes nothing into it. Quitting still ends every chat, and so does an
  update. If chats misbehave in the session host, you can run them in the app again while purlis
  still carries both: on macOS run `launchctl setenv PURLIS_CHATS_IN_THE_HOST 0` in a terminal,
  then quit purlis and start it again (`launchctl unsetenv PURLIS_CHATS_IN_THE_HOST` and a
  restart undo it); on Linux start purlis with `PURLIS_CHATS_IN_THE_HOST=0` set. Switched back
  after a crash, purlis first ends the chats the session host kept, as a quit would, and then
  reopens them in the app, so no conversation runs twice. Tell us what made you switch back
  (#2004).
- **The Chats view scrolls as one piece, and each row leads with its persona** (#3342). The
  title with New chat, the filter, the scope and the chips stay at the top on the panel's own
  fill while the rows scroll. Each workspace's name stays under them, and rows are 30px.
  Every chat's row starts with the mark of the persona it runs as, in its colour. The chat's
  state is a small dot on the mark's corner, and a done chat shows none. The tooltip and the
  screen reader say both, for example "steward, needs you".
- **The Chats view says when, and how many** (#3484). Each chat's row ends with the time it came
  into its state: "now", "2m", or the clock time, such as "10:42". In a narrow sidebar the name
  is cut short first and the time stays whole. The Needs you and Working chips show how many
  chats each would leave, and a screen reader hears the count once, after the chip's name.
  Where the list is grouped by workspace, each workspace's name has the same group heading as
  the other sidebar views, with its count at the end.
- **`purlis profile sign-in <name> --check` answers in its exit status.** It exits 0 if signed in, 3 if
  not, 4 if its harness cannot tell, 5 while its harness is being fetched, 6 if there is no such profile,
  and 1 if it could not ask. A harness that cannot tell used to exit 0, so a script that reads 0 as "go
  ahead" should accept 4 and 5 too (#4113).
- **A workspace's notices stack on its chip, and its clone shows there** (#3649). Several
  notices about one workspace now share one card on its chip, newest first, with a line that
  says how many. The chip's dot shows the most urgent of them: ● for news, ▲ for a warning, a
  shape and not a colour alone, and the chip's description says the count and the most urgent
  kind. Cloning a new workspace's repos now shows on its chip as "Cloning N repos…", counting as
  each repo lands, and turns in place into "Cloned …" or "Could not clone …", which offers Retry
  and the workspace's repo settings. It never closes on a timer.
- **Claude Code chats now go through purlis's proxy, as Codex and opencode chats do.** Each
  Claude Code chat gets its own pair of proxy ports, HTTP and SOCKS5, and purlis names both in
  the settings it starts the chat with. Every host the chat reached before is reached the same
  way, and every connection is in the network record and on the chat's Network view. This needs
  Claude Code 2.1.285 or later. An older Claude Code keeps its own proxy and the same allowed
  hosts, and says so once.
- **A Claude Code chat can no longer connect to other local ports or listen on one**, even where
  your own Claude Code settings turn local binding on, so it reaches the network only through
  its own two ports. Codex and opencode chats already could not.
- **`purlis clone` into a workspace that is not there makes it.** The workspace is created and
  scaffolded first, as `purlis workspace create` does, and the clone says so, instead of
  refusing and asking you to create it. A clone the app runs for a sandboxed chat still clones
  only into a workspace that exists (#1382).
- **The close that ends a chat keeps its danger cue under any theme** (#3295). A theme can draw
  the quiet buttons' hover its own way, which used to replace the red look of the pane close
  that ends a chat. Under the pointer, its × now always takes the danger colour and a thin edge
  of it, drawn after a theme's own rules, so ending a chat never looks like any other quiet
  hover.
- **Closing never ends a chat.** Close pane clears a pane and Close tab closes a tab. Their chats
  keep running in the sidebar, nothing is asked, and the close button no longer turns red under
  the pointer. To end a chat, use End… in its list. Closing the last tab on a strip leaves one
  empty pane (#4756). Undo, ⌘Z or the palette's row, puts a closed pane or tab back as it was
  (#4763).
- **A chat whose program ended keeps its pane.** Its last screen stays, read-only, under a line
  that says it ended, with Resume to start it again on its conversation and Clear pane. The
  keyboard stays where it was (#4756). A task left in a pane as it ended does the same: the line
  says how it ended and shows its report, and Resume reopens it in that pane (#4757).
- **A cluster operator Claim's runner runs in its requester's own namespace**,
  `purlis-runners-<hash>`, where a role binding gives that person alone the new cluster role
  `purlis-runner-owner` (their pods, `exec` and logs) and a quota, `purlis-person`, caps their
  runners: the chart's new `perPerson.quota`, by default 5 claims, 4 CPUs, 8Gi of memory and
  50Gi of storage. A Claim over it says `OverQuota`. A finalizer, `runners.purlis.dev/runner`,
  removes a Claim's runner when it is deleted, and the statement the operator signs names the
  runner namespace, so a desktop and an operator of this release go together. A Claim made
  before the upgrade gets a new runner there; make it again to free its old one (#2055,
  docs/cluster-operator.md).
- **The cluster operator changes only upstream objects it made.** An agent-sandbox object
  under the name it would use that it did not make is left as it is, and the Claim says
  `UpstreamObjectInTheWay`, naming it, until it is removed or renamed. Its ClusterRole gains
  `get` on `sandboxclaims`, `sandboxtemplates` and `sandboxwarmpools`, to read each by name
  first (#2258, docs/cluster-operator.md).
- **A cluster operator Claim blocked by a pool's objects that belong to Claims made before the
  policy says so.** Its `Ready` reason is `HeldByClaimsMadeBeforePolicy`, naming those Claims;
  a Claim blocked by an object the operator never made still says `UpstreamObjectInTheWay`
  (#2580, docs/cluster-operator.md).
- **Deleting a cluster operator Pool stops no runner.** A Claim whose runner was asked for
  keeps it until the Claim is deleted, and says `PoolDeleted` with the runner's own state; a
  pool's template and warm pool in a namespace now belong to its Claims there (#2259,
  docs/cluster-operator.md).
- **A cluster operator pool's template and warm pool leave a namespace with its last Claim
  there**, and a Claim made at that moment is served all the same. Its ClusterRole gains
  `list` and `watch` on `sandboxtemplates` and `sandboxwarmpools`, which it watches by their
  metadata alone (#2260, docs/cluster-operator.md).
- **Codex and opencode chats on Linux run at the floor**, as on macOS, in a project that has not
  turned the full sandbox on. So a Codex chat there starts only on a profile for sandboxed chats,
  and a chat at the floor does not run over ACP (#1040).
- **A Codex chat leaves out a plugin the project turned off** (#2769). Codex 0.163 takes a
  plugin turned off for one session, so Settings no longer says Codex plugins are not supported:
  it says a Codex plugin can only be turned off, since one Codex's own config turned off stays
  off.
- **A refused new workspace names `purlis workspace create`.** A chat that tries to make a
  workspace's folder or its `workspace.md` by hand is told to run
  `purlis workspace create <name> --vision "<text>"`, which purlis makes for it (#1408).
- **Codex and opencode chats dispatch and follow their tasks without their harness's prompt.**
  As in Claude Code, each dispatch tool is allowed by name, as Codex's `approval_mode =
  "approve"` and opencode's `permission` rule: consent to a dispatch is purlis's own dispatch
  grant. Your own rules still win: an approval you set on purlis's server in Codex's config, or
  an opencode permission rule that names the tools or asks about every tool, is kept (#3794).
- On Codex, a dispatched task's own question prompt now goes to the chat that dispatched it, as it does on Claude Code. Codex asks once more to trust purlis's hooks for this. If a redirect fails, or the question is for you, Codex asks in the task's pane and the chat shows in the Inbox as waiting on you.
- **A project switch no longer waits on the disk or on git.** The reads a switch makes of every
  pane and notice on screen (the sandbox's state, a chat's usage gauge, its persona grants, the
  network record) are answered off the window's thread, and so is every command that reads or
  writes a file, runs a program or starts a chat. The window's tabs are written down behind it.
  Where the window reads and changes the same thing, the answers still come in the order asked
  (#1949).
- **Counts agree with their noun everywhere purlis writes one.** The doctor's rows, `purlis
  save`, `purlis change`, the vault commands, the persona stats and lint, workspace fork,
  restore and remove, and the rest now say *1 file* and *3 files* instead of *3 file(s)*, and
  the verb agrees too (*1 repo has*, *2 repos have*). A test fails on a new "thing(s)" in
  shipped code (#2358).
- **`purlis workspace current` and `purlis persona current` say which rung decided.** The name
  on stdout is unchanged; a second line on stderr says where it came from (`• via cwd`,
  `• via session`), as `purlis status` and `purlis persona list` already did (#999).
- **`purlis workspace vision "<text>"` confirms the write.** It says `✓ Vision set for '<name>' →
  workspaces/<name>/workspace.md` on stderr instead of finishing silently (#999).
- **Settings picks the default persona, workspace and harness from what the project has.**
  Project › General's *Default persona* and *Default workspace*, and Harness & profiles' *Default
  harness* and *Default profile*, are pickers over the project's personas, workspaces and harness
  profiles instead of free text. Each has a *New…* entry: New persona… and New workspace… open the
  usual dialog and pick what they made, and New profile… opens `charter.local.toml` under Edit as
  TOML. A value set by hand that names nothing is shown as such, with purlis's sentence about it
  beside the setting, until another is picked. A save that would make `[persona] default` name no
  persona is refused, as one for `[harness] default` already was; a default workspace may still be
  declared before it is made (ST-1, #1225).
- **A chat keeps out of other harnesses' default folders.** A chat no longer reads or writes
  `~/.claude`, `~/.codex` or opencode's data folder unless they are its own harness's. On a pool,
  Claude Code's and Codex's built-in default profiles stay signed in again after a runner is
  replaced; opencode's signs in again for now.
- **Delete branch says why in its own words.** When git refuses to delete a finished task's
  branch, the window no longer shows git's own message, which could name a folder or suggest
  forcing the delete. purlis says that nothing was deleted, and git's words go to the log
  (#1102).
- **A skill deleted on this machine is kept for 30 days, then removed** (Skill studio preview,
  #3004). A skill whose delete could not be saved as a commit, a local one for example, is kept on
  this machine so Restore can bring it back. Those copies used to pile up. Now each stays 30 days
  after its delete and is then removed, as the Skill studio opens or before a `purlis skill`
  change. Each row of Deleted skills, and `purlis skill restore`, says how many days it has left.
  A skill whose delete was saved stays in the project's history, as before.
- **Deleting a vault asks like every other delete.** Its dialog ends in the same answer bar as
  deleting a workspace: Cancel first, then _Delete vault_ at the trailing edge. You still type
  the vault's name before anything is deleted (#1210).
- **New chat says "project".** Its line about built-in profiles, a persona's "project default"
  and the footer's reason no longer use the retired word "plane" (#602).
- **Devices names each chat's project when more than one is open.** With two projects or more,
  each chat and browser row says which project it is in, so two projects' chats of one name tell
  apart. With one project the rows stay as they were (#3534).
- **Devices: a runner whose key changed has Remove pool on its row.** It asks the same question as
  Remove pool in the Pools settings, removes nothing until you answer, and reads every device
  again once the pool is gone (#3533).
- **A task's questions name what their button acts on.** *Delete branch*, *Merge branch* and
  *Discard folder*, where they said *Delete*, *Merge* and *Discard*. Ask a persona says a
  *task* starts, as the rest of the window does, and the reading lines of two dialogs are
  said to a screen reader (#1719).
- **The first run and the opener say what they could not read.** The kill switch, the recent
  projects, the first run's look at the machine, the First task tab and the Vaults panel each
  say when a read failed, rather than drawing as if nothing were there. The first run asks for
  the project template before either way of opening a repo. The opener's path box is drawn as
  every other form's, and its act reads Open project. New persona's Inherits from is a pick of
  the project's personas, and Create says why it waits. About opens with the keyboard on Close.
  A vault's provider is named as New vault offers it (System keychain, 1Password), and a vault's
  token is kept in "your system keychain" on every system (#1719).
- **Discard names what git keeps for a task's folder alone.** Before it removes the folder of a
  task's own branch, the question now lists the refs only that folder has, its own
  `config.worktree` and the commits only its history of HEAD holds, all of which go with it,
  or says that purlis could not read them. A change in them since the question refuses the
  Discard and says so (#1472).
- **A dismissed Notice stays dismissed until its cause changes.** Dismiss a dormant pin, or a
  chat that came back as a new chat, and it stays hidden after a relaunch on this machine. Once
  the cause has gone (the workspace is back, the chat came back as it was) the dismissal is let
  go, so it shows again if the cause returns (NO-2, #1229).
- **At most two Notices stand under the strip.** The most important come first, trouble before
  news, and the rest are behind "+N more", which opens them as a list (NO-2, #1229).
- **A dispatch with no grant is no longer an error.** `purlis dispatch` used to answer `needs a
  grant` and exit 1. It now holds the task for your answer, says so on stdout and exits 0.
- **A chat on no harness profile can dispatch to a persona that names one.** It is refused only
  where there is no profile at all to start the new chat on.
- **Dispatch limits stack into a form in a narrow window.** Where Settings is too narrow for the
  limits table, each row shows its level, then each limit's box under its full name, with
  nothing cut off and no sideways scrolling (#1859).
- **A task you start yourself from a chat's tab is yours to steer.** The chat whose tab you
  asked from sees it in `purlis dispatch list`, marked as started by you, and reads its report.
  It cannot wait on it, send it a follow-up, answer it or cancel it, and the task sends that
  chat no note or question: that chat never asked for it and holds no grant for the pair.
- **There is one stop, and one line for it.** *Stop them*, as you close a chat with others at
  work below it, now stops them the way **Stop** does: each gets one short turn to write what
  it did, then ends, and none starts another chat meanwhile. The chat that asked is told in
  the same line (`purlis: the operator stopped …`) whether you pressed Stop, answered *Stop
  them*, or closed the tab of a task that had not reported.
- **Cancel and Stop do not collide.** A chat can cancel a task it dispatched; only you stop any
  other chat. A task you are stopping cannot be cancelled as well, and a cancel under way
  stands down when you stop its task. You can still ask a persona from the tab of a chat you
  are stopping; that chat itself starts nothing.
- **A chat's own list uses the window's words.** `purlis dispatch list` says `waiting on the
  operator` for a task stopped on a permission prompt or a question (#1443).
- **A cancelled task is recorded as cancelled, and a stopped one as stopped**, in the
  Dispatches tab. Neither is shown as failed.
- **A chat you are stopping can send its one last report.** It is still refused a new chat,
  and the command that sends its report now gets through.
- **Claude Code no longer asks before `purlis dispatch wait`, `list`, `cancel`, `tell`, `note`,
  `ask` and `answer`**, each allowed by name. Each reaches only a task the chat itself
  dispatched, or the chat that dispatched it (ADR 0064, amended).
- **`purlis doctor` checks three more of the rows it used to leave unchecked.** `harness` names
  every harness the project has and the most each offers (hooks, ACP or its terminal alone),
  and warns about a declaration in `harnesses/` that purlis refused. `vault registry` reads both
  halves of the vault registry, lists the vaults with their providers, and warns about a half
  that cannot be read or an entry no command can use; it opens no vault and asks no provider.
  `news` says whether this build carries its own release notes. The `mcp` row, still unchecked,
  now gives a reason of its own (#994).
- **`purlis doctor` checks `gh` or `glab` and its sign-in.** For each forge a workspace repo has
  its origin on, the `gh`/`glab` row says where the CLI is, or that it is not found, and the
  `… auth` row asks the CLI whether it is signed in on that host. purlis never reads the token.
  A forge no repo is on yet is said as unused instead of as not checked. The preflight a chat's
  start runs starts no CLI.
- **`purlis doctor` checks your vaults and the files that hold credentials.** The `vaults` row
  says, for each vault, whether its credentials are where it says they are: a keyring vault's
  items are asked for by their attributes only, a plain-file vault's file is looked for, and a
  1Password or reference vault's program is looked up. The `credential paths` row warns of a
  plain-text vault file that other accounts can read or that is reached through a link. Neither
  row reads a value or runs a provider's program (#994).
- **`purlis doctor` checks the version pin.** Its `version lock` row used to name the pin and
  say it was not checked. It now gives the same verdict as `purlis version`: a pin this purlis
  meets, or one on the Python charter's line, is fine, and any other pin is a drift warning that
  points at `purlis version` (HY-10, #573).
- **A gone workspace's pin shows in the title bar, and its notice hangs from it** (#3651). A pin
  whose workspace is gone is now drawn after the live pins as a dormant chip, with muted, slanted
  words and a dotted edge. "X is gone, kept dormant" hangs from it with Forget, behind a ● dot;
  pressing the chip shows it again, even after it was dismissed. A notice about the workspace
  you are in while it is not pinned hangs from its dashed "name +" chip, and stays with it once
  you pin it. A notice about a workspace with no chip is listed in the Notices centre alone, with
  an "Open X" link. "Forgot the pin to X" and its Undo stay in the Notices centre.
- **Each chat's prompt filter is keyed by a key of its own.** The filter a chat's hooks send to
  confirm a skill Use skill… typed, or a curation action's prompt, is now keyed by a random key
  purlis makes for that chat as it starts (`PURLIS_PROMPT_KEY`), on this machine, on a runner and
  for a chat taken back after the window restarts. A chat that was already running before the
  update gets its key at its next start (#3369).
- **Each new build of the app holds your keychain items again at its first launch.** Until
  builds are signed, the Keychain trusts the exact build that made an item, so the record of
  what the items are held to now names the build as well as the app. An item that would ask
  waits for your press, as it did after the rename (#1309).
- **Each Codex and opencode chat gets its own pair of proxy ports, HTTP and SOCKS5.** purlis's
  proxy beside the chat now also speaks SOCKS5. A chat's sandbox lets it reach only its own two
  ports, so no chat can use another chat's. The chat a connection belongs to is the port it
  came in on, never anything the connection sends. Both ports close when the chat ends.
- **The proxy refuses this machine, link-local addresses and cloud metadata services**, both
  as addresses and as whatever a name resolves to. The only exception is that exact address
  and port, if it is listed. The refusal is a Block whose Notice does not offer an Allow,
  because allowing the host would not let it through.
- **Every connection the proxy carries or refuses is now in the network record.** The record
  keeps the host and port, how it was decided (an Open host, a Persona host, an Allowed host,
  or refused), and a count. Connections are grouped into one line per host and port each
  minute, so the record stays small.
- **An empty view tab says what goes there.** The Saving tab with no saves yet, a chat's Network
  view that reaches no host or was refused nothing, a task's Changes with no changed file, and the
  repo instructions tab when the workspace's repos hold none now say what is missing and what
  would be listed, in the same empty state as the other tabs. The repo instructions tab names the
  files it looks for and has Read again (#626, #614).
- **Ending a chat is the window's alone.** Ending a task, stopping a chat and closing one are
  no longer served to a window on a link, as answering an ask is not (#1488).
- **A task you ended says so in its own words.** Its finished row reads "stopped by you" or
  "closed by you", each with a mark of its own, and stays a row of its own until cleared. The
  interim "cancelled" and "closed by the person" are gone from the window; "cancelled" is a
  task its asking chat cancelled (#1488).
- **A task's menu no longer has Stop chat and Stop with everything below it.** A session and
  a chat a handoff opened keep both (#1488).
- **A report a task sends once you have pressed Stop is the stop's report**, whatever it says
  of itself, and its row does not fold. A task that reported before you pressed ended by
  itself, and the chat that asked is told nothing more (#1488).
- **Ending a chat leaves its pane on the ended band.** After End…, or a Smart close once its
  record is written, the chat's last screen stays, read-only, under the ended band, and the
  keyboard stays where it was. A Smart close's band has Resume, which starts the chat again from
  its record in the same pane. Clear pane now closes the pane, and the strip's last tab keeps one
  empty pane (#5019).
- **Every dialog follows one set of rules.** A dialog's title stays at its top and its answers
  stay in view at its bottom, under a rule, while only what is between them scrolls, so no
  dialog scrolls its buttons out of reach. A dialog is as wide as its size, never its content, at
  most the window less 48 px tall, and anchored 24 px under the window's top, so a change in what
  it holds moves only its bottom edge; a button whose words change ("Create", "Creating…") keeps
  its width. Cancel always leads and the main action always trails, in the same place in every
  dialog, with at most one other answer between them; Return in a field is the main action,
  except for an act that cannot be taken back or one that grants, and Escape closes one layer at
  a time. An alert dialog starts on its safe answer, and no dialog or confirm row starts on an
  answer that grants, so a key pressed by habit never answers yes (#2980). A list of more than seven items in a dialog has a filter (Open vault, Add to a
  chat's context, Extensions). Reviewing an extension asks in place of the Extensions dialog
  rather than over it. A theme can set a dialog's surface, title and footer rule through its
  parts (`dialog.root.corner-radius`, `dialog.title.font-weight`), and `purlis theme parts` lists
  them; a dialog's corner is drawn at most 16 px at the default text size, and its quieter lines
  are held to 4.5:1 in the tier they are drawn in (#2910).
- **A theme's `focus-ring.*` reaches every focus ring.** The strip tabs, a tab's `×` closer, the
  strip gear, the Activity tabs, the needs-you button, Show more, the title bar's buttons and
  every other ring the window draws now take the theme's ring width and offset. Purlis Classic
  draws them as before (#2867).
- **Every form in the window now looks like Settings.** New workspace, New branch, New persona,
  Link to work item, a vault's secret dialogs, Delete vault, the forge question, First task, the
  repo picker, an extension's on/off, the repo's instruction files and Land's squash box draw
  each answer as Settings draws a setting: a name, the control, and a line on what it means. A
  form's buttons (Save and Cancel, Use this, Restore, Create) are drawn alike everywhere. The
  repo picker names each repo by its name, with where it lives and what it is under it. In First
  task, one arrow key now moves the pick, and nothing starts until you press the button
  (DS-3e, #1177).
- **`persona_where`'s answer may be larger than one line.** The chat's hook socket speaks a
  framed stream beside its lines, chosen by the client at the start of a connection, which can
  also carry bytes for tools that come later; hooks and commands that speak lines are unaffected
  (#1996).
- **Every question is answered from the same bar.** A dialog that asks something, such as
  deleting a workspace, removing a persona, approving a project or an extension, Push and Land,
  Save all, Make live, the doctor or About, now puts its buttons where the quit warning and
  Start a chat always did: in one row at the dialog's trailing edge, with the way out first and
  the act last (#1210).
- **More refusals in Settings link to the setting they are about.** A refused harness profile
  now links to that profile's own page, and the project file's `[plane] worktrees`, `[[forge]]`
  and `[harness] default` findings and `[chat_env]`'s refusals link to their settings too. Each
  reader of the files now says which key it refused, so no link is guessed from the sentence
  (#1292).
- **The Explorer's and the panels' words are sized by what they are.** A file's, a folder's, a
  repo's and a branch's name is 13px (it was 12px), and a row in a panel too (it was 11.9px).
  What is said about them, such as "Nothing here", "the workspace itself" or an empty view's
  sentence, is 12px in the secondary colour instead of dimmed text. The workspace's name beside
  _Files_ is 12px, and the _Files_ title is the same small capitals in the same colour as
  _Repos_ and _Memory_. A repo's branch count is bold, and a path purlis names and does not read
  is in the monospace face (#1920).
- **A branch's row in the explorer reads its branch and its repo.** It used to show the name of
  the branch's folder, with the branch beside it. It now reads _`fix/login` in svc_, and its
  folder's path is in the tooltip. A folder with no branch checked out still reads as the
  folder's name. A typed letter in the tree finds a row by its branch (#1102).
- **Explorer is in sections: Workspaces, Repos and branches, and Files.** Each folds on its
  heading and stays folded on the next launch. Workspaces lists every workspace with the focused
  one marked, and a press focuses it as its tab on the strip does. Files shows the files of the
  picked branch or repo, so a branch is one row and its files are drawn once (#1677).
- **Explorer no longer lists the workspaces.** The left sidebar's Explorer view had a Workspaces
  section above Files, the same list as the workspace tabs at the top of the window. It is gone:
  Explorer is the files of the workspace selected on the strip, and follows the strip. The Files
  heading still names whose files they are. A workspace's live mark and its menu (rename, Safe
  remove and the rest) are on its tab, as they always were. On the plane root's tab, Files says
  it lists a workspace's files and names the plane root in its heading. A layout file that had
  the Workspaces section folded is read as before, and nothing is said about it.
- **A chat touching files no longer redraws the whole Explorer.** Each file a chat reads or
  edits redraws only that file's mark and the marks of the folders above it, so an agent working
  fast keeps the window responsive. A project that is not in front does no work for its chats'
  touches; its marks start again when you bring it back. A file tab's tree is not redrawn for a
  chat working elsewhere. A screen reader now hears which chat is working on a file after the
  file's name, as its description, rather than as part of the name (#4730).
- **Three Skill studio capabilities are now version 1 of the extension API.** `grader`,
  `studio-panel` and `skill-router` no longer read as experimental in the approval prompt or the
  Extensions list, and [`docs/extension-api.md`](extension-api.md) records their messages.
  `skill-source`, `skill-lint` and `skill-template` stay experimental (#2786).
- **The file tab is a tree beside a resizable preview.** *Browse the files* now shows the
  branch as the explorer's tree, folder by folder, instead of a flat list of its first 500
  paths. The divider between the tree and the preview can be dragged or moved with the arrow
  keys; the tab remembers where you left it when you close and reopen it, and across a
  relaunch. Opening the same branch's files again brings its tab forward. The preview draws
  images as images and markdown rendered, with a *Source* button for its text, and gives a
  binary file, one over 2 MiB, or an image over 40 megapixels a one-line summary with its
  size. The window also no longer follows any link off the app itself; links open in your
  browser. The type-to-narrow box went with the flat list (FM-2, #1105).
- **Filter and search boxes show their glass again.** Every box that filters or searches (the
  chats, the explorer's files, Search, the find bar, Settings, the vault, the memory archive and
  the panel lists) is the shared field with a magnifier or filter icon at its start, and the
  text starts past it (#1856).
- **The title bar's right end is status pills**: the needs-you hand, the save, About, the kill
  switch and the update offer are each a 24px pill with full corners and 12px words (#2913).
- ⌘⇧J (Ctrl+Shift+J) opens a menu of only the focused chat's own tasks, under its pane. The task you pick opens in that pane, or comes forward if it is already on screen. The tab's task menu still opens from its chip, or with Down on the tab.
- **A forge or a profile names every user before it goes.** Removing a forge in Settings now
  also names each workspace clone on its host that `inventory/repos.json` does not list, at its
  workspace. Removing or renaming a harness profile also names a persona whose `model:` line
  starts its chats on that profile. Changing a forge's kind or host in its row is now refused
  when another forge already holds that host as another kind, as adding one is (#1241, #1720).
- **purlis asks a forge what it can do.** On GitHub it asks whether a repo's owner is an
  organisation: a personal account's repo has no issue types and no merge queue, and an
  organisation's repo on github.com has issue types. On gitlab.com it reads a group's plan,
  which GitLab shows to the group's owners. On a self-managed GitLab it reads the version and
  edition, and the licence if you are an administrator. A question nobody answered still takes
  its fallback (#802, #1202).
- **A GitLab auto-merge uses `auto_merge` from GitLab 17.11.** An older instance, or one that
  does not say its version, is still sent the deprecated `merge_when_pipeline_succeeds`, which
  it reads as "wait for the pipeline" (#805).
- **A self-managed GitLab shows a work item's own status.** This needs GitLab 18.1 and a Premium
  or Ultimate licence that your account can read. Elsewhere the item shows its board's status,
  as before (#1202).
- **purlis asks a forge what it can do once in a while, not on every question.** A probe's answer
  is kept in memory for 15 minutes, for the account, surface and host that asked it, and is never
  written to disk. A refusal is asked again next time. A question the forge refused or did not
  answer now says so, apart from one purlis never asked (#802).
- **`gh`, `glab` and `kubectl` settings join the names a chat does not write.** `~/.config/gh`,
  `~/.config/glab-cli`, `~/.local/share/gh` and `~/.kube/kuberc` are held as git's own config is, at every sandbox
  level, the floor among them. Chats on your own machine still read them, so a chat's `gh` keeps
  working; run `gh auth login` or `gh extension install` in your own terminal.
- A task's own cluster runner now stays, with the window's notice, while it holds work the proof used to miss: a change git was told not to look at, a stash under the newest, a file the task saved in the runner's home outside its project, or work from a start that failed after its program began there. Hidden folders of the runner's home and temporary folders are left out.
