- A task's own cluster runner also stays while the task saved a file anywhere else on it that its user owns, outside its home, such as beside the home on its volume; system and temporary folders are left out. A runner whose host started again still finds what the task saved before (#4933).
- **A project you get from your forge saves with your purlis sign-in from the start.** Get a
  project, by its URL or from your repos, now records the project's remote as soon as the clone
  lands, as Create and Publish do, so its first automatic save pushes with your purlis sign-in
  without a save from the window first (#1849).
- **gh and glab are general-purpose tools.** A persona tool whose program is gh or glab now
  shows the general-purpose caution beside its Allow, as curl does, and a declared gh or glab
  run reads none of the chat's own gh or glab settings: its home and settings folders are the
  run's own, and the variables that name another settings folder, host, pager or browser stay
  behind (#3421).
- **When git refuses to make or remove a branch's folder, the window says so in its own words.**
  What git printed (which could name a path inside the workspace, or carry git's own advice to
  force it) now stays in the terminal's `purlis worktree` message; the window names the branch
  and says that nothing was made or removed (#1102).
- **Grading after each edit follows a skill across a rename and a move** (#3612). Renaming a
  skill, moving it to another level or sharing it keeps grading after each edit on for it, with
  what you accepted unchanged: where a grade at its new place would run more chats, spend more,
  run other tests or compare with another version, the next edit waits for you to see the plan
  again. Deleting a skill turns it off, and a skill brought back asks for it again.
- **Every Skill studio page reads and fails alike.** While a read is under way it holds
  placeholder rows and says what it is reading after about a second; a read that failed says why
  in place, with Try again (#3978).
- **Grading a skill happens on pages inside the Skill studio** (Skill studio preview, #3688). A
  skill's Grades tab shows its latest grade as bars (with it, without it, its previous version),
  every grade with how it ended, and the grade-after-each-edit row, which says what each edit may
  spend before it is turned on. Grade opens the plan with its totals first and Start fixed at the
  foot, saying what it may spend of whose account; a plan that changed under you is held until
  you read the new one. A running grade shows its chats, its spend against its limit and its
  tokens, with Stop. The scorecard opens with how the grade ended, its totals and a row per
  trigger test, and each kept chat opens read-only from it. The scorecard and grade-chat tabs are
  gone: ones kept from an earlier launch come back as these pages.
- **Gradle and cargo keep your settings in a project's own caches.** A sandboxed chat's Gradle
  now gets the settings from your `gradle.properties` that say how it builds and caches, and an
  init script that sends its downloads through the chat's proxy, which Java does not find on
  its own. cargo keeps your certificate file, revocation check, `git-fetch-with-cli` and
  `offline`. Your proxy, JVM options, project properties and init scripts are not copied, and
  the written files say what was left out (#1364).
- **Each harness says where `purlis guard` writes its rule.** The writer for a project's ask or
  allow rule is now part of each harness's adapter, instead of a list of harness names inside
  the guard command. What `purlis guard ask|allow` writes and prints is unchanged (#922).
- **A command fed to a shell on its stdin, or run by `find -exec`, is told so.** A refusal of
  one used the sentence for a string or a heredoc a shell runs; it now names where the command
  was fed (#1426).
- **Handback reports are only ever written by the app.** The folder in which a dispatched task's
  report waits for the chat that asked for it is now held as purlis's own for every harness.
  The chat's hook reads the reports, and the app takes them off disk. Each report carries a seal
  that only the app makes; a report without a valid seal is handed only as quoted text, never in
  purlis's own words.
- **A handoff's refusals name the command a chat can run without being asked.** The heredoc a
  missing or empty brief is answered with, and the line for a workspace that is not there, now
  spell `purlis handoff` with a flag first (`purlis handoff --name "<task>" <workspace>`,
  `purlis handoff --create --vision "<what it is for>" <workspace>`), and no longer say
  `charter`. `purlis handoff report` no longer says "a handoff owes none", which read as a
  contradiction to a chat that owes a report as a task; it says the command sends none and
  names `purlis dispatch report` (#1471).
- **Every report is sent by `purlis dispatch report`, and `purlis handoff report` only says
  so.** A handoff owes no report, so the first message of a chat you hand work to no longer
  says how to send one. When you stop a chat that was handed its work, its one last report is
  sent with `purlis dispatch report`, as a task's is. `purlis handoff report` sends nothing and
  names that command, and an open from an older command line that asks for a report opens
  nothing and names `purlis dispatch` (#1471).
- **The refusal of a handoff whose words the shell rewrites names both of its names.** It is
  met whether the command was spelled with `purlis` or with the older `charter`, and now says
  so (#1288).
- **A skill's History and Grades follow a rename that keeps its folder** (#4021). Where a skill's
  folder already had its new name, a rename changes only its `name:` line. Its versions from
  before now keep the name they had, with their runs and grades, and its Grades tab and each
  grade's scorecard read the grades recorded under that name.
- **The Doctor's verdicts, the Curate submenu's arrow and the settings tick boxes are drawn as
  icons.** They were text characters, drawn in the font's weight and size; they are now the
  window's icon set, like every other icon (#627).
- The runner and cluster operator images are public: pulling them needs no GitHub sign-in, and a cluster needs no image pull secret. Each release's image is pulled and checked from outside before the release names it. The cluster pool guide no longer needs a registry of your own: your nodes pull both images from `ghcr.io`.
- **The runner and cluster operator images are checked before they are pushed.** Each
  architecture's image is built once into a file, checked, and only then pushed by its digest,
  so an image that fails its checks never reaches the registry. The `main` tag moves last,
  only after the image has been pulled and checked with no sign-in.
- **Imported themes keep their own quiet and disabled greys.** `purlis theme import` maps a VS
  Code theme's line numbers (`editorLineNumber.foreground`) to `text.quiet` and its disabled
  words (`disabledForeground`) to `text.faint`, and its muted words take the louder of the two.
  A base16 or base24 scheme's invisibles (`base03`) are its faint, walked to the 3:1 mark floor.
  No tier is drawn louder than the one above it: a tier the source has no grey for, or whose
  grey would read louder, follows the tier above it, as faint follows quiet and quiet follows
  muted (#2941).
- **A task that failed is an update, not something waiting on you**: the ✋'s number no longer
  counts a chat that is listed only because a task of its failed (#1693).
- **A dispatch refused while you were away is answered in the Inbox**, with its three answers
  (Never for this pair, Allow from now on, Dismiss), and the away summary's part for it opens the
  Inbox. It and a Smart close that stopped are no longer rows in the title bar's list (#1693).
- **Switching back to one of your last three chats is instant.** The last three chats shown
  across the window keep their terminal while you look at another, and go on taking what their
  program writes. Switching back shows the screen as it is now, with nothing started and nothing
  sent again. Showing a fourth chat lets go of the one shown longest ago (#4735).
- **No burst of keychain prompts after an update.** On macOS the app's launch copies keychain
  items to the purlis names with the Keychain's dialogs off. A vault whose items macOS would ask
  about (items an earlier build made) stays on its old items, where it keeps working, and the
  window offers **Finish moving N vaults**: only that press lets macOS ask, once per secret.
  `purlis migrate` in a terminal now copies the vaults whose secrets the command wrote itself,
  without asking, which also moves an install that has no app; `purlis migrate --undo` puts
  vaults moved either way back (#1306).
- **New keyring items are stored under `purlis/`, and items under `charter/` are still read.** A
  new keyring vault's items, and a newly stored 1Password identity, are written under `purlis/…`.
  A vault or identity stored before the rename keeps working from its `charter/…` item, and the
  check that an item is charter's own accepts exactly those two prefixes. 1Password items charter
  writes are tagged `purlis` (RN-4, #1261).
- **New keys for panes and tabs.** ⌘⌥ and an arrow moves to the pane in that direction (Alt and
  an arrow off a Mac, once Ctrl+Tab has left a chat's terminal). ⌘⇧] and ⌘⇧[ go to the next and
  previous tab (Ctrl+Shift+] and [ off a Mac). ⌘⇧J shows the focused chat's tasks, and ⌘⇧H goes
  back to the chat the pane showed before. The keys that went to the next and previous chat in a
  tab are gone, since a chat isn't a tab (#4767).
- **Closing a pane gives the keyboard to the pane that takes its space**, not to the tab's first
  pane. Ctrl+Tab out of a pane's terminal lands on the next pane's controls. A screen reader
  hears each pane of a split by where it is ("Left pane"), and hears one line when a chat you
  pressed is already in another pane and the keyboard moved there (#4767).
- **The left side has an activity bar, and shows one view at a time.** An icon strip at the
  window's edge switches the left side between Chats and Explorer; pressing the open view's icon
  puts the side away, and the strip stays with a count of the chats that need you. ⌘B puts the
  side away and brings it back, ⌘⇧E shows Explorer and ⌘⇧C shows Chats (Ctrl elsewhere), and
  both views are in the palette. Each project remembers which view it showed, how wide the side
  was and whether it was away. The explorer no longer lists chats: the Chats view is the one
  place they are. The status line's toggle for the left side is called Navigation now (#1673).
- **The layout file is version 2.** Each project keeps its own arrangement under `projects`,
  and the left region is `navigation`. A version 1 file is read and moved forward at the first
  change, so every arrangement you saved is kept (#1673). Going back to an older purlis is
  safe but forgets the arrangement: an older purlis cannot read version 2, so it draws the
  default layout and says so, and its first change rewrites the file as version 1, without
  each project's own arrangement.
- **Leftover persona sub-agent files are a Notice with Fix, not a line in every briefing.** When
  the project still holds sub-agent files purlis generated for a persona, the Inbox shows one
  Notice whose Fix runs `purlis doctor --fix persona-agents`, and it goes once the files are
  gone. A chat's briefing no longer mentions them (#1990).
- **A held connection waits in the Inbox as soon as purlis asks.** Each host a chat's proxy holds
  a connection to is listed straight away and says the connection waits on your answer, even
  when the chat's sandbox Notices come too fast to show each one. Allow and Keep blocked there
  answer it as its Notice does, one ask at a time (#1709).
- **The main views share one look.** The explorer, a file tab's tree, the Changes view, the
  Inbox, the files view, the panel lists, Search, the vault, Dispatches, Saving, the opener and
  every empty state now draw their buttons, fields, selects, rows, trees and tables with the
  window's shared styles: one control height, one row height, a tree's levels in one step with
  straight guides, and an empty page's way out as the primary button. A filter box no longer
  carries its own glass; a pressed toggle stands on the accent (DS-12, #1844).
- **A memory's body is edited in the text editor**, with line numbers, Markdown colours and find
  (⌘F or Ctrl+F). If the memory changes on disk before you save, the memory as it now is opens
  beside your edit, and you can take lines from it before you choose Reload or Overwrite
  (#1862).
- **Every right-click menu is shorter and says less twice.** A row is now a short verb and no
  longer repeats the name of the thing you right-clicked: *Rename…*, *Pinned*, *End*, where a
  chat tab's menu said *Rename chat console-developer 16…*. The sentence that stood under almost
  every row is now the row's tooltip, shown when the pointer or the keyboard rests on it; a
  short sentence stays under a row only where it cannot be undone, or to say why a row cannot
  run, and it is never cut short.
  A chat tab's personas are behind one *Ask* row instead of a row each, its Activity and Network
  behind *Open*, and its three ways to stop behind *Stop*, so the menu is at most ten rows
  whatever the project holds. Red is kept for what cannot be undone: *End*, the ways to stop,
  closing a project, and deleting a workspace, a persona or a vault. *Restart*, *Remove folder*
  and a memory's *Delete*, which has an Undo, are no longer red. A pinned tab, workspace or
  project shows *Pinned* with a tick. *Rename…*, *End* and *New shell* show their key. The tab
  in front no longer lists a greyed *Switch to*. The same holds for a workspace's, a project's,
  a branch's, a repo's, a persona's, a vault's, a todo's and a memory's menu, a secret's menu in
  a vault, and a setting's *Move to…* menu. The command palette still names each thing in full.
- **More dialogs say what they are doing, and answer in one order.** Updates and a task's brief
  put Close first and the act last, as every other question does. Rename workspace says it is
  asking which chats would start fresh while Rename waits, and the doctor, a persona's profile,
  a brief and the palette's file search say what they are reading. An extension's action, Make
  live and Make local read Running…, Deleting… or Making live… while they run. A task's
  question about the tasks still working below it is a radio group Tab and the arrows reach.
  The pin on the status line is named Pin 9.0.0 and says "project", and a pin purlis could not
  read is said rather than hidden (#630, #1719).
- **A dispatch's "Needed you" counts the times its task waited for your input.** That is a
  permission or a question it asked mid-turn, or an ask of its open in the window. A turn that
  ended, a report that reached nobody and a task below it that came to nothing no longer add to
  it (#1457).
- **A persona's Skills line counts what needs you without reading the whole Skill studio**: no
  compatibility badges and no router are read for it, and it counts what the Needs you page
  holds (#3781).
- **More database clients keep the certificate's name through the tunnel.** A brokered
  `purlis secret exec` honours `PGSSLMODE=verify-full` beside a `postgres://` URL or a libpq
  string that names no mode, gives a SQL Server URL `hostNameInCertificate`, and points
  `MYSQL_HOST`/`MYSQL_TCP_PORT` and `REDIS_HOST`/`REDIS_PORT` at the tunnel as it does
  `PGHOST`/`PGPORT`. A value whose client checks the certificate by name with no way to keep it
  (MySQL's `VERIFY_IDENTITY`, MongoDB over TLS, `rediss://`, a `verify-full` value run by `usql`)
  is handed as it is, with a note naming the variable (#1708).
- **A Claude Code chat starts only its proxy.** purlis no longer makes a temp folder and an ssh
  route beside a Claude Code chat, which never used them (#1699).
- **The old `.purlis/app/sandbox-blocks.json` is taken away** when the project opens: nothing
  has read it since the network record took its place (#1681).
- **The network record is written on time.** Repeats of a sandbox block held back within a minute
  are written when the chat's turn ends, when the chat ends and when the project is let go of,
  not at the next block the project hears; and a burst of connections is written a few seconds
  after its minute ends, not at the next connection (#1681, #1699).
- **Allowing a chat its own persona's grants is audited and recorded**, as every other Allow is
  (#1681).
- **A host refused before a chat had its number is still shown.** One purlis's proxy refused in
  the moment before the chat was numbered is raised as its Block once it is, not dropped (#1683).
- **The sentence about an older Claude Code counts as said once a tab shows it**, so a chat that
  never reached its tab does not use up the one telling (#1699).
- **The new-chat dialog opens again without checking everything again.** Its profiles, personas
  and each profile's sandbox, sign-in and approval are kept for the project once read. A change
  to a profile, a persona, the sandbox policy or an installed harness drops them, so the next
  open reads them again (#4737).
- **The new-chat dialog opens at once.** It shows the personas and the profiles straight away,
  and each profile's billing, approval and sandbox fill in as they are checked, in room kept for
  them, so nothing moves. A chat started before then waits for them. If it turns out to need an
  approval, or the sandbox cannot hold it, nothing starts: the keyboard goes to Cancel, the
  footer says why, and the button holds still for a moment so a second click grants nothing
  (#4736).
- **New project and New vault look like the rest of purlis's forms.** Both dialogs now draw
  each answer the way Settings does: a name, the box, and one line of help under it. A screen
  reader now reads that line as the box's description (#1175).
- **New skill… asks how you want to make the skill** (Skill studio preview, #3684). Write it
  yourself, ask a chat to draft it, or install one from a source. Writing it yourself asks for a
  name (checked as you type: its shape, a built-in skill's name, one the level already has), what
  it does, where it lands and a template, then opens the new skill's page with its text in the
  editor. Asking a chat asks what the skill should do and where it lands, and opens a chat with
  the request typed and not sent; its draft comes back to Drafts. The Skills view's New skill…
  opens the same dialog. The inline New skill panel and the empty studio's three starts are gone.
- **`purlis theme check` reads a notice card where it is drawn** (#4210). A card's title and mark
  are measured on the ground each card stands on (news on the overlay, trouble and attention on
  their own), and a news card's mark is held in its success colour at 3:1. A new finding,
  `notice-way-not-apart`, names a theme whose notice card's secondary button would stand too
  close to the card to read as a button.
- **A notice card's mark and title are theme parts, and its secondary ways look like buttons**
  (#3478). Themes reach a card's mark as `notice.mark` (its colour) and its title as
  `notice.title` (colour, size and weight). The theme check reads the title's words on the card's
  ground. On a notice card, a secondary button such as "Add a vision" now has a visible fill in
  Purlis dark and light, where it used to read as plain words.
- **A pin to a workspace that is gone is kept dormant, not dropped.** The window used to say
  "Unpin from the palette, or put the workspace back", and the palette had no such row. Now it
  reads "ide is gone, kept dormant", and the pin comes back in its place by itself when the
  workspace does (a pull, another branch). Forget drops it for good, with an Undo that puts it
  back where it was (NO-1, #1223).
- **Every standing line in a project's window has a way out.** A chat that came back as a new
  chat, a resumed or guessed chat, a chat that did not start, a project the last quit could not
  reopen, a project that is gone from your recents, and the window's trouble line can each be
  dismissed now. They were lines you could only read (NO-1, #1223).
- **An AGENTS.md of yours that purlis's exclude line hides has Open file and Move aside….**
  The note on a chat's pane used to tell you to commit it or move it aside, with nothing to
  press. Open file shows it in your editor. Move aside… asks first, then renames it to
  `AGENTS.aside.md` (or the next free name), never over another file, so `git status` shows it
  again (NO-4, #1231).
- **A slow start on Linux offers Copy command** for the relaunch without the session bus it
  suggests, so you don't retype the environment variable (NO-4, #1231).
- **A refused read in the explorer has Read again.** A workspace that could not be read, a
  repo purlis will not read, and a repo whose branches could not be listed each offer Read
  again, and the line goes once a read works. The bottom bar shows the same lines and stays
  read-only (NO-4, #1231).
- **Notices use the shared buttons and surface.** Every button on a Notice, in a pane, in the
  Inbox or on a Settings page, is now the app's shared small button, and the buttons still wrap
  onto new lines in a narrow pane rather than being cut off. A Notice's box, and what one of its
  buttons opens under it, share one bordered surface with the rest of the app (#1855).
- **A project file's on/off keys are switches.** Sign commits, Auto-save, an extension's on/off
  and its own on/off settings, and Certificate checks show the value in force; not set here is
  the switch at the value beneath it, and Reset takes a value set here back out. A harness
  plugin's on/off stays a select, since purlis does not know what the harness decides (#1865).
- **The dispatch grants table stacks into a form where Settings is narrow**, as the Dispatch
  limits table does: each cell under its column's words, nothing cut (#1865).
- **A chat's actions are one list, the same on its pane, its sidebar row and in the palette.**
  The pane's new ⋯, the row's ⋯ (on hover and focus), its right-click and Shift+F10 all open the
  same list in the same words, and the palette has a row for each action of every chat,
  including chats with no tab. Rename, Restart, Start fresh, Move to, the work link, Use skill,
  Ask, Activity, Network and the new End… act on that chat, never on its tab's first pane. A
  tab's right-click holds only the tab's own rows. A row that can't run now is greyed with its
  reason, such as Start fresh while nothing the chat read has changed (#4753).
- **The palette has one Ask row per persona, for the chat in front.** It used to list one row per
  persona for every chat tab, all titled alike. Each tab's menu keeps its own rows (#1468).
- **Every button in the window is one button family** (#2904). Buttons, icon buttons and
  buttons that read as links are drawn and behave the same everywhere: one look per variant
  (primary, secondary, ghost, danger, soft accent, soft warning, link, and the grant's look an
  Allow keeps), three sizes, and every button in a row the same size. Every Allow and Accept
  leads with its open lock and its accent edge, and is never drawn as the suggested answer. The
  window's buttons sit on React Aria, so they press the same way from a pointer, a key or a
  screen reader, and show their focus ring only from the keyboard.
- **One chat card at a time, and the next one comes at once.** A card the keyboard brought up on
  one row goes when the pointer brings up another's, and moving the pointer from one row to the
  next while a card is up shows the next card without waiting again. A finished task's row is
  one line too, as a chat's row is: its state is the mark, and the words, with how many times it
  was tried, are in the row's tooltip and read to a screen reader (#1687).
- **`purlis memory` snippets read a memory's frontmatter the way the persona and skill
  readers do.** The line shown under a search hit is the first line worth showing below the
  frontmatter's closing `---` line. A `---` with text after it, or indented, is text and
  closes nothing. A memory whose frontmatter is never closed shows no line. purlis-core's
  memory, inventory, workspace-section, git-config and init readers now strip and split lines
  through the line format's one copy of Python's `str.strip` and `str.splitlines` (#3482).
- **The explorer marks a file you moved without staging it as renamed**, not as one file deleted
  and another added, and **a file edited and then put back as it was at the base is no longer
  marked**. Its change markers are now read by purlis's one diff engine, which reads the
  contents of changed and untracked files (up to 128 MiB in one read; past that a file is
  marked without being read, so one put back to its base content is still marked changed) and also computes a branch against its base, any two refs, what is
  not committed and a cross-repo change, each checked against `git diff`, for the Review tab to
  draw (RC-2, #704).
- **Every checkbox, radio, switch, segmented control and slider is drawn one way.** A ticked box,
  a picked radio and a switch that is on take the accent's fill with a mark in the window's colour
  on it, and nothing beside a choice moves when it changes. A switch is a 34 × 20 pill whose thumb
  slides across in 150 ms in Purlis, and never under reduced motion. Settings' You / Project / Workspace
  switch and the Chats and Inbox scopes are one segmented control: the chosen segment stands on the
  window's ground with a thin edge under it, and its words keep their weight. Start a chat's harnesses are cards
  of one height with no radio circle, the chosen card told by its wash, its accent edge and its
  check; a persona's icon and colour are picked from tiles. Every group of options is one Tab stop
  with the arrow keys moving the pick, and the Chats list's state chips stay one Tab stop too. A
  theme can set each choice through its parts (`switch.track.selected.fill`,
  `option-card.root.card.selected.border-colour`, `segment.root.selected.fill`), and
  `purlis theme parts` lists them (#2907).
- **Every box you type in is one field family** (#2905). A name, a token, a filter, an answer
  and a list of entries are drawn and behave the same everywhere: a label, the box, a line of
  help and the reason a value is refused, as one. A field says what is wrong with a value when
  you leave it, and follows your typing until it is right; a form says it at each field and takes
  you to the first before it sends anything. **⌘⏎** (Ctrl+Enter off macOS) sends a form's main
  answer from anywhere in it, a box of several lines included, and starts a chat from Start a
  chat; it never presses an Allow or something that cannot be undone. A filter keeps your caret
  where it was while its list redraws.
- **A skills folder of more than 2000 names is not read, and says so.** A plane level holding more
  names than purlis reads of one folder lists none of its skills, and names the folder once with
  the reason, as a clone's skills folder and a project's opencode plugin folder already did
  (SK-52, #3205).
- **A project's opencode config with a second name is not read.** An `opencode.json` or
  `opencode.jsonc` inside the project that is a hard link is listed as a config purlis cannot
  read, as a skill's own file with a second name is. The home folder's and the folders above
  the project still read one (SK-52, #3205).
- **You can allow a held tool folder for one chat.** At the default sandbox level, a chat blocked on
  the `gh`, `glab` or `kubectl` settings, or on the folders below, offers **Allow only for this
  chat**, naming the folder whole, and never Always. On macOS, a Codex or opencode chat may then
  write that one folder. Claude Code's sandbox can't allow one folder alone, so a Claude Code chat
  may write that name in any folder for its run; the Notice says so. A chat purlis wraps on Linux,
  and a chat on a runner, still get no Allow here.
- **The folders fish, Neovim, bash completion and the session bus load code from** under
  `~/.local/share` are now held from chats, and can be allowed the same way.
- **`.claude/rules` is held in every folder**, as `.claude/commands` is, with no Allow. A chat can't
  write a repository's rules, and a chat's update of a clone that changes them is refused; make that
  change in your own terminal.
- **Every list is one family** (#2911). A panel's todos, personas and memories, the vault picker,
  the memory archive, Use skill, the search hits and the theme gallery are walked the same way:
  one Tab stop, the arrows stopping at the ends, typing to find a row, Enter to open or choose,
  and Shift+F10 for a row's menu. A row's pill under the pointer stands in from the panel's edge,
  a chosen row keeps its size, and the keyboard's ring is drawn inside the row. A long list in a
  dialog, a panel or Settings has a filter over it. Themes can now style a list's rows part by
  part.
- **One list: the Inbox holds what the Alerts drawer and the band under the tab strip held.**
  Every line that stood under the tab strip, two at a time, is now a Notice in the project's
  Inbox, after what asks for you and before what happened, every one listed with its ways out.
  The alerts are Notices there too: this project's and this machine's whole, and one line for
  each other open project that has some, which opens that project's Inbox. The status line's
  Alerts button is its Notices button, counting them and opening the Inbox. A Notice that
  answers what you just did (a refusal, an Undo, a saved record) or the summary of a time away
  brings the Inbox on screen (#1695).
- **The title bar's hand opens the Inbox, and drops no list of its own.** What its list named
  is in the Inbox: a chat waiting in another window's project is a group of its own there, with
  Go to chat and Ignore, and each chat that cannot tell purlis it is waiting is a Notice with Go
  to chat. A window with no project brings the chat in the other window forward (#1695, #1700).
- **Every menu is drawn the same way.** The overflow menu on a strip, the menu a tab's task chip
  opens, the right-click menus and their submenus share one surface, one row height and one
  highlight, where they had three copies that had started to differ. Checkboxes and radio
  buttons in forms and Settings are drawn from the same sizes as the rest of the controls
  (#1834).
- **One mark for every character you cannot see.** A control, zero-width, direction-changing,
  blank or other invisible character is now written as `⟦U+XXXX⟧` everywhere purlis shows text
  it did not write: the install review, every table and report on the command line, a brief
  that holds one, and a skill version's changes, where some used to show `‮` or `<U+202E>`.
  The same list of characters is checked everywhere, and it is longer: variation selectors,
  Hangul fillers, Arabic number signs and wide or no-break spaces count now. A joiner that
  holds an emoji, a Persian word or a Devanagari conjunct together reads as text and is not
  marked, so `👨‍👩‍👧` shows as one family (#3172). Every emoji Unicode names is one here, so
  `©️`, `▶️` and `㊗️` read as text too, as do a keycap such as `#️⃣` and the flags of England,
  Scotland and Wales; a black flag with any other tags after it is still marked (#3219).
- **Every menu, context menu and popover is one family** (#2909). A tab's menu, a row's
  right-click menu, a terminal's, a tab's task chip, the strip's show-more, a secret's and a
  setting's *Move to…* are drawn and walked the same way: under what opened them, lined up with
  it and never against the window's edge, closed by a click outside or by Escape, the arrows
  stopping at their ends, a row that cannot be undone in the danger colour, the key that does the
  same at a row's end. A row's card and a refused name share their surface. Themes can now style
  a menu's rows and a popover's surface part by part.
- **A chat's pane draws its asks from the Inbox's own list.** A sandbox block, a folder write, a
  dispatch grant and a prompt held off screen are drawn on the chat's pane while the Inbox lists
  them, at most two per chat, the longest waiting first, so an answer in either place clears
  both. Their answers say the same words in both places (#1695, #1700).
- **The Inbox lists what waits longest first,** by when each ask began, where its source knows
  it (#1700).
- **A report with nowhere to go and a refused commit are updates in the Inbox,** not asks: they
  raise no notification, and Dismiss puts the chat's needs-you item away with them (#1694).
- **A folder write is asked as a folder write,** in the Inbox and its notification, apart from a
  host (#1700).
- **The theme parts manifest's version moves once per release.** `purlis theme parts` prints
  `version` as the last release's manifest version; a family, part, variant, state or property
  added since then is listed with `since` one above it, and the schema says "plus unreleased
  additions" while there are any. What a release shipped never changes (ADR 0103, amended
  2026-10-25).
- **Coming back to the window asks git once.** A return both shows the window and gives it focus,
  and the save standing was read for each, so every return ran `git status` twice. The two now
  count as one return (#1392).
- **Work a chat needs an answer from has one route, `purlis dispatch`.** A chat told to
  dispatch to a persona could run a reporting handoff instead, because the handoff skill
  taught `--report` as the way to get an answer and `--persona` for another persona. The
  handoff skill, the persona skill, `purlis docs show handoff`, `purlis handoff --help` and
  the briefing of a chat the app started (as where such work goes, not as a reason to give
  work away) now say one thing in the same words: work a chat
  needs an answer from, for its own persona or another, is `purlis dispatch` (with `--in
  workspace:<name>` when it must run elsewhere), and a handoff is fire-and-forget. The
  refusals that named `purlis handoff <workspace> --persona <name>` as the way to dispatch to
  a persona (a vault a chat may not use, `purlis persona use` inside a chat) name `purlis
  dispatch --to <name>` (#1515).
- **`purlis handoff --report` is carried out as a task.** It is still taken, and it sends the
  app the ask `purlis dispatch --in workspace:<workspace>` sends, so the new chat is a task of
  the asking chat in every respect: `purlis dispatch list` shows it, `wait`, `tell`, `answer`
  and `cancel` work on it, the window shows it as a task, and its report is delivered as a
  task's is. The result says so and names `purlis dispatch` as the route from now on. A task
  with no `--name` is called `handoff to <workspace>`; it leaves no todo and no `handoff` row
  in the dispatch log, and no extension is told a handoff was created; and `--report` with
  `--create`, or into a workspace that is not there, is refused with the two commands that do
  it, because a task works in a workspace that exists (#1515).
- **Every select and every box with suggestions is one family** (#2906). Settings' choices, the
  filters of Dispatches and the Skill studio, Search's scope, the browser bar's page size and
  Add a skill are drawn and walked the same way: a drawn chevron and a quiet placeholder, the
  list under the box on the menus' surface with the menus' rows, the arrows stopping at their
  ends, Escape leaving the value as it was, and a long list (ten options or more) opening with a
  filter that takes what you type. Themes can now style a select's box and a combobox's part by
  part.
- **Every select is the same select.** Settings, dialogs and the Dispatches and Search filters
  open one list in the window's menu style, with a tick on the current choice. Enter or an arrow
  opens it, and typing a letter jumps to an option (#1860).
- **On/off settings are switches.** The Chats list settings under You, and an extension's on/off
  in Extensions, turn on and off at once. Options in a form, such as Start a chat's, stay
  checkboxes and are applied by the form's button (#1860).
- **The bar at the bottom of the window reads as one status bar.** Notices and Doctor are flat
  items on it, each with its icon, its word and its count, in place of two boxed buttons. Where
  you are is on the left (the project, the workspace and its counts) and what wants a look is on
  the right (Notices, Doctor, a pin that drifts).
- **The project is shown by its name.** The bar shows the last part of the project's directory
  and no longer the whole path; rest the pointer on it, or reach it with Tab, to read the
  directory.
- **Every table is one family** (#2911). The Dispatches tab, a workspace's repos in Saving, a
  skill's runs, totals and history, the Skill studio's tables and a vault's secrets are walked
  the same way: one Tab stop, the arrows along the rows and across the cells into a cell's
  button, and a row's menu under the ⋯ at its end, on a right-click or Shift+F10. Each table
  stands in a rounded card that scrolls it sideways where it is narrow, its column names in small
  capitals. Settings' tables of fields keep their own keys and still stack into a form where
  Settings is narrow. Themes can now style a table part by part.
- **The Changes view is a tree of the tree family** (#2911). Its rows are walked as every tree
  will be: one Tab stop, ↑ and ↓, → into a row's first child and ← back to its parent, Home and
  End, typing to find a row, and Shift+F10 or the menu key for a repo's menu. A row's pill under
  the pointer stands in from the view's edge, the keyboard's ring is drawn inside the row, and a
  screen reader hears each row's whole line, its kind first ("changes: 3 changed"). Themes can
  now style a tree's rows part by part.
- **The chat in front looks selected, and every tree draws its levels the same way.** The Chats
  tree, the explorer and a file tab's files share one tree style: a straight guide per level
  under the row it hangs from, and the selected row (the chat in front, the spot the next chat
  starts in, the file shown) drawn with an accent fill and an edge. A row under the pointer and
  the row the keyboard is on each look different from it. Themes gain `list.selected`,
  `list.selected-edge` and `tree.guide` (#1672).
- **A repo nobody touches no longer costs a `git status` every ten seconds.** A clone's save
  standing (its Saving row, and auto-save's look at a repo that saves itself) is now read again
  when something in its working tree changes, heard by the same watch the explorer uses for a
  branch's changes, rather than on a ten-second clock. In a large repo one `status` can take a
  second of several cores, so an idle project with one open used to keep the machine busy. On
  Linux, where a tree is watched folder by folder, a clone is still read on a clock for now,
  but never more often than every 200 times what its last read took. The alerts now read the
  project root's changes from the same shared reading instead of a `git status` of their own,
  and purlis's own reads no longer ask git for the untracked cache, which a read that never
  writes the index could not use; saves still add it (FD-11, #651).
- **A chat's start note links to where your editor is chosen.** When *Open file* on the note
  about a hidden `AGENTS.md` finds no editor chosen, the note says so with *Choose your editor*,
  which opens Settings › You › Editor (#1244).
- **opencode gets purlis's built-in skills under their own `purlis-` names.** In an opencode
  chat, purlis's skills are `purlis-secrets`, `purlis-handoff` and so on, as Claude Code knows
  them as `purlis:secrets`, and the index skill a chat past its skill budget gets is
  `purlis-skill-index`. A skill of a repo's or your own named `secrets` is then another skill
  beside purlis's, each reached by its own name. _Use skill…_ types `/purlis-secrets`, and a
  chat's own list of its skills names them the same way. A project skill named like one of them,
  such as `purlis-secrets`, is left out and says to rename it. A repo's or your own of that name
  still loads beside purlis's, and the Skill studio says the chat may use either one. Claude Code and Codex chats are unchanged.
- On opencode, a dispatched task's own question prompt now goes to the chat that dispatched it, as it does on Claude Code and Codex. If the redirect fails, or the question is for you, opencode asks in the task's pane and the chat shows in the Inbox as waiting on you.
- **Bringing many chats back at a launch no longer reads the sandbox policy once per chat.** The
  list of open chats is worked out off the window's thread, and the browser sites each chat's
  sandbox mark counts are read once and kept until this machine's policy changes or you allow
  or remove a site for every chat here (#4739).
- **Pointing a Pool at a GitHub App key takes `use` on that key** (`forgekeys`, by the Secret's
  name). A Pool or Claim made before the new policy `purlis-forge` settled must be made again to
  mint, and `use` on a minting Pool must be granted to the person by name: a right held only through
  a group is refused (#4206).
- **Dialogs, popovers, menus and tooltips look related.** Every surface the window draws over
  itself now has the same background, border, corner and shadow, and dialogs and popovers the
  same padding. The buttons in every dialog are the shared buttons: the one a form submits with
  is marked, and an answer that cannot be undone keeps its danger colour (#1845).
- **A pane head's buttons are in two groups.** The chat's actions come first, in this order:
  the state button, the bell, then ⋯. After a thin divider come the pane's controls: Split right,
  Split down, then Close in the corner. Tab moves through them in the order they're drawn. A pane
  showing a task, which has no Close, keeps the same groups. So does a view's pane, which has
  only the pane's controls (#5203).
- **A pane's notices fold into a bell in its header.** The bell sits in a fixed slot before
  split and close, and counts the pane's notes, in the trouble colour when one is trouble. The
  band of notices is under the header now, so the header never moves when one arrives.
  Minimised, the default, notes fold into the count and asks stay as full cards; expanded shows
  every notice, with Dismiss all, which leaves the asks. The choice is one for every pane and is
  kept across restarts. The cap of two per pane and its "N more in the Inbox" line are gone, and
  an ask has no Dismiss (#4754).
- **An empty memory list offers its way out.** A workspace's, a persona's or the shared memory
  list with nothing in it now shows the same New memory… button as the `+` on its heading, and
  a command in a panel's empty-state text is shown in code font instead of with its backticks
  (#1156).
- **A workspace's panels read again only the section a change is part of.** The app keeps the
  focused workspace's repos, todos, memories and session records in memory once it has read
  them. A memory an agent saves now reads that workspace's memories again, and not its todos,
  its session records or its repos. A change the app cannot place still reads everything
  again. A closed todo no longer makes the window check which chats run on old instructions or
  read the curation actions again: only a change to the project's files, the harness settings,
  a persona or a workspace does (FD-10c, #934; FD-10d, #935).
- **A theme's button parts are held in states that hold at once.** A button hovered and pressed,
  or focused and selected, is measured as the stylesheet draws it, against the same floors as one
  state; a part that breaks one there draws its default, and the theme check names the states
  (#2958).
- **A theme's button parts are held on every surface a button is drawn on.** The parts check
  measures a button's words, its edge and its look on each surface the window puts buttons on,
  a Notice's danger surface and wash included, and a test finds those surfaces from the
  window's components (#2959).
- **A theme with component parts is measured once.** Its stylesheet, the theme check and the
  gallery's cards share one pass over the workspace tints, so applying a parts theme and drawing
  a gallery of them take about half the time (#2954).
- **`purlis persona list` and `current` name the variable that decided under both its names.**
  A persona or workspace chosen by the environment reads `via $PURLIS_PERSONA or
  $CHARTER_PERSONA` (and the same for the workspace), and the way out says to unset both, since
  the old name still decides when the new one is unset (#1344).
- **`persona lint` warns about a `color:` purlis cannot draw**, and names the fix that rewrites
  Claude Code's `cyan` and `magenta` (#1460).
- **`purlis doctor --fix persona-agents` also removes what this machine kept for the retired
  sub-agents**: the in-flight records and the map of sub-agents to personas in the state
  folder (#1460).
- **The README roster block says what the committed dispatch log holds**, from before a persona
  ran as its own chat, and sends a reader to `persona stats` for the dispatches since. It no
  longer draws a share of "generic agent" dispatches (#1460).
- The persona view's label reads **Dispatch to it for**, and the persona skill says a chat's
  persona is fixed when it starts and teaches a task's `note`, `ask` and `report` (#1460, #1463).
- `posttooluse-message` is no longer wired into the plugin; an installed plugin that still names
  it is answered with nothing, as before (#1460).
- **A persona is no longer a harness sub-agent.** A sub-agent call whose type is a persona is
  refused on Claude Code, and the refusal names the route: `purlis dispatch --to <persona>`,
  or, for a draft, that its definition has to be finished first. A helper that is not named
  for a persona still runs, as its chat's persona. On opencode the `task` tool reaches the same
  refusal; Codex's sub-agents carry no type, so there is nothing to refuse there (#1451).
- **A persona chat on Claude Code is started with its persona's MCP servers.** The servers of
  `personas/<name>/mcp.json` were started for the generated sub-agent; they are started for
  the chat that runs as the persona, for that chat alone. A server that takes a credential
  from the persona's vault still goes through `purlis secret exec`, and is started only once a
  person approved it on this machine. An approval given before carries over. An unapproved
  server is withheld, and the chat is told which and how it is approved. On Codex and opencode
  a persona's servers are not started, and the chat is told (#1451).
- **`disallowed-tools:` is honoured for a persona chat on Claude Code, and refuses the chat
  elsewhere.** The chat is started with those tools denied. On Codex and opencode purlis
  cannot deny them, so starting a chat as that persona, or dispatching to it, is refused with
  a sentence (#1451).
- **A persona's one-line description is told to its chat.** `agent-description:`, or
  `description:` where there is none, is quoted in the briefing of a chat that runs as the
  persona and shown by `purlis persona show`. `purlis persona create` and a project template
  write no sub-agent file (#1451).
- **`purlis persona stats` and the persona skill count and describe dispatches.** `DISP` is
  read from the committed dispatch log and stops moving until it is counted from each
  dispatch's record. `purlis persona lint` no longer checks declared skills against the
  installed ones, and warns when a charter still teaches the sub-agent route (#1451).
- **The Personas view groups its personas** (#3483). Working now lists the personas with a chat
  at work or asking for you. In this workspace lists the ones that have worked in the focused
  workspace, by a session record there or a chat there. On the plane lists the rest. Each
  group's name stays at the top while its rows scroll, with its count at its end. A persona
  moves to Working now when one of its chats starts, and back when they all rest.
- **The Personas view keeps its rows still under you** (#3566). A persona that worked in the
  focused workspace stays under In this workspace after its chat closes, with or without a
  session record, for as long as the window holds the project. While the pointer is over the
  list or the keyboard is in it, no persona changes group or place. The move happens once both
  have left, as in the Chats list.
- **The right activity bar comes straight after the right sidebar in Tab order**, before the
  Panel, so Tab reaches a side's icons beside the side they switch (#1686).
- **A chat's plain git is held to a branch folder's one live writer too.** A chat started
  without the sandbox that runs `git commit`, `git push`, `git pull` or `git rebase` (or a merge,
  cherry-pick, revert or am) in a branch folder another live chat holds is refused before the
  command runs, naming the chat that holds it, in the words `purlis worktree commit`, `update` and
  `push` are refused in. The first chat to write in a free folder takes it. When the app
  doesn't answer, the git runs. Your own terminal, and a harness you start yourself, are never
  held to it (#3931).
- **Agents writing the plane without pause make the sidebar read it again about once a second,
  not four times.** The plane watcher now waits for 250 ms with no change before it tells the
  window, and tells it at most 1 s after the first change of a run. A single change still shows
  within about a quarter of a second (#4741).
- **A host an administrator's policy forbids is refused when you save the file.** Saving
  settings under Edit as TOML now refuses a new host the policy does not allow, as Add already
  did. Hosts the file already held are kept and still reach nothing (#1431).
- **You can revoke a grant the policy has locked out.** On Settings › Sandbox › Granted, an
  entry the policy no longer allows still has Revoke (#1431).
- **A refusal says when the policy requires the sandbox.** Where an administrator's policy
  requires the sandbox, a chat that cannot start sandboxed is told it is the policy that
  requires it, not the project (#1431).
- **A refusal no longer points to an opt-out policy forbids.** Where policy locks "Start
  without the sandbox", a chat that cannot start says what to change and names the policy and
  who set it (#1423).
- **A host policy does not allow is refused when you add it in Settings**, with the policy's
  sentence, where it was written and then never reached. The Granted list marks a host or folder
  you granted that policy now drops as not in force, and the Notice of a change to the project's
  hosts names only hosts a chat reaches (#1423).
- **Removing a pool ends its links at once.** Chats still on a pool's runner end as they do when
  their host goes, and the next chat reaches the runner kept under that name now.
- **What a runner must be to receive a vault value or token.** A cluster runner whose claim or
  pool is stopped, or whose operator no longer says it vouches for it, is sent nothing. A kept
  claim's pod made again asks again for a browser login. A pool that a chat ran on without the
  sandbox is sent no tool values, tokens or browser logins.
- **A cluster operator's statement may hold at most fifteen minutes ahead.** If your computer's
  clock runs more than about five minutes behind the cluster's, purlis refuses the pool and tells
  you to set the clock right.
- **A kubectl or Docker command given a time ends what it started** when that time is up.
- **Pool setup is where a Docker pool is added.** Add a pool… in the palette and in Settings opens
  Pool setup in the project in front; a cluster pool has its own Add a cluster pool…. While this
  machine keeps no pool, a chat offers Move chat … to a pool…, and Welcome has one quiet row, Run
  chats on another machine. The chat picker marks a pool whose setup isn't finished and says why,
  with Finish Pool setup… on that pool, and doesn't offer a pool where a chat can't start (#4484).
- **Try it in Pool setup can be cancelled.** While its test chat starts, Cancel beside the button
  stops it, as Cancel does in the chat picker: the chat closes and nothing is kept. Leaving the
  step or closing the tab cancels it too. A quit in the middle of Try it no longer brings back a
  "Try it on <pool>" chat at the next launch (#4976).
- **A pool's runner where a chat ran without the sandbox is signed in on no more, on a Docker pool
  as on a cluster pool.** The sign-in says so and how to get a new runner: remove the pool and add
  it again. Vault values, tokens and browser logins already stopped there.
- **A pool sign-in started from the command is confirmed in the window.** `purlis profile sign-in
  <profile> --pool <pool>` now asks the running purlis window, on Docker and cluster pools alike,
  and goes on once you press Sign in there. With no window running, the command says so and starts
  nothing.
- **A prompt purlis fills in now starts its skill directly.** In Claude Code, the Skill studio's
  prompts, Try it, the Curate menu and the theme chats type
  `/purlis:purlis-skill-studio write outcome evals for login in skills/login`, unsent, in place of a
  sentence naming the skill. opencode gets its own `/<name>` form, and Codex keeps the sentence,
  because purlis only lists skills there (#5186).
- **A press on a chat goes to the pane you used last, in whichever of the project's windows.**
  With a tab window open, a press on a chat that no window shows lands in the most recently
  used pane across the project window and its tab windows, and that window comes forward. A
  minimised window is passed over. With one window nothing changes: the chat lands in the
  focused pane (story 97, #5108).
- **`purlis profile remove` reaches the pools' runners.** With the window running, each
  pool's runner shown to be yours forgets the profile and its sign-in, as Remove in Settings does, and the command
  names any pool whose runner is too old to forget it. With no window, it says each runner
  forgets it at its next tidy, and no drain carries its sign-in.
- **Renaming or removing a profile says which open chats run on it.** Where open chats were
  started on the profile, its Rename form says how many, and Remove asks first: they keep
  running, but the next launch cannot start them again under a name no profile has. A profile
  no open chat runs on is still removed at one press (#1290).
- **A project's Claude Code settings are screened again when they change.** While a sandboxed
  Claude Code chat that loads its project's own settings is open, purlis watches those files.
  When they change and no longer hold only what a sandboxed chat keeps, purlis restarts the chat
  on its conversation at once, even with no window open, on your own Claude Code settings and
  purlis's. Its tab says which keys were not applied. A chat that cannot be started again is
  ended, and its tab says why. A change that still passes changes nothing. Where the files cannot be
  watched, the chat starts on your own settings and purlis's from the first.
- **A project's or the app's result pops from the status bar** (#3653). A refused pin and the
  other results of project and app actions no longer push the window down from the top of the
  content: they pop from the status bar's Notices item, as the same card a workspace's notice is
  on its chip, pointing down at Notices. A click elsewhere hides the card and leaves a ● dot on
  Notices, which brings it back; × or Esc dismisses it, and F6 reaches it. Each is still listed
  in the Notices centre under Results, and dismissing it in either place dismisses it in both.
  Themes reach the new dot as `status-item.dot`.
- `purlis doctor --fix project-skills` now runs with the Skill studio preview off. It still runs only when you name it.
- **Publishing a project commits a file only under the one name it has on disk, as a save
  does.** Publish refuses a file with a second name (a hard link), or one that is not the file
  that was staged, names each one, and makes no commit and no push. A new project's first
  commit and a `purlis doctor --fix` commit are held to the same rule.
- **Publishing a skill says up front when the forge says you cannot push to the source.** The
  review asks the forge first, and where it says no, the publish page and `purlis skill publish`
  say so and offer Export. The push still answers for itself (#4342).
- **The command line is `purlis`, and `charter` still runs it.** The app ships `purlis` beside
  itself with `charter` as an alias for the rename's window, and **Install `charter` command in
  PATH** now links both names; the `.deb` installs both. Every guard that recognises charter's
  own command recognises `purlis` too (RN-3, #1255).
- **The product's environment variables are now `PURLIS_*`, and `CHARTER_*` still works.** Every
  variable that steers a command, set by you, by the app for a chat, or by a harness
  (`PURLIS_ROOT`, `PURLIS_HOME`, `PURLIS_WORKSPACE`, `PURLIS_CONFIG_HOME`, `PURLIS_DATA_HOME`,
  `PURLIS_LOG_DIR` and the rest), is read under its `PURLIS_` name first. Its `CHARTER_` name is
  read when the `PURLIS_` one is not set. Chats and extensions are given both names until 1.0,
  so hooks and scripts that read the old name keep working. A harness profile may set neither.
  A variable that chooses what a command acts on is refused rather than guessed when both names
  are set to different values. Those variables are the project, its state, the workspace, the
  worktrees, the persona, and the config and data homes. The refusal says to set both
  names to the same value (`PURLIS_ROOT=<x> CHARTER_ROOT=<x> charter …`). So a single name
  typed in front of a command inside a chat tells you what to type, instead of acting on the
  chat's own project (RN-2d, #1260).
- **Purlis now matches its Figma record** (#3177, #3113). The default primary button is filled
  in the accent with white words, and Allow keeps its edge and its lock, so the two never look
  alike. Controls, fields, dialogs and menus draw no hairlines; every md control is 28px tall
  with 8px corners; controls' and dialogs' words are 13px, with 15px and 18px headings; every
  corner is on the record's 7/8/10/12 scale; a chosen activity button takes the record's
  lavender wash and lighter icon, and the update pill's words are lavender. Purlis Classic
  looks as it did.
- **purlis has its own look: a calm teal on warm greys.** Both built-in themes are drawn in
  Verdigris, a slightly desaturated teal accent on warm graphite (dark) and warm paper (light)
  neutrals, easy on the eyes in long sessions. Every text and mark still clears its contrast
  floor in both themes and in every workspace colour, and the status colours did not move. The
  themes are now called `purlis-dark` and `purlis-light`; a project, a workspace or a saved choice
  that names a theme by its old id keeps drawing the same theme under the new name (#1838).
- **The built-in icon theme is now called `purlis-icons`.** A project, a workspace or a saved
  pick that names it by its old id keeps drawing the same icons, and the Icons setting shows it
  under the new name (#1854).
- **Purlis is the default theme.** A new install, and any project, workspace or machine where
  nobody chose a theme, now draws Purlis: the lavender dark from the designer's foundation, in
  IBM Plex Sans and JetBrains Mono with Lucide's icons. When your system asks for more contrast,
  it draws Purlis's high-contrast dark. A dark, light or "Follow the system" pick now draws
  Purlis too: `purlis-dark` (and `charter-dark`) draw Purlis's dark, `purlis-light` (and
  `charter-light`) its light, and `system` follows the system with your own `theme.json`, or
  else with Purlis. No file is rewritten. Settings › Theme no longer offers `purlis-dark` and
  `purlis-light`, and labels a file that still holds one. To keep the green look purlis had
  until now, choose **Purlis Classic** (`purlis-classic`). Purlis is no longer marked Preview,
  and a new theme draft extends Purlis (#3034).
- **A red, orange or pink workspace keeps its colour on its strip.** A workspace's colour now
  dims only the accent and the marks beside the danger colour, which must stay apart from it.
  The strip and every other token it tints keep the colour's full hue in every theme (#3034).
- **A stored Purlis light pick follows the system's contrast.** If your theme was saved as Purlis
  light (`purlis-light`), Purlis now draws light high contrast while the system asks for more
  contrast, the same way Purlis dark already draws dark high contrast. An appearance you chose by
  name, such as `light`, still draws exactly as chosen (#4677).
- **High contrast's code comments and punctuation are easier to read.** They moved up a step of
  grey, as the rest of Purlis's high-contrast words did (#3182).
- **Every marker charter writes is recognised under the purlis name too.** The `.gitattributes`
  merge rules, the live-workspaces block in the `.gitignore`, the personas block in the
  project's README, the `persona sync-agents` marker and a workspace manifest's digest key are
  read under either name. They keep charter's spelling until the project is migrated to purlis
  names, so a teammate on an older build still finds them; after that each is rewritten in
  place under purlis's, never left beside a second one. Files that are never committed move to
  purlis now: a checkout's `info/exclude` block, the layer record (`.purlis-generated`), the
  structure stamp (`.purlis-structure`), a chat's `AGENTS.md` line and the opencode shim's
  first line. A file charter's record or digest owned stays charter's after the record moves,
  so it keeps being updated instead of reading as hand-edited (RN-2b, #1258).
- **New saves, landings and requests use purlis names on the forge.** Branches purlis creates
  are now `purlis/…` (`purlis/save/<host>-<clone>`, `purlis/<workspace>/<sha>`, `purlis/<sha>`),
  agent commits carry `Purlis-Chat`, `Purlis-Persona` and `Purlis-Change` trailers, and pull
  request bodies carry the purlis markers. A save pull request still open from a `charter/…`
  branch carries on there until it merges, so the rename never opens a second one. `Charter-*`
  trailers and charter markers in existing history and on existing requests are recognised for
  good: `change revert` still finds old landings, an amend never adds a purlis twin of an old
  trailer, and an old change block is rewritten in place (#1259).
- **Purlis draws its italic and bold text in real faces.** Comments, emphasis, headings and the
  terminal's bold text use IBM Plex Sans Italic and JetBrains Mono Italic and Bold, bundled with
  purlis, instead of faces the window slants or thickens itself. A project file's theme select
  now offers `purlis` and `purlis-classic`, and a chat's `theme_preview` marks Purlis as a
  preview and can draw its high-contrast dark (#2709).
- **Everything purlis holds in its state folder is held under every spelling of its name on
  macOS.** The rows the sandbox keeps there from a chat (the app's folder, the theme drafts, what
  skill deletes keep, the reports waiting for a chat, your approvals, every chat's settings file,
  the vaults and their key, and a state folder that is not there yet) are now held in any case on
  macOS's case-folding disk, as the Skill studio's records already were, under either spelling of
  the state folder and where `$PURLIS_HOME` puts it. On Linux, whose disks do not fold case, each
  is held as it was.
- **Old `[harness_plugins]` keys are ignored, and said once.** A project that still holds them
  starts as any other. One ask in the Inbox names the files, and its Remove shows the change that takes the
  keys out for you to apply, a workspace's `workspace.json` included; nothing is rewritten until
  you do (#3467, #3486). If a file changes before you apply its change, dismissing that stale
  change brings the ask back, with Remove, while the file still holds the keys (#3569).
- **The theme skill and the theme docs say which corners a theme reaches.** The rail, the title
  bar's workspace chips and the session tabs are rounded through their parts; only a tree's rows
  wait for their family (#2928).
- **The app, the command line and the skills say purlis.** Messages, refusals, doctor rows,
  the command line's help and usage line, the window's text and the plugin's skills name the
  product purlis, always lowercase. What the window, a project or a harness reads by name is
  unchanged: the `charter` alias, the `CHARTER_*` variables still read, the commands a
  project's ask rules spell (`charter handoff`, `charter report --yes`, a todo's promote,
  `charter session record`) and every file name stay as they were until the project is
  migrated. Text written into a project's committed files (the generated persona agents, a
  new persona, the README's roster, `workspace.md`, the topology and the inventory) names the
  program `charter` until the project is migrated with `doctor --fix rename-plane`, and
  `purlis` after. The crates and packages are `purlis-core`, `purlis-cli`, `purlis-app`,
  `purlis-session-protocol`, `purlis-same-user` and `purlis-site` (RN-11a, #1269; RN-13, #1272).
- **The note about where questions from tasks go is one line.** "Questions from this chat's
  tasks now come here" has **Change**, which opens Settings at Where you answer, and a × that
  puts it away for good. The "Answer from each session" and "Keep this" buttons are gone; keeping
  the setting needs no answer (#5213).
- **Reading a task works as a tool and asks nobody.** Claude Code no longer asks you before a
  chat runs `purlis dispatch read` on one of its own tasks, and the same read is there as the
  `dispatch_read` tool for harnesses that prefer tools to commands. The `dispatch_report` tool
  now says that a turn ending without a report is asked for one, and that purlis then sends the
  task's last message in its place (#2084).
- **Read again where a read failed once.** A session record's tab, the Vaults section and About
  purlis each offer Read again beside a read that failed, where closing and reopening was the
  only retry. A workspace made live whose save did not happen offers Go to Saving (#1296).
- **Read again in the First task tab and a vault's tab.** When the First task tab cannot read
  the profiles it starts on, it says why with **Read again** beside it. A vault's tab offers
  **Read again** beside its provider's health line, and when the vault could not be opened at
  all, so a provider signed in or unlocked meanwhile is read without closing the tab (#1296).
- **A read purlis was refused can be read again with the explorer hidden.** The bottom region's
  line saying what purlis could not read (the workspace, the forge cache, a repo or its working
  tree) has a menu with Read the workspace again, and the palette has the same row while a
  refusal stands. It is the explorer's own Read again (#1244).
- **On a read-only project, Settings turns off only what writes a committed file.** Settings ›
  Project decides row by row from the file each row writes: what is kept in `purlis.local.toml`
  (`charter.local.toml`) alone, such as the default profile, the environment passed to chats,
  your profiles and your hosts, and Edit as TOML on that file, stays on. A row that may move to
  the committed file stays off, and the links out of Settings stay on (#1759).
- **More of a read-only project's Settings stay on.** On a set-aside dispatch grant, **Give
  back** and **Remove** stay on, because they change only this machine. On Dispatch's Limits,
  the limits you set for yourself on this machine stay editable, and the project's own limits
  and overrides are off with the project's sentence as why. A harness declaration's **Open
  file** stays on: it only opens the file in your editor. Discover stays off, because it writes
  the project's committed list of repos (#1795).
- **A Secret ask writes to the persona only when you ask.** The Fill notice has an unticked
  **Remember this need for the persona**. Tick it to read the exact line and edit its purpose, and
  Fill writes it to the persona's definition. No proposal follows a Fill any more, so one-off keys
  and what a chat said they were for stay out of git. A key's row in its vault still has
  **Offer as a Secret need ▸**, which now shows the same line for you to edit and add (#5240).
- **A change purlis holds says so.** In the Inbox it reads "purlis" and the chat and ask behind it,
  never "chat 0 · Plane root" (#5240).
- **Removing a branch folder counts the git state only that folder keeps.** `purlis worktree
  remove` and removing a workspace now refuse a folder holding a ref only it has or settings of
  its own (`config.worktree`), and name what would be lost. A commit that was amended or
  rebased away does not stop a removal. Where git would not say, the folder is kept too.
  `--force` still discards it (#1472).
- **A workspace or a persona in use by a running chat is not removed.** Removing a workspace is
  refused while a chat is running in it, and removing a persona is refused while a running chat
  has adopted it, `--force` or not, from the command line and the window alike. The refusal names
  the chats; close them first (#1373).
- **Remove pool now tells you when older runners may still hold conversations.** If an older runner of the pool holds your chats' conversations, or purlis has not checked it yet, the Remove pool question lists it and asks a second time before those conversations are deleted with the pool. If another such runner turns up after you were asked, nothing is removed and purlis says so (#4860).
- **Remove pool names what goes back to this machine.** Its question, in Settings › This machine ›
  Pools and in Devices, names each project and workspace set to run on the pool, and says nothing
  of them when none is (#4678).
- **Removing a repo from a workspace names its branches when it refuses.** A repo whose
  branches have folders of their own is refused with each branch by name and the way out in
  the explorer, and a repo whose branches could not be read says so in the same words as the
  explorer's own refusals, with no "worktree" in them (#1102).
- **Rename workspace, Start a chat, the first run and Updates look like Settings.** Their boxes,
  choices and ticks are drawn as Settings draws a setting: a name, the control, and a line on
  what it means. In Settings, _Your editor_ now moves to the editor a single arrow key reaches.
  Updates holds the channel you pick until you press **Use this channel**, so moving through the
  channels with the arrow keys no longer moves the machine to one (DS-3d, #1176).
- **A Claude Code chat reads purlis's todos, memory, session records and change status without
  asking.** The five read-only tools of purlis's MCP server are pre-allowed for each chat the
  app starts, for that chat alone. Writing a todo or a memory, and `ask_operator`, still ask, and
  your own `ask` or `deny` rules still win (#1050).
- **The `pr` and `pr-merge` save modes are called request modes in purlis's messages and docs,
  on GitHub and GitLab alike.** `charter.toml` still takes `pr` and `pr-merge` (#1087).
- **The window calls a worktree its branch, and its directory the branch's folder.** The
  explorer and the command palette say *Merge branch …* and *Mark branch … done* by the branch's
  own name, and *Remove folder …*. The bottom bar counts branches. When purlis refuses to
  merge, remove, mark done or list one, the window says why in those words, with no
  command-line flag to run; `purlis worktree` keeps its own sentences (#989).
- **Restart to update asks what to put back before it restarts.** The update's dialog now has
  *After the restart*: **Reopen every chat** (in front) or **Start fresh**. purlis carries the
  answer across the restart, so the new version no longer asks *Reopen your sessions?* when it
  starts (#1078).
- **A deleted skill whose name a built-in skill took comes back under a new name** (Skill studio preview, #3729). When a newer purlis ships a built-in skill with the name of a skill you deleted, Restore used to refuse it until it expired. Now its page on Deleted says "Its name belongs to a built-in skill now, so it comes back under a new name." and asks for one, starting as `my-<name>`. `purlis skill restore <name> --as <new-name>` does the same, and the list marks such a skill. The new name is checked as a rename's is: a built-in skill's name is refused with "That name belongs to a built-in skill; pick another, or make a copy." The skill's `SKILL.md` `name:` and its folder are renamed to match, in the restore's one commit.
- **Revert works on a skill's versions from before a move or a rename** (#4017). The version's
  files come back in the folder the skill has now, as one commit, with the same checks as any
  revert. A version from before a rename comes back with its `name:` line changed to the name the
  skill has now. The History tab's confirm says where the version is from and what changes.
- **The right side has an activity bar too, and shows one view at a time.** Todos, Memory,
  Personas, Sessions and Vaults are each a view, switched from an icon strip at the window's right
  edge, and an approved extension's panel is a view of its own after them. Memory is open by
  default. Pressing the open view's icon puts the side away, and the strip stays with a count of
  your open todos. ⌥⌘B puts the side away and brings it back (Ctrl+Alt+B elsewhere), and every
  view is in the palette. Each project remembers which view it showed, how wide the side was and
  whether it was away (#1678).
- **The project-root guards read a git command whose words the shell fills in as unknown.** A
  git subcommand, or one of git's own options, built from a variable, a quoted substitution or a
  function's arguments is refused in the project root unless a branch move or reset is spelled
  among the words after it, which is then judged as written. An unquoted command substitution
  among git's own options is refused: quote it (`git -C "$(…)" …`) and purlis reads it as one
  word. A function's body is read wherever the shell may call it. Spell the command out and purlis reads
  it.
- **An earlier command on the line that may change the repository makes the guards judge what
  follows as unknown.** After it, an alias is not read from the configuration as it stood, a
  `git checkout <word>` is not taken to restore a file, and a `git reset` or `git update-ref` is
  not measured against the commits the branch held before the line ran. Run the command on its
  own and purlis reads and measures it as before.
- **Every `git reset` mode, and `git update-ref` of the root's branch, is measured for unpushed
  commits.** `--soft` and `--mixed` keep the files but take the commits off the branch, so a reset
  in any mode, or a ref update of `HEAD` or the branch the project root is on, that would leave
  commits no upstream has with only the reflog is refused until `purlis save` pushes them. A
  commit only the shell can name is measured as the furthest back, and `git update-ref --stdin`
  in the root is refused.
- **`git symbolic-ref HEAD <ref>` in the project root is refused as a branch move.** It points
  the root at another branch without touching a file. Reading a symbolic ref stays allowed.
- **Rows on the right are one line.** Todos, Memory and Sessions show each row's title, with its
  date on hover, under Today, Yesterday and Earlier. A persona's row is its badge and its name:
  how much it remembers and its Statistics are on the persona's tab (#1674).
- **A chat on a pool's runner starts a chat here only with your Approve.** A handoff or a task
  that a runner chat asks this machine for now waits in the Inbox and on the chat's tab, saying
  the pool, the persona and the brief, whatever persona it names and whatever kind of pool it
  runs on. Approve decides it as a dispatch of a chat here is decided, so one to another persona
  still needs its grant; Refuse starts nothing, and the chat is told in words on its next turn.
  Your own chats' dispatches are unchanged.
- **A runner gives a chat back a port only while its own policy still gives it.** After a
  re-link, each port a runner withdrew for want of a window is checked against the runner's
  sandbox for the project as it is then. Forgetting a project also removes the name its window
  link kept, so the project opened again takes back none of the old runner chats (#2738).
- **A chat's start on a runner clears what its harness would load that your desktop never sent.**
  Claude Code's `rules`; Codex's `AGENTS.override.md`, `hooks.json`, `rules` and `skills`;
  opencode's `plugin`, `tool` and `skill` folders. On a runner, each new chat starts from your
  profile's own settings, so an "always allow" Codex saved on a runner lasts until the next start.
- **What a pool's runner carries to its next runner waits where a chat cannot reach it, and a
  runner a chat ran on without the sandbox carries nothing.** Its profiles are signed in again on
  the new runner in that case, and after an update for sign-ins an earlier version had carried but
  the runner had not yet taken in.
- **A built-in default profile signs in again after its pool's runner is replaced.** Profiles
  purlis made for the pool stay signed in.
- **The Rust toolchain is pinned.** `rust-toolchain.toml` names Rust 1.99.0 instead of `stable`,
  so a new Rust release no longer changes a local build or CI on the day it ships. CI installs
  exactly that version, and Dependabot proposes each bump (#888).
- **Removal, grant, settings and credential commands are pressed in purlis's own window.**
  A page shown anywhere else lists what there is and says where the press is made (#1927).
- **What you allowed before a policy fixed the scopes no longer reaches a chat at a scope it
  leaves out.** A folder, a local socket, a system service or a host an Allow kept at such a
  scope, and anything one chat holds at one, is judged against the policy at every start and contributes
  nothing while it stands. It stays on this machine, listed in Settings › Sandbox › Allowed as
  not in force, held by policy, with Remove; `purlis doctor` counts it (#1927).
- **A sandboxed chat can write a `purlis.toml` where it can't change a sandbox.** Before,
  `purlis.toml`, `charter.toml` and their `.local.toml` forms couldn't be written anywhere,
  so a chat couldn't check out a repo that carries one, write a test fixture or a scratch
  project, or run purlis's own test suite. Now they are denied only at the project root and in
  each folder from the chat's folder up to the root, the files purlis reads when it starts a
  chat there. Below the chat's folder and in temp folders they are ordinary files. A manifest
  purlis can't read still starts no chat (#1336).
- **Settings › Sandbox says when the project's manifest is gone.** A project whose manifest is
  missing or cannot be read refuses every chat, and the page now says so in place of "Off in this
  project", with no Turn the sandbox on, which would write a new manifest in its place (#1411).
- **A vault tab put back at launch asks the core whether opening it reads a secret.** The vault
  list says so for each vault, so a provider the window does not know waits for a press instead of
  being read (#1660).
- **A refused write that a purlis command does for a chat names that command.** A commit in a
