  branch folder points to `purlis worktree commit`, and a direct write of a session record, a
  memory, a todo or `workspace.md` points to the command that writes it. These Notices offer no
  grant (#1476, #1408).
- **The sandbox's refusals say "project".** The rest of the sentences that say why a chat did
  not start sandboxed, and the warning about a `[sandbox].mode` that is not `"on"`, now say
  "project" where they said "plane", as their opening already did (#1180).
- **Settings › Project › Sandbox says what a chat here can do.** The page opens on one sentence
  that follows the settings as you change them: what a chat can write, the folders you allowed
  every chat on this machine included, and which hosts it can reach, counting only the hosts
  purlis actually grants. It also says plainly that a chat can read any file you can, except
  vaults and what purlis keeps for itself. Internet access is now a box per preset, *AI
  providers*, *Code hosting* and *Package registries*, and each opens to the hosts it covers,
  your project's forges included. The mode is a status line ("On for everyone in this project.
  To run one chat without it, use that chat's tab"), with **Turn the sandbox on** where it is
  off. *Certificate checks* can be set here, each persona's own hosts are named, and two lists
  say what chats can change and what is always protected, each with why. Settings names the
  project's files as the project names them, `purlis.toml` or `charter.toml`, in every Project
  group and in the refusals it shows for them (#1340).
- **A sandboxed Claude Code chat takes its settings from purlis and from you, not from files
  in the project.** At each start of a sandboxed Claude Code chat, full sandbox or floor, purlis
  reads the project's `.claude/settings.json` and `.claude/settings.local.json`. They are loaded
  as they are while they hold only deny and ask rules, plugins, model, output style, theme,
  and the entries purlis's own `init` writes.
  If they hold anything else, or cannot be read, the chat starts on your own Claude Code
  settings and purlis's. The project's deny and ask rules still apply. The chat's tab names
  the keys that were not applied, and says that the project's CLAUDE.md, rules, skills, agents
  and commands are not loaded in that chat either. A chat with no sandbox is unchanged.
  Commands and the Edit tool in a sandboxed chat do not write your own Claude Code settings
  files, at the floor or with the sandbox fully on.
- **A project cloned before purlis had its own sign-in says to save it once from the window.**
  On a machine without `gh` or `glab`, its automatic save no longer fails with a bare sign-in
  error: it commits locally, and the Saving view names the project's remote with *Save once from
  here*, which confirms that remote. From then on automatic saves push with your purlis sign-in
  (#1848).
- **The Saving tab and a memory's editor look like Settings.** Their fields are drawn as Settings
  draws a setting, with the line on what a field does under it rather than inside it. A project
  with no saving mode yet answers _How should this project be saved?_ by picking one of three
  choices and confirming it with _Use this_; nothing is written until then (DS-3b, #1174).
- **Saving's on/off rows no longer flash as selects.** While purlis reads what a project's
  saving has in force, an on/off key the file does not set says "Reading…" in its place, and a
  key the file sets is its switch at once. Neither turns from a select into a switch on load
  (#1875).
- **Search and Changes are views on the left, and the bottom panel is gone.** ⌘⇧F (Ctrl+Shift+F
  elsewhere) shows the Search view on the left side instead of opening a Search tab, searching
  the branch, workspace or project you are on and keeping what you typed. ⌃⇧G shows the Changes
  view: each repo's branch, uncommitted files, branches and pipeline, which the bottom panel
  showed. Its icon counts the uncommitted files, also while the side is put away. The terminals
  now have the window's whole height, and the status line has two toggles, Navigation and
  Attention. A layout file that still places the bottom panel is read without it (#1676).
- **A chat refused macOS's per-user temporary folder is told where to write instead.** No Allow
  is ever offered for those folders, so the chat is no longer told to wait for one: it is told,
  in fixed words, to write under its own `$TMPDIR` (`mktemp -p "$TMPDIR"`). Any other block in
  the same turn is still waited on (#1416).
- **⌘⇧F reads a branch's files on several threads.** A search for something rare reads every
  file of the branch, and one thread left the disk mostly idle. Results still arrive in the same
  order, page after page, and Stop and the page's time limit work as before. Searching a
  100,000-file repo for a word it does not hold took 28–30 s and now takes 7–13 s (#1153).
- **Secret shapes recognise more token formats.** The documented GitHub, GitLab and Slack token
  prefixes are recognised by every check that looks for a credential, including saving settings,
  a written memory, a session record and a handoff brief.
- **Settings at a workspace's level is titled "Settings · <workspace>".** It was "Workspace
  settings · <workspace>", while the You and Project levels were titled "Settings". A tab left
  open from an earlier version comes back under the new title, and still follows a rename of
  its workspace (#1192).
- **Settings edits a whole file in a real editor.** Edit as TOML and Edit as JSON now show the
  file in the same editor as the file viewer, with line numbers, colours and find (⌘F or
  Ctrl+F). If the file changes on disk while you edit it, the file as it is now opens beside
  your edit. Take what you want from it, then keep your edit or discard it. Neither is lost
  until you choose (#1842).
- **List fields are the row's width and grow with what you type.** A list such as the
  environment passed to chats, or a forge's repos never listed, sits under its name and shows
  every line (#1842).
- **Dispatch says once where its limits are kept**, in the group's header, not under each
  table.
- **⌘, opens Settings where you are.** `⌘,` (`Ctrl+,` off a Mac), the app menu's Settings… and
  the palette's Settings… open Settings at the focused workspace's level, else at the project's,
  else at You when no project is open (SE-23, #1173).
- **An arrow key in Settings' level switcher goes to the next level.** You, Project and
  Workspace now follow the arrow keys as every other radio group in the window does, and the
  keyboard stays on the switcher. Before, an arrow only moved the focus and Space picked (#626).
- **Add an override's picker is the settings set's own select.** On Settings › Project ›
  Dispatch it now looks and behaves like every other select in Settings (#626).
- **Sandbox blocks are kept in a network record on this machine, for 30 days.** Each block,
  Allow and removal is written to `<data>/network/<project key>.jsonl` in purlis's data home,
  with the chat, its persona, the host and port of a refused connection, the scope and who
  decided. It is never in the project, never committed and never sent. It replaces the project's
  `.purlis/app/sandbox-blocks.json`, which is no longer written and can be deleted. `purlis
  doctor`'s `sandbox blocks` row reads it and now also names the hosts refused most (#1662).
- **A workspace's settings are in the Settings tab.** Its level switcher now offers Workspace
  beside You and Project, with the workspace's settings in five groups: Live, Repos,
  Extensions, Appearance and Plugins; a group with nothing to set is left out. As at the
  Project level, each change is written to `workspace.json` as you make it, the last change has
  an Undo, and a value purlis refuses is said beside its setting. The workspace's icon theme
  has a control here for the first time. Workspace settings… on a workspace's menu and in the
  palette opens Settings at that workspace's level, and the separate Workspace settings page is
  gone (SE-20, #1170).
- **Preferences is now Settings.** The app menu's Settings… (`⌘,`, or `Ctrl+,`) and the
  palette's Settings… open a Settings tab in two columns: the level at the top, which is You
  for now, the groups on the left, and the chosen group on the right. Text holds the window's
  and the terminal's text size, and Editor holds your editor. Each applies as you change it, as
  before. A Preferences tab left open by an older version comes back as Settings (SE-16, #1166).
- **Settings' tables share one look.** The Dispatch limits and the dispatch grants tables keep
  each heading on one line. A long heading shows a word or two; hover or focus it to read the
  whole name and what the column holds. Their boxes and buttons are the same height as every
  other control (#1841).
- **Settings says when a reset widens Internet access.** In Settings › Project › Sandbox, the
  Internet access row's reset reads "Reset: reach every preset", and the line under the row says
  that a reset, or an Undo that takes the setting out of the file, turns every preset on (#1197).
- A tabbed chat's own question now counts the questions waiting behind it, and the line that
  offers where you answer shows in one pane only (#4566).
- The cluster operator's policy on upstream claims now holds every write it makes to what upstream writes on a claim of a purlis pool, and no upstream claim on a purlis pool's warm pool may carry a `created-by` label. A claim that already holds something else is refused the next time it is written.
- **A shell follows a chat's rules.** New shell takes the focused pane, and what that pane showed
  keeps running in the sidebar. Closing or replacing a shell's pane leaves it running, so a dev
  server survives. End… on a shell asks only Cancel or End. When a shell's program exits, its row
  goes and its pane is left empty (#4761).
- **A terminal editor opened from a file, and a forge login, open beside what you were reading.**
  Each opens as a split beside the focused pane, with the keyboard, and goes when its program
  exits, the keyboard back where it was. Its pane cannot be dragged, closed or swapped, has no
  sidebar row, and is never kept for the next launch (#4761).
- **Show what changed reads its branch in one bounded read.** Finding the branch's folder no
  longer runs git in the app itself: the reader that already compares the file finds the folder,
  checks the path inside it and reads the comparison, in one child that a deadline and a memory
  cap bound. A refusal reads as it did (#1189).
- **Switching between open chats no longer reads the sidebar again.** The window reads it when a
  chat is opened or closed, or when the project changes on disk, and an answer that found nothing
  new draws nothing again (#4729).
- **Personas, Vaults and extension panels scroll as one piece** (#3341). Like Memory, Todos and
  Sessions, each is one scroll with its heading, its actions and its filter held at the top.
- **Memory, Todos and Sessions scroll as one piece** (#3340). Each view is one scroll: its
  heading, its actions and its search or add box stay at the top while the rows move under
  them, each day's name stays under them while its rows are in sight, and the rows are 30px.
  The list no longer scrolls in a short box of its own inside the view.
- **A device code on a pool's runner runs in the sign-in strip.** Where this Mac's port for the
  browser's answer is taken, Use a device code runs the harness's device flow in the strip's own
  terminal, with no project open and no shell tab (#4106).
- **A move that waits on an opencode profile asks which plan.** Its notice offers Sign in to
  ChatGPT and Sign in to GitHub Copilot, as the pool's line does, and each signs in in the strip
  under it (#4181).
- **`purlis profile sign-in <profile> --pool <pool>` puts the profile on the runner first.** While the
  purlis window is running, a profile the runner does not keep yet goes there as Sign in on its line in
  Settings › Pools does, and the pool names it from then on. With no window running, the command says so
  and starts nothing (#4112).
- **Signing a profile out of a pool reaches its draining runners too.** Sign out in Settings › Pools
  now also runs on any runner of the pool still finishing its chats after an update, says which
  it reached, and nothing carries that sign-in across when the runner finishes.
- **A drained runner's sign-ins are carried once.** It is unpaired first, and a removal that failed
  only tries the removal again.
- **opencode signs out on a pool's runner from its line.** Sign out in a terminal opens a shell tab
  where opencode asks which sign-in goes.
- **Claude Code chats list 60 skills and 15,000 characters** where they listed 30 and 6,000, counting names and whole lines as Claude Code does. Codex and opencode stay at 30 and 6,000 (#4610).
- **A save names the skills it changed** (Skill studio preview, #2876). A save's message counts a
  skill's files under the skill's name, `skill deploy 2`, `ops skill review 1`, where before they
  were counted as the project's, a workspace's or a persona's files. The window tells its readers
  a skill changed as its own kind of change, so the Skills view and a persona's page read again
  for it, and a workspace's todos and memory do not.
- **A skill is edited in place on its page** (Skill studio preview, #3683). Edit turns the
  skill's Text tab into the editor, checked as you type ("It is a whole skill.", or what is worth
  knowing), with Save and Discard; Stop editing turns it back. While there is something to save,
  the page's header says "Unsaved changes", and what you typed stays when the studio's tab goes
  behind another. Save says "Saved. Chats started from now get this version." Leaving with
  unsaved changes (another skill, another page, back, Stop editing, or closing the studio's tab)
  asks Keep editing, Discard and leave, or Save and leave.
- **`purlis skill list --json` and `show --json` say which repo copy won** (Skill studio preview,
  #3461). A project skill a repo's own copy replaces on Codex and opencode now carries its
  `clashes` too, naming the repo, as the copy purlis hands does.
- **The Skill studio's Library no longer has its own Ask a chat to draft a skill** (Skill studio
  preview, #4041). New skill… is the one way to start a skill there, its Ask a chat to draft it
  included, which asks what the skill should do first. The Drafts page keeps its ask.
- **A skill opens as a page inside the Skill studio** (Skill studio preview, #3682). Choosing a
  skill in the Library opens its page beside the list, or alone with a way back on a narrow tab:
  its name, skill level and state, with Use in this chat, Edit, Grade and a "…" menu (Rename,
  Move to another level, Deprecate, Archive, Open the file, Delete). A banner says why a skill
  isn't plainly on (off, left out, a change to review, an update waiting, hidden by the router)
  and offers the one fix. Its tabs are Overview, Text, History, Grades and Runs, with their
  counts. A built-in skill's page says it can't be edited, moved or turned off. The skill's own
  tab is gone: a run's chip and the Skills view open the skill's page, and a skill tab kept from
  an earlier launch comes back as it.
- **Rename, Move and Delete a skill in dialogs that say what changes** (Skill studio preview,
  #3685). Rename checks the new name as you type, and lists the personas, skills and pins that
  name the skill and change with it. Move lists each skill level with who gets the skill there,
  and says which chats stop or start getting it for the level you pick. Delete says who uses the
  skill now and that it stays in Deleted for 30 days. Each ends in the result notice with Undo,
  or Bring it back after a delete. A rename now also renames the skill in every workspace's and
  persona's pins. Two labels that meant two things are split: a persona's Remove is now Take
  out of this persona, and a source's Remove is now Remove source.
- **A Skill studio chat refused for an unapproved profile offers Approve and start in place** (Skill studio preview, #3942). Try it, Ask a chat to draft a skill and a draft's redo start their chats without the new-chat picker, and purlis refuses a profile nobody has approved on this machine. That refusal now has an Approve and start… button. It asks the picker's own question, showing the command the profile would run, and once you approve it starts the same chat with its request typed and not sent. Before, you had to leave the studio and approve the profile from a new tab.
- **Drafts and Deleted in the Skill studio are pages of their own** (Skill studio preview,
  #3690, #3691). Drafts lists each skill a chat drafted. Pick one to see what it writes, file by
  file, then Try it on a program, Accept it or Discard it. A draft whose project copy changed
  since says so and offers to ask the chat to redo it, in place of Accept. Deleted lists the
  skills deleted in the last 30 days with the days left to bring each back. Pick one to Bring it
  back, with its history and grades, or to read its last text.
- **The Skill studio is one tab per project, laid out as pages** (Skill studio preview, #3681). A scope picker says
  whose chats it covers; Library, Sources, Deleted, Harness skills and Routing sit in a left
  navigation, with Needs you and Drafts there while they hold something; ⌘[ and ⌘] and the
  mouse's own buttons go back and forward inside the tab, and a path says where you are. The
  Library lists every skill as a row with its skill level, one mark and one line of what it
  does, with a search box and filter chips, and the skill chosen opens beside it. Every way in
  says "Open Skill studio" and lands on its page and scope; ⌘-click opens a second studio tab.
- **A LIVE workspace's `skills/` is committed with it**, as its memory and todos are. `purlis init`, `purlis reinit` and every save keep each level's `skills.local/` out of git (#2767, #2874).
- **The Skill studio's Harness skills and Routing pages** (Skill studio preview, #3692). Harness
  skills lists each program's own skills under its name, each with whose it is (you, a repo, a
  plugin) and one mark; the skill chosen opens beside the list with its facts and an on/off
  switch for these chats, or says why a plugin's is read-only. A program with none says so.
  Routing says the router these chats are routed by, with Change… to pick the built-in router or
  an installed router extension for a workspace or a persona, the budget, and how the router did
  at each chat's start: its timing, or that it fell back, and what it hid.
- `purlis skill grant` and Share now commit their change right away, as one commit, instead of leaving it for the next save.
- A chat can't run `purlis skill` to change a skill. Changes made from a chat are coming as drafts you accept in the studio.
- **The Skill studio's Needs you lists what needs a decision** (Skill studio preview, #3689).
  Changes to review, clashes, problems in a skill, pins no chat reads and tidy-ups are grouped
  by kind, each with why in a sentence and one fix, and the item chosen opens beside the list in
  the attention tone. The skills-to-move notice, the pins-refused line and the old plugin keys'
  Ask move there: while the studio is on, the old keys are asked about in Needs you and not in
  the Inbox. A repo skill with a built-in skill's name is one of its clashes, fixed by switching
  the repo's copy off.
- **The Skills view keeps the last chat's skills while the Skill studio or another tab that is
  not a chat is in front.** It used to switch to what a new chat would get and read it again. It
  now goes on naming the chat you came from until that chat's tab closes, and follows a chat as
  soon as one is in front again (#4351).
- **The Skill studio's records are held as integrity paths.** The records that say which
  workspace and persona folders a running chat could have made, the folders waiting for your
  Accept, the drafts, the tries and grades' arms, the grades of local copies, the grades under
  way, the grades' chats and the opt-in to grade after each edit are kept in the project's state
  folder. They are now held as purlis's own, like its other records there, so no sandboxed chat
  writes them, under either spelling of the state folder or where `$PURLIS_HOME` puts it.
- **Skill sources have pages of their own in the Skill studio** (behind the Skill studio
  preview). Sources leads with the updates waiting and the sources not yet confirmed on this
  machine, then your sources and the ones to start from. Each source opens on a page that marks
  its skills Installed, Update available, or with what their files do ("runs a script", "reaches
  1 host"), with Check for updates and Remove source…, which keeps the skills installed from it.
  Installing and updating are review pages with the pinned commit, every file readable under its
  own mark, and Install or Accept update fixed at the bottom. Add source… is a short dialog,
  with the branch, the folder and the sign-in under More (#3687).
- **A persona's page and Settings › Workspace › Skills say what needs you** (Skill studio
  preview, #3695). Their one line of counts adds "K need you" while something does, which opens
  the studio's Needs you on that persona or workspace; Open Skill studio lands on its Library.
- **An update of a project skill reaches where the skill does** (Skill studio preview, #4186). A
  skill the update brings along lands with the updated skill's grant, instead of at the root
  alone. A project skill its newer commit refers to is granted to those workspaces too, in the
  same commit, as an install with that grant does. The update review says both before you accept
  it, and an update whose skill was regranted since its review changes nothing.
- **The Skills view's levels fold** (Skill studio preview, #3281). Each level (Needs you, Built-in, Workspace, a program's own) is now a branch of a tree, with how many skills it holds: ← and → fold and open it, as Enter or a click on it does, and the window keeps which are folded across a restart. While a filter is typed every level is open, so a match is never folded away.
- **Only this chat's follows the chat's persona and repo** (Skill studio preview, #3462). With
  the Skills view narrowed to the chat in front, each program's own skills and each repo's carry
  the marks the studio gives that chat's persona, and only the repo skills of the clone the chat
  works in are listed. A chat in no clone lists none.
- **The Skills view's tidy-ups** (Skill studio preview, #3308). Show in Explorer on a repo skill now opens its folder in the workspace's clone. Only this chat's is kept in the layout file, so it is still on after a restart. A side left on Skills no longer shows Chats for a moment at start. New skill…'s menu opens inside the view, and a program's group is headed like the others.
- **Smart close is written one way, and a failed update says what to press.** The needs-you
  list says *Smart close stopped — …* and *Smart close did not start*, as the button reads. The
  status line's *update failed* now says *press to see why*, and its dialog says *Check now
  tries again* (#1156).
- **Smart close saves its record from a sandboxed Claude Code chat, one in a clone included.** In
  a chat purlis started, the session record is now written by purlis itself: the smart-close
  skill calls purlis's new `session_record` tool, and `purlis session record` hands the record to
  purlis over the chat's own connection instead of writing it. The chat's sandbox no longer has
  to reach the project's files. Codex and opencode sandboxes are not covered yet (#1332).
- **Typing `/smart-close` in a terminal chat closes the tab too.** A smart close you type into a
  waiting terminal chat now counts as yours, like the tab's **Smart close**: the record is written
  with no prompt and the tab closes when that turn ends. A chat that starts a smart close on its
  own still writes its record, and its tab stays open for you to close (#1332).
- **A Smart close you reached without a pass is never silent.** If a chat runs Smart close without
  a typed `/smart-close` behind it and writes no session record within five minutes, the window
  now says so, as it does for a Smart close you start from the tab (#1361).
- **A workspace's stale repos and its layout behind hang from its chip** (#3650). A repo left off
  its default branch ("Switch to main") or on a moved remote ("Use the new address"), and a
  workspace behind the current layout ("Update workspace layout"), each show as a ▲ warning on
  that workspace's chip in the title bar, with the same buttons as in the Notices centre. They
  are still listed there. Dismissing a stale repo in either place dismisses it in both, until
  the finding changes. A layout behind has no Dismiss in either place: it goes once it is
  updated.
- **Start a chat ends in its form's row.** Start (or Approve and start) stands first and Cancel
  after it, as in every other dialog that makes something. Cancel still has the keyboard when
  the dialog opens (#1719).
- **Start a chat has two panes.** The persona list, with a filter once it is long, sits beside
  the persona picked, the harness cards, the name and the footer box. The dialog keeps one
  height and place whatever the list holds, each pane scrolls on its own, and Start is always
  in view. ⏎ in the filter or on a persona starts the chat (#2918).
- **Dialogs are 600 or 800 px wide**, up from 560 and 780 (#2918).
- **Every dialog sits at a fixed top, 6% down the window and never closer than 24px, and keeps
  24px clear of the bottom.** In a short window the dialog grows shorter, so its answers stay in
  the window, Start chat's included (#3389, #3510).
- **A report is no longer a needs-you item.** A report from a chat another chat started goes to
  the chat that asked, which reads it on its next turn. It raises no item for you while that
  chat is open, on either chat. A report whose asking chat has closed has nowhere to go, and
  that is an item, on the chat that wrote it, whether the asking chat closed before the report
  was sent or before it was read (#1448).
- **A chat the Skill studio starts for a skill starts where the skill lives, and its button says
  where.** A workspace's skill gets a chat in that workspace, a project's skill one at the
  project's root, and a persona's skill a chat as that persona, the only chats its skills reach:
  "Ask a chat at purlis-demo to write these", "Ask a chat as steward to write checks". New skill…
  names the place it opens the chat at too (#5184).
- **A workspace's tab says less, in less room.** Its open chats and the ones that need you are
  one pill, the second in the needs-you colour, read as "3 chats, 1 needs you". A live workspace
  is a small dot after its name, and a pin is a small grey mark in the tab's top corner, on
  every strip. The project root's tab is a house with a tab's own padding. Every tab's title is
  one step smaller.
- **A line under the workspaces' row and between the Panel's halves.** The row of workspace
  tabs is parted from what is under it by one hairline, and the tab you are on still joins its
  content. The bottom Panel's left and right halves have the same line between them, which is
  the handle that resizes them; it was there to drag and drawn no pixels wide.
- On Claude Code, a dispatched task's question prompt and a plain `ask_operator` now go to the chat that dispatched it, and the task is told who answered. Handoffs, tasks you started from a tab, your own chats and browser takeovers still ask you directly. If a redirect fails, the question stays in the task's pane and the Inbox.
- A task's open question now survives a restart of the app: it stays with whoever was asked, and the answer reaches the task, so the task isn't told to ask again.
- **A task's row says who its question waits on, and since when.** `asking steward 2 · 1m`
  while the chat that dispatched it has the question, `needs you · 3m` once it has reached you,
  timed from when it reached you. Only a question that has reached you raises the ✋, the hand
  on its tab and the rows above, and a folded row says `1 asking` for one its asking chat still
  has, with no red (#4564).
- **A chat's row says its state in a word beside a mark, and each state has its own shape.**
  The Chats list and the explorer show the same word for the same chat: working, needs you,
  `asking <chat>`, done, failed, cancelled, or ended without a report. A task that has
  reported no longer looks like a chat waiting on you. A chat at rest that is not asking for
  you reads idle, and one whose harness has sent nothing reads
  `running (no detail from <harness>)`. A task you stopped reads cancelled, and a row says
  needs you whenever the title bar's list does (#1484).
- **The app says "task" and "helper".** A chat a dispatch started is a task, and a harness's
  own sub-agent under a chat is a helper, in the explorer, the close dialog, the dispatch
  question and the dispatch settings (#1484).
- **purlis's refusals say "task" and "helper".** A dispatch past a limit says how many tasks are
  running, and a dispatch or handoff from inside a harness's own helper is refused in those words
  (#1525).
- **Tasks keep their place across a restart.** A task still at work when you quit or update
  purlis comes back under the chat that asked, on its conversation, and is told to carry on;
  its report still reaches that chat. A task that cannot be brought back on its conversation
  has ended by itself: the chat that asked is told, once, and it is a failed row you can
  Reopen. One whose start was refused (after Stop every agent, say) waits under the chat that
  asked: Try to start again brings it back told to carry on, and End task ends it. Nothing is
  dispatched twice: a task is never sent its brief again, and a chat that asks for the same task again
  after it was started again, while the first is still working, is told it is running (#1513).
- **A task whose asking chat has closed keeps its report.** Its row reads "asked by <chat>
  (closed)". Its report is kept on its dispatch record and for the workspace, and when you
  bring the chat that asked back (Resume from any of its session records, Retry now, or the
  next launch) that chat is handed the report once, also when the report lands after you
  resumed it. So is a report it never read before it closed. A report a task sends after a
  restart names the session record it wrote last (#1513).
- **A chat's output reaches its pane as the bytes the program wrote.** It used to be turned into
  text, escaped into JSON and read back on the way to the window; now the terminal decodes it
  itself, so output heavy with colours and cursor moves costs the window less to take in, and a
  character split between two pieces of output is put together by the terminal. A
  byte that is no character at all is now left out, where it used to show as `�` (#4745).
- **opencode's Sign out in a terminal says what it reaches.** Its line in Settings › Pools says a
  draining runner keeps its sign-in until it is removed, and is asked again when the terminal's
  tab closes, so it stops saying signed in once you have signed out.
- **Test fixtures are tracked under neutral names.** A fixture whose name a sandboxed chat may
  not write (`.claude/settings.json`, `opencode.json`) is tracked as `<name>.fixture` and copied
  to its real name at test time, and the editor recommendation `app/.vscode/extensions.json` is
  no longer tracked, so a sandboxed chat can bring a clone of purlis up to date across any change
  to them. A test fails on a tracked path a sandboxed chat may not write (#2089).
- **The window's words have roles.** Seven text roles (title, heading, body, secondary, meta,
  label, code) each fix a size, a weight and a colour, with new core tokens for the two weights,
  the two line heights and the one monospace family. Nothing looks different yet: the Inbox's
  rows wear the roles with the sizes and colours they had, and the other surfaces follow one at
  a time. A check now refuses a new font size, weight or text colour written outside them
  (#1920).
- **The app is purlis now: `purlis.app`, bundle identifier `dev.purlis.app`.** At its first launch
  the app moves its log folder from `dev.charter.app` to `dev.purlis.app` before it writes a log
  there, and holds its keychain items again under the new identity without asking: a vault whose
  items macOS would ask about keeps working and waits for **Finish moving**, which asks once per
  secret. Nothing moves while another charter is running, and purlis does not start while the
  old app still runs. macOS treats the renamed app as a new one, so it asks again for permission
  to show notifications. An install that updated itself keeps the folder name `charter.app`; a
  fresh `purlis.app` replaces it, and the old `charter.app` can be deleted. On Linux the
  one-per-user lock and the D-Bus name follow the new identifier, and the `.deb` is the `purlis`
  package, which replaces the `charter` package. Updates, the release assets
  (`purlis-macos-arm64.dmg`, `purlis-linux-x86_64.deb`, …), About's links and `charter report`
  use `purlis/purlis`; installed builds still find new releases through GitHub's redirect from the
  old address (RN-9, #1267).
- **The Changes view reads like an editor's source-control view.** Each repo is a heading with
  the branch it is on, and under it are rows for its changes, its branches (each branch one row
  further in), its pipeline and any column an extension adds. It used to be a wide table that
  scrolled sideways in the side. The branches are drawn with the same tree guides as the
  explorer. The view is now one Tab stop that takes the arrow keys, so ⌃⇧G (Ctrl+Shift+G) puts
  the keyboard in it, and Shift+F10 on a repo's row opens that repo's menu (#1701, #1682).
- **An empty Changes or Search view says what goes there.** With no workspace focused, with no
  repos in the workspace, or with a search that matched nothing, the view says what it would
  list and what to try (#614).
- **The Chats view lists this tab's chats, the workspace's, or all of them.** A switch beside
  its title picks This tab, Workspace or All, in place of the *all workspaces* chip. Workspace
  is where it starts, and each project keeps the one you picked. Whichever it is, a chat it
  leaves out that needs you is named at the top, with Go, and so is one the filter hides (#1679).
- **The workspace you are in stands out in the title bar.** Its chip is drawn on the accent's
  wash, where before it looked exactly like a chip under the pointer; under the pointer it takes
  a stronger wash. Themes gain the token `accent.wash-hover` for it, which a theme that leaves it
  out follows from its `tab.active` (#3345).
- **The commitment point waits for an ask.** purlis's prompt hook reads the first prompt of a
  harness session for a fork as before, and after that only a prompt that opens by asking for a
  code change ("refactor the importer…", "please add…", "ok, now fix…"). A short reply, the
  answer to a question and a design answer such as "agree at all, but …" no longer get its
  advice, so a design grill is not told to reproduce a failing test on every turn. It is the
  same under every harness that runs the hook (#1988).
- **The consent floors hold exactly under every workspace tint** (#2526). A tinted shade keeps
  the contrast it had untinted at every hue, custom colours included: each channel is rounded on
  the side of the shade's own luminance. The focus ring, the selected row's edge, the accent's
  surface and the active tab stay apart from the danger colour as the accent does, and a grey
  accent keeps as much of its tint as holds it apart. In Purlis Classic most tinted colours move
  by one step of a channel or two, too little to see.
- **The asks, the danger colours and the state marks stay readable in any theme.** When a theme
  breaks a consent floor, purlis draws its own colours for those tokens and the rest of the theme
  as written, and a Notice names the theme and the floor (#2451).
- **The consent floors hold in every combination of a theme's appearances and option values.**
  An option value that breaks a floor is drawn with purlis's own values for those tokens, with
  the Notice that names it, and the theme specimen a chat asks for is drawn with the floors held
  as the window draws it. `purlis theme check` says how many combinations it checked against the
  consent floors and in which of them the window holds one (`consent floors: held in 1 of 4
  combinations:`) (#2528).
- **A dev channel build takes about half the time.** It is compiled with a lighter profile,
  `dev-release` (thin LTO), and makes no `.dmg`; a first install of a dev build on macOS uses the
  `.app.zip`. A stable build is unchanged. `purlis --version` and About purlis now name the
  profile a build was made with, for example `purlis 0.4.2 (dev-release profile)`. A nightly
  profile guard builds `main` with the stable profile and opens an issue if it fails (ADR 0092,
  #1429).
- **The session host keeps the event log and each chat's end.** With chats in the session host
  (the default, #2004), it is the event log's one writer, and a chat that ends while the window
  is gone still has its end recorded. If that chat was a task, its dispatch
  is settled as one that went without its report, and the chat that asked is handed that when the
  window is back (#2003).
- **The event log keeps what a store written from it has not taken yet.** A sealed segment of
  the event log older than 30 days is now deleted only once every consumer the host opened the
  log with has taken its last event, so an audit writer or a telemetry store that was down for
  longer than that finds everything it had not taken. There is a hard limit: a segment older
  than 90 days is deleted whoever has not taken it, the app's log says which consumer lost
  which events, and that consumer is told what it missed when it reads on. Nothing is a
  consumer yet, so today's log is kept exactly as before (#940).
- **The explorer lists a workspace's own chats, and one line for a session's tasks.** Under a
  workspace it lists the chats that have a tab of their own: sessions, handoffs, shells, and a
  task you gave a tab. Tasks are not listed there any more. Under a session that has tasks,
  one line says how many and how they stand, `5 tasks · 3 working · 1 waiting · 1 done`, in
  the same count and words as the session's row in the Chats list. Pressing it puts the
  keyboard on that session's row in the Chats list, opened and marked for a moment, which is
  where its tasks are listed; a filter in the way is taken off, and the list says so (#1490).
- **A branch still says a task is working in it.** Under a branch's row, and in the branch's
  own view, one line: `1 task in this branch · 1 working`. Tasks working in a workspace that a
  chat elsewhere asked for are one line under the workspace, `2 tasks from other places`.
  Pressing either shows those tasks in the Chats list (#1490).
- **A chat's helpers are a count on its row.** `3 helpers · 1 working`, with `1 failed` when
  one did, in place of a row of ids each. Pressing it, or Right on it, unfolds a row per
  helper, `helper a3882da5` with its state in the words every row uses; the whole id is the
  id's tooltip. It stays as you left it for each chat while the window is open. A task shown
  inside its session's tab says the same count on its row in the Chats list (#1490).
- **A task that needs you puts the hand on its session's row in the explorer**, as it does in
  the Chats list. Pressing the hand goes to the task (#1490).
- **The explorer lists the paths a branch changed that purlis will not read.** Under a
  branch's files, and under *Changed only*, each such path is drawn as text with its mark and
  the reason, past fifty counted. Nothing opens, drags or picks it, and a branch whose only
  changes are such paths no longer says it changed nothing (#704).
- **The file preview plays animated images, and draws an SVG as a picture where it can.** An
  animated GIF, APNG or WebP plays on the preview's canvas, decoded frame by frame from its
  bytes, where the window's webview can decode frames (WebView2 can); it has *Pause*, stops while
  its tab is out of sight or the window is hidden, and shows one frame and *Play* under reduced
  motion. Where the webview cannot, the preview shows the first frame and says so. An SVG is
  decoded as an image, so it runs no script and loads nothing it names, with its text under
  *Source*; where the webview does not decode SVG that way, the preview shows its text as before.
  Nothing new is loaded from a URL (#1132).
- **A file's comparison reads again when its branch moves.** While the explorer watches the
  branch, the comparison tab compares again by itself, keeping the comparison on screen until the
  new one comes; *Compare again* still asks at any time (#1189).
- **"Choose your editor in Settings first" links to Settings.** In the file tab and a file's
  comparison, the sentence now has a *Choose your editor* link that opens Settings at the Editor
  group with its setting focused (#1201).
- **A sandboxed chat at the floor is held from more of what purlis itself runs.** A chat is not
  started where purlis's own files lie in a folder it may write; it says so, and to install
  purlis outside the project and outside what a chat may write.
- **Every chat now runs at least at the floor** (#2071). In a project that has not turned the
  sandbox on, a chat reaches every host and writes every folder but what the floor holds, so
  it works much as its harness does unsandboxed. It still cannot read a vault or purlis's own keys, cannot write
  what a later program runs (git hooks and config, `.claude` settings, editor tasks), and
  cannot write a folder on your `PATH` or your harness's own program; a refused install raises
  the usual block Notice. A project with `[sandbox] mode = "on"` keeps the full sandbox. Each
  chat's tab shows its level: full sandbox, floor, or no sandbox.
- **A skill's Grades tab asks one question** (Skill studio preview, #3928). Its grades now say
  whether the skill has trigger tests and which grade of it is running, at its latest step, so the
  tab and a running grade's page no longer read a whole grade plan to learn it, and a skill's page
  no longer builds a Grades panel nothing draws.
- **The title bar's ✋ counts every ask, from every source.** A dispatch waiting for a grant and
  a host a chat's sandbox refused now count beside permission prompts and chats waiting on you,
  each listed with Go to its chat, and a chat at a prompt purlis already holds counts once. A
  dispatch refused while you were away is listed but no longer counted: nothing waits on it.
  Keep blocked on a sandbox block now clears it from the count too (#1690).
- **The harness plugin is `purlis`.** A Claude Code chat the app starts loads it as
  `purlis@inline`; its skills are `purlis:<skill>` and its MCP tools `mcp__purlis__<tool>`.
  Every id it had before (`charter@inline`, `charter-app@inline`, and `charter@charter-app`, the
  copy `charter plugin install` wrote) is turned off in each chat, so an old copy never loads
  beside the new one, and a project file that still names one is told the new id.
  `charter plugin install` now registers `purlis@purlis-app` and writes the opencode guard as
  `purlis.ts`, taking out the install under the old names in the same write. The local migration
  (`purlis migrate`, and the app at its launch) moves an existing install for every harness, and
  `purlis migrate --undo` puts it back under the old ids. A project's own permission rules that
  name `mcp__charter__<tool>` need the `mcp__purlis__<tool>` spelling to keep applying (RN-8,
  #1266).
- **Settings › Sandbox checks a host as you type it.** The host field of the project's hosts
  and of your own says why what is typed is not a host (a URL, a path, a range, a space) while
  you type, in the same words Add uses, instead of only after Add is pressed (#1405).
- **An Inbox row reads in three ranks, and takes less room.** What needs you is the strongest
  line; where it is (project, workspace, persona) is quieter under it; its kind and how long it
  has waited are smallest, trailing. Each kind has a mark beside its words. A long line is cut
  to two with the whole of it in its tooltip, except the words of an ask you can allow from
  there, which are always drawn whole. Go to chat and Ignore sit side by side, and the cards
  are tighter.
- **What waits in other projects is under All projects.** The chats waiting in other windows
  and the lines for the window's other projects were listed in every Inbox; they are now listed
  in the All projects scope, and This project says how many wait there.
- **The last odd buttons and fields match the rest.** The Save, Cancel, Move and Restore
  buttons in the Memory, memory archive and repo instructions views, the explorer's section
  headings, a finished task's "Changed:" link, the title bar's save indicator, and the token
  and colour boxes in a few dialogs now use the shared buttons, rows and fields. A colour the
  picker refuses shows on the field's edge (#1857).
- **The last dialogs nobody had walked follow the same rules as the rest.** New project's
  Advanced form has a Cancel of its own. Renaming and deleting a vault's secret say Renaming…
  and Deleting… while purlis writes. A task's second step reads Keep, then Stop it (or Close it),
  so the way out comes first as in every other question. The sentences in Make live, the doctor,
  a persona's profile, opening a project, a brief and an extension's action say one thing each
  (#1719).
- **The last hand-built form controls are drawn by the settings set.** The Chats list's state
  chips, the choice of where a dispatch's Allow holds, the selects of the dispatch grant table
  and of Add a grant, the dispatch limits' boxes, the box for a folder a block's Allow may name,
  and the host or folder to allow when a sandbox block named none now have the same look,
  labels and keyboard as every other setting. The chips are still one Tab stop with the arrow
  keys between them, and the box for a block that named nothing is a labelled row under its
  Notice, with a line on what an Allow does (#626).
- The Skill studio's Library draws its rows a screen at a time as it opens, so a long list of
  skills no longer holds the window up while it fills (#4351).
- On Linux, purlis's own sandbox wrap starts with an environment purlis builds, and only the
  program it runs is given the chat's variables. This holds for a chat's start and for a
  brokered `secret exec`.
- **Claude Code no longer asks before listing a chat's own tasks.** The `dispatch_list` tool
  runs without the harness's permission prompt, as the same list's command line already did.
  It lists only the tasks that chat dispatched, or that you started from its tab, and a helper
  sub-agent's call of it is still refused (ADR 0064, amended, #1463).
- **The going-LIVE dialog says "project".** Making a workspace live or local, the dialog, the
  live mark's title and the not-saved line now say "project" where they said "plane", as
  Settings does (#1192).
- **A local project in the config home moves to the data home at the next launch.** It moves in
  one rename, with a link left at the old place until its clones' worktrees, the chats it
  reopens and the projects this machine remembers all name the new one, so nothing is lost and
  its approval and pins go with it. A launch that stops halfway is finished by the next one. One
  that something still works in (a terminal, an editor, another purlis) is left where it is: the
  app's log and the project's doctor say so, and the move is made at a launch when nothing works
  in it. A worktree outside the project keeps the link, and the log names the
  `git worktree repair` to run (#1670).
- **A Claude Code conversation from a chat that ran in the old place does not come back by
  Resume.** Claude Code keeps a conversation under the folder its chat ran in, and that folder
  has a new name. The conversation's file is not touched (it stays in `~/.claude/projects/`);
  Resume starts the chat fresh with its session record in its briefing, as for any conversation
  the harness cannot find (#1670).
- **The question for several tasks reads like a chat's own sandbox Notice.** It says when a
  task's command is waiting on your answer, says what your administrator's policy ruled out,
  and offers its scopes in the same order: a host for you on this machine first, then only these
  tasks or everyone in the project under **Other scopes…**; a folder for these tasks first
  (#1709).
- **A database host given alone in `PGHOST` reaches its database through the tunnel.** A
  brokered `purlis secret exec` now reads its port from `PGPORT` (or libpq's 5432) and points both
  at the tunnel, as it does for a connection string (#1708).
- **A certificate checked by name still matches through the tunnel.** For a libpq connection
  string or `postgres://` URL with `sslmode=verify-full` (and `PGSSLMODE=verify-full` beside
  `PGHOST`), purlis keeps the host name and adds the tunnel as `hostaddr`, so the name the
  certificate is checked against is the database's own. Other drivers are pointed as before
  (#1708).
- **A credential file's database value reaches its host through the tunnel.** A brokered
  `purlis secret exec` now points a value a `--file` holds alone, and each value of a
  `--dotenv` file, at the tunnel as it does an `--env` value, in the file itself; every other
  line stays as it was (#1708).
- **More certificates checked by name are handed as they are.** `amqps://` URLs, CockroachDB
  URLs with `sslmode=verify-full`, and `postgresql+asyncpg://` (or another driver that is not
  libpq's) with `verify-full` are handed to the command unchanged with a note, instead of being
  pointed at a tunnel whose address the certificate would not match (#1708).
- **A background command's output read back with another tool is read for a sandbox block.**
  A Claude Code chat that reads a background run's output file with its file tool, or with the
  harness's own tool for background output, now raises the same Notice as reading it with
  `cat` (#1683).
- **The cluster operator's downloadable install names its image by digest.** Each published
  operator image's run artifact holds `install/`: the plain manifests and the Helm chart of the
  same commit, with the image and the chart's default digest already set to it. The kind
  end-to-end tests install exactly that (#2281).
- **The palette opening and closing no longer redraw the project in front.** Running a row from
  the palette, such as Open Skill studio, gets to what it opens sooner (#4351).
- **The command palette no longer makes the window inert while it is open**, as VS Code's does
  not: it still keeps the keyboard, and Esc or a click outside it closes it. Closing it no longer
  restyles the whole window, so a row run from it, such as Open Skill studio, gets to what it
  opens sooner (#4351).
- **A chat's pane has a foot.** A quiet line under the terminal now says the chat's harness ·
  workspace and its `ctx` and `cache`, with `ctx`'s fill a thin bar under its number. They left
  the line above the terminal, which now says which chat this is and what you can do to it, and
  the row of gauge bars is gone. A theme styles the foot as its own part, `pane-foot` (#5202).
- **A pane's head names its chat and holds its one state button.** It shows the chat's name, its
  state, its harness and workspace, and its sandbox, then one button chosen by the chat's state
  (Stop while it works, Answer while a task asks, Cancel smart close while it wraps up, Brief on
  a task), then ⋯, the bell, Split right, Split down and Close. A narrow pane drops the details
  first and keeps the bell, ⋯, Split right and Close. Right-click on the head lists the chat's
  actions, then the pane's. A task's Stop and Close now, and its Move to its own tab and Open
  beside, are in its ⋯ (#4760).
- **A tab's right-click holds only the tab's rows**: Pin, Keep open, Close other tabs and Close.
  Pressing the tab switches to it. New tab and New shell are no longer on a pane's right-click
  (#4760).
- **A chat's row in the Chats list shows its sandbox, and breathes while the chat wraps up**
  (#4760).
- **The last hand-drawn buttons are the window's own, and take no border in Purlis** (#3129).
  On a pane showing a task, Brief and the two ways to end the task (Stop, Close now) are the
  window's small buttons, as tall as the skills and harness beside them, and a way that cannot
  run still takes the keyboard and says why. The mark on a chat's tab that says the project
  changed since it started is a small button with no border, and lists the files that moved in
  its tooltip. A disabled button on the welcome and the guided steps is dimmed once, as every
  other disabled button is.
- **A narrow window draws one half of the Panel at a time**: below 900 px wide, counted at the
  default text size, the half used last, and the other side's Lower icons switch to theirs.
  The window is never under 1024 px, so this is the narrowest window with its text at 16 px or
  more. Widen the window or make the text smaller and both come back as they were (#1741).
- **Each half of the Panel is one Tab stop and a named region** for screen readers; the chevron
  on its line is no longer a Tab stop of its own (#1741).
- **A pin belongs to its tab.** A tab whose only pane is empty can be pinned now, and a pinned
  tab stays pinned whatever its first pane goes on to show (#4935).
- **A chat's tab says the state its row in the Chats list says.** The tab used to name the
  board's state (*running*, *waiting on you*) while the row said *working*, *needs you*,
  *idle* or *waiting on 2 tasks*. Both now say the row's word, so a screen reader hears the
  same state for a chat wherever it is (#4935).
- **Projects are a rail at the window's left, and it can hide itself.** The project tabs in the
  title bar are gone. Each project is a button in a column at the far left, showing its two
  letters in its own colour, how many things wait on you there, a dot while it has unsaved work,
  and a ring on the one you are in. **+** opens a project. The rail's last button hides it; while it is hidden, the title
  bar's first button shows it again, and moving the pointer to the window's left edge slides it
  in over the work, where **Keep sidebar shown** pins it again. Hiding and showing slide, and
  don't under reduced motion. The layout file remembers which way you left it (`rail`). A project's menu
  (right-click, or the menu key) still closes, pins and moves it, Delete closes the focused one,
  and Shift+Space moves it up or down the rail (#2915).
- **Themes have three more motion durations**: `duration.slide`, `duration.reveal` and
  `duration.leave`, for the rail sliding, its peek coming in, and the peek going (#2915).
- **The project root's tab and four more of the window's errors say project and branch.** The
  root tab's tooltip reads _Project — chats here start at the project root_. A task that did not
  start, and the project that refuses to be made inside another one, no longer say worktree or
  plane, and neither does opening a persona that is not there (#602).
- **The project rail no longer crowds a narrow window.** In a window narrower than about
  1080px, or about 1330px with both sidebars open, the rail hides itself so the work keeps its
  room. The
  window's left edge still peeks it, and the title bar's first button still shows it. It comes
  back when you widen the window or put a sidebar away. This hide is never written to the layout
  file. A rail you hid stays hidden. A rail you show or keep shown stays shown, in any window,
  until you hide it again (#3077).
- **New windows open at 1440×900**, or at your screen's usable size where that is smaller, so
  the project rail is shown beside both sidebars on a first launch (#3077).
- **A repo's own folder is marked against its upstream.** With no recorded base, the change
  markers, "Changed only" and the cockpit's ahead and behind count from the branch it follows
  (`origin/main`, say), not only from its last commit. An upstream that is not one plain remote
  and branch is no base, as before (#1130).
- **The update manifests say they are attested.** SECURITY.md now says that `dev.json`,
  `latest.json` and their weekly twins carry the same SLSA provenance as the builds, and how to
  check one with `gh attestation verify`. The app still checks each build's minisign signature
  before it installs anything (#778, #1133).
- **`persona remember --help` says where a persistent memory is written.** Only a unix build
  (macOS, Linux) writes one; elsewhere the write is refused, and `--ephemeral` scratch is
  written on every platform (#1408).
- **The project-root guard's `cd` hint says what `&` does, and comes with every named refusal.**
  A `cd` sent to the background by `&` never moves the shell at all, which the hint now says
  apart from the `;`, `||` and newline case. The refusal of an alias chain longer than purlis
  follows gains the same hint where such a `cd` comes before it. Nothing that was refused is
  allowed now (#1093).
- **A sandboxed chat's project protects the same scripts with far fewer entries.** Where a
  project's hooks load packages from `node_modules` (`node -r dotenv/config`, `--import tsx`),
  the sandbox now protects each package's folder once instead of each file in it, and a
  missing folder such a name starts with once instead of each file below it. A path a protected
  folder already holds is not listed again. Every path protected before is still protected, and
  a little more is. A large monorepo's hooks name about a quarter of what they did, so a
  project is much further from the limit past which its chat is refused (#1425).
- **purlis's network record keeps a share per chat.** One chat's lines past a fifth of the
  record now let go of that chat's own oldest lines, never another chat's, so one busy chat
  cannot push the others' counts out. `purlis doctor` counts purlis's own sandbox blocks at
  most once per chat a day (#1353).
- **The team's sandbox off is named by its commit only where that history checks out.** purlis
  names the commit and author of a project's sandbox off when the commit is on the upstream it
  fetched itself. Each commit on the way from that upstream down to the off is now read back and
  checked against its own id, and so are the author and the manifest the ask names the commit by.
  The off is called local where one does not match, and where the upstream fetched has since
  turned the sandbox back on (#2166).
- **Every hint is one tooltip, drawn in the theme and reached by the keyboard.** The window's
  hints were the platform's own tooltips, which a keyboard could not open and no theme could
  draw. Each is now the shared tooltip: beside what it is about, opened by the pointer after a
  moment or at once by Tab, taken down by Esc, and readable with the pointer on it. An icon
  button's tooltip is its name, and a disabled button whose hint says why stays reachable so the
  reason can be read (#2908).
- **The sidebar remembers each project as you left it.** Explorer's folded sections, the repos you
  folded and the folders you opened come back for each project after a relaunch, and so does the
  Chats view's This tab / Workspace / All pick, which moves from the window's storage into
  `layout.json` (#1686, #1696). Existing layout files load as they are.
- **The Chats list keeps its folds across a relaunch.** A chat you folded or opened in the Chats
  view comes back that way after purlis restarts, kept with the project's other views in
  `layout.json` and keyed by the chat's id, which it keeps across launches (#1687).
- **The Changes icon counts each branch's uncommitted files.** A branch folder's changed and
  untracked files are counted with its clone's (#1701, #1718).
- **The Personas view lists the project's personas at the project root**, where it said there
  was no workspace focused (#1686).
- **The skill lint reads at most 1 MiB of a skill's other files, and a studio list at most 16 MiB
  for the skills from outside the project and 16 MiB for the project's own.** A skill whose scripts and notes go past either says how many of its
  files were not read for the lint, so a clone full of large skills no longer makes the Skill
  studio or `purlis skill list` read tens of megabytes (#3459).
- **The files beside your own skills are read the way their `SKILL.md` is.** A script or Codex's
  `agents/openai.yaml` that is a hard link (the Nix store, `cp -al`, `rsync --link-dest`) is now
  linted and read in your own skill folders, as its `SKILL.md` already was. A repo's or the
  project's is still refused (#3459).
- **The Skills view shows what the chat in front gets, as small cards** (Skill studio preview, #3693). Its header names whose skills they are, "steward 5 · 11 skills", or "A new chat in ops" while no chat is in front. Cards are grouped Needs you, In this chat (A new chat gets, while no chat is in front) and Left out, each with its skill level, two lines of what it does or why it is left out, Use, a ⋯ menu, and one fix where it has one, such as Turn on in ops. The built-in skills fold into one quiet line, with Make my own copy under it. A click opens the Skill studio at that skill, and the chat keeps its pane. The menu adds Open the file and Open in Skill studio, and says why an item can't run. Only this chat's is gone.
- **A tab says what its focused pane holds, and the pin is the tab's.** A tab wears its focused
  pane's chat icon and name, and `+N` where other panes share it; hovering it lists every pane.
  Tabs shrink to 120px and then go behind *N more*, newest activity first; a pinned tab never
  goes there, and pinned tabs show only their icons when they alone would fill half the strip.
  *N more* wears ✋ when a tab behind it asks. A narrow tab shows its × only in front or under
  the pointer. *Pin tab* is on the tab's menu and the palette, *Close other tabs* in the
  palette leaves pinned tabs open, and a chat pinned before this keeps its pin on its tab
  (#4762).
- The Skill studio asks for its skills as you open it, instead of once its tab is drawn, so a
  studio with many skills shows them sooner (#4351).
- **The project's sandbox off says only what purlis verified.** The ask names the commit and
  its author only where purlis found that commit on the upstream its own fetch of the project
  saw; otherwise it says the off is local and not on that upstream. Your answer holds while the
  off stays, even where the history under it is rewritten; purlis asks again only once it has
  seen the off leave and come back (#2156).
- **A theme names the schema of the purlis it is for.** The theme schema is published per format
  and release, at `https://raw.githubusercontent.com/purlis/purlis/v<version>/docs/schema/theme.v2.schema.json`,
  so an editor completes only the tokens that purlis knows. Within a format the schema only
  grows. Purlis Classic's folder names its release's schema, and `purlis theme list --json` and
  `purlis theme check --json` give the address as `theme_schema` (#2448).
- **Your workspaces are in the title bar.** After the project's name, each workspace you pinned
  is a chip, with how many things wait on you there and the one you are in lit; the workspace
  you are in, when it is not pinned, is a dashed chip that pins it. **⌄** (or **⌥⌘P**,
  Ctrl+Alt+Shift+P elsewhere) opens every workspace with a filter, a pin toggle on each, the project root first and
  **New workspace…** last. **⌘1–⌘9** (Ctrl+1–9 elsewhere) go to the first nine pins, and a
  sideways swipe over the title bar steps one pin at a time. Switching slides the workspace in;
  reduced motion has none. The workspace strip under the title bar is gone (#2916).
- **With the projects sidebar hidden**, the project's name in the title bar (or ⌥⌘P) opens a
  switcher of every project and workspace. Choosing a project goes back to the workspace you were last on.
- **Themes have a `titlebar` family** of parts for the chips (`titlebar.workspace.*`,
  `titlebar.count.*`; parts manifest version 12).
- **⌘P is unchanged**: it still finds files and projects, and ⌘P ⏎ still goes back to the last
  project.
- **A long last message keeps its end.** Past 4 KiB, a chat's last message is cut in its middle,
  so a question on its last line still shows in the Inbox, the strip, and a report purlis makes
  from a task's last message (#4563).
- **The window marks the characters you cannot see the way the command line does.** A
  sandbox block's folder or host, a recent grant, a runner's branch and a repository's
  instruction file now show each invisible character as `⟦U+XXXX⟧`, where they used to show
  `‮` or `U+202E`. They mark the same characters as the core, from the same generated
  table: a variation selector, a Hangul filler or a no-break space in an instruction file is
  marked in its preview too, and a joiner that holds an emoji or a word together still reads as
  text. A command holding a no-break or an en space now shows it as `⟦U+00A0⟧` in the Inbox,
  where it used to read as a plain space. The Inbox also says that this is why only Deny is
  offered (#3202).
- **More of the window says project, branch and folder instead of plane, worktree and piece.**
  The status line counts `branches`, not `pieces`. The bottom bar and the status line say
  *Reading the project…*. The project-updated mark on a chat's tab, the repo picker, New project,
  New vault and the sandbox settings say project. In Settings, *Worktrees folder* is now
  *Branch folders*. The rest follow as their screens are next changed (#602).
- **The window's forge calls use your purlis sign-in, so `gh` and `glab` are optional.** Once
  you are signed in to a host in Settings › You › Accounts, the workspace repo picker, the
  Doctor's discover, the save button and the workspace's LIVE switch (and the pull or merge
  request they open), and the workspace panel's request and CI column ask that forge over HTTPS
  with your sign-in, read from the keychain for each request. A host with no purlis account
  still uses `gh` or `glab` when they are installed; when they are not, the message says to
  sign in under Settings › You › Accounts. Chats, `purlis` commands and saves nobody pressed for
  never use the sign-in (#1816).
- **The window's git uses only your own network settings, not a repository's.** A fetch, push
  or save the window runs takes its proxy, TLS and certificate settings, extra headers and
  address rewrites from your global or system git config only. Where a repository's own config
  sets one of these, the window's git uses your value or git's default instead, or stops with a
  sentence naming the kind of setting and asks you to move it to your global config.
- **A window with no project lists what it says in one place.** A slow start, a launch without
  the session bus, vaults left waiting, a project that has moved or gone, and the opener's own
  lines now form one list at the top of the opener's page, the most important first (#1688).
- **An alert's fix says what it acts on.** The Inbox's alert rows press "Update workspace
  layout" rather than "Reinit", and "Use the built-in theme…" rather than "Use built-in…". The
  questions about moving a file aside offer Keep it first (#1719).
- **A screen reader hears the lines that say something is being read.** Examples are "Reading
  the vaults…", "Finding files…", and a list purlis could not read (#1719).
- **A project's Inbox has a place for the window's own lines.** With a project in front, the
  lines the window says about itself are listed at the top of that project's Notices and
  counted in its status line, once the window draws them there (#1688).
- **Purlis Classic light's code properties and attributes are a shade darker** (`#1283ff`, was
  `#218bff`), so they read on the editor's current line (#2522).
- **The theme check measures the modal scrim, the terminal's cursor and the words on the diff's
  washes.** A cursor is held at 3:1 on the terminal and the word under a block cursor at 4.5:1, the
  editor's words at 4.5:1 on a changed line's and a changed word's wash, and a scrim has to move the
  window it lies over at least 2:1. Your own colour that breaks one is left out with a notice (#2987).
- **A link's close of a chat with theme drafts is asked in the window.** Purlis's window asks
  Keep or Revert, says a link asked, and closes nothing until you answer there. It never asks
  over a question already on screen. Drafts folders made before each named its clone are adopted
  in the plane's own state folder, and deleted once their chat is gone (#2761).
- **Keep says when the theme folder it replaces changed since the draft started.** A theme
  draft records the folder it copied, and Keep's question says so before it replaces a folder
  that your own edit, a pull or another chat changed since. Closing a chat that kept several
  drafts asks who draws each one. A refused kept theme's Notice waits while a draft is drawn,
  and the strip says so. **Use in the whole project** says the project's next save commits the
  theme for everyone. The drafts of a chat that is no longer open are deleted (#2708).
- **Theme folders hold only names every platform can.** A theme folder or a file in it named as
  a Windows device (`CON`, `NUL`, `COM1`, …) or ending in a dot or a space is refused with a
  sentence, on every platform, in import, export and the theme folder reader (#2588).
- **`purlis theme check --json` is not `clean` when a consent floor is held.** A theme the
  window draws with purlis's own values for a floor it breaks now answers `clean: false`
  (#2518).
- **`purlis theme list` names your own `theme.json` by its level.** Its FROM reads
  `machine <path>` (#2518).
- **A theme made on one platform opens on every other.** A theme folder's name and every name
  inside it hold none of `< > : " / \ | ? *` nor a control character: `purlis theme import`,
  `export` and the theme folder reader each refuse such a name and say why in one sentence
  (#2671).
- **Every theme file is read from the folder purlis opened.** `purlis theme check <folder>`,
  your own `theme.json` and `purlis theme export <level id>` open the folder once, refusing a
  link, and read every file from it (#2604, #2670).
- **A theme choice names the level of the folder it picked.** Choosing a theme folder in Settings
  › Theme now records whether it is your own, the project's or the workspace's, so a folder of
  the same name at another level is never drawn in its place. The gallery shows a card for each
  folder of one name, each saying its level. Choices made before keep drawing as they did and
  gain their level the next time they are written (#2516).
- **A chat's theme specimen draws any theme the window could draw there.** `theme_preview` names
  a theme folder of the chat's workspace, the project or your own by its id, an extension's
  theme, or `draft:<folder>`, the chat's own theme draft, with the theme's option values, and
  draws it side by side with another, such as a draft beside the theme as kept. The specimen is
  tinted with the workspace's colour and drawn in the theme's own fonts, and its terminal in the
  theme's terminal font. Settings › Theme's cards are pictured in their fonts too (#2536).
- **⌘⇧Enter is now Focus this pane.** In a split it zooms the focused pane to fill the tab, and
  the tab shows a zoom mark until the same key brings the other panes back. In a tab with one
  pane it is Focus mode, as before (#4765).
- **A todo's row no longer opens a card beside it.** Its tab holds the whole text instead, as a
  memory's and a persona's do (#1214).
- **The Skill studio keeps its own records in purlis's data folder, outside the project.** Drafts,
  tries, this machine's grades, grades under way, grading after each edit, the kept grade chats
  and the records of which workspace and persona folders reach chats now live in
  `<data>/app-state/<clone key>/`, which a chat's sandbox reads and never writes. The first time
  you open a project after updating, purlis moves your drafts and this machine's grades there.
  Grading after each edit is off again until you turn it on from a grade's plan, and where a
  sandboxed chat had run in the project, each workspace and persona folder waits for your Accept
  in the Skill studio again before its skills reach chats (#3718).
- **The window's copy has a house style.** `docs/ui-copy.md` writes it down, and the build now
  refuses a stock error phrase, a title-cased label or a capital "purlis" in a sentence.
  *Open Project…* reads *Open project…*, About says *This is purlis {version}*, and the empty
  todo and persona lists and an unreadable Search tab each say the way out (DS-2, #625).
- **The README describes purlis as it ships.** Its status is version 0.4 on macOS and Linux, and
  it names the five concepts, the harnesses, the forges and where credentials are kept (#605).
- **A chat's skills chip turns warning-coloured for every need of the chat's own that the Skills view lists:** its budget, pins it does not read, a router that fell back, skills it started without, or skills changed since it started. Its tooltip names each (#3953).
- **The Use skill… row no longer says the chat's budget.** The Skills view says it (#3954).
- **The refused vault Notice leads with the persona's mark.** Its sentence names the persona the
  chat runs as, and now starts with that persona's mark, as the dispatch question does; so does
  what Allow answered (#1454).
- **Every vault command in a sandboxed chat says what works.** `secret set`, `secret rm`,
  `secret audit`, `vault add`, `vault remove` and `vault verify` are yours: in a sandboxed chat
  each is refused before anything is read, with a sentence naming the vault's tab in the app or
  the same command in your own terminal, rather than ending in the sandbox's own refusal
  (#1969).
- **The waiting colour is never taken for the accent.** A theme's accent, and the edges drawn
  in it (the focus ring, a selected row's edge, the primary's edge), stay visibly apart from the
  waiting amber, as written and in every workspace colour. In a yellow or an orange workspace the
  accent gives way: it is drawn with less colour, or as the theme writes it where no amount
  holds, while the accent's washes keep the workspace's colour. A theme that sets the two too
  close is drawn with purlis's own waiting colour, and `purlis theme check` says so (#3130).
- **What a Codex or opencode chat cannot tell purlis is said from its harness card.** The
  sentence on the chat is made from the card's lines, so the two never disagree: a Codex chat
  now also says that a later conversation started inside it is not followed, as its card does
  (#1134).
- **Chats already running are told when a socket or a service is allowed.** The Sandbox
  changed notice now lists a chat that started before a socket or a service was allowed for
  its project or for every project, with Restart.
- **A workspace renamed from inside a sandboxed Claude Code chat leaves its kept reports for
  the app to move.** `purlis workspace rename` says so, and the app moves them when the
  project is next opened.
- **The parts of who may dispatch to whom say the same thing.** A box ticked under a
  dispatch question is kept where the answer you press holds: in the task's workspace for
  an Allow, in any workspace for the wider one. The Notice that says a teammate's grant
  arrived, and a refusal kept while you were away, say what the other persona works with in
  the question's own words. Where that persona may dispatch onward only for work in one
  workspace, the sentence says which. Settings › Project › Dispatch says under a persona's
  name what its definition wants, and that this grants nothing. Reopening a finished task
  is refused, with the reason, where the project no longer lists the task's profile for its
  persona (#1502, #1504, #1505, #1506, #1507, #1509).
- **A chat is told how it was asked for.** Where a chat is working, at its start, in
  `purlis persona where` and the `persona_where` tool, now says whether the chat that asked
  for it dispatched a task or handed its work off, and whether it still waits on a report.
  The chat that asked is matched by the lineage it is in as well as by its number (#1455).
- **The summary of a time away leads the news under the tabs.** It no longer stands behind
  "+N more" while other news waits; trouble still comes first (#1551).
- **A chat already waiting on you that asks again while you are away is counted.** The
  summary's "waiting on you" counts what is new for you, not only chats new to the list
  (#1551).
- **Who committed a project's grant is read once for the whole list.** Settings' dispatch
  grants and the Granted list each read the project's history once per page instead of once
  per grant, and the name they show is cut to a sensible length with any character that
  draws as nothing taken out (#1464).
- **Edit as JSON refuses a workspace manifest its readers would misread.** A `name` that is not
  the workspace's folder, or `repos` that is not a list of `{"name": …}` records (each with an
  optional `"branch"`), is refused with the key it is about, unless the file already held it
  (#1292).
- **Making a workspace takes you there, and its notice hangs from its chip** (#3648). Creating
  a workspace now opens it and pins it, even with a chat in front. Its "Workspace X is ready"
  notice no longer pushes the window down: it hangs from the new workspace's chip in the title
  bar, as a card with a point, offering Add a vision (while it has none) and Details, and no
  longer Open. A click elsewhere hides the card and leaves a ● dot on the chip, which brings it
  back; × or Esc dismisses it. F6 reaches the card. It is still listed in the Notices centre
  under Results, and dismissing it in either place dismisses it in both.
- **`purlis worktree commit` works in a chat with no sandbox** (#4534). It used to refuse and
  point at plain git, which a harness's own rules can refuse too, leaving the chat no way to
  commit. It now commits there with that chat's own git, with your hooks, signing and filters,
  and a terminal does the same. To bring the refusal back, set `[plane]
  refuse_unsandboxed_commit = true` (Settings › Saving). Sandboxed chats commit as before.
- **A chat the app starts with no sandbox in a project whose sandbox is on is told so** (#4534).
  Your own level can start a dispatched chat with no sandbox while the chat that asked for it
  has one, and until now only its tab said so.
- **`purlis worktree remove` leaves a task's branch folder alone.** A folder purlis cut for a
  task is refused, `--force` or not, and the refusal says to discard it from the task's Changes
  tab, as the explorer's own Remove already did. A folder already gone, and an ended task's
  folder in a repo where Discard cannot run, are still removed, but never with
  `--delete-branch`: a task's branch can hold commits nothing else has. A dispatch record that
  does not read now keeps the folder it names from both, where before it kept nobody off it
  (#1534).
- **Open in your editor from a file's row opens at the line you were reading.** The line last
  read in that file's preview, in this window, is where your editor opens it; a file not read
