  opens at line 1 as before. The line is kept in memory only (#1143).
- **Your level now starts every chat as you chose it** (#2071). Full sandbox starts the full
  sandbox and Floor the floor, whether or not the project turned the full sandbox on. A Floor
  written into `purlis.local.toml` any other way, in a project at the full sandbox, waits for
  your Confirm, as No sandbox does. The title bar shows the level of the chat in front.
- **Your level `off` now takes effect** (#2071). Where you set or confirmed no sandbox for a
  project, or for a persona, in Settings › Sandbox › Your level, its chats start without the
  sandbox, as "Start without the sandbox" does, and each tab says *no sandbox — your setting*.
  A level written into `purlis.local.toml` any other way waits for your Confirm and changes
  nothing until then. A chat another chat dispatches or hands off to starts at the strictest
  level across the chain of chats that asked, so asking for a chat never turns the sandbox off. Elsewhere chats start as before: at the floor in a project that has not turned the full
  sandbox on, and in the full sandbox in one that has, whether you picked Full sandbox or Floor.
- **A project's per-chat files no longer pile up.** When the app opens a project, it removes
  the per-chat markers in `.charter/sessions/`, the chat traces in
  `.charter/persona-state/trace/` and the old report drafts in `.charter/reports/` that nothing
  has written for 30 days. The files of every chat the app is about to reopen are kept, however
  old, and so is a trace that records a secret being handed out (SC-7, #682).
- **Switching into a project with many chats is quicker.** Each chat's row in the explorer and its
  state mark on the tab are dimmed in their colour rather than by transparency, and the mark for a
  chat that has said nothing yet is a ring broken into two arcs rather than a dashed one, so fifty
  of them no longer cost the switch a slow paint (FR-27, #891).
- **Per-machine logs are named by the device id, not the hostname.** The dispatch and skill
  logs (`personas/_dispatch/`, `personas/_skills/`), the piece claim log, the landing log and
  pending landings are now filed under this device's id from the machine store. Two machines
  that share a hostname no longer write into one file, and renaming a machine no longer starts
  a new one. The hostname stays as a label: a piece claim still says which machine made it.
  Files an earlier version wrote under a hostname are still read; a later migration renames them
  (FD-25, #662).
- **The window no longer waits on the project's files.** The sidebar, a workspace's panels,
  the project root's session records, the Curate menu and every memory read or edit are read
  off the thread that draws the window. On a project with sixty workspaces and a thousand
  memories, a workspace's panels used to hold the window for about 45 ms per read and the
  sidebar for about 27 ms; now each holds it for about 10 µs. A terminal's resize and watch stay
  where they were, so they keep their order (SC-2, #680).
- **No hook call is lost when the app is down.** A hook now waits for the app to say it has
  recorded the call, on disk, before it answers the harness. When the app is not running, is
  slow or quits mid-turn, the hook writes the call to its chat's spool in `.charter/app/spool/`
  instead, and the app records it the next time it opens the project, saying which lines were
  missing or did not check. A hook call takes about a millisecond longer (FD-30, #667).
- **The sidebar no longer reads every workspace's todos for each change.** The app keeps what
  the sidebar draws in memory and reads again only what a change is part of: a todo closed in
  one workspace reads that workspace's todos, and nothing else. A change the app cannot place
  still reads the whole sidebar again (FD-10b, #933).
- **Fewer redraws when switching projects.** A project's tab strip comes back at the width it
  had instead of drawing every tab and then folding them away, the palette closes in the same
  frame as the switch, and the project's theme and its repos' save standing are drawn from what
  the window already knows, then checked again behind them (FR-27, #620).
- **A new project tracks the forge its repo is on, and asks when it cannot tell.** The first
  run, the New project dialog and `purlis init` now follow one rule. The forge, and its owner or
  group, come from the `origin` of the repo the project is made for, when that remote is on
  github.com or gitlab.com. Otherwise the window asks GitHub or GitLab with two buttons, and
  `purlis init` writes nothing and asks for `--forge` or `--adopt`. Before, the first run made
  a GitHub project with no owner, and `purlis init` defaulted to GitLab. **A script that runs a
  bare `purlis init` now exits 2 and makes nothing, where it used to make a GitLab project:
  add `--forge gitlab` to keep the old result.** `--forge` and `--owner` still win when given,
  and running `init` again on an existing project asks nothing.
- **purlis runs far fewer git processes in your repos while it is idle.** Auto-save, the
  title bar's save indicator, the Saving tab and the alerts used to each run `git status` and
  its friends on their own timers — about ten git processes every two seconds per project, and
  more in a busy repo, where they could pile up on each other. They now share one reading per
  repo, made again only when the repo's git files move, its project's watcher sees a change, a
  save or fetch finishes, a chat ends, or ten seconds have passed. Only one git process runs in
  a repo at a time for them. Where your git config says nothing about `core.untrackedCache`,
  purlis turns git's untracked cache on for these reads and for its saves, so `status` stays
  quick in a large repo: the cache is then kept in that project's and those clones' index, as
  git keeps it (`git update-index --no-untracked-cache` removes it, and setting
  `core.untrackedCache` yourself, to anything, stops purlis asking for it).

## Deprecated

- **The charter names stop working at 1.0.** Until then purlis reads its old names and writes
  only the new ones. From 1.0 it stops reading them: the `charter` command (run `purlis`), the
  `CHARTER_*` environment variables (set `PURLIS_*`), a project's committed files under their
  charter names (`purlis doctor --fix rename-plane` moves them), this machine's local state under
  its charter names, such as `.charter/`, `charter.local.toml` and the config and data homes
  (`purlis migrate` moves them), and keychain items under `charter/` (the same migration copies
  them to `purlis/`). The removal waits past 1.0 while `purlis doctor` still sees an old name in
  a project you opened, so run it before you update: it names every old name it finds. A
  migration waits until nothing named charter or purlis is running, and going back to a build
  from before the rename on the same machine needs `purlis migrate --undo` first. A project
  `rename-plane` moved is no project at all to a teammate on a build from before the
  compatibility check, so update every teammate before you move a shared project. Every
  version's notes say this until 1.0 (ADR 0091).

## Removed

- **Settings › Chats list › Rows.** A row is always one line. A layout file that still says
  `chats.lines` is read as if it did not (#1675).
- **A pressed task no longer becomes an ordinary tab.** It did, for good, and its close button
  read as ending the session. A task whose session has no tab in the window (the session was
  closed and left it running) still opens in a tab of its own. The "no tab" badge on a task's
  row is gone: no task has one (#1486).
- **`purlis browser install` is retired.** A chat purlis starts drives a real browser with
  purlis's own browser tools, which the `browser` skill teaches, so purlis no longer generates
  Playwright's page-driving pages into a project. Running the command writes nothing and says
  what to use instead. Pages it generated before stay where they are (#2575).
- **The separate Project settings page.** Its forms are the Project level's groups in Settings,
  and its Raw TOML view is Edit as TOML. Project settings… on a project's menu and in the
  palette opens Settings at the Project level. A Project settings tab left open by an earlier
  version comes back as that too (SE-19, #1169).
- **The two icons at the bottom left that put a side away.** They did what each side's own
  strip of icons already does: press the open view to put the side away, and any view to bring
  it back. ⌘B and ⌥⌘B (Ctrl+B and Ctrl+Alt+B off a Mac) and the palette's rows do the same.
- **Persona sub-agents are retired. After updating, run `purlis doctor --fix persona-agents` in
  each project, then save.** purlis no longer generates `.claude/agents/<persona>.md`, and
  `purlis persona sync-agents` (with its `--approve-mcp`) is gone: the word is still recognised
  and answers with one sentence that says what replaced it. The fix removes the files purlis
  generated, where git tracks them and they have no uncommitted change, and leaves and names
  every other file. It prints everything it changed, makes no commit, runs only by name, and
  changes nothing on a second run. Until it is run, Claude Code still lists each generated
  file as an agent type; a call to one is refused, and each chat is told so at its start. A
  project's own `CLAUDE.md`, README, charters and scripts may still say `sync-agents` or
  `subagent_type`: search for both (#1451).
- **A persona whose `model:` named a model now runs on the asking chat's profile.** `model:
  opus`, `sonnet` or `haiku` picked the generated sub-agent's model, and nothing reads it now,
  so that persona's chats run on the model of the chat that dispatched them, which may cost
  more or less. Name the profile a persona's chats start on with `profile:`. The fix and
  `purlis persona lint` say this for each persona it applies to. A `model:` that is the name of
  a profile the project carries is rewritten to `profile:` (#1451).
- **`agent-tools:`, `skills:` and `memory:` are read by nothing.** A
  persona chat has every tool of its harness, so a persona that listed no editing tool could
  not edit files as a sub-agent and can as a chat. Nothing asks before two persona chats write
  in one tree; `dispatch-isolation: worktree` now gives a dispatched chat a worktree of its own
  instead (#1453). `purlis persona lint` and the fix say what widened for each persona and leave
  the lines. To keep a persona from a tool, name it in `disallowed-tools:`. The hooks no longer
  log a returned sub-agent or a message to one in the dispatch log (#1451).
- **purlis no longer turns other harnesses' plugins on or off per project.** A plugin brings
  hooks, MCP servers, subagents and code as well as skills, and each harness handles those its
  own way, so which plugins load is now the harness's own settings' to say. The Plugins group in
  Settings, the plugin rows in the Skill studio and `[harness_plugins]` are gone. purlis's own
  plugin loads as before on all three harnesses, and `purlis plugin install` stays. The Skill
  studio still lists the skills a plugin brings, read-only, naming the plugin (ADR 0050, #3467).
- **The old overlay and menu classes are gone.** `.ui-menu`, `.ui-menu-item`, `.ui-popover` and
  `.ui-overlay-arrow`, which nothing in the window had worn since the menu, popover and tooltip
  families replaced them, are no longer drawn. A theme that targeted them reached nothing already;
  the families' parts are what a theme reaches (#3365).
- **Search no longer has a view tab.** The left side's Search view is the only place a search
  is shown (#1701).
- **The explorer no longer lists the chats a chat started in other workspaces under its row.**
  The Chats list is the one tree of who asked whom (#1490).

## Fixed

- **A sign-in whose server redirects to another site now finishes after `browser_fill_secret`.**
  A redirect from the approved site's own server, after a form sent there, takes the page on: to a
  site this browser was on before the fill by itself, and to any other once you allow it. The filled
  page is gone before anything reaches that site. Links, scripts and the chat's navigate stay
  refused, and a redirect whose address holds the value is refused. A page that ends on an error page
  no longer holds the browser (#5230).
- **A bare `ssh` in a sandboxed Claude Code chat reaches an allowed host.** Its route through
  the chat's SOCKS port is written where no chat writes, and Claude Code puts it first on each
  command's `PATH` before the command runs, so `ssh` works with the command unchanged, as it
  already did in Codex and opencode chats; a host the chat may not reach is a Block with Allow.
  The harness's own `PATH` never names it (#1667).
- **A sandbox block is named from the sandbox's own report first.** Where Claude Code reports
  what its sandbox refused, the Notice names that socket, service, file or host whatever the
  program printed or ended with: down a pipe, behind a build runner, or from a tool that blamed
  something else. The report is read past the note Claude Code may write after it. A refused
  listen on a port is no longer shown as a host to allow, and a refusal that is not about a file
  is no longer shown as one in the chat's own folder. Allowing still asks you, and still checks
  the target as before.
- **A blocked task can report what it found next.** A task whose report came out blocked, or
  one you took up again after its report by typing in its tab, can now send one more report.
  It reaches the chat that asked and wakes it like any report, and the Activity tab shows both
  reports. Before, purlis refused every report after a task's first, so you had to carry the
  result across by hand (#1768).
- **A project blocked by an old "conflict" clears itself.** Save on a project whose last push
  stopped now pushes again even when nothing changed, so the block either goes or comes back
  naming the files that conflict. A conflict record that names nothing reads "Save stopped
  earlier — Save to retry" and is retried. A successful Update clears the block its replay
  settled.
- **A save's conflict is never sent round in a loop.** The Saving view names the conflicting
  files and the git commands that settle them, with _Open terminal here_, and no longer offers a
  chat, which may not rebase the project's root. Update's conflict answer names the same
  commands.
- **A note that names a variable no longer blocks the project's save.** A line such as
  `token = DEPLOY_TOKEN` or `` `password = KEYCLOAK_ADMIN_PASSWORD` `` says which environment
  variable or vault entry carries a credential, and holds none. The save read it as a
  credential and refused. A value that is only such a name (capitals, digits and underscores,
  in words, one of them a word like `TOKEN`, `SECRET`, `KEY` or `PASSWORD`) is now let through.
  A key written in capitals is still refused, and so is a real value after the name.
- **A blocked task can ask before it reports again.** A task whose report came out blocked, or
  one you took up again after its report, can now send the chat that asked progress notes and
  questions until its one more report, as a task still working on its first does. Before,
  purlis refused them as if the task had finished for good (#1786).
- **A page that holds a frame from another site settles.** A chat's browser waited out its whole
  settling time on such a page and then said the frame's document was still loading, because the
  engine answers that document in the frame's own session. It now settles once the frame has
  loaded (#2689).
- **A box that cuts off a frame from another site marks what it hides.** A snapshot or a find
  marks a frame's element `(out of view)` when a box on the page around the frame hides that
  part of it, for a frame from another site as for one from the page's own (#2689).
- **A branch cut for a new chat waits its turn.** It no longer runs beside a Remove or a Merge
  of the same repo from the explorer, and a project reached through a link, or typed in another
  case, shares one turn per repo (#1534).
- **A chat in a branch folder counts the repo skills of its branch** (Skills, #4238). Such a chat
  used to count no repo skills at all, so a skill on that branch did not take the place of a
  plane skill of the same name, and the budget counted both. It now counts the ones its harness
  finds in the branch folder, under the name of the clone the folder was cut from.
- **A branch folder pushes again after its update, with commits added since.** `purlis worktree
  update` notes the commit the remote's copy of the branch was at, and a plain `purlis worktree
  push` goes over exactly that commit, so a pull request keeps its branch and history instead
  of being rebuilt on a new one. A remote someone else moved, a branch rewritten any other way,
  or remote commits the folder never had still refuse the push, and say what to do
  (#3895).
- **A branch folder is cut from and updated onto the remote's base where the clone's own has
  diverged.** Where the clone's `main` holds commits its remote never took and the remote has
  moved on too, `purlis worktree add` and `purlis worktree update` start from `origin/main`
  instead, and leave the clone's `main` where it is (#3890).
- **A file an agent writes just as you open a branch's files gets its change mark.** The
  explorer read what the branch changed at the same moment it asked for the branch to be watched,
  so a file written after that read and before the watch held was drawn unmarked until something
  else moved in the branch. What a branch changed is now read once its watch holds, or after two
  seconds and once more when the watch holds (#1107).
- **A branch whose reads stayed busy is watched again.** When the reader was busy for every
  retry, or paused the branch, the explorer stopped following that branch's changes and said
  nothing. Its open folders now say "Changes on disk are not shown yet", and purlis asks for the
  branch again once the pause is over (otherwise after about thirty seconds). Once the branch is
  watched, its changes are read again, so a file written in the meantime is still marked
  (#1745).
- **A host refused to a command a sandboxed chat runs with a vault now raises the chat's block
  Notice.** `purlis secret exec` in a sandboxed chat is run by the app, behind a proxy carrying
  the chat's hosts. When that proxy refused a host, the command said only what its client says
  (kubectl's "Forbidden"), no Notice came, and the chat was stuck. Now the chat's tab shows the
  sandbox block Notice naming the host and port the proxy refused, with Allow for this chat,
  Always allow and Keep blocked, and purlis says on the command's stderr that its sandbox
  refused that host and where to allow it. The host comes from the proxy's own record, never
  from the command's output, and one that carries a value from the vault is never named or
  offered. Once allowed, the chat is started again with it and the next run reaches the host.
  A second host refused within a minute now gets its own Notice instead of being held back.
- **On macOS a brokered `secret exec` command can always read the credential file it was given.**
  macOS can name a file in the temporary folders by two paths. The command's sandbox now gives
  the file back under both of them, so the command is no longer refused its own credential now
  and then. It still reads nothing else in the vaults (#2489).
- **A browser call answers at once while another browser is stuck.** When purlis could not end a
  chat's browser yet, it now keeps trying on a timer of its own, waiting longer between tries,
  so no chat's browser call waits on it. A browser that is not ended yet still counts toward the
  project's three until it is (#2283).
- **A chat's browser reads a page whose script cut an emoji in two.** Half of the emoji reads as
  �, and the browser goes on; a page's very large network request no longer ends it either
  (#2745).
- **A browser that ends on its own leaves Needs you at once.** When a chat's browser crashes or
  its session host stops it while it waits for you to take over, its Ask ends straight away and
  the Inbox keeps an update; the chat's next browser call says the browser has gone (#2385).
- **A browser you take over after its chat clicked a field takes your keys.** Your first key was
  held with "the page cannot tell which field has the focus", since the page said that both
  the document and the field had the focus. The field is what has it (#2294).
- **A busy folder no longer stalls purlis.** A write that finds its folder locked waits up to ten
  seconds, then says the folder is busy and to try again, and writes nothing.
- **A side view's card rows read as cards in Purlis Classic.** In Classic dark, the raised ground
  was almost the side panel's own, so the cards read as plain rows. Classic now draws a card row
  on its sunken ground, a step from the panel in dark and in light. The theme check reports a
  theme whose parts put a card row less than 1.05:1 from the side panel it stands on, with no
  edge a hairline from it. The check only reports it and redraws nothing (#3774).
- **A chat blocked on a local socket no longer sends you looking for an Allow.** A sandboxed
  chat that could not reach Docker's socket asked you to choose Allow for this chat, which a
  socket's notice never offers: purlis grants no local socket. A chat is now told that, and says
  which socket was blocked and that Start without the sandbox, or running the command yourself,
  is the way on.
- **A chat started on a pool before this update stays yours when Runs on changes.** Once a window
  restart takes it back, it's found on that pool again after the setting moves (#4683).
- **"Started" is when a chat's current run began.** Where a chat is told where it and the chats
  around it are working, a chat brought back today no longer says it started the day it was
  first opened (#1455).
- **A chat started again at once counts and records one run** (#2250). When a sandboxed Claude
  Code chat is started once more at its start because its project's settings changed, this
  machine's sandbox count and the event log say one run: the one that goes on.
- **Starting a chat while a pool's runner is being replaced just works.** The chat starts on the
  pool's new runner, and chats still on the old runner stay reachable until they end. It used to
  be refused with "this runner is being replaced" until purlis restarted.
- **A slow machine or runner no longer fails a chat's start.** The dialog says "Starting the session
  host…" for as long as it takes, Cancel works throughout, and it shows an error only when the host
  has actually failed. A chat that comes up after you cancel is closed.
- **A Claude Code chat waiting for its background agents is shown as working, not as needing
  you.** When a chat's agent started background agents and its turn ended while it waited for
  them ("Waiting for 4 background agents to finish"), purlis put it in needs you and sent a
  notification. Now it reads as working until those agents are done and the chat stops with
  nothing left in flight, or until it asks you something. A chat whose agents were stopped
  before they woke it shows needs you once Claude Code says it is idle, without a "waiting on
  you" prompt it never showed. Background shells and monitors, which can run for as long as
  the chat does, still hand you the chat when its turn ends (#1626).
- **A chat waiting on its own background work shows as waiting, not as needing you.** When a
  Claude Code chat's turn ends while its helpers, monitors or background shells are still running,
  or while it has a wake-up scheduled, its row, tab menu and persona mark now say `waiting on 2
  monitors` or `waiting on a wake-up at 14:05`. It raises no hand and sends no notification. The
  chat that dispatched it reads it as `waiting on its own work`, never idle. A background shell
  holds the wait for an hour, and a recurring schedule holds it only when its next run is within
  the hour. After that, or as soon as the chat asks you something, it needs you again (#3878).
- **A chat whose program has ended leaves nothing of it running.** Ending, stopping or closing
  a chat always ended everything its program had started, as long as the program itself was
  still running. A program that ended by itself (you quit it, or it left on the interrupt that
  Stop sends first) left the rest to the hang-up the system sends, and whatever ignored that
  ran on with nothing left to end it: a server the chat had started, for one. purlis now ends
  what such a program left in its process group as it finds the program gone: hung up, given
  half a second, then killed. A process that put itself in a session or a group of its own is
  not reached, as before.
- **A chat started without the sandbox gets a browser like a sandboxed chat's.** Allowed this
  project's sites, its browser reaches the hosts a sandboxed chat of its persona lists and the
  services on this machine you allowed, and nothing more. A site new to the project asks you, as
  it does for any chat (#2242).
- **`purlis workspace create <name> <repo>…` in a chat makes the workspace and its clones.** The
  app makes both in one ask, with the chat's internet access, as it makes a plain create and
  `purlis clone`. A sandboxed chat is told, before anything is made, that `--live` and `--use`
  are the person's to run. A workspace whose folder or baseline files could not be written is
  never reported ready: the command fails and names what is missing (qw387).
- **Refusing to remove a branch folder from a chat names the window's command:** *Remove folder
  <piece> in <repo>*, in the palette (qw387).
- **A clone or worktree gives back an agent or skill the project no longer has.** purlis copies
  the project's `.claude/agents/` and `.claude/skills/` into each checkout, but a copy stayed
  after the project's own file was removed, for example by `purlis doctor --fix
  persona-agents`. The next wire of the checkout now removes it, with its line in the
  checkout's `.git/info/exclude`. Only a copy purlis wrote and that is still as it wrote it goes:
  a file you added or edited, one git tracks, one reached through a link, and one whose project
  file purlis could not read all stay (#1583, #1460).
- **A workspace chip's theme focus colour no longer disappears from every focused chip**
  (#4086). When a theme's focus colour can't be read on a chip that is current, under the
  pointer and reached from the keyboard at once, only that chip draws its default. A chip that
  is only focused keeps the theme's colour.
- **A checkbox, chip, radio, switch, slider or small segmented control is never under the 24px
  target size in the compact density.** Each is at least 24px tall at any text size, as a small
  button and a small field are: a slider takes a press anywhere in that height, and a segment
  anywhere in its control's (WCAG 2.5.8, #4173). In the compact density, a small list's row with
  a checkbox in it (a todo in the Todos panel) is 24px tall now, where it was 18.
- **A checkbox or radio with no words takes a press evenly around its mark.** The 24px square that
  takes its press is now centred on the box, where it sat about 4px to one side, and nothing it
  draws moves (#4303).
- **A checkbox, radio or switch with no words beside it takes a press across 24px.** A row's
  selection box, drawn 14px wide, now takes a press anywhere in a 24 by 24 square around it, and
  nothing it draws moves (WCAG 2.5.8, #4197).
- **A chat that cleared its conversation still counts what the earlier one cost.** What a
  chat's harness reports it has cost is kept by conversation, so a task's dispatch record, the
  tokens on a tab's tasks and a session's token figure add every conversation the chat had,
  where before a `/clear` started the count again (#1457).
- A click, a form or Back that leads to another site while a page holding a filled secret holds its browser now tells the chat why it stopped, the site the browser is held to and what ends the hold, in place of only the browser's own error page.
- **A clone and a removal at the same moment no longer lose a workspace's repo.** Cloning a repo
  into a workspace and removing another from it both rewrite the workspace's `workspace.json`.
  When the two ran at once, from the window and a terminal for example, the later write could put
  back the list the earlier one had changed, so a repo it had just recorded or removed came back
  or went missing. Each now waits for the other (#1249).
- **Projects closed together let go of them one at a time**, as they did before closing moved
  off the window's thread, rather than all ending their chats at once (#1949).
- **A command purlis has not answered for 20 seconds is said on the window's line**, naming it,
  instead of a dialog that waits on it never coming up in silence (#1949).
- **A closed project leaves every window that shows it.** When charter closes a project, every
  window that shows it now removes its tab, its chats and its views, and shows the next project
  or the opener. This happens however the close was asked: from another window or from outside
  the window. Before, the window kept showing a project charter had already closed (#1242).
- **A cloud CLI's option value is no longer read as its subcommand.** An ask for
  `aws --region eu-west-1 s3 rm …` read as an ordinary command, because the region was taken
  for the subcommand. The global options that take a value are now skipped for `aws`, `gcloud`,
  `az` and `kubectl`, so such a line is classed as the delete or the secret read it is. The old
  reading is kept beside it, so no line is classed as less risky than before. `az` deletes,
  purges and Key Vault secret reads are classed too (#1046).
- **`purlis profile sign-in --pool` on a Docker pool** no longer stops at asking whether the runner
  keeps the profile: the question it asked the runner was one the runner refused.
- **A cluster runner comes to use its Pool's mint port without being claimed again.** Its desktop
  tells it where to ask at each link, so a runner whose Pool opts in later, as long as the Pool named its key
  when the runner was made, or one stopped through a key change, works from the next link. A chat's start also waits a few seconds for its repos to reach
  the Claim, so its first token covers them.
- **A chat that keeps running a refused tool on a cluster runner no longer keeps asking you.** Its
  runner asks the operator less often, and once you have refused such a run, it waits before asking
  you again and says so. Runs on a cluster's token are now recorded as from the cluster.
- **A code typed one character a box is kept out of the agent's answers as a whole.** When you or
  a login type a code into a row of boxes, purlis keeps the whole code out of every snapshot, find,
  wait, title and address the agent gets, as it already did each box's own content (#2144).
- **A commit made right after a checkout in the cockpit's branch now shows.** `git checkout -b
  topic/one && git commit` in the branch the sidebar is focused on moved only the new branch's
  ref, which purlis began watching a moment after the checkout, so the cockpit kept its old count
  until something else moved. Once the new ref is watched, the window reads the branch again
  (#2463).
- **A control whose theme colours fall back keeps its hover, pressed, selected, refused and
  unavailable looks** (#4040). When a theme's colours for a control at rest can't be read and
  are drawn back as the default, the control's other looks are no longer covered by that
  default: the control, and the words of its label, icon and other parts, draw as the default
  of each look, including a look that is selected and unavailable at once. Colours the theme
  set for a look are kept wherever that look holds. This was already the case for the title bar;
  it now holds for every kind of control.
- **A plain count coloured by a theme stays told from the hot count in every workspace tint.** A
  rule on `activity.count` whose fill a tint recipe turns draws the family default if it comes near
  the Needs-you count at any hue, not only as written (#4384).
- **A grade purlis stopped under is recorded as interrupted even when another program now has
  its process number** (Skill studio preview, #3466). A running grade holds a lock on its own
  record of being under way, and the next start reads that lock, not the process number, to tell
  whether it still runs. This also makes the check work where process numbers can't be asked.
- **A workspace's own colour measures Allow's edge as it is drawn.** Under a theme that tints Keep
  blocked's edge, the accent could give way to the waiting amber and land a shade too near that
  edge, at a hue only a custom `#rrggbb` reaches. Every rule is now measured at the chroma each
  side is drawn at (#3388).
- **Yellow and green workspaces keep the accent apart from the waiting amber.** On Purlis light
  (hues 90 to 117) and Purlis's high-contrast dark (hues 92.75 to 148), the window tinted the
  accent and the edges drawn in it, which put them too near the amber. It now draws them as
  written, as the theme engine always measured them (#3388).
- **Persona marks and rail project buttons follow the same rule.** A yellow mark on Purlis light,
  and yellow and green marks on its high-contrast dark, keep their tinted ground, but their glyph
  is now drawn in the theme's accent, so it stays apart from the waiting amber (#3388).
- **A drag cut short leaves no drag behind.** When the person takes a chat's browser over during
  a drag, or the drag ends another way, the browser cancels the engine's own drag even where the
  engine says that drag started only after the agent's drag had ended (#2839).
- **A harness declaration's `chosen_by = "purlis"` loads.** The reader took only `"charter"`,
  so a declaration written as the project format documents it was refused. `"purlis"` is the
  word, and `"charter"` is still read as its old spelling (#1756).
- **A dismissed "project gone" line stays dismissed for the whole run.** Dismissing the line
  about a remembered project that has moved or gone used to last only as long as the place it
  was dismissed in: the opener drawn again after the last project closed showed it once more.
  The window and the opener now share one list, and a dismissal lasts until purlis's own list
  of remembered projects no longer says the project is gone (it is back, located or forgotten).
  It is not yet kept past a relaunch (#1291).
- **A task dispatched to an idle cluster runner runs with no second try.** It waits for the runner
  as a chat you start does, and the window stays responsive while the runner comes back.
- **A handed-off chat started again with no conversation is handed its brief again.** Start
  fresh, or the fresh start that follows a resume its harness could not bring back, used to give
  a dispatched chat nothing to say what it was asked. Its first message is now its brief, read
  from purlis's own record of the dispatch, under a line saying it is a fresh start and not a
  new request. The brief is handed only where purlis can confirm it is the one the dispatch was
  sent, and only where it still passes the checks a first brief passes. Otherwise the chat is
  told why, and the Dispatches tab shows what was kept (#1609).
- **A Docker pool keeps its sign-ins when the app updates.** The pool's new runner takes the old
  runner's sign-ins once the old runner's last chat has ended, carried between the two runners'
  volumes on the Docker host just before the old one is removed, so a profile signed in on the
  pool stays signed in and no sign-in is held by two runners at once. Until then, a new chat on
  the new runner asks to sign in there. Only the sign-in files are carried, nothing passes
  through your machine, and a sign-in that cannot be carried never holds the update back: that
  profile is signed in again (#4011, #4055).
- **A door pressed on Add another project stays pressed.** On a machine that has been through
  the setup steps, the first `+` of a launch drew the setup steps' welcome for a moment and then
  swapped it for the plain one. A door pressed in that moment, such as Create a project, was
  undone and the welcome came back. purlis now finds out where you are in the steps before it
  draws the welcome, so the right one is drawn the first time (#2400).
- **A draft's outcome eval table names its arms as the tiles above it do.** In a draft's grade,
  the table and the lines under it say "The draft" and "Current version", where they said "With
  the skill" and "Its previous version" (#4923).
- **A runner with only its home left is just removed.** After a removal that took its container but
  not its home volume, a draining runner no longer waits for an answer it can't give.
- **A sign-in Docker failed to carry gets one more try.** If the removal failed too, the next look
  carries it, so the profile isn't signed in again.
- **A pool's sign-out runs once on each draining runner.**
- **A mouse button you let go of is let go in the browser too.** When the page moved on between
  your press and your release, the release was dropped and the engine kept the button held, so
  the next click could read as a drag. purlis now sends the release at the point of your press,
  and handing a browser back lets go of any button still held (#2989).
- **A failed background command's output, read back by file, raises its Block.** Reading a
  background command's output file with the file tool, `cat` or `tail` raised nothing, even when
  the command had failed on a refusal. Where Claude Code's own record of the task says it
  failed, what was read is now that command's own error, and its Block comes up with what it
  names (#2203).
- **More readers that can start a program are read as running one**: `rg --pre`, `sort
  --compress-program`, `less` and `more`, and `git` given configuration on its line, an external
  diff, or `git grep -O` (#2203).
- **A folder dialog that could not open no longer hides a newer refusal.** In the opener, the
  first run and New project, the dialog's failure gives way to any refusal that comes after it,
  such as a recent project that would not open or a forge answer that was refused (#1291).
- **Locate… on a gone project says when the folder picker fails.** A picker that could not
  finish was silent, the same as a cancel; the window's Notice now says why and stays, so you
  can pick again. A cancel still says nothing (#1291).
- **A release ships even when its runner image fails.** The desktop is published without a
  runner image; every pool stays on the runner it has, and the Pools group says the pool does not
  move to that version (#2880).
- **When one look of a control can't be read, only that look falls back** (#4174). If a theme's
  colour for a control under the pointer, pressed, chosen or focused can't be read, purlis now
  draws that look's default back, and only where it holds: every colour of it, the control's,
  its label's and its other parts', whatever set them. Before, it reached further and could take away
  colours the theme set for the control's other looks, for example a button's focus edge, or the
  fill of a row under the pointer that is also focused. This was already the case for the title
  bar; it now holds for every kind of control.
- **A title-bar control whose colours fail in two states at once falls back only there**
  (#4049, #4064). A workspace chip whose theme colours can't be read while it is both current
  and under the pointer now draws its default only in that case: under the pointer alone, or
  current alone, it keeps the theme's colours. A switcher row's see-through fill is checked on
  the popover colour the theme sets, not on the default popover.
- **A branch thousands of commits from its base shows a number.** The branch cockpit stops
  counting commits ahead and behind past 10,000 and says "10,000+", where a very long count
  used to run out of time and show an error instead. A branch exactly 10,000 commits away shows
  10,000 (#1152).
- **A screen reader names the text of a file and both sides of a diff.** The light editor's text
  was a text box with no name, so a screen reader said only "text box". It now says the file's
  path, and in a comparison which side it is, before or after. Every control the Settings tab and
  the editor tabs draw is now checked for a name (DS-6, #629).
- **The first browser on a slow connection starts.** A browser's start waits for its engine's
  download, however long that takes within its own limit, where before the window gave up after
  30 seconds and said the session host did not answer in time.
- **A refusal a chat can fix itself no longer sends it to you.** `git add` or `git commit` in a
  branch folder purlis made, in a sandboxed chat, is now refused before it runs, naming `purlis worktree
  commit -m "<message>" <path>…`, instead of failing on the sandbox and raising a Notice for
  you. And a refusal that already names the shape to retry (a dispatch, handoff or commit
  beside another command, a live substitution in a forge's or purlis's own text, a commit that
  skips the hooks, a handoff's brief) no longer ends by telling the chat to have you run it in
  your own terminal; refusals with no fix the chat can make still do (#3830).
- **A focused branch's count follows a commit that writes no file.** With the explorer focused on
  a branch, `git commit --amend --no-edit` or a commit of what was already staged moves its
  ahead and behind count at once, rather than at the next write in its folder: the branch's ref
  in the clone's git folder is watched too, for the focused branch only (#1152).
- **A row you fold in the Chats list stays folded when the window reloads.** A reload used to open
  every row again. A new launch still starts from the folds the list makes by itself (#1459).
- **A folder in a workspace that becomes a clone shows up without a restart.** Running
  `git init` in a plain folder of a workspace, or moving a `.git` into it, used to change nothing
  the window heard, so the workspace went on showing the folder as it was until the project was
  read again. purlis now watches each plain folder a workspace holds (the folder itself, not
  what is inside it), and reads the workspace again when one becomes a clone (#1160).
- **A file made while a folder opens in the explorer is drawn.** The folder was read before it
  was watched, so a file an agent made in between was missing until something else changed
  there. A folder is now read once its watch holds (#1427).
- **A folder removed while the explorer reads a branch no longer blanks its changes.** The read
  of files git does not track starts again, and the folder is simply gone from it. On
  Linux, a folder swapped for a link just before it is watched is no longer watched through the
  link (#1130).
- **A folder the explorer could not watch is tried again on its own.** When the system would
  not watch an open folder (it ran out of watches, for example), the folder showed "Changes on
  disk are not shown yet" until you opened or closed another folder. purlis now tries it again
  every few seconds, less often the longer it is refused, and the note goes away as soon as it
  is watched. Closing a window that freed watches clears the note in the other windows at once
  (#1160).
- **A folder the system would not watch is named as that folder, not as its branch.** When the
  system refused to watch every open folder of a branch, the explorer said the whole branch was
  waiting to be read. purlis now says which folders the system refused, and the explorer says
  "the system would not watch it" on them, whatever else of the branch is open (#1160).
- **A folder chain deeper than the system's path limit no longer blanks a branch's markers.** The
  walk for files git does not track read each folder by its whole path, so the first folder too
  long to name ended the whole read and no change was marked. Now such a folder is marked once,
  as not read past, and every other change in the branch is still marked (#1130).
- **A forge's refusal is shown as one clipped line.** When GitHub or GitLab refuses a request
  that purlis sent with your own sign-in, its words reach the window with every control and
  direction-changing character shown as an escape, and cut at 500 characters (#1038).
- **Input aimed at a frame before it moved to another site is held back.** While you drive a
  chat's browser, a frame of the page that goes to another site counts as showing something new,
  so input aimed at what it showed before is not sent to it (#2973).
- **A browser no longer stalls for half a minute on a page whose frame keeps reloading.** A
  rotating advert or any frame that loads new documents quickly could leave purlis waiting on
  the frame it had just left, so a key you typed beside it was refused. purlis now stops
  waiting as soon as the browser says the frame has gone (#3081).
- **A frame its page sends back into the page's own process is usable again once its new document
  is known.** A frame from another site, shown in a process of its own, that its page navigates
  to `about:blank` was refused ("try again in a moment") until it navigated once more. It now
  follows its page's word of its new document, whether that comes before or after its old session
  ends (#5162).
- **The git identity fix takes a name written with a joiner.** A name with a family emoji or a
  flag (two emoji joined by a zero-width joiner), a Persian name written with a zero-width
  non-joiner between two letters, or a Hindi or other Indic name whose conjunct asks for a half
  form or a shown virama with either joiner, was refused as holding an invisible character. It
  is now written, and the confirmation shows the name as you typed it. A joiner anywhere else,
  and every other control, zero-width or direction-changing character, is still refused
  (#1301).
- **A git reader whose repository's config names a program raises its Block.** `git log`,
  `git status` and the other reading subcommands, run in a repository whose own config names an
  fsmonitor hook, a diff or textconv driver, a filter, a signature program, an index hook or a
  promisor remote, are read as running a program, so a refusal that program met comes up as a
  Block (#2212).
- **A git purlis stops is stopped with everything it started.** When a git purlis ran from the
  window passed its deadline or was called off (a rebase in a save or an update, a push, a
  fetch, a clone you cancelled), purlis ended git itself and reported the call as stopped, but
  the programs that git had started went on: a filter, a credential helper, and under a `pull`
  another git that could keep writing the working tree and holding its lock. Each git now
  leads its own process group and the group is what is ended, asked first so that every git in
  it removes its locks, and killed only if it has not gone in two seconds. The forge's own
  command line (`gh`, `glab`) is ended the same way at its deadline. The `purlis` command in a
  terminal is unchanged: the gits it runs stay with it, so that Ctrl-C still reaches them.
- **A Go tool refused the certificate check now raises its notice.** In a sandboxed chat,
  `glab` or `gh` failing with `x509: OSStatus -26276` raised no notice, because the failure
  was only read from a command that succeeded. It is now read from a command that failed too,
  so the notice comes up with what you can do about it.
- **A chat that ended with a gone runner says so.** After **Make the runner again**, after removing a pool,
  or once a draining runner removed outside purlis is forgotten, its chats say they ended with the runner.
  They no longer say nothing was lost or offer Resume, because the conversation was on that runner (#4350).
- **A task that ended with a gone runner says why.** Its report names the runner, and its finished row
  says it can't be reopened because the conversation went with the runner. A chat lost earlier, when the
  session host stopped, is told too once its runner goes, and a task in that state now reports instead of
  waiting for ever (#4420, #4421).
- A router's grade that ended while another router was chosen opens its scorecard when you choose that router again, rather than leaving its page with no way on. An end that lands after you left the page no longer moves you, and an end opens its scorecard only once.
- A grade's running page offers a way back once the grade has ended, not "Leave it running". If it can't listen for the grade's steps, it says so and lets you try again. A skill's running page keeps Stop even when that skill's grades can't be read.
- **An extension that is grading says so** (Skill studio preview, #3236). Anything else it is asked
  during a grade is refused at once with that reason, rather than waiting and failing. A Stop ends
  a Grader's question promptly while purlis is writing to it. A Grader whose id is over 64 bytes is
  refused as it is declared, so none of its grades is lost from the record.
- **A `git` variable set on the line turns the clone guard's sparse-checkout reading off.** Any
  `GIT_*` assignment or export on the line now counts as configuration: the paths a sparse
  checkout leaves out are counted again (qw387).
- **`purlis workspace use` and `create --use` say when nothing was selected.** Where the plane's
  state folder refuses the pointer, the command fails and says so, instead of announcing a
  selection that was not kept (qw387).
- **Open file on a harness declaration works with a terminal editor.** Settings opens the
  declaration in a shell tab at the project root when `$VISUAL` or `$EDITOR` is a terminal
  editor, as a branch's file opens (#1044).
- **A dispatch waiting on your answer is recorded when the chat that asked closes.** Before, it
  was dropped without a trace. Its dispatch record now ends failed, as a task that did not
  start, and says its chat closed before you answered. Past tasks lists it (#1464).
- **A handoff you allow later leaves its todo too.** A handoff to another persona waits for
  your Allow, and the command that asked has returned by then, so its todo was never written
  in the workspace the work moved to. The app now writes it when you allow, as the command
  does for a handoff that opens at once. If the todo or the handoff's row in the dispatch log
  cannot be written, the chat that asked is told with the rest of what it hears (#1471).
- **A helper's permission prompt stays on its chat until that helper moves on.** When a
  background helper asked and the main agent kept working, the main agent's own tools coming
  back took the chat out of "waiting on you" while the helper's prompt was still open. Now only
  the chat's own prompt is answered by its own tools; a helper's prompt goes when that helper's
  own tools show it was answered in the pane, when it is answered in the window, when that
  helper ends, or when the turn ends (#1644).
- **Only the chat's own harness run can say its prompt was answered in the pane.** A tool line
  from another harness started inside the chat, or from a job it left running, no longer takes
  the chat (or a helper of it) out of "waiting on you" (#1601).
- **A host refused by Claude Code's sandbox proxy now raises the chat's block Notice.** Claude
  Code reports a refused connection as `deny network-outbound host:443 (reason)`, and purlis read
  only the other shape of violation line, so no host it refused ever showed a Notice or an Allow,
  and `purlis doctor` counted none. Now each host refused in one command gets its own block,
  naming the host to allow. A lookup the sandbox refused to a program that resolves its host
  itself (psql's "could not translate host name", curl's "Could not resolve host") and a refused
  Docker socket now raise a Notice too, saying why no grant would help and offering to start the
  chat without the sandbox. The chat is also told, in the turn it was blocked, that the person
  has a Notice, and to say what was blocked and wait instead of working around it (#1631).
- **A host Notice says how many more hosts were refused.** A wrapped chat's proxy names the first
  eight hosts it refuses; past them it counts, and the chat's host Notice now says how many more
  there were, and that no Allow on it reaches them, so a ninth host is never hidden (#1353).
- **A Smart close's "tab stayed open" notice no longer comes back on a later chat.** When the
  tab closed another way, its chat stayed on the list until the window reloaded, and a new chat
  given the same number drew the notice again (#1361).
- **A key typed into a large page is held in words, never failed unknown.** While you drive a
  chat's browser, a key into a field of a very large page that takes the browser long to read
  is held back with a note saying so, and the read goes on, so the key typed again reaches the
  field (#3043).
- **Typing beside a rotating advert stays quick.** While you drive a chat's browser, a key into a
  field reads the page at most once, and not at all while the field keeps the focus, however
  often another frame of the page reloads (#2974).
- **A keychain item written again keeps its value if the write is cut short.** purlis deletes
  an item and makes it again so that it is held to the app. A spare copy now holds the value
  until the new item is made, so a write that is refused or interrupted leaves the value in the
  keychain (#1309).
- **Two writes to one keyring vault never lose each other's secret.** A `secret set`, a
  `secret delete` and the move of an item under purlis's access rule now take the vault's own
  lock, so a write that lands while another is in progress, or while an item is being moved,
  waits for it instead of being overwritten with an older value. The wait is bounded: a writer
  still held up after ten seconds is refused and writes nothing (#1180).
- **A launch no longer waits for its chats to start.** With many chats to put back, across
  several projects, the window could take minutes to be usable: every chat was started before
  it. Now each chat has its tab in its place at once, marked as restoring, and the chats start
  behind the window, a few at a time, the one in front first. One that does not start is listed
  with its reason and Retry now, as before, and holds up no other.
- **A definite refusal no longer offers a longer wait.** A code send refused before its time, or a cluster add refused after a long wait, says why, and offers more time only where the wait itself ran out (#4398).
- **A pool's page now uses the answer wait you set** when it asks a runner about its profiles (#4397).
- **A pool with its own CPU, memory, process or `/tmp` limits now links to its runner.** purlis read a kept runner back with the default limits, so it refused the runner it had just made (#4286).
- **A limit's row shows what was saved** even if reading the limits again fails (#4390).
- **`purlis plugin install` and `purlis doctor` find the plugin a Linux package ships.** They
  look in `/usr/lib/purlis/plugin`, where the package keeps it, and still in
  `/usr/lib/charter/plugin` for a package built before the rename. purlis's requests to a forge
  carry the `purlis/<version>` user agent (#1284).
- **A long line that alternates exports or assignments with git commands is judged in time
  instead of refused for taking too long.** The project-root, clone update and project-root
  update guards gave every git on a line its own copy of everything the line had exported and
  assigned before it, so such a line cost the square of its length: at the size cap one took
  several seconds, past the guard's two-second budget, and was refused. The gits on a line now
  share that environment, the verdicts are the same, and the time grows with the line (#2648).
- **A long-running task's last note survives an app restart.** After a restart,
  `purlis dispatch list` said "no note yet" for a long-running task until it sent another note.
  It now reads the task's last note from its dispatch record: when it was sent and, where the
  record kept them, its words (#3956).
- **A merged task's folder that holds git state of its own is no longer taken away by itself.**
  A ref only that folder has (`refs/worktree/…`, a bisect or a rebase in progress), its own
  `config.worktree`, and a commit only its HEAD's history holds (made, then amended or reset
  away) go with the folder when git removes it, and nothing else counted them. Such a folder
  now stays, listed with Discard (#1472).
- **A chat says it moved when its move went ahead after a sign-in.** A short "Moved to pool" line
  stays on the moved chat's pane until you dismiss it (#4135).
- **Try the move and Cancel move no longer seem to do nothing.** When purlis no longer holds a move,
  its notice now goes away (#4138).
- **A memory's Move says when a LIVE workspace's journal will publish it.** A move into a LIVE
  workspace's journal is published with the project, as a move into a persona's or shared memory
  is. The memory tab's Move help now names the LIVE workspaces among its stores, and a row's
  *Move to* submenu says it on that workspace's row. A move into a LOCAL workspace's journal
  says nothing of the kind. The Undo after a Move or a Delete is disabled while it is on its way,
  so a second press sends nothing (#1190).
- **A local project moved out of the config home keeps its sandbox grants.** The move now
  points each folder you let chats write, each folder you listed as one chats may be granted,
  and their records in the Granted list at the same folder in the new place. Only a folder in
  the project is pointed, step for step, and never one reached through a link there: such a
  grant is left as it was, and the link at the old place is kept. While that link is kept, the
  doctor's `local project` row says why in the window, not only in the app's log (#1698).
- **A task's record follows the local project to its new place.** When purlis moves the local
  project out of its config folder, a task record that named a folder in the old place by its
  whole path now names it in the new place, as the record of open chats already did. Before, the
  task read as working in a folder that was gone (#1698).
- **A pane's Notice that grants something waits a moment after it moves.** When a Notice above
  it was answered and went, the next one's Allow could slide under the pointer. A press then
  does nothing and says so, as it already did in the Inbox (#1700).
- **A view moved between its sidebar and the Panel keeps what it held.** Moving a view no longer
  draws it again from scratch, so a query you typed, a list you scrolled or a box you ticked in
  it is still there (#1752).
- **The palette's Show or Hide the Panel row matches what is on screen.** A half of the Panel
  holding only an extension's panel that is not contributed now no longer counts as the Panel
  shown (#1752).
- **Undoing a memory's Move puts it back under its exact name.** A workspace memory moved to a
  persona or shared memory and back by Undo now has its first name again to the second. Before,
  the seconds of its name came back as `00`, because the memory's stamp line holds only the
  minute (#1190).
- **A tab in a narrow centre column keeps its title.** Where the centre is at its narrowest (both
  sidebars open or dragged wide, or a bigger text size), a tab drawn at its floor gives up its
  task chip before its title, so its name and `×` stay inside the tab and "N more" still reaches
  the rest. The chip comes back once there is room (#1867).
- **A host allowed already no longer offers Allow buttons that do nothing.** Its Notice says the
  host is allowed and that this chat takes it once it restarts, with Restart this chat. An Allow
  pressed for a host allowed already now closes the Notice and says why.
- **A notice card hung from a title-bar chip follows the chip when the strip scrolls, even on a
  busy machine.** In the macOS and Linux app, a scroll of the pinned workspaces could leave the
  card where the chip had been, off to one side, until something else moved it (#4026).
- **An action that opens a page answers with the page's address.** A link that opens a new page
  is settled once that page has its address, so the answer names where it went instead of an
  empty one.
- **A page settles after a frame of it goes.** When a frame is removed while something it asked
  for is still loading, a chat's browser stops counting that load and waits only a quiet while
  from the frame's removal, rather than its whole settling time (#2841).
- **A Notice on a narrow pane is readable, and stays inside its pane.** With two panes side by
  side, a Notice's sentence was squeezed to one word a line, its buttons were broken over
  several lines, and what a button opened was drawn beside the Notice and off the window. The
  sentence now has the row, the buttons go under it when they do not fit beside it, and what a
  button opens is under them at the same width. Several Notices stack and scroll inside the
  pane. A dialog is drawn over a pane's Notices, and the window is no longer scrolled sideways
  by one (#1481).
- **Ask {persona}'s box for what to ask is as wide as the dialog**, the dialog fits a narrow
  window, and its buttons stay at its bottom edge while the form scrolls (#1481).
- **A paste in a chat no longer quits purlis on macOS.** When macOS raised an error of its own
  while it handled a key (seen on Cmd+V under macOS 27), purlis quit with "purlis quit
  unexpectedly". macOS now reports the error and purlis keeps running. A fault in purlis itself
  still ends the app, as before.
- **The explorer says when a branch's folders are not watched, and watches them again.** When
  purlis's reader had paused a branch (its reads kept running past their time or memory) or had
  no answer for it, the folders you opened in it were left unwatched with nothing said, so the
  tree looked live but never moved. The tree now says "Changes on disk are not shown yet" on the
  branch's topmost open folder, asks for the branch again once the pause is over, and reads the
  folders again once they are watched (#1727).
- **"Start a chat here" no longer holds the window while the reader is busy.** Finding the
  branch's folder could wait on a busy reader for two of its deadlines, on the thread that draws
  the window. It now waits off it (#1727).
- **The branch cockpit follows a checkout in its folder after a failed look-up.** A look-up of
  the cockpit's refs that failed unexpectedly left its folder marked as being looked up, so
  later checkouts there were not followed (#1152).
- **A persona's MCP server no longer fails at random as its chat starts.** A credentialed server
  that asked for its run before the app had finished recording the chat as started was refused,
  and Claude Code reported it as closed (`CONNECTION_CLOSED`) for the life of the chat; it
  happened most when several chats started together. The app now waits for a chat that is still
  starting (qw381).
- **An update leaves behind the commits of the base a piece was cut from that its new base
  lacks.** A piece cut from a clone's `main` that held commits its remote never took no longer
  carries them onto `origin/main` when it is updated: only its own commits move (#3836).
- **A Docker command run down a pipe gets its Allow.** When a sandboxed chat ran
  `docker run … 2>&1 | tail` and the sandbox refused Docker its socket, the Notice said "The
  sandbox did not say which socket it refused" and offered only *Start without the sandbox*.
  The pipe ended with `tail`'s status, so the command did not count as failed, and a socket was
  named only from a failed command. A line that runs `docker`, `docker-compose`, `podman`,
  `podman-compose` or `nerdctl` now names the socket its output says it was refused, so the
  Notice shows the socket and offers *Allow once*, *Allow for this chat* and *Always allow*.
  What a line that only reads printed (`cat` of a log, `git show`) still names no socket.
- **A certificate check refused down a pipe gets its own Notice.** When a sandboxed chat ran
  `gh pr list … 2>&1 | head` and the sandbox refused `gh` the system's certificate check, the
  Notice said "The sandbox did not say which system service it refused" and offered only
  *Start without the sandbox*. The pipe ended with `head`'s status, so the command did not
  count as failed, and the service was named only from a failed command. The certificate check
  is one service, and its name is purlis's own, never taken from what the chat printed. So a
  line that runs a program now names it however the line ended (a pipe, `|| true`,
  `; echo $?`, and the one text Codex and opencode hand over), and the Notice says what stands
  for certificate checks in this project and the way on (they are on by default now, so there
  is nothing to allow). A line that only reads (`cat` of a log, `grep`, `git show`, a here-document's body)
  and a file a chat read still name no service.
- **A plugin install still on its old names is kept current.** After `purlis migrate --undo`, the
  app's launch refresh repoints that install when its hook binary moves, under the same old names,
  instead of skipping it. It never moves the names, so the undo stays undone (#1305).
- The form that raises a pool's limit now appears only beside a refusal that limit caused, and on
  a pool's page a profile over the pool's limits offers it too.
- **A profile on a pool says when its harness is being fetched, and answers once it is.** On a
  runner where the profile's pinned harness is not installed yet, its row says the harness is
  being fetched and asks again on its own until it can say whether the profile is signed in, so
  you no longer press Ask again (#4008).
- **A sign-in on a pool keeps its Ask while the runner cannot tell yet.** Signing a profile in on
  a pool with Open in terminal, its Ask could leave the Inbox while you were still in the browser,
  on a runner that could not tell yet or was still fetching the harness. It now stays until the
  runner says the profile is signed in, or you close that shell (#4009).
- **A pool sign-in question waits for a dialog already open.** It opens once that dialog closes, so it
  doesn't arrive on top of what you're answering (#4504).
- **A chat's several runs of a refused tool on a cluster runner ask you once.** Runs started at the
  same time now wait for the first one's answer rather than each asking. A chat started again under
  the same number no longer waits on the pace its predecessor left.
- **purlis's own lock files moved into its session host's folder.** Nothing you need to do.
- **Moving a pool to a new runner leaves nothing behind.** If a move stops after Docker made the
  new runner and before purlis kept it, the next move removes that container and its home
  volume first, then makes the runner (#2869).
- **A bad limit in the pool's file no longer stops every pool being listed** (#4381). That limit
  follows purlis's default and says why on the pool's page, and the rest keep working.
- **Settings › This machine › Pools says how each runner was really made to suspend.** A
  pool's row said "Suspends after …" from the pool's `suspendAfter`, even for a runner made
  before purlis suspended runners, which never suspends itself. The row now reads the runner's
  container: such a runner says "Never suspends: its runner was made before purlis suspended
  runners", and one made with another time than the pool's says the time it was made with
  (#3717).
- **A profile with skills reaches a pool's runner whatever its ordinary size** (#4081). Every chat
  on a pool was refused once a profile's settings passed 512 KiB, which a few skills do. A runner
  of this version takes them in several messages and keeps them all at once, or none, up to
  128 MiB and 8192 files. A skill's `node_modules`, `__pycache__` and `venv` folders stay on this
  machine. Past that the chat still starts, and its tab says which skills or files
  stayed behind and how to bring them.
- **Switching back to a project builds nothing for the four projects you were in last.** A
  project you were just in keeps its view and its chats' terminals while another is in front, so
  going back to it puts it on screen as you left it instead of building it again; what it showed
  is read again behind it. A project you have not been in for longer, or one you left with a
  dialog open, is drawn again when you come back to it, as before.
- **A prompt too long to send no longer ends an ACP chat.** A prompt over 8 MiB is refused
  before it is sent, saying it is longer than purlis sends to an agent, and the chat goes on;
  it used to end the chat as if the agent had exited (#1117).
- **On Linux, a refused file that is no longer linked is sorted by the name it had.** A
  protected file that was unlinked is told as a protected file, so its Notice offers no Allow
  (#2574).
- **`purlis secret exec` finds the 1Password CLI when purlis was started from the Dock.** In a
  sandboxed chat the app reads the vault, and an app started from the Dock is given the
  system's short `PATH`, so it answered "the 1Password CLI ('op') is not on PATH" for an `op` in
  `/opt/homebrew/bin` that the chat's own shell found. A provider's program (`op`, and `vault`
  for a reference) is now looked for where purlis already looks for a harness and a forge's
  CLI: its own `PATH`, then `~/.local/bin` and the other directories installers use under your
  home, then Homebrew's and the system's. The refusal names every directory it searched, and
  `purlis doctor` has a row for each such program a project's vaults use, saying where it was
  found and warning where only this `PATH` finds it (#1516).
- **Use the new address on a moved repo's Notice no longer leaves pushes going to the old
  address.** Where every push URL of `origin` is its old address, with the same scheme and the
  same user, it goes with `origin`, and the Notice says pushes move to the new address too. Where
  one names another repository, or the same one over SSH or as another user, every push URL is
  left as it is, and the Notice says where the repo pushes (#2117).
- **A chat put back at launch no longer waits for ever on a pool's runner.** A start nobody can
  cancel, at launch or a dispatch's, now waits at most the pool's *Longest wait for a runner's
  answer* (30 seconds unless the pool sets it). Past that, the chat says the runner did not
  answer in time, and Retry starts it on the pool's runner of that moment. One launch waited
  4 minutes on a runner older than the desktop (#4988).
- **A task question's trail says when its asking chat saw it, even after that chat was stuck.**
  A question whose 100 seconds started while its asking chat sat on a prompt or a usage limit
  now still writes `question.shown` for the turn that has it, and its time is not started again
  (#4653).
- **A question's trail is never the next question's.** When purlis has no record of a task's
  question, its "What happened" now says so, instead of showing the trail of a question the task
  asked within the next minute (#4841).
- **One window link at a time holds a window's name, and a quick restart still gets it.** The
  desktop's host refuses a second link a name another of its relayed links holds, and a window
  that restarted before its old link ended asks again a moment later. A window-names file too
  long to read is started again rather than leaving every link unnamed (#2744).
- **A close with nothing to ask no longer holds back a link's close.** Closing a tab that shows
  only tasks left its project counted as asking, so a link's close of a chat with theme drafts
  was not asked there until the next close question. The project is clear once the close is
  done (#2845).
- **Quitting while a launch is still putting chats back keeps every chat** (#3114). A chat whose
  start finished just as purlis quit could drop out of the record of open chats, and the next
  launch did not put it back. It is now kept as a chat still to start, in its place on the strip
  and in front if it was.
- **A branch whose reads run past their memory cap is paused however busy the machine is.** A
  read that ran out of time counts against its branch only when it was given at least half its
  deadline. A read that ran past its memory cap now always counts, since what it took is the
  branch's own doing (#1605).
- **A chat taken back after its project's sandbox setting changed is judged by how it was
  started.** Browser logins treat it as sandboxed or not by the session host's record of how its
  run started, and a chat with no such record is treated as sandboxed and offered a restart. A
  chat on a runner that you started without the sandbox keeps its persona's browser logins
  there (#2636).
- **A chat put back from the session host keeps the skill routing it started with** (Skill
  studio preview, #3578). A chat whose workspace or persona chose a router extension is no longer
  routed again when purlis reopens and finds it still running: its router is not asked a second
  time, and Use skill… and the Skill studio say what that router hid at the chat's start, which is
  the list the chat actually holds. A chat started again is routed anew.
- **A chat put back from the session host keeps the Skill studio setting it started with**
  (Skill studio preview, #3466). Turning the Skill studio on or off while purlis was closed no
  longer changes which project skills a chat that kept running is armed with, what its Notice
  says, or what Use skill… offers it, once it is reattached. A chat started again reads the
  setting as it is now.
- **A skill that refers to a built-in skill installs** (Skill studio preview, #4155). Where a skill
  refers to a built-in skill such as `secrets`, and its source also holds a folder of that name,
  the install brought that folder along and then refused, as no skill may take a built-in's name.
  The reference now resolves to purlis's built-in skill: nothing is brought along, the review
  says it is left as it is, and an update that newly refers to one goes ahead.
- **A skill another refers to is no longer copied where its chats have it already** (Skill
  studio preview, #4154). Installing into a workspace now leaves out a skill it refers to when a
  project skill of that name is granted to the workspace and not turned off there, and installing
  for a persona leaves out one its `skills:` list names. Before, a copy landed beside it and hid
  the project's. A local install also relies on the level's shared skills. A shared install still
  brings its own copy where only a local skill has the name, since a teammate does not have that
  one.
- **Installing a skill that refers to one installed already goes ahead** (Skill studio preview,
  #4032). A skill another one refers to (`skills:<name>`) is no longer brought along into a level
  that holds it already, where the install used to refuse with "already have it installed".
  The review says the skill it refers to is installed there already and is left as it is, and
  reads again when you pick another level. The same holds for Install all… and
  `purlis skill install`.
- **A refusal in Settings links the setting it is about, whatever its key.** The core now hands
  each standing refusal of `charter.toml`, `charter.local.toml` and a workspace's settings over
  with the key it is about, so Settings no longer reads the key out of the sentence. An
  extension whose id holds a dot (`my.ext`) now gets its link too (#1292).
- **A workspace folder that is a link is refused in its own words.** Saving a workspace's
  settings, or any other write of its `workspace.json`, used to say the workspace "was renamed
  or removed" when its folder is a link to another folder. It now says that the folder is a
  link, and that purlis writes `workspace.json` only in a real folder. The link is never
  followed (#1292).
- **A handed-off chat that comes back with no conversation is no longer started blank.** When
  purlis relaunches a handed-off chat whose harness never named a conversation, the chat now
  gets the same first message as Start fresh: its brief again, or why purlis could not hand it
  and where the person can read it (#1609).
- **A task put back by a launch says its age again.** The list of a chat's tasks says how long
  each has been at work from its dispatch's record, where a relaunch left it saying nothing
  (#1463).
- **A workspace removal no longer claims a reset it could not make.** Where purlis could not
  write the new selection after removing the workspace you were on, it now says so and exits
  with a failure, instead of "Active workspace reset to …" (#2103).
- **A window forgets its focus on a branch that was removed.** Once the workspace's branches have
  been listed without it, the window stops remembering the branch it was focused on, so the next
  launch does not try to put it back. While the branches are still being listed, or when listing
  them failed, the focus is kept (#1152).
- **Chats of a runner that is gone say they ended.** After **Make the runner again**, or once a draining
  runner removed outside purlis is forgotten, its chats no longer stay dimmed as if they would come
  back (#4168).
- **A file moved out of a folder marks that folder.** In the explorer's change markers, a file
  renamed out of `src/` now marks `src/` as having lost a file, as well as the folders it moved
  into (#1130).
- **Renaming an ignored folder that holds a file you added with `git add -f` updates a branch's
  change marks.** The rename was taken for a change to ignored files only, so the explorer's
  marks waited for the next full read (#874).
- **Renaming a workspace keeps the links to its todos.** A chat linked to one of the workspace's
  todos still reaches it under the new name: `purlis workspace rename` writes a `renamed` alias
  for each todo key a work link names, and a rename finished after an interruption writes each
  alias once. Renaming a workspace back to a name it had says which links stay under the name it
  left (#887).
- **A reopened task is held to its profile's rules each time it is started again**, not only
  at the Reopen. When purlis is opened again, and on Restart chat, a finished task you
  reopened is no longer started on a profile the project has stopped listing for its persona,
  or on one whose command has come to switch the harness's permission prompts off (#1543).
- **A task that reported while it still runs can be told and cancelled.** When purlis made a
  task's report from its last message, or the task reported `blocked`, its program kept running
  but `dispatch tell` and `dispatch cancel` were refused as if it had finished. Such a task is
  now listed as "reported, still running" in `dispatch list` and in the open-tasks roster, and
  `tell`, `cancel`, `note`, `ask` and `answer` all reach it. A cancel that gets no new report
  keeps the earlier one and ends the task's program. Once the program has ended, the "has
  finished" refusal applies as before (#3899).
- **A repo's own folder is compared with the upstream git uses.** Its change markers and how far
  it is ahead or behind now follow the remote's fetch refspec, as `@{upstream}` does, so a remote
  fetched under another name is still the base. A branch no refspec maps has no base, as before
  (#1130).
- **A window that restarts takes back its chats on a pool's runners.** A chat on the pool's runner,
