  or on an old runner being replaced, comes back in its tab, and ending it lets the old runner go.
  This needs a runner of this version or later. The Away summary also reads the old runner's record
  of finished chats (#4271).
- **A restart, a move or a save waits for a chat's own work.** A chat waiting on its own
  monitors or background shells is no longer at a pause between turns: the restart a sandbox
  Allow owes, a move between runners and a repo save wait until that work has woken it and its
  turn ends, and Restart chat on its tab says it restarts when the turn ends. Restart now still
  restarts it at once (#3887).
- **A chat that comes back under a new number at launch keeps its tab.** The tab stays pinned, in
  its place, with its split, and now shows the chat under its new number. Before, the window
  closed the tab and opened a new one at the end of the strip, unpinned (#4962).
- **The palette's row for a chat that needs you lands the keyboard on the task's row.** A failed
  task's row it brings into view in the Chats list takes the keyboard once the palette closes,
  so Enter opens its report, as the title bar's list used to (#1695).
- **A chat no longer stops on a permission prompt around its own tasks.** A call whose every
  dispatch only looks (`list`, `read`, `wait`, `--help`) is left to the harness's own rules
  whatever stands beside it, so `purlis dispatch list 2>&1 | head -20` no longer asks, unless a
  redirection on the line writes a file. A dispatch that writes, a handoff or a worktree commit
  that shares its call with another command is now refused with the shape to retry ("run the
  dispatch in a call of its own") instead of asking the person. `purlis dispatch close` no longer
  prompts in a Claude Code chat, and `purlis dispatch cancel` is refused for a task the person
  has typed in, as `close` already was (#3785).
- **A router's grade purlis stopped under is recorded as interrupted.** A crash, a fault or a quit
  while a router's grade ran used to lose it, and nothing said it ran. It is now held while it
  runs, as a skill's grade is, and the project's next start records it as interrupted with what
  its chats spent, so the studio's router line says so (#3616).
- **A chat the runner starts by its names is asked about a service you allowed it alone.** When
  the runner's own sandbox does not give that service, the chat's tab says the runner left it
  out. When the chat reaches for it there, you are asked about the runner's service, and
  allowing it, once or for this chat, lets that chat reach it on that runner (#2590).
- **A persona's tools now work in a chat on a runner.** A runner never had your Allow of a
  persona's tools, so it armed none of them and their commands were refused there. A chat's start
  now carries what you allowed on your desktop, and the runner arms those tools while its copy of
  the persona matches. It never gets the persona's hosts this way, and every run still asks you
  (#4071).
- **A chat on a runner starts even when you allowed it a service on this machine alone.** The
  runner starts it without that service, and the chat's tab says so. When the chat reaches for
  it there, you are asked about the runner's service, and allowing it, once or for this chat,
  lets that chat reach it on that runner (#2510).
- **A chat on a runner shows up in the Skill studio's runs, and gets the same skills** (Skill
  studio preview, #3084). A chat running on a Docker or Kubernetes pool logged its skill runs on
  the runner, where the studio never saw them, and with the preview on it could start without the
  project's skills. Its runs are now logged on your desktop with the persona, harness and
  workspace it ran in, and the runner gives it the same project skills a chat here gets.
- **Cancel ends a sign-in on the runner too** (#4043). A cancelled, retried or timed-out sign-in
  used to run on inside the container until it stopped by itself. It now ends there at once.
- **A runner's browser stays watchable over the link while it is also watched on the runner.**
  A view on the runner's own host no longer widens the frames sent to your window past the
  link's 1280 pixels, which the window would drop as too wide (#3297).
- **When a pool's runner cannot start a browser safely, the notice says which runner.** The
  notice about the browser engine's sandbox now names the pool whose runner refused, and its
  command is the one to run on that runner, not on your own machine. Your own machine's notice
  is unchanged and can stand beside it, and the chat is told a browser is not available on that
  runner (#2990).
- **A chat on a pool stays yours when Runs on changes.** After a window restart it's found on the
  pool it runs on, its branches come back from there and stay in Changes, and that pool is sent no
  code until a chat starts or moves there again (#4590).
- **A sandboxed chat can no longer leave a clone or a branch folder half-updated.** A chat's
  sandbox never lets it write the files a later program loads code from (`.vscode/`,
  `.husky/`, `.claude/settings.json`, `.mcp.json`, `.envrc` and the like), in any folder, and
  many repositories track one. A `git pull`, `rebase`, `merge` or `reset --hard` whose other
  commit changed such a file wrote every other file and failed; a `git checkout` or `switch`
  did the same and reported success, with that file left behind as if the chat had changed
  it. Before such a command runs, purlis now asks git which files it would write and refuses
  only one that would write a file the sandbox denies. The refusal names the files and says
  the person runs the command in their own terminal. A move that touches none of them runs
  as before.
- **`git pull` in a repository that tracks such files is told to fetch first.** A pull
  fetches the commit it moves to, so it cannot be checked before it runs. In a repository
  that tracks one of those files the refusal says to run `git fetch`, then `git merge
  --ff-only @{u}` or `git rebase @{u}`, each as a command of its own, which purlis checks.
  A move with a command that may write before it on the same line (`git fetch && git rebase
  origin/main`, `gh pr checkout 7 && git merge main`) is told to run as a command of its
  own. In a repository that tracks none of them, nothing changes.
- **A `git clone` of a repository on this machine that tracks such files is refused up
  front**, with `purlis clone <repo>` (the app makes the clone, whole) and the person's
  terminal as the ways through. A clone from a URL cannot be asked before it is fetched.
  A checkout in a folder cloned with `--no-checkout` is refused the same way, since it
  writes the whole tree.
- **A chat is told when git stopped partway all the same.** After a git command that said it
  could not write one of those files, the chat is told in that turn that the folder is
  half-updated, not to commit from it, and the command that puts it back or finishes it.
- **A long line of `cd <folder> && git …;` no longer makes the Bash guard slow.** Every git
  on a line is read against each folder the shell may be in, and each such `cd` left one
  more, a level deeper, which the guard then asked the disk about again for every git: a
  16 KB line of them took the project-root guards 27 seconds. Each folder is now asked
  about once for the line, and past 64 folders, or 8 KiB of their names, none is spelt: a
  git there is one the guard cannot place, which it refuses as it would in the root.
- **A sandboxed chat can no longer leave the project half-updated.** A chat's sandbox never
  lets it write the project's manifest or the folders a later program loads code from, and git
  writes a tree file by file, skipping what it may not. So `git rebase origin/main` or `git
  pull` from a sandboxed chat at the project's root left most files as the remote has them and
  the rest, and the current commit, as they were, with nothing to say an update was tried. A
  chat's git that rewrites the root's working tree from another commit (`pull`, `rebase`,
  `merge`, `cherry-pick`, `revert`, `am`, `stash pop` and `apply`, `bisect`, a hard reset to
  another commit, a checkout of a branch the root is not on) is now refused before it starts,
  and the refusal says to ask the person to update the project. `purlis save` and `purlis save
  --pull` from such a chat bring nothing in where they would stop partway, and say which files
  are in the way; the window's own save is unchanged.
- **The way back from a half-updated project is open.** Restoring files to the current commit
  (`git restore --source=HEAD --worktree -- <paths>`, `git checkout HEAD -- <paths>`, `git
  reset --hard HEAD`, `--abort` of a rebase or merge) is never refused by that check. One that
  names a file the sandbox denies is refused up front and prints the `git restore` command for
  the person's terminal. `git checkout HEAD` with its paths in a file or from `xargs`, which
  the guard reads as a branch move, now says so and names the `git restore` spelling that is
  allowed.
- **A sandboxed chat says why it runs at its level, and where to change it.** The sandbox mark and a
  block's Notice now name the reason (the level you chose, a persona's row, a level waiting for
  Confirm, a policy, or a stricter chat that asked for it) and Settings › Project › Sandbox › Your
  level. Where you changed your level after the chat started, they say a restart
  applies it. The chat is told your level is yours alone, and to ask you for the reason shown rather
  than guess (#5207).
- **A request-mode save no longer blocks for good after the plane's history is rewritten.** When
  the save branch on the remote holds only commits the plane already has under new shas (the same
  changes, rewritten with new dates), the save pushes over it instead of saying it "has commits
  this clone did not push there". A commit on it that the plane does not have still blocks the
  save.
- **A save's pull request is never merged while it is red, or before its checks could run.** In
  `pr-merge`, purlis read the checks once, straight after it opened the pull request, and took
  "no check yet" for "no check": it merged, and CI then failed on a pull request already
  merged. Where the repository had auto-merge, a failing check that the branch did not require
  merged too. Now purlis merges the pull request itself, on every forge and whatever the
  repository's settings are, and only once it has read every check on the pushed commit as
  passed. A save merges nothing: purlis looks again by itself, a minute after the push and
  then every few minutes, so a pull request that goes green is merged without you saving
  again. With no check at all it is merged once the commit has been there a minute and nothing
  shows the repository runs checks on its pull requests.
- **A save says when it could not record how its push went.** Where the plane's push record could
  not be written or cleared (a full disk, say), `purlis save` now warns that the saving status may
  show the plane as it was until the next save, where it used to say nothing (#1144).
- **A saved grade chat is read as text.** A screen reader walks what the chat showed line by line
  instead of hearing only its name; the screen is one Tab stop that says it takes no input, ⌘F
  finds in it, and ⌘A then ⌘C copies it. The theme specimen's terminals are read the same way
  (#3676).
- **A page a script retitles is listed under its new title.** Listing a chat's browser's pages
  reads each page's title from the page itself, where Chrome did not always say it had changed
  (#2753).
- **A second prompt is its own wait.** A chat you answered in its own pane that asks again
  before it moves on now counts as waiting on a new prompt: a line you put away for the first
  prompt shows again for the second (#2098).
- **Another purlis with a config home of its own has a session host of its own.** A second
  purlis on the same device that names its own config home, such as a development build beside
  the installed one, starts a session host of its own and runs its chats there (#2114).
- **A `secret exec` run from a chat in the session host no longer waits forever now and then.**
  When the command's input arrived, or ended, before the window had started the command, the
  window lost it, and the command waited for input that never came. Piped input, which ends at
  once, hit this most. The window now keeps that input for the command, up to 64 KiB, and input
  with no reader is not kept: none outlives its command or the window's link to the session
  host (#2271).
- **A message that could not be queued points to purlis's dispatch tools only where they
  queue.** Under Codex and opencode, whose sandbox holds purlis's tools too, the command and the
  tools say to send it again once the app answers (#3914).
- **A server that did not start is said as one.** A sandboxed chat's server refused with no port
  you could allow was shown as a block of a system folder. It is now shown as a server the chat
  started, which did not start (#3440).
- **A test server on a port the system picks gets a Notice.** A test suite that starts its
  servers on port 0 (Go's `httptest`, Node bound to port 0, or any program whose refusal the
  sandbox reports, Python's among them in a Claude Code chat) was refused with no Notice at all. Its Notice now says there is no one port to allow, how to start the server on a port of
  its own (`purlis listen 3000 -- <command>`), and offers Start without the sandbox for tests
  that pick their own ports (#3396).
- **A server that did not start on Linux says why.** Where purlis's Linux sandbox could not take
  a chat server's socket, because the machine refuses the call that takes it (a runner added by
  an older purlis, or a runner on Kubernetes), the Notice now says so and what to do: remove the
  runner and add it again, or start the chat without the sandbox. A runner on Kubernetes cannot
  be given that call yet (#3440).
- **No notification for a task that finished.** A system notification is sent when a chat
  itself comes to need you, and no longer each time one of its tasks reports or each time a
  chat that already needs you moves (#1491).
- **Saving settings reads the project's settings file as a chat's start reads it.** A file past
  1 MiB is refused with a sentence instead of read whole under the project's lock, and a save of
  the machine-only file reads the shared one with no link followed and without waiting on it
  (#1100).
- **A folder that a chat and its tasks' tasks share is warned about once.** When a chat asked
  for tasks and one of them asked for tasks of its own, all in one folder, the chat's pane said
  the same "tasks share a folder" warning twice: once for the chat and once for its task. It is
  now said once, on the chat highest up that asked for a task there (#1645).
- **A sign-in on this machine keeps its Ask while the harness cannot tell.** Its Ask could leave
  the Inbox while you were still signing in. It now stays until the harness says the profile is
  signed in, or you leave that sign-in, as a sign-in on a pool does (#4223).
- **Leaving a sign-in is seen when the shell's program ends.** Running `exit` in the shell now ends
  the watch and puts the Ask away, as closing its tab does (#4202).
- **An Ask raised just after you left a sign-in stays.** A chat refused in that moment keeps its
  Ask rather than losing it to the sign-in you had left (#4203).
- **Every project's window hears of a sign-in on a pool.** Another open project no longer keeps
  drawing an Ask that has already gone (#4205).
- **A skill delete cut short by a crash or a quit is finished** (Skill studio preview, #3013).
  If purlis stopped after deleting a committed skill and before saving that, the skill was gone
  from the Skill studio and from Restore until the next save, and every later delete was kept on
  this machine instead of saved. Now the Skill studio, or the next `purlis skill` change, finishes
  the delete in one commit, so Restore brings it back from there. If the project cannot save it
  then, the skill is put back. A Notice says which, and if neither works it says so as trouble
  and tries again the next time.
- In the Skill studio's Library, a skill purlis hands to no chat now says why under its name and is marked Left out. It used to show its own description and count as on.
- **A small field is never under the 24px target size in the compact density.** A small search
  box, filter, select or suggestions box, beside a small button in a compact row, is at least
  24px tall at any text size, as a small button is (WCAG 2.5.8, #3250).
- **A chat can move a sparse clone that leaves the editor's and agents' files out.** The guard
  on `git checkout`, `reset --hard`, `merge`, `rebase` and `pull` in a clone or a branch folder
  counts only the files git will write: a file the sparse checkout leaves out is not one
  (qw387).
- **`git rebase <upstream> 2>&1 | tail -5` in a clone is judged as `git rebase <upstream>`.** The
  shell's redirections are no longer read as git's words, so a move that names one commit and
  touches no denied file runs however its output is sent (qw387).
- **A hook line written while purlis was reading the spool is no longer thrown away.** When
  purlis is not there to take a hook's line, the hook keeps it in the chat's spool, and purlis
  records it the next time the project is opened. Purlis used to forget how to check a chat's
  lines as soon as it had read the spool once. So a line a hook was still writing at that
  moment, and every line from a hook that was still running afterwards, was rejected at the
  next open and its content was never recorded. Purlis now keeps what it needs to check a
  chat's lines, and the number of the last line it recorded, until the chat is closed or the
  project is opened without it. A late line is recorded at the next open, a line that is put
  back after it was recorded is rejected as repeated, and an open that stopped part-way no
  longer reports the lines it had already recorded as missing. A chat's spool is also read
  when the chat is closed or restarted, so nothing waits for the next open (#983).
- **A task's branch that was squash-merged reads as merged.** purlis used to keep its folder
  until you discarded it, because git finds none of its commits in the branch it was cut from.
  Where every file the branch changed reads there as the branch has it, its folder is taken
  away as a merged one's is; the branch itself stays, since it is the one place its commits
  are (#1472).
- **A start while a pool's runner is still fetching says to sign in on the pool.** If the runner found
  the profile signed out, the start told you to sign in on this machine, which signed in the wrong
  one. It now names the pool and Sign in on pool, with the pool's own Inbox wait (#4233).
- **A start put aside at once leaves nothing in the event log** (#2252). A sandboxed Claude Code
  chat started once more at its start writes the sandbox coming back on once, for the start
  that goes on, and what the program of the start put aside still sends is recorded with no run.
- **A grade purlis stopped under says what its chats spent** (#3582). A grade that a crash, a
  fault or a quit interrupted used to be recorded as having spent nothing. Its record now says
  how many chats ran and the tokens and cost they reported before it stopped.
- **A grade's chat is never listed as needing you** (#3583). A chat that a grade runs is shown
  nowhere, but until the grade ended it at its first question it could briefly appear in the
  needs-you list and the away summary's count. It no longer does.
- **Stopping a search in files stops it at once.** ⌘⇧F's listing of a branch's files now hears
  Stop, so a branch whose ignore file holds git's listing no longer keeps the search running
  until git's 30-second deadline (#1137).
- **A pool sign-in that purlis had to stop says why.** The strip gives the stop's reason however the stop
  falls, and offers Try again rather than the page. A profile that signed in just as its sign-in stopped no
  longer leaves its pool's waits standing (#4367).
- **The word that a task was stopped always reaches the chat that asked for it.** Where the
  branch it names was not one purlis would have cut, the whole word was dropped, and the asking
  chat never heard that its task ended. Now only the branch line is left out (#1472).
- **A sub-agent's run now ends in the event log.** A child run gets a `run.ended` when its
  `SubagentStop` is heard (`completed`, `child-ended`), and otherwise when its parent's run
  ends, in the parent's end state and cause, where before it was only forgotten (#1084).
- **The keyboard goes back where it was after a submenu pick or a row's menu, inside a dialog
  too.** A row picked in a submenu now hands the keyboard back to the menu's trigger, and a menu
  opened on a list's row hands it back to that row, the moment the menu goes. Before, in a dialog
  opened less than half a second earlier, the dialog could take the keyboard instead (#3642).
- **A submenu's row runs on the first press.** A submenu opened by a screen reader's press, or
  by any press that is not the pointer's, before its menu had taken the keyboard, stays open
  with the keyboard in it, as the tab chip's *End a task* does (#3074).
- **A reader of the event log whose place is past its end is told so.** After a power loss took
  lines it had already read, it gets an `ahead` marker and every event written after, where it
  used to skip the new events that reused those numbers (#941).
- **A theme reaches a switcher row's count, and the title bar's controls are held where they
  are drawn** (#3947, #3949). A switcher row's waiting count is now `titlebar.row-count`, apart
  from a chip's `titlebar.count`, so a theme colours it. The crumb, the ⌄, and a switcher's rows
  and pins are checked against their contrast floors on the ground each is drawn on, under the
  pointer, open or pinned; one whose colours a theme set too faint draws its own default back,
  and no longer takes the workspace chips' colours with it.
- **A screen reader counts only tabs on the tab strips.** The projects, workspaces and chat-tab
  strips announced their `×`, settings gears and `+` buttons as members of the tab list, so the
  count was wrong and the list held items that are not tabs. Each strip's tab list now holds its
  tabs only. The buttons stay where they were and work as before (#1204).
- **A worktree cut for a task by an app that quit before the task started is listed.** The
  task's record is now written before its worktree is cut, so the project's next open settles it
  and takes away a worktree nothing was written in (#1472).
- **A task no longer stops to ask before reading where it works.** A Claude Code chat purlis
  starts, a task included, now runs `purlis persona where` without asking, as it already ran
  the `persona_where` tool. A task whose brief read its own place stopped on a permission prompt
  in a tab nobody was looking at.
- **A task stopped on a permission prompt is said where you are.** Its session's tab wears the
  hand from the moment the prompt is held, the session's pane names the task and what it asks,
  with **Show the task**, while purlis holds the prompt (up to a minute), and the chat that asked
  for it is told once, at its next turn, that the task waits on you. You answer it in the task's own tab, as before; purlis answers nothing for
  you.
- **A task stopped on a prompt stays said until it goes on.** The Notice on its session's pane
  no longer goes after about a minute, when purlis stops holding the prompt and the task's own
  pane asks it. It stays until you answer the prompt, its turn ends or the task ends, so you
  still see it when you come back later. It no longer says what the prompt asks after that
  first minute. A chat whose name has "(a task of" in it no longer gets **Show the task** on
  its Notice when it is not a task (#1601).
- **A task that reports done while its own monitors or background shells still run is no longer
  ended under them.** Its program is ended once that work has ended and its turn ends with
  nothing in flight. The two minutes a reporting turn is given run from when that work ends, and
  a cancel still stops the task and its work at once (#3921).
- **The explorer's Merge and Remove read the dispatch store as `purlis worktree remove` does.**
  A dispatch record that does not read now keeps the explorer off the branch folder its text
  names, and the refusal names that record's file; a branch folder's name matches without
  regard to case. A record cut off before it names its folder keeps every folder of the repo it
  names, in the window and from a terminal (#1534).
- **A dispatch record's interrupted write no longer leaves a copy of the brief behind for
  good.** The temporary file is collected with the records, 30 days after it was written
  (#1452).
- **On macOS the window stops asking once the command that asked has ended.** When you stopped
  `purlis profile sign-in --pool` while the window asked you to confirm it, the window kept
  asking until its two minutes ran out, because macOS refuses the way purlis checked whether the
  command was still there. It now closes the question once the command is gone, as it does
  on Linux.
- **An extension's theme name is held to a label's rule.** A colour or icon theme whose `name`
  is longer than 40 bytes or holds a control or invisible formatting character is left out, and
  the extension's other contributions still work. The approval and the extension's row in
  Extensions name the theme left out by its place, never by the name, as a view's or an
  action's title is. An extension that contributes nothing else is refused with that reason. A
  project's `[theme]` pick of such a name is not a pick (#1145).
- **A memory's title is one line for every reader.** The line and paragraph separators
  (U+2028, U+2029) and the direction overrides are folded to a space wherever a title is
  written, as a newline already was, and a chat's brokered write of a title holding one is
  refused (#1408).
- **A 1Password token is not stored where purlis finds no `op`.** It used to be kept with no
  program pinned, so the vault looked set up and every read was then refused until the token
  was given again. Storing it now says purlis could not find the 1Password CLI, names every
  directory it searched, and keeps nothing (#1517).
- **A token given while purlis moves its keychain items to the app leaves no old item behind.**
  Storing or replacing a vault's token, and the move of its items to the app's own keychain
  access after the rename, now take turns on the vault's keys. A token replaced during the move
  no longer had its old item written back with nothing referring to it (#1180).
- **A persona's tool that wasn't allowed says so when its program is missing from a runner's image.** It
  now gets the sentence naming the program and the image, not a shell's `command not found` (#4373).
- **A tool declared under another name runs on macOS.** A vault tool whose declared name differs
  from its program's file name (`gzcat` for `gunzip`) failed to start through the app's sandbox on
  macOS with "Operation not permitted". purlis now starts the tool through a link the
  sandbox lets it read (#2617).
- **A persona's tool declared through a link does what its declared name says.** A tool runs
  the program its links resolve to, and that program now starts under the name the tool was
  declared as. A tool `unxz`, whose link resolves to `xz`, unpacks again instead of packing,
  and the same goes for `gunzip` and `git-*` links. Which program runs and which credential it
  is handed are unchanged (#1977).
- **A chat's open tasks at every turn include the ones a restart orphaned that only their
  dispatch records know.** The roster purlis adds to each turn named a task orphaned by a
  restart only where a launch had tried to start it again. A task with no chat open, coming back
  or waiting to start was named only when the task list was asked for. The roster now names it
  too, without a chat number, since the one it had may belong to another chat. purlis reads the
  dispatch records for this once after a launch and again only after one changes, not at every
  turn (#3932).
- **Allowing a vault answers about "the chat", not "this chat".** The refused-vault Notice can
  be drawn for a chat that is not the one on screen, such as a task's, and its answer after
  Allow now says "The chat is told to run the command again" or "Ask the chat to run the
  command again" (#1538).
- **A sandboxed chat lists a vault's key names through the app.** `purlis secret list <vault>`
  in a sandboxed chat is answered by the app for a vault the chat's persona may use, so after
  you press Allow on a vault's notice the chat's listing works instead of failing on the vault
  file. The chat is told exactly what the Allow opened: the key listing and the persona's
  declared tools. `secret get` and `secret cp` stay refused in a sandboxed chat, with a sentence
  naming the route that works (qw385).
- **A vault notice no longer loops.** One Allow answers every chat of the same persona refused
  the same vault; pressing Allow where the vault is already allowed says so and closes the
  notice; Dispatch closes it too (qw385).
- **A vault whose bindings all read one variable has its token box.** The vault's tab counted
  bindings, so a vault that reads one token variable for two targets said it needed two tokens
  and drew no box. It now counts variables, as storing the token does (#1528).
- **A vault tab reopened at launch reads nothing until you ask.** A 1Password vault's tab that
  was open when purlis quit no longer reads its token as purlis starts, which could make macOS
  ask about the Keychain or another app's data before you had done anything. The tab says it was
  open and reads the vault when you press *Read*. A keyring vault's tab still shows its table at
  once, since that reads no secret (#1660).
- **A token deleted in Keychain Access is no longer used until purlis quits.** Before purlis
  reuses a token it read earlier in the same run, it checks that the Keychain item is still
  there. The check does not read the token (#1660).
- **A 1Password Connect sign-in leaves the 1Password app's data alone.** An `op` handed a
  Connect token is told not to read the 1Password app's settings, as one handed a
  service-account token already is (#1660).
- **A vault's tab says what the system keychain kept.** When a token you store replaces older
  ones that purlis could not remove from your system keychain, the tab now says how many are
  left there, rather than only logging it (#1528). The one note that a vault's secrets were
  moved under purlis's access rule is now said in the vault's tab too, after the reveal or copy
  that moved them, not only by the next `purlis secret` command (#1180).
- **A vault tab's note beside a failed read follows what purlis diagnosed.** Whether the tab
  says to try again or to sign in was decided by words in the failure's sentence, which also
  names the vault's identity variable. It now follows the cause the 1Password provider
  recognised (#1528).
- **A vault whose token is nowhere shows the box that stores it.** The tab of a 1Password vault
  read through a service-account token drew that box only after the vault had been read, which
  takes the token. So a purlis opened from the Dock, which never sees what a shell exports,
  showed the refusal and no way out. The tab now draws the refusal and the box under it, and
  lists the vault's secrets by itself once the token is stored. A token is stored per vault:
  after a store the tab names the other vaults read through the same variable that still have
  none, each a link to its own tab. A token stored again replaces the old one, which is deleted
  from the keyring. When a kept token does not read the vault, the tab says the provider's own
  reason and blames the token only for a refused sign-in. The refusal now leads with the
  keyring, then the export, and no longer leads with unbinding the vault. `purlis doctor` has a
  `vault tokens` row: for each such vault, whether its token is marked as kept in the system
  keyring, in this environment only, or nowhere (#1526).
- **A chat nobody is at, whose project's "any persona" waits for your yes, is told to have it
  reviewed.** It was told no grant exists. It now reads the sentence a waiting pair gets: the
  project's file allows it, and a person reviews it under Settings › Project › Dispatch
  (#1464).
- **A Docker engine that stops answering holds up no pool surface.** Every `docker` run that only
  reads (an inspect, a version, a list, the check before each link to a runner) is ended after 20
  seconds. The Pools settings, the drain and a link to a runner then say Docker did not answer.
  A pull or a make still takes as long as it takes (#3546).
- **Answering one prompt in the window leaves a chat's other prompts open.** When a chat and
  one of its helpers both asked for a permission, an answer in the Inbox or on the pane cleared
  both, and the chat read as working while the other prompt still waited. Now only the prompt
  you answered goes (#1644).
- **A window opens in the theme its levels choose** (#2602). A machine-default theme folder, a
  project's choice and a workspace's are drawn from the window's first frame, in the native
  window too, with no repaint once purlis has read the project.
- **A window opens in the high-contrast appearance when the system asks for more contrast**
  (#2582). With Increase contrast or a high-contrast desktop setting on, a theme with an
  appearance tagged high contrast is drawn from the first frame.
- **An appearance a theme does not have honours more contrast**: the theme's first appearance
  for the system's contrast is drawn in its place.
- **A chat can no longer be linked to a todo that does not exist.** Linking a chat to a
  `todo:` work item now checks that the workspace it names has that todo open, or that a
  promote moved it to an issue. A mistyped or closed todo is refused with a sentence saying so,
  and nothing is written, where before the link was kept and the Work list could never show
  it (#918).
- **A change to `workspace.json` that waited while the workspace was renamed is refused.** A
  settings save, a clone, a removal or a snapshot that was waiting its turn on the manifest
  while `purlis workspace rename` moved the folder used to go on at the old path, and could make
  `workspaces/<old>` again. It now says the workspace was renamed or removed while it waited,
  and writes nothing (#1292).
- **Edit as JSON refuses a repo's `branch` git would not take.** A branch starting with `-`, a
  full `refs/…` name, or one `git check-ref-format --branch` refuses, such as `a..b`, is
  refused, unless the file already held that exact record (#1292).
- **A workspace purlis cannot read is not called behind the layout.** The status line no longer
  shows its `reinit` tip for a workspace whose folder or layout stamp purlis cannot read, and the
  `reinit` alert no longer counts one, since `purlis ws reinit` could not reach it either. The
  doctor's `workspace layout` row already left them out (#1289).
- **A move back here is no longer refused for a clone the runner never had**: a repository added
  here while the chat ran on the runner stays as it is. A repository cloned only on the runner
  stays there, as Move here's row says (#3454).
- **A refused move says the pool's own reason**: no pool of that name, no runner of its image, or
  its runner draining, rather than always that its runner is not known to be yours. A move that
  failed names where the chat still runs once (#3646).
- **A chat over ACP reads its agent on a thread of its own.** A process that left an agent's
  process group and kept its output open used to park a thread of a pool every chat shares, so
  enough of them could slow every chat's reads. Now it holds only its own chat's reader, which
  ends once that process lets go. A tool call's kind and status, and a turn's stop reason, are
  purlis's own words, and a stop reason purlis does not know no longer reads as a cancel. When
  purlis restarts itself to leave the terminal it was started from, and the first process is
  killed in the instant before the second one checks, the second one now ends too, rather than
  run on as a window nothing started (#1117).
- **What a chat's Activity forgets is gone on time, and an open tab stops showing it.** An open
  Activity tab drops the words Clear finished, closing the chat that asked or removing a
  workspace forgot, without being read again. A dispatch record is collected 30 days after its
  task ended, however lately it was rewritten, so forgetting no longer keeps a brief and report
  a month longer. A project held open for weeks expires its older records' words once a day. A
  task that ends as a project opens, whose asking chat did not come back, is forgotten like one
  that ends after its asking chat closed. Files named for a time to come no longer push the
  real records out of a timeline's read (#1556).
- **Allow once covers every task its Notice lists.** Each task the Notice names holds the grant
  for its next run, is audited for it and restarts able to reach it. A one-chat Allow ("Allow
  once", "Allow for this chat") reaches only its chat wherever it is applied or taken back
  (#2629).
- **A click or drag inside a frame the page turns, scales or zooms lands where the element is
  drawn.** The agent's click, hover or drag aimed at an element inside a frame from another site
  lands on the element where it shows on screen, however the page transforms the frame, and only
  inside the frame that shows the element. When purlis cannot tell where the frame is drawn, or
  the element lies outside what its frame shows, the act is answered "not shown" (#2557).
- **A click, hover or drag inside frames nested below another frame's fold reaches its
  element.** Where the element is not shown on the first read, purlis scrolls each frame that
  holds it into view, outermost first, and reads again before it answers "not shown". An act
  lands only at a point the page's own window shows (#2690).
- **An Activity line follows its chat while the tab is open.** When a chat on a session's
  Activity closes, its lines drop the button that showed it, and its Answer, and say "(chat
  closed)" after its name. Before, the button stayed until the tab was read again, and pressing
  it brought nothing forward. A chat restarted under another number keeps its button. The
  "also names" sentence is now drawn in the body text colour, with only its sign in the waiting
  colour, so it stays readable in the light theme (#1457).
- **A chat's read of a large page finishes in time, or says why.** A snapshot, find or wait on
  a very large page that the browser takes long to read answers inside the chat's call limit:
  with the page, or saying in words that the page is too large to read in time, never that
  whether it acted is not known. The read goes on, so the same call made again in a moment gets
  the page. Handing a browser back after typing into such a page reads the page for at most
  20 seconds, and a code you typed one character a box stays out of the chat's answers even
  where the page could not be read again in that time (#3277).
- **A fix in the Alerts drawer that needs your input opens its form.** A drawer row whose way out
  is the git identity fix now opens the same name and email form as the doctor, instead of
  applying the fix with nothing and being refused (#1301).
- **An answer that ends something can be read in the dark theme.** Its red words, on a Delete or
  an End button and in a menu, were 3.73:1 against the button, under the 4.5:1 that text needs.
  The dark theme's danger red is lighter now, in the same hue, and clears 4.5:1 on the button, on
  the button under the pointer, on a menu and on the window (#1210).
- **A permission ask's deadline counts from when its hook started.** The harness gives up on
  purlis's permission hook a minute after it starts it, and the ask's deadline used to count
  from when the app raised it. Time the hook spent before that, starting up or waiting to be
  heard, was not counted, so an answer could land after the harness had stopped listening. The
  hook now says how long it has run, and the deadline counts from its start; a hook with too
  little time left raises nothing, and the harness asks in its own pane (#1063).
- **An edit to a file with a family emoji or Persian text can be allowed from the window.** A
  change holding two emoji joined by a zero-width joiner, or a Persian word written with a
  zero-width non-joiner between two letters, was never shown whole, so its Allow was missing
  and it could only be answered in the pane. It is now shown and may be allowed. A joiner
  anywhere else, such as between two Latin letters, still keeps the change from being shown.
- **A question's labels keep a Persian word's non-joiner.** A form an agent asks you to fill
  dropped the zero-width non-joiner from Persian labels and text, which ran the word's parts
  together. It is kept now, and so is a family emoji; a joiner anywhere else is still dropped.
- **A page too large to read fails only the call that read it.** An answer from the browser
  engine past the most one call may take now fails that call with a sentence, and the browser
  keeps answering; before, it ended the browser. The read that marks what a box doesn't show is
  held to a smaller bound, so a page heavy in inline script or attribute text has nothing marked
  by it (#2694).
- **A file an agent writes just as you open a folder shows up.** When finding the branch for the
  folder's watch took longer than two seconds, the explorer drew the folder without waiting, and a
  file made before the watch held was not drawn until something else changed there. The folder is
  now read once more when its watch holds (#1189).
- **A linked install no longer keeps a chat from removing its finished branch folder.** A folder
  whose ignored `app/node_modules` is a symbolic link into another folder, as lanes share an
  install, is removed like one with its own: an ignored link goes with the folder, wherever it
  points, and what it points to is never touched (#4245).
- **An install that ends after you leave Sources no longer pulls the Skill studio back** (Skill studio preview, #3973). If you went to Library, or anywhere else in the studio, while a skill from a source was still being installed, the tab used to jump back to the source's page when the install ended. Now it goes on to the source's page only if you are still on the install review.
- **Deciding a dispatch reads a bounded number of dispatch records.** Reading an older chat's
  chain back from the records reads the newest 2,000 and no more (#1548).
- **A chat an older purlis opened to report back now wakes the chat that asked.** Before the
  update, a handoff that asked for a report wrote it, and the asking chat read it only when you
  next typed into it. Such a chat, still open after the update, is now a task of the chat that
  asked, in every way. Its report wakes that chat as a task's report does. That chat lists it
  and can wait on it with `purlis dispatch`, and can tell it or cancel it. If it ends without
  reporting, the asking chat is told. Like any task, purlis ends it once it has reported, and
  you can reopen it from its finished row (#1519).
- **A handoff that asks for a report never opens as one now.** `purlis handoff --report` sends
  a task, which counts against the same limits as `purlis dispatch`, and a request for one
  from an older command line opens nothing and names `purlis dispatch` (#1471).
- **An older reporting handoff is pointed at the persona it named.** A chat still running an
  older `purlis handoff --report` line is told to send a `purlis dispatch` to the persona that
  line named, instead of a placeholder. When the line was also creating a workspace, the reply
  names `purlis workspace create` first (#1471).
- **A chat on a pool whose runner runs an older purlis is found again once that runner is
  updated.** purlis can't ask an older runner what it runs, so it no longer treats it as running
  nothing (#4684).
- **A branch whose chat did start is no longer marked `unclaimed`.** The explorer used to date a
  branch's cut from its folder's `.git` file, which `git worktree repair`, `git worktree move` and
  a copied plane rewrite, so a quiet branch could be marked `unclaimed` five minutes later. The
  cut is now read from the branch's own history, which those leave alone. When purlis cannot
  write down that a chat started on a branch, it leaves a mark on the branch itself, so that
  branch is not marked either (#835).
- **An unpinned or dormant workspace chip's edge is easy to see** (#3999). The title bar draws the
  current workspace that is not pinned, and a pin whose workspace is gone, with no fill of its own:
  their dashed and dotted line is what shows them. That line was the window's faint hairline, which
  in Purlis dark reached only 1.38:1 against the bar. It is now drawn in the chip's own muted words,
  at least 3:1 in every built-in theme and in every state (WCAG 1.4.11).
- **A chat nobody is at that runs with no sandbox is told that first.** Asked to dispatch or
  hand off into another workspace as another persona, it was told that a grant naming the pair
  would carry it, and none would: it dispatches to no other persona outside a sandbox. It is
  now told that (#1543).
- **A refused append, and a folder made ahead of a write, name their file.** When the filesystem
  refuses with "Operation not permitted", an append to the work, dispatch or trace log or a
  memory index, a folder made ahead of a write, a memory's archive, restore or move, a new
  persona and a workspace's vision now say which file or folder it was, and, in a sandboxed
  chat, that the chat's sandbox refused it. `purlis init` names a refused file once, not twice.
  A handoff whose dispatch row could not be written says the chat is open and nothing needs
  running again (#1359).
- **Asking again for what is already in front no longer redraws the whole window.** Pressing the
  tab already in front, opening a view whose tab is in front (Settings… from the palette, say),
  focusing the workspace already shown, or renaming a tab to the name it has left the tabs as
  they were but still drew the window again and read the plane's sidebar again; now they do
  neither.
- A chat waiting on you keeps its ✋ and its Inbox card when a task reports back or its own background work wakes it. Only your reply clears the wait.
- **The window no longer holds still while purlis asks git about a branch or a workspace.**
  Listing a repo's branches, finding which branch a chat works in, merging, removing or
  declaring a branch done, and creating a workspace, reading what removing one would lose, or
  removing it, now run off the window's thread, as New branch already did. A second press of
  Merge, Remove or Done on a branch while the first is on its way sends nothing, and another of
  them on that branch says what it is still doing (#1007, #1610).
- **Many branches whose reads hang no longer start a reader each.** purlis reads a branch's
  changes in a short-lived child process. At most six run at once now, across every window, and
  a read that waits for a place past its deadline says purlis is busy. When a window starts
  watching its branches, each is looked up on its own, so one that hangs no longer holds back
  the others (#1130).
- **Reading a branch waits its turn, and a branch that keeps hanging is paused.** purlis reads
  at most six branches at once. A read waiting for a place is now let in before any read that
  came after it, so it no longer runs out of time while newer ones go first. A branch whose
  reads ran out of time or memory twice in a row is not read again for a pause that grows each
  time it happens again, so it cannot keep the places full for other branches, comparisons and
  searches. When a read does run out of time, the message names the time it actually had. A
  file tab now also marks a chat that touched a file before the tab could name it, and finds
  its branch again after a lookup that failed (#1605).
- **A build in one branch no longer has every other branch read again.** A burst of more files
  than the branch watch holds, such as `cargo build` writing into `target/`, counted against
  every branch listened to and marked them all as moved. The cap is now counted per branch: only
  the branch over it is checked again, and a burst only where git ignores tells nobody (#4740).
- **purlis's `session_record` and `persona_remember` tools never write outside a chat's
  sandbox.** In a chat purlis started they hand the write to purlis, and where purlis cannot
  take it (under Codex, which gives the tools no connection to purlis, or when the hand-over
  fails) they refuse and name the command to run in the chat instead: `purlis session record`
  or `purlis persona remember`. Outside such a chat, or once purlis has quit, they write as
  before (#1408).
- **A memory too long to hand over is refused, never written twice over.** In a chat purlis
  started, a memory or a memory command's text past what one hand-over carries (12 KiB) is
  refused with a sentence saying so, where it used to break the connection and be written by
  the chat itself (#1408).
- **A brokered `purlis secret exec` keeps its output whole with a long value.** In a sandboxed
  chat, a vault value longer than about 190 KiB could make the app send a piece of output larger
  than the command reads, and the command then said the app had stopped answering. Output now
  goes back in pieces that always fit, masked as before (#1407).
- **A brokered run says how many more hosts were refused.** The sandbox names the first eight
  hosts it refused a brokered command; past those, the command is now told how many more there
  were, instead of nothing (#1353).
- **A chat whose spool key could not be recorded at its start gets it recorded later.** When
  another process held the hook spool's lock as a chat started, its key was never recorded, so
  every hook line that chat spooled while the app was busy was rejected. The key is now recorded
  at the next chance (the chat's next hook line, or the next chat to start), while the chat
  still runs on that key (#1426).
- **A declared tool handed a credential as a file (`secret exec --file`) reads it again** under
  the sandbox its run is held to, on macOS as on Linux (#2342).
- **`purlis secret exec` works from a sandboxed chat.** Inside a chat the app started sandboxed,
  `purlis secret exec <vault> … -- <command>` no longer reads the vault itself, which the
  sandbox correctly forbids. It asks the app over the chat's hook channel. The app checks that
  the vault registry tags the vault with the chat's persona, resolves the secret, and runs the
  command in a sandbox built from what the chat's own sandbox was compiled to when it started.
  Output streams back with each value's literal text masked, followed by the exit status. A
  vault the persona may not use is refused with a sentence. Outside an app chat, the command
  runs as before (#1407).
  What this keeps from the chat: the vault's storage and its provider's session, every vault
  not tagged for the chat's persona, and a `--file` credential, which only the command may read.
  It does not keep the values from the chat: the command is the chat's own, so the chat can
  obtain any key of a vault tagged for its persona.
- **Browsers start on Ubuntu 23.10 and later, their engine's sandbox on.** The engine purlis
  downloads needs an AppArmor profile there to make its sandbox, and without one every browser
  ended at its start. The `.deb` now installs that profile. Where purlis was installed another
  way, a Notice offers the command that adds it, or this machine's own Chrome for every browser,
  and the chat is told a browser is not available here instead of the engine's crash (#2835).
- **A busy chat no longer redraws the whole window each time it moves.** Every move used to reach
  the window's title bar and switchers, in the project in front and in every project behind it.
  Now only what shows that chat is drawn again, and a list of asks that the move left unchanged
  changes nothing (#4727).
- **A button that gains a hint under the keyboard shows it.** A button or a toggle that turned
  unavailable, or gained a hint, while the keyboard was on it kept the focus but showed nothing
  until the keyboard came back to it. Its hint now shows at once, and a hint that goes is taken
  down (#4671).
- **A chat that waits for its turn to end before it restarts says so.** A chat that is
  mid-turn when you allow something says that it restarts once its turn ends, with **Restart
  now**, where it used to show nothing until the turn ended. And a chat blocked on a socket or
  a service you already allowed on this machine offers **Restart this chat**, where it used to
  ask for the same Allow again.
- **`purlis change show` counts a blocker landed only as `change land` does.** A blocker is ticked
  when its request merged and purlis landed it: in the landing log, with the clone's default
  branch still holding that commit, or as a landing purlis started. One merged outside purlis is
  crossed with the land gate's reason and still blocks its dependent, in `show` and in the
  changes view alike (#877).
- **The keyboard has somewhere to go after Forget this chat….** It moves to the next Notice, or
  to the strip when no Notice is left, instead of landing on the page. A screen reader on a tab
  now hears its plane-updated mark too, because the tab is described by it (#1246).
- **The Chats list holds still while the keyboard is in a row's menu.** Its rows used to move
  under an open context menu. A list now also lets go as soon as the focus goes to a menu that is
  not one of its rows', or the pointer moves on after a row's menu closed under it. The Chats
  list and the Personas view use the same rule for this (#3594).
- **A screen reader no longer meets the rolled-up hand as a stray button in the Chats tree.** The
  hand stays a pointer target beside the row. The row already says which chat below needs you
  (#3658).
- **The Chats list holds still while the pointer crosses from a row to its card.** The card stands
  a few pixels beside its row, and moving the pointer across that gap let the list go, so the rows
  could reorder and the card move with its row before the pointer reached it. While a card is up,
  the list now waits as long as the card does before it lets go (#3773).
- **Chats put back together at launch all start on macOS.** A Claude Code chat's settings there
  are long enough to go through a file of their own, and two chats writing theirs at the same
  moment, in a project none had written for yet or under one id, could leave one of them not
  started with "a chat's settings could not be written to its file". The second write now finds
  the folder or the file the first made and starts.
- **A Chats row's card now says what the row says.** A chat below it that needs you, the whole
  task-limit sentence, what waits on memory and where those dispatches are listed, and what a
  restart said are lines of the card too. A screen reader, which is told the card while it is
  up, still hears them, and a keyboard user reads the limit and memory hints without hovering.
  The restarts' announcement is there from the start and only its words change, so screen
  readers that skip a region arriving already full announce it too (#3886).
- **A screen reader no longer meets a row's task limit, memory wait or restart words as stray
  parts of the Chats tree.** The lines under the row are still drawn, and the Dispatch settings
  link still opens with the pointer. The row now says the whole limit sentence, which names where
  the limit is changed, and what waits on memory. A restart's words are announced from beside
  the tree (#3759).
- **A workspace's notice card now ends up centred under its chip after the strip scrolls the
  chip into view.** WebKit, which purlis runs in on macOS and Linux, can finish a smooth scroll
  without a scroll event for its last steps. The card stopped where the last event left it,
  short of the chip. It now keeps following the chip until the chip stops moving.
- **Tabbing into a notice card just after opening it from its dot now stays put.** The card
  pulled the keyboard back to its edge for a few frames while it was being placed (#3896).
- **Chrome no longer ends itself on a page whose frame reloads quickly.** purlis no longer holds
  a frame at its start, and it reads the address of a frame from when the frame attaches. Opening
  a page Chrome is slow to report now says the page stayed blank, instead of "no page open"
  (#4472).
- **A warning button's words are easier to read in Purlis Classic's light appearance.** The
  waiting colour is a shade darker, so the words of a warning-soft button hold 4.5:1 on a
  control and a hovered one (#2945).
- **Claude Code chats start on a pool's runner.** A sandboxed Claude Code chat on a Docker or
  cluster pool was refused for want of bubblewrap and socat. It now runs inside purlis's own Linux
  sandbox there, as Codex and opencode chats do, with Claude Code's own sandbox off, and the runner
  image needs neither program. Its commands can read the runner's sign-in, as Codex's can. On a
  runner a Claude Code chat always starts sandboxed: a start without the sandbox there is
  refused. On your own machine nothing changes (#4083).
- A failed clone's notice goes once its repo lands, from its row, its chip or Settings. A failure that named several repos keeps only the ones still not cloned.
- A new workspace's repo whose clone failed keeps its row in the Repos and Changes views, with the reason and Retry, and Dismiss puts it away.
- Explorer no longer says "No repos in this workspace" above the repos it lists as not cloned here.
- A repo that landed while its workspace was not focused, and was dropped before it was, no longer stays as a "Cloned" row.
- A new workspace's repos have a row in its Repos view, with their percent and Cancel, while they clone. The view used to say the workspace had no repos until each one landed.
- Every push purlis makes names its commit in a form no ref can stand for. A branch whose local ref
  went bad could delete the branch on the remote and report success.
- `purlis change push` refuses a member's branch that git's own grammar refuses. A `:` in the name
  could send the push to another branch.
- The check of a clone's Git LFS store no longer takes a `.git` folder that git itself climbs past.
- A clone's large files (Git LFS) now show their progress in the window, and a large file that is still downloading is no longer stopped as stalled after 5 minutes.
- A clone purlis wired no longer shows its Git LFS files as changed in purlis's own git, and a save there stores an LFS file as its pointer rather than whole. A file purlis checks out there stays a pointer until `git lfs pull`. A push from purlis does not upload LFS objects yet: run `git lfs push --all origin` in the clone.
- **A clone signs in once, with your purlis account, and has no time limit** (#4079). A clone the
  window runs now signs in with your account for the repo's real server, port included, so a
  self-hosted forge's account is found. A large repo on a slow line takes as long as it takes:
  git is stopped only after five minutes with nothing new, not after two minutes in all. A clone
  lands whole or not at all, so a failed or cancelled one leaves no folder and Retry really clones.
  The chip's card and the Repos row show one percent and the stage, and both offer Cancel. What a
  failed clone says comes from what failed, and the window's words no longer name `gh` or `glab`.
- A chat's large clone no longer gives up after about 7 minutes while git is still working, when its chat runs in the session host. A clone that has truly stalled still says so.
- **The Explorer's line for a branch the file filter could not look in is drawn in the danger
  colour**, not as plain grey text. The mark that says you are driving a chat's browser is bold,
  and a done todo's words are quieter as well as struck through. All three had been drawn in the
  wrong colour or weight (#3917).
- **Compare lets go when the pointer leaves the window** (#4628). Holding Compare on a theme draft
  and letting the pointer leave the window could leave the kept theme drawn. A hold from the
  keyboard stays until the key comes up or the window loses focus. Chat cards, activity items,
  fields and menu tooltips no longer stay up or lit after the pointer leaves the window.
- **A submodule checked out at another commit shows as changed.** A comparison with what is not
  committed now draws a submodule whose folder checked out a commit its pointer does not name
  as git does, the commit it checked out on the working tree's side. purlis reads that commit
  from the submodule's git folder as plain files and starts no git in it (#704).
- **A lock charter lets go of is free at once, even while one of its programs is starting.** A
  program charter starts has a copy of the lock's descriptor until it runs, and that copy used
  to keep the lock held, so `rename-local` and its undo could find the config home busy for a
  moment after the app or a chat's server let go of it. The config home's lock, the event log's
  writer lock and the hook spool's locks are now unlocked before they are closed, as charter's
  other locks already were (#1316).
- **The Curate menu offers the harness's card again under rows that cannot run.** When the
  default profile's harness cannot have a prompt typed in (opencode), every Curate row is off
  with the card's line as its reason, and the card's own row ("What opencode can do here")
  should follow them. It never did: the reason went on past the card's label with advice to
  change the default, and the window links a card only where a reason ends with its label
  (ADR 0072 §3). The advice now comes first and the card's line and label end the reason
  (#1134).
- **The dialogs say what they are doing, and every answer is reachable by Tab.** Closing a chat
  whose chats are still at work asks Keep them running or Stop them with a radio group Tab
  reaches, each answer saying what it does. New branch, New persona, New vault, New workspace,
  New project, Delete workspace, Delete vault, Delete persona, Remove from workspace and Link
  work item say _Creating…_, _Deleting…_, _Removing…_ or _Linking…_ while they run, and New
  project says it is copying your repo. Extensions says when it is reading, says a list it could
  not read, and says _No extensions installed yet_ rather than _None_. Acts name what they act
  on: _Open repo_ on the first run, _Link work item_, _Test sign-in_ and _Store sign-in_. Start a
  chat's labels are in sentence case, New project says _repo_ throughout, Open vault no longer
  points at a + it does not have, a repo filter that matches nothing says so, and the thrown
  kill switch is named by the words it shows (#630).
- **Comments in a changed word can be read in a diff.** Every built-in theme now holds syntax
  colours at 3:1 on a diff's changed words, with a slightly thinner word highlight that still
  stands out from its line, and brighter comments. Purlis Classic's light modal scrim is a little
  darker, like the other built-ins' (#4424).
- **Discard compares what a task's branch folder holds, not only its paths.** A file you were
  shown that was written again, a file added inside a folder git ignores whole, and a commit
  made in a repository nested in the folder each count as a change, and nothing is removed
  until you are asked again. A nested repository is named in the question, since its history
  goes with the folder. The last look is taken in the same step as the removal, and no chat
  starts in the folder while it is being removed (#1472).
- **`purlis discover` finds the repos of a GitLab user, not only of a group.** A GitLab owner
  that is no group was refused with `404 Group Not Found`. purlis now asks GitLab for that
  user's own repos, as it already did for a GitHub personal account; any other refusal still
  fails (#803).
- **`purlis discover` on a GitLab group lists only the group's own repos.** A repo another
  namespace had shared with the group was listed as if it were the group's. GitHub's
  organisation listing has no such case (#804).
- **Closing a chat in the middle of a chain no longer splits its lineage in two.** Each chat a
  dispatch starts keeps the id of the chat you started, and a lineage is counted by it, so the
  lineage limit holds when a chat between two others closes or is started again (#1436).
- **A message to or from a dispatched task is no longer lost when the app does not answer.**
  `tell`, `note`, `ask` and `answer`, and their tools, are queued and delivered, in order and
  once, when the app next hears from the chat; the sender is told the message is queued, not
  yet delivered, and `purlis dispatch list` shows each message as queued, delivered or
  undeliverable, with why (#3902).
- **Messages queued by a chat that never came back after a restart are reported, not cleared
  silently.** Each is kept, marked not delivered, on the dispatch it was between, where the
  Dispatches tab shows it; what no running dispatch can keep is one Notice in the Inbox, naming
  the chat and how many, until you put it away (#3958).
- **A chat can dispatch several tasks in one step.** Two `purlis dispatch` calls made at once
  from one chat used to collide: the second was refused with "try again in a few seconds",
  because the app kept one live ticket per chat. Each run of the command now has a ticket of
  its own, on its own connection, spent once and gone in ten seconds either way, so six tasks
  sent together start six chats. A handoff is asked for and opened exactly as before (#1441).
- **Private-registry pulls work from a window opened from the Finder.** purlis runs `docker`
  with Docker's credential helpers found where `docker` itself is (#2752).
- **A command purlis suggests for a git repository pastes as the command it names, whatever the
  path.** The doctor's `plane root` hint (`git -C … checkout …`), its `clone git config` hint
  (`git -C … config --remove-section branch.`), its `index lock` hint and the stale-lock remedy a
  save or update prints (`rm -f …`) quote the path (and the branch) for the shell and never
  shorten it: a folder with a space, a quote or a `$` in its name no longer pastes as a broken or
  different command (#4830).
- **The doctor's personas row counts in words that agree.** It, and the Inbox Notice that
  carries its text, said "1 generated sub-agent file(s) remain" and "1 persona(s), all clean".
  It now says *1 generated sub-agent file remains*, *2 generated sub-agent files remain*,
  *1 persona, all clean*, *2 drafts* and *2 with warnings* (#2078).
- **A chat too long to start is refused in plain words.** Every start now measures its program's
  words with the whole environment it starts with, and refuses one the system would not start,
  before anything is opened, instead of failing with `E2BIG` (#1425).
- **`purlis doctor` warns about a version pin on a project that follows the dev channel**, as
  the status line already did, instead of reporting it OK (#1036).
- **An older runner that stops before its chats end keeps its home.** After an update or a Replace,
  a runner that stopped while chats may have been running on it was removed with everything they
  left. purlis now keeps it until you bring their conversations back or discard them in Devices, and the pool's row
  in Settings says so. A purlis from before this refuses a `runners.json` holding `last_stop` or
  `held`, as it refuses any key it does not know, so a person who goes back to one removes those
  keys first.
- **Edit as TOML keeps a refused save's reasons with the edit.** Opening a group and coming back
  to the file shows why the save was refused, as it shows what was typed. The "changed on disk"
  line is a live region that stays in place, so a screen reader hears its first sentence (#1198).
- `purlis worktree update --continue` after an update with `--base` recorded the new base on the branch again, rather than writing an empty `[branch ""]` section that stopped every chat on the clone. A clone that already has that section recovers on its next `purlis worktree add`, `update` or `push`, and a push on a config git will not read says so rather than "has no remote to push".
- **The harness setup tab no longer says no harness is installed when it could not look.** A look
  at the machine that failed now says so, with the reason and Check again (#626).
- A task kept in its pane after it ends keeps its tab on its workspace's strip, beside the tabs it stood with, instead of moving to the strip outside every workspace.
- **The event log no longer turns away a quick relaunch.** Opening the device's event log waits
  up to a second for a lock that a moment ago belonged to this host or a just-exited one, held
  only by a program still starting, instead of running the session without recording hook calls
  as if another host were writing it (#972).
- **A browser whose engine stops reading is still stopped in time.** Every DevTools call to a
  chat's browser engine ends within its limit, writing included, and stopping a browser ends its
  engine within its grace however the engine behaves (#2123).
- **A hook can't get stuck on what sits at its spool path.** Anything there that is not a plain
  file is refused at once. A new spool's directory sync and the read before the append are
  bounded too, so the hook still answers its harness on time and says the line is lost. When the
  app starts, a spool path that does not open as a plain file (a directory, a link or a pipe) is
  reported as unreadable and every other chat's spool is still drained (#1417).
- **purlis's chat tools that the app answers work in Codex and ACP chats too.** `dispatch`,
  `dispatch_list`, `dispatch_report`, `persona_where`, `persona_remember`, `session_record` and
  the `workspace.md` tools reach the app that started the chat from every harness, as they did
  from Claude Code and opencode. The tool server is handed the chat's own connection to the app,
  the one its hooks already use, and nothing more (#1996).
- **Every line purlis says marks the hidden characters in the names it quotes.** A colour
  code, a direction-changing or a zero-width character in a skill's, a persona's, a repo's or a
  piece's name, in the reason given to `worktree abandon`, or in anything else a `•`, `✓`, `!`
  or `✗` line quotes, is now written as `⟦U+XXXX⟧` instead of reaching your terminal, where it
  could hide or reorder the rest of the line. A line break inside a quoted name is marked the
  same way, so it cannot start a line that looks like purlis's own.
  purlis's own colour is unchanged (#3225).
- **A network refusal printed on standard output now raises the chat's sandbox block Notice.**
  A command run with `2>&1`, a failed command's output, and a background command's output file
  read back later were never read, so a database client's "no such host" inside
  `purlis secret exec … 2>&1`, or Docker's refused socket in a background run, raised nothing.
  Now each raises a Notice. A line on standard output counts only when it ends the way the
  refusal does, so a file that quotes the words raises nothing. A host named there is never
  offered to allow.
- **A refused name lookup names its host.** The Notice for a program that looks its host up
  itself (psql, usql, ssh, Go and Node programs) now shows the host it tried, and still
  offers no Allow, because allowing the host would not let such a program through.
- **Codex and opencode chats get a Notice for each host purlis's proxy refused them**, named by
  the proxy itself, with Allow, as a Claude Code chat does.
- **The chat that dispatched a task is told when the task waits on a sandbox block's Notice**,
  at its next turn, as it is told of a task's permission prompt.
- **Every check that tells a sandboxed chat from one without the sandbox goes by how the chat's
  run started.** Dispatching to another persona, a handoff, a dispatch while you are away, the
  Network view, the app's git actions and the vault Notice read the session host's record of how
  the run started. On each check, a chat with no such record is treated the way that allows it
  less. A chat on a runner is judged by the runner's record: one that runs there without the
  sandbox keeps its persona's browser logins, and one in the runner's sandbox is told why it has
  none, instead of being offered a restart that would not help (#2692).
- **Every refused write names its file, and blames a sandbox only where one refused it.** The
  last writes that printed a bare "Operation not permitted (os error 1)" now name what they were
  writing: a session record's and the reopen record's folders, the event log, rename-local's
  log folder and undo, the default workspace, a removed workspace or clone, a harness plugin's
  files, and the app's git and shell shims. A refusal a hook or the MCP server meets in a Claude
  Code chat is no longer told as the chat's sandbox's, since Claude Code's sandbox holds only
  its Bash tool. `purlis init` and a handoff's warning keep saying "this
  chat's sandbox refused it" in a sandboxed chat, and a refused `.gitignore` reached through a
  link names the file the link leads to as well. A sandbox's refusal of purlis's own write says
  that purlis does not grant its own writes to a chat, so the operator runs the command outside
  it, and on Codex and opencode it now shows the Report notice for purlis's own block (#1421).
- **A handoff from a sandboxed chat keeps its dispatch row.** The app writes the row where it
  opens the chat, since a sandboxed chat may not write the project's dispatch log, and a
  handoff's own lines start `purlis handoff:` (#1421).
- **A folder's chevron is in the middle of its row.** In Explorer's Files, in a file tab's tree
  and on a repo's row in Repos, the `>` beside a folder stood above the row's middle, closed or
  open, at every depth. It is now centred on the row's line, in every tree that draws one.
- **An older answer about which extensions a project has on no longer replaces a newer one.**
  After a question failed twice, a slow earlier answer could undo what a later one said, and the
  window drew the wrong extensions' theme (#4872).
- **`F2` pressed as the window appears opens the palette.** The palette started listening a frame
  after the window was drawn, so a key pressed in that moment was lost (#1469).
- **Plain-file and reference vaults no longer look empty after your project's state folder
  moves.** A vault records its file as `.charter/vaults/<name>.json`, and moving the state folder
  to `.purlis/` left that record pointing at nothing, so the vault read as empty and the next
  `secret set` could start a second file. A vault file under the state folder is now read and
  written in the folder the project has, under either name, with nothing to rewrite. A vault file
  that is missing after values were written to it is now refused with its path, instead of being
  read as an empty vault (#1285).
- **Find in a diff opens the folded stretch its match is in.** The diff view folds long
  unchanged stretches, and a match inside one used to be counted and selected but stay hidden.
  Finding it now unfolds that stretch on both sides, as a click on the fold does, and leaves
  the other folds as they were (#1797).
- **Every window hears when the vaults finish moving.** Pressing *Finish moving N vaults* in one
  window now updates the Notice in every open window, so none goes on offering vaults that
  already moved (#1311).
- **Focus mode run from the command palette keeps the keyboard on your work** when the palette
  was opened from the sidebar, a side panel, the bottom Panel, the activity bar, the project
  rail or the status bar. It was left on nothing (#4072).
- **A folder dialog that could not open is said.** *Open project…*, *Open a repo…* on the first
  run, *Browse…* in New project and *Locate…* in Settings › You › This machine used to treat a
  dialog that failed like a cancelled one and say nothing. They now say the failure where each
  already says a refused open; a cancel still says nothing. Forgetting or locating a project in
  This machine also clears the window's line about that project having gone, so its *Locate…*
  no longer answers that purlis does not remember the old path (#1291).
- **A forge on a non-default port signs in with its purlis account.** A project got by its URL
  from GitHub Enterprise Server or self-managed GitLab on a port of its own, such as
  `git.example.com:8443`, now uses the purlis account signed in on that host and port. An
  account on another port of the same host is never used for it (#1850).
- **Deleting a task's branch no longer blames git for purlis's own refusal.** When purlis cannot
  tidy away the folder's record first, the sentence now says so instead of "git would not
  delete" (#1720).
- **Two programs sending as one forge account no longer lose a count of its hourly request
  budget.** The window and a `purlis` command counting at the same moment each count now (#1164).
- A task's own cluster runner also stays while the task saved a file in purlis's data home on it outside every repository, such as beside the projects. purlis's own folders on the runner are left out wherever the image puts them, and a runner on a large image is no longer kept for its size: only the places its user may write are looked through at each check (#5028, #5029, #5030).
- **Git works in a clone at the floor on Linux.** A Claude Code chat at the floor on Linux could
  not commit or check out when the home had no `.gitconfig` yet: git stopped on a config it could
  not read. purlis now makes that file, empty, before such a chat starts. A `.gitconfig` you
  already have is left as it is.
- **A git identity name has to show something.** The git identity fix refuses a name made only
  of characters that draw nothing on their own, such as Hangul fillers, the braille blank,
  combining marks or variation selectors. It also refuses a name or email that looks like a
  secret, as every other writer does, naming its kind and never repeating the value (#1250).
- **purlis checks for git before it runs it, so a Mac without git no longer shows a surprise
  system dialog.** On a Mac without Apple's command line developer tools, `/usr/bin/git` is a
  stub that opens the system's install dialog. purlis now asks `xcode-select -p` first (and
  looks for git on `PATH` elsewhere), and runs no git while it is missing. The window can show
  its own guided screen instead: Install opens Apple's installer, Check again looks again, and
  the action you started carries on once git is there. On Linux the screen names your
  distribution's package manager line (#1813).
- **The network log names where a git call really went.** A push that names no remote is listed
  at the remote git pushes to, and a URL is listed after git's rewrites, a push's own first
  (#1853, #1828).
- **A save to a branch that a GitHub ruleset protects takes the protected-branch path.** GitHub's
