  refusal for such a push says "Changes must be made through a pull request" or "Cannot update
  this protected ref". That is now read like a protected branch's refusal, as a GitLab protected
  branch already was. The project's save pushes to a branch of its own and links to opening a
  pull request, and a repo's save names the setting that takes it through one. A push that a
  ruleset refuses for what it carries, a secret or a file, still reports the push failure. Before,
  every such save said only that the push failed (FG-3, #711).
- **The palette's "Open changes" row says "request"**, not "pull request", because a member may
  be on GitLab (FG-3, #711).
- **A save on GitLab calls its merge request a merge request.** In the `pr` and `pr-merge`
  modes, a save whose origin is on GitLab said "pull request #12". It now says "merge request
  !12", as GitLab does. This covers the save's messages, the description it writes, `doctor`,
  the plane-root alert, the memory note, and the Saving view and save indicator. Where repos on
  GitHub and GitLab are listed together, the Saving view calls each one a "request". Link to
  work item now gives a GitLab key as an example too. GitHub's wording is unchanged (FG-3,
  #1067).
- **Turning on grading after each edit for a new skill no longer asks again at its first edit.**
  Its plan now shows and keeps the chats with the previous version's arm counted, as the first
  saved edit makes a version to compare with, and says so. An opt-in turned on before still asks
  once, and now says why (#4035).
- **Grading after each edit keeps grading after the first edit of a skill that has a previous
  version.** Each saved edit is committed, so the version a grade compares with is the one before
  that edit, and it moves with every edit. The opt-in no longer pauses when it does. It still
  waits for you when a grade would run on another profile or model, run other trigger tests, run
  more chats or may spend more (#4016).
- **Back to the scorecard always lands on that grade's scorecard.** A saved chat opened from an
  old grade tab went back to whatever page came before it; it now opens its scorecard (#3978).
- **Leave it running and Back to its grades add no step.** Back on the Grades tab afterwards no
  longer reopens the running grade (#3978).
- **A scorecard or saved chat of a workspace's or a persona's skill opens from an old grade tab.**
  It used to open the skill's page instead; now it opens the scorecard, and the Skill studio
  moves to that workspace or persona (#3978).
- **A grade of a same-named copy at another level no longer moves this copy's Grades tab.** A
  workspace `deploy` ending its grade no longer raises a notice on the project's `deploy` (#3978).
- **The sandbox reads more spellings of a protected script and of a chat's own folder.** A
  script named in a value attached to its option (`-bf./tools/x.awk`, `--from-file=./x.jq`,
  `-javaagent:./agent.jar`) is protected the same as one given as a separate word. On macOS
  a folder reached under its data-volume name (`/System/Volumes/Data/Users/…`) counts as the
  same folder. That holds when a chat's ground is checked, and in the rules of every
  sandbox purlis compiles. On a volume that ignores letter case, a folder that doesn't
  exist yet and differs from a chat's ground only in case counts as that ground. When a chat
  is refused because a config names its ground, the refusal now names the repo or workspace
  the config sits in (#1356).
- **A `commit -v` under a comment mark of several characters commits again.** Where git's
  `core.commentString` (or `core.commentChar`) is more than one character, the commit-message
  scan now sees git's scissors line, so a verbose commit that removes a credential is no
  longer refused for the diff git puts below it.
- **The harness cards follow a declaration edited by hand.** The palette's *What … can do
  here* rows were read again only when the project came to the front or its settings changed
  in the window, so a harness declared in the project's files from an editor got no card row
  until then, while the curation rows already followed the file. The window now reads the cards
  again when it comes back into focus, as it does the curation rows (#1134).
- **A theme with a tint recipe and see-through colours no longer holds up the window for its whole
  measure at launch.** The first frame waits about 50 ms for the theme's parts, where it used to wait
  hundreds of milliseconds per appearance, and draws those parts in their family defaults until the
  measure lands (#4337).
- **A heavy theme's parts land when they are measured, not when the restore ends.** The first frame
  says its parts are coming and the window asks for them as it starts, so a slow project restore no
  longer leaves a theme drawn in its family defaults, and an ask that fails is made again (#4410).
- **Pools and Devices no longer wait while purlis reads a stopped runner's home.** Checking an older runner's home for chats' conversations could take minutes, and starting a chat on a pool, Replace and Devices waited until it ended. The check now runs on its own. If it keeps failing, purlis waits longer between tries, up to four hours (#4861).
- **The cache and Codex homes of a project that is gone are removed.** A project's package
  caches and Codex home under purlis's data home are taken away once the project's folder is
  gone (not merely on a disk that is not mounted) and nothing has used them for a month (#1364).
- **An ended chat's hook spool no longer stays behind.** Its empty folder in
  `.charter/app/spool/` and the emptied file an older build kept for it are removed once the
  chat ends. A project opened by a host that has no event log drops the spool keys of chats
  that have ended, unless the chat's spool still holds a line, so those keys no longer pile
  up from one launch to the next (#983).
- **A hook that runs `jq … // …` no longer makes a sandboxed project read-only.** The sandbox
  read every word with a `/` in a committed hook or MCP command as a script to protect, so
  jq's `//` operator denied writing `/`, and no chat could write anything. Now only a word
  that reads as a path counts as one. jq's filter text, operators, options, where output goes
  and the folders a command works in don't count. Scripts a command runs are still protected,
  however the command hands them over. If a rule would still cover `/`, the home folder, the
  project or the chat's own folder, the chat doesn't start, and the refusal names the file and
  the word (#1327).
- **Hooks of one chat that fire at once no longer lose a line while purlis is away.** When
  purlis does not take a hook's line (it is restarting, has quit or is slow), the hook keeps the
  line on disk for the next open of the project. Every hook of a chat wrote to one file, one at
  a time, and gave up after 250 ms of waiting for its turn. With several tool calls or
  sub-agents reporting together on a busy machine or a slow disk, some hooks ran out of that
  wait: each said on stderr that its line was lost, and that tool call or report was missing
  from the chat's record. Each hook now writes a file of its own and waits for no other hook.
  A line is still said to be lost when the disk refuses it or the chat already has 16,384
  lines waiting. When the disk takes more than a second over it, the hook now says the line
  may be lost, since the write can still finish and be read at the next open. Lines an
  earlier version left waiting are read as before (#983).
- **The hosts Notices follow the project while it is open.** A persona's hosts Notice now reads
  the project again when its settings change on disk, as after a pull, and both it and the
  project's hosts Notice read again each time the window comes back into focus. A list a
  teammate changed is asked about then, not only the next time the project opens (#1407).
- **A long run of stacked accents no longer draws over the Inbox's other rows.** An ask's line
  keeps up to four combining marks on a character, so an accented path stays readable, and cuts
  the rest. An ask whose line was cut offers no Allow in the Inbox, since what it shows is not
  what would run: deny it there, or read it whole in the chat's own pane (#1146).
- **An Inbox card for a chat waiting on your reply shows what the chat said.** The card used to
  say "Waiting on your reply" twice, so you had to open the chat to find what it asked. It now
  shows the chat's last message, masked and bounded as a report's text is, and says so once when
  there is no message to show. This covers your own chats as well as tasks (#4550).
- **Install all… goes ahead when a ticked skill is there already** (Skill studio preview, #4153).
  The list is ticked before you choose where the skills land, so a skill the chosen level holds
  already, made there by hand or installed from another source, used to make the install refuse.
  The review now shows it under "There already", unticked, and installs the rest.
- **Keep blocked holds for the rest of this chat's run, even where the project's hosts list has
  allowed the host since the chat started** (#3407).
- **Keep blocked also takes back the chat's own Allow of that host.** It leaves the Granted list,
  the chat's next start no longer has it, and the chat's browsers end, as when an Allow is
  removed (#3407).
- **A sandboxed project with a keyring vault starts its chats again.** Both defaults together
  refused every chat. On macOS purlis now writes every keyring item so that only purlis's app
  reads it without asking you, so the sandbox holds a keyring vault for Claude Code, Codex and
  opencode, and Claude Code chats start. An item written before is moved under that rule the
  next time purlis reads it, and the vault's next `purlis secret get`, `cp` or `exec` says so
  once. The `purlis` command is another program to the Keychain, so it now asks you before it
  reads a secret. Answer each ask as it comes: Always Allow for the `purlis` command lets any
  chat that runs the command read that secret without asking. A fix that takes the command out
  of the way is planned (#1180). On Linux, where the system keyring keeps no such rule, a Claude
  Code chat is still refused, and the refusal says how to go on: start that chat without the
  sandbox from the new-chat picker, or move those secrets to a plain-file or 1Password vault
  (ruling V90, #1179).
- A chat waiting on you keeps its ✋ and its Inbox card when its own background work wakes it after the wait on that work ran out or a sandbox block ended it. Only your reply clears the wait.
- Create project on this Mac makes the project. Pressing it did nothing, because the forge question it raised was never shown.
- A line about a project that has moved now sits in the launcher's page, and the ways in stay put.
- The launcher's ways in keep one height at a narrow window.
- **A push through purlis sends its Git LFS objects first.** A repo save, `purlis worktree push`,
  `purlis change push` and a project's first publish upload each object the commits going out
  need before the push leaves, to the push's own server with its one credential. Where that
  cannot be done, the push does not happen and purlis says what to do, so a forge is never left
  with a pointer nobody can download (#4399).
- **A branch's file tab opened after a file's own tab shows at once.** It no longer waits for the
  light editor to load a second time, with "Opening the light editor…" in its place (#4799).
- **Blocked lately and `purlis doctor` count every refusal.** The same block repeated within a
  minute was shown once and counted once; the repeats are now counted on a line of their own
  once the minute is over (#1681).
- **A local skill's grade that was running when the skill was renamed shows under its new name.**
  And after a rename of a local skill, a skill made at its new name some other way (an install,
  a draft's accept, an update that brings it, or a folder made by hand after the first was
  removed by hand) no longer shows the renamed skill's grades from before (#4104).
- **Checking whether a local project is in use no longer waits on a stuck process list.** On
  macOS, purlis asks `lsof` which folders your other programs work in before it moves a local
  project. It now asks `lsof` not to make kernel calls that can block, and gives it 5 seconds.
  When `lsof` takes longer, purlis ends it, leaves the project where it is and says the process
  list could not be read. Before, a stuck `lsof` held the launch with no limit (#2091).
- **Swift and clang builds work in a wrapped opencode chat.** A wrapped chat's `TMP`, `TEMP`,
  `xcrun`'s cache and clang's module cache now point into its own temp directory, so `swiftc`
  and `clang -fmodules` no longer fail on macOS's per-user cache folder. `mktemp` without a
  path, and Swift or Objective-C programs that use `NSTemporaryDirectory`, still ask the system
  for its per-user temp folder, which no sandboxed chat may write; `mktemp -p "$TMPDIR"` works
  (#1120).
- **A sandboxed Claude Code chat's block notice names macOS's per-user folders.** A block in
  the per-user temp folder says so and gives `mktemp -p "$TMPDIR"` as the way round. A block in
  the per-user cache folder says Swift and clang builds cannot write it there yet, instead of
  reading as "a temporary folder" (#1120).
- **Make the runner again keeps the old runner's conversations.** When a pool's runner was removed outside purlis and you make it again, purlis now checks the old runner's home first. If it holds your chats' conversations, purlis keeps it, and Devices offers to bring them back to the new runner or discard them. Before, the old home was removed with them (#4859).
- **A pool's runner removed outside purlis says so, and is made again on your word** (#4149).
  When a Docker pool's container was removed outside purlis (a cleanup, say), every chat start
  there failed with "No such container" and purlis tried to link again forever. Now purlis tells
  that apart from a runner that is only away, stopped or suspended, stops trying, and says it
  plainly on the pool's row and when a start is refused, with **Make the runner again**: a runner
  made from the pool's own image and limits, paired, and given the pool's profiles again. It
  takes up the old home volume where that is still there, with its sign-ins; where the volume went
  too, it says so, and the profiles are signed in again.
- **Opening or closing a chat with many chats open no longer recompiles every chat's sandbox**
  (#2157). The check for chats running on an older sandbox, which runs on each open and close,
  compiles once per distinct kind of start, so with fifty chats started alike it does one
  compile where it did fifty.
- **What purlis tells a chat about memory no longer leads it to a permission prompt.** The
  skills, the briefing, the hooks' reminders, the first task and the docs now name the
  `memory_add` and `persona_remember` tools first. Where they give the command, it names the
  chat's own persona or workspace (`purlis persona remember <persona> …`,
  `purlis workspace remember -w <workspace> …`), and where the text knows that name it is
  written in. Those are the forms a Claude Code chat runs without asking. A check in CI now
  fails when a shipped text gives the command without the name (#3880).
- **A menu row that turns unavailable under the keyboard says why.** The row used to be drawn
  afresh as it gained its reason, so on macOS and Linux, where purlis runs in WebKit, the tooltip
  did not show. The row now stays as it is, the keyboard stays on it, and its reason shows at once
  (#4659).
- **A menu's rows no longer overlap.** In a menu taller than its room, such as a chat tab's
  menu in a project with many personas, every row was squeezed to one line and drawn over the
  description of the row above it. Each row is now as tall as its title and description, and the
  menu stays inside the window and scrolls. Menu rows are written one step smaller, and a
  description shown in a row is no longer repeated in a tooltip.
- **A menu opened with a screen reader lands on its first row** (#3105). Opening a menu or a
  submenu with VoiceOver or another screen reader left focus on the list itself. It now lands on
  the first row. Opening with the pointer or the keyboard works as before.
- **More menus opened with a screen reader land on a row** (#4304). A part of the "while you were
  away" summary now lands on its first row, and a tab's task counts land on the chat the tab shows,
  or the first line. They used to leave focus on the list.
- **Merge as it stands merges only what you were shown.** If, between the fresh look and the
  merge itself, a save pushed a new commit onto the pull request or its checks failed, the
  merge is now refused with "The request changed since you looked" instead of going ahead.
  Look at it again and decide on what is there (#1978).
- **`purlis migrate` makes git ignore the right folder when a project's path holds `*`, `?`,
  `[` or `\`.** The line it adds to the repository's `info/exclude` matches that path and no
  other (#1285).
- **A half of the Panel whose only views are extension panels no longer contributed** is not
  drawn as an empty half; it comes back with its panels (#1752).
- purlis refuses to record a branch folder's base under a name git does not take as a branch, as it already did for an empty one, and leaves the clone's git config untouched. `purlis doctor` names a clone whose config holds `[branch ""]`, which stops every fetch and push in it, with the command that removes it, and a clone whose config git cannot read at all, in git's own words.
- **Names in more command output show their hidden characters.** A colour code, a
  direction-changing or a zero-width character in a deleted skill's name, a name a skill's
  text uses, a commit's author or subject in `purlis skill versions`, an extension command's
  name or title, a session record's title, a curation action's label, or an earlier
  `worktree done` read from the log, is now written as `⟦U+XXXX⟧` instead of reaching your
  terminal, where it could hide or reorder the rest of the line. purlis's own colour is
  unchanged (#3173).
- **The new-chat dialog never opens on a persona or icon from before a change.** Its kept
  answer is dropped as soon as a persona or a profile's own icon changes, even before the plane
  watch tells it, and a change made while the dialog reads is never kept (#4885).
- **New project names the file it writes.** *Make this repo itself the project* says it writes
  `purlis.toml`, which a new project is written with, not the old `charter.toml` (#1719).
- **A New tab opens faster: the picker compiles each harness's sandbox once, not once per
  profile** (#2179). With several profiles of one harness listed, the picker does one compile
  for them all, and still checks each profile's program for itself.
- **A chat nobody is at, started with no sandbox, is told that before a dispatch limit.** It
  starts no chat as another persona whatever the limits say, so it is no longer told to wait for
  a slot (#1543).
- **The welcome no longer shows "Step 1 of 2" to someone who has been through the steps.** A
  window with no project drew its welcome before it had read where this machine got to, so the
  count showed for a moment and then went. The count now waits for that read; the doors don't.
- **A refusal no longer outlasts its cause.** The window's line about a picker or a shell that
  could not open stayed after the next try worked, and a workspace read that failed once kept
  its line after a later read succeeded. Each now clears when the same action succeeds
  (NO-4, #1231).
- **A notification clicked with the window closed brings it back at the Inbox.** On macOS, with
  every window hidden, clicking an ask's notification or the dock icon shows the window holding
  the project that notification was about, and it opens the Inbox at that chat's group (#1694).
- **npm's and pnpm's own setting names no longer read as an npm token.** The commit scan and
  every guard built on it took `npm_` and any sixteen more letters, digits, `_` or `-` for a
  token, so a file that set pnpm's store or cache folder through npm's environment spelling was
  refused as holding a forge token. An npm token's body is letters and digits only, and the
  rule now asks for that, so the setting names pass and a real token is still refused (#1364).
- **The merge view's differences can be taken from the keyboard.** Under the file changed on
  disk, a button per difference, named by the lines it takes, follows the edit in the Tab order
  (#1862).
- **Two branch changes on one repo run one at a time.** Remove, Done, New branch and Merge from
  the window now wait for one another on the same repo, instead of the second failing on git's
  lock in git's words. One still waiting after ten seconds is refused with a sentence that says
  another change to the repo is running (#1610).
- **Starting the app asks the Keychain about a forge sign-in once, not several times.** Each of
  purlis's processes now reads a forge account's item once and keeps the token in its own memory
  for as long as it runs. A listing no longer asks again whether the item is there, and git's
  credential helper reads the token without asking that first. After an update of an ad-hoc
  signed build, macOS still asks once per process, until builds are signed with a Developer ID
  (#2658) (#2656).
- **An Allow in the Inbox waits for its row to settle.** Pressed just after the ask was drawn,
  or after another ask moved it, it allows nothing and says so, as an update's Allow does.
- **The Inbox's Notices show while they list only a doctor finding** (#1695).
- **A reply from the Inbox is checked before it is sent.** If the chat no longer waits on a
  reply, nothing is typed into it and the Inbox says so. Home and End move the cursor in the
  reply box, a chat waiting on a reply that also has a reason to be listed gets the box, and the
  keyboard stays in the list after an answer takes its ask away (#1700).
- **A connection whose hold ran out says so.** A sandbox block whose connection purlis held for
  your answer, and gave up on after a minute, now says that nobody answered in time and that an
  Allow tells the chat to run it again (#1709).
- **What an ask names is drawn safely.** A folder's or a chat's name in an ask is drawn with
  every character that draws as nothing written out, in the Inbox and on the pane (#1688).
- **An Inbox Notice that grants something waits to settle,** as an ask's Allow does: a press on
  it just after it was drawn or moved does nothing, and says why (#1695).
- **A chat's browser keeps the persona its sandbox was started for.** After a handoff, or for a
  chat on no persona, the sites its browser reaches and the Asks about them follow the persona
  whose grants the chat started with, until it starts again. Its browser logins still use the
  vaults of the persona it was started as (#2691).
- **The Notice of the project's browser sites says nothing in a project without the sandbox**,
  where those sites reach no browser. A site you were shown is no longer told as taken out when
  the project turns the sandbox off (#2691).
- **A project whose chats hang as they start no longer holds up every other project's chats at a
  launch.** One project's chats take all the places a launch starts chats in but one, so the
  other projects' chats come back at once instead of one project at a time, minutes apart. A
  launch now starts three or four chats at once, by the machine's cores (#4986).
- **A reporting handoff's report could sit unread.** It was left for the asking chat's next
  turn and nothing started that turn, `purlis dispatch wait` refused its chat and `list` did
  not show it. As a task, its report starts the asking chat's turn where purlis may type into
  that chat, and can be waited for (#1515).
- **`purlis handoff --help` is no longer refused for lacking a heredoc.** purlis's Bash hook
  lets `--help` and `-h` through as the word right after `handoff`, where nothing is fed to
  the command and the call holds no other handoff. Every other refusal stands: from a
  sub-agent, inside a string a shell runs, with a spelling purlis cannot read, and beside a
  file, a pipe, a here-string or a live substitution (#1515).
- **The update channel reads the same everywhere in the window.** Moving this machine to another
  update channel in Settings › You › This machine now shows on the title bar's updater at once,
  and a move made from the updater shows in Settings, rather than after each one's next read.
  This machine also reads the store again when the window comes back into focus or into view,
  and after a project is pinned or unpinned on the project strip, so a change made elsewhere is
  shown while the group is open (#1240).
- **purlis's reads no longer take `index.lock` from under your `git add`.** Every
  `git status` purlis runs now leaves the index as it is, so a commit or an agent's `add` in
  the same repo is never refused because purlis was reading it (FD-11, #651).
- **Out-of-view marks follow every box around a frame.** A snapshot or a find marks a frame's
  element `(out of view)` when any box around the frame hides it: a box on the page, or one in
  a frame further out. The frame is placed inside its own border and padding, at the size the
  page draws it, for frames from the page's own site and from others alike (#2840).
- **A chat no longer stops on a permission prompt for its own work.** A Claude Code chat now
  runs its own memory, todos and branch folder without Claude Code asking: the tools
  `todo_add`, `todo_done`, `memory_add`, `persona_remember`, `workspace_vision` and
  `workspace_section`; `purlis persona remember <its persona>` (`--shared` included) and
  `purlis workspace remember` and `note` with `-w <its workspace>`; `purlis ws todo` to list;
  and `purlis worktree add -w <its workspace>`, `update`, `push`, `done`, `abandon` and
  `list`. A line that names another persona or workspace is still asked about. purlis's reads (`recall`, `persona show` and
  `list`, `workspace list` and `current`, `docs show`, `news`, `theme check` and `list`,
  `dispatch list` with arguments) run unasked too, and `ask_operator` asks you its question
  once instead of twice. Anything that reaches past the chat's own work, such as `secret exec`,
  `forget`, `move-memory`, `save` or `clone`, is still asked about, and your own `ask` or `deny`
  rules still win (#3829).
- **Focus the next region and Focus the previous region from the palette always move the
  keyboard.** On a busy machine the palette sometimes put the keyboard back where you opened it
  from after the row had moved it, so it stayed where it was. The move is now made once the
  palette has handed the keyboard back (#1769).
- **A pane's warnings show when there is more to scroll** (#3168). In a narrow pane the warnings
  above the terminal can be taller than their room, and the lower buttons looked cut off. A soft
  fade into the pane's background now shows at the top or bottom edge while there is more to
  scroll that way.
- **⌘J brings the Panel out where nothing of it is drawn.** Where the Panel's only half left
  holds an extension's panel that no extension contributes now, that half is not drawn, and the
  first ⌘J (or Ctrl+J) hid a Panel nobody could see. It now shows the Panel, as the palette's
  Show the panel row already said (#1752).
- **Each tab keeps its own split sizes.** Switching to another tab split the same way no longer
  draws it at the sizes of the tab you left (#4755).
- **The last per-session stores stop growing.** When the app opens a project it now also
  collects, a month after they were last written, the commit gate's per-session cooldowns, the
  first-edit-in-a-clone markers, the saved-record lines a workspace's chat left for a `Stop` that
  never ran, and a session's ephemeral memory, which goes whole once every file in it is a month
  old. A chat the project brings back keeps its own, however old (#1004).
- **A sandbox Notice about macOS's per-user folders reads true for each of them.** A write
  refused in `/var/folders/…/0` or `…/X` was said with the temporary folder's sentence; the
  sentence now names the per-user folders and gives `mktemp -p "$TMPDIR"` as the way round for
  the temporary one. The cache folder's Notice no longer names one harness. A Swift program's
  refused write, which Foundation reports as `NSCocoaErrorDomain Code=513` with the file's path,
  is now read as a block (#1416).
- **A persona in the Personas view opens its page from the strip outside every workspace.** With
  that strip in front (a chat that works in no workspace, or that strip's empty tab), the view
  listed the plane's personas but pressing one opened nothing. The palette had no row for it
  either (#4758).
- **The Personas view lists the project's personas with no workspace focused**, as it does at the
  project root; it said "No workspace focused." although personas are the project's (#1686).
- **A chat whose workspace and persona pin more than 64 skills between them says so.** Each list
  under 64 is accepted, but a chat reads both together and reads none of them past 64. Its
  Skills chip now takes the warning look, and Use skill… names both, how many each pins, and
  opens either one's Skill studio in one press (#3391).
- **A pool keeps working after its runner is made again or updated**. The first chat after
  **Make the runner again** was refused with "no persona on this plane", since the new runner was
  never sent the project. And once a runner updated beside an old one had taken over its sign-ins,
  every chat on that pool was refused, saying its profile "names a folder outside purlis's profiles
  folder". Now the new runner is sent the project, and carrying sign-ins leaves a running runner's
  folders where they are.
- Pool setup reading how a profile stands on a runner no longer fetches a harness there.
- **Pool setup's Sign-ins step measures each profile against what the pool's runner takes.** On a
  runner from before 1.64, which stages less than a pool's limit allows, the step said a profile
  fit when a send would refuse it. It now holds each profile to the lower of the two, where the
  runner can say which version it runs (#4719).
- **Signing a profile out of a pool says "signed out" only once the runner confirms it.** Where
  its harness's status check can't say, Settings › Pools now tells you purlis could not confirm
  the sign-out, and to look at the pool's row.
- **A sign-in on a runner is tighter about where the browser's answer goes.** The answer reaches
  only the login that sign-in started, on the runner it started on, and once. Cancelling while
  the runner fetches its harness no longer goes on to start the login.
- **A `pr-merge` save merges where the forge has no auto-merge.** A private repo on GitHub's
  Free plan has no auto-merge, so a save's pull request stayed open and nothing said why. Now,
  purlis merges it itself once it is ready: when the forge says it may merge and every check
  on the pushed commit has passed, asked again on every save and fetch. A failing check, a
  conflict or a review the branch requires leaves the pull request open, and the save says
  why, with its link. GitLab merge requests are merged the same way.
- **Printing a file that quotes a refusal no longer raises a Block.** `sed -n`, `cat`, `grep` or
  `git show` over a test or a log that quotes a socket, host or folder refusal brought up a
  Notice and told the chat to wait, although nothing was refused. A line that only reads or
  prints now raises nothing from what it printed, and neither does a background command's
  output read back. A failed command's own error, the sandbox's own report and purlis's proxy
  still raise a Block, in Claude Code, Codex and opencode chats alike (#1972).
- A harness profile can no longer be named after any `purlis` command: the names a profile may
  not take are now the command line's own words, checked against its parser, so `purlis serve`,
  `purlis profile` and every command added later are refused as profile names like the rest.
  A profile you already have under one of these names is now listed as refused: rename its
  `[harness.<name>]` table (#2422).
- **A pool's Remove no longer deletes a harness's own folder under a running chat.** Forgetting a
  desktop's adopted folder on a runner is refused while a chat with no profile runs there on that
  harness, with a sentence that says to end the chat first.
- **Taking a profile off a pool clears its Ask in every open project**, not only the one you were
  looking at.
- **A project's pool asks only about workspaces that ran there.** When a chat ends, or the window
  comes back into focus, purlis fetches work back from a project's pool only for workspaces that have run a chat there. A
  project is marked as not held on a pool only while a workspace follows that pool. If a workspace
  folder is removed or renamed outside purlis, a pool chosen for it becomes This machine when the
  project opens, so a new folder with that name never runs on a pool nobody chose for it (#4591).
- A chat on a runner now gets a moved project's skills even when the desktop that started it has not pulled the move yet.
- **A commit you make in an editor opened from a chat is no longer stamped as the agent's.** An
  editor or terminal started from a chat keeps the chat's environment, and its commits used to
  carry the chat's `Assisted-by` and `Charter-*` trailers. purlis now stamps a commit, and a
  `purlis save`, only when it runs below the program the app started for that chat. Commits a
  sandboxed chat makes on Linux get no trailers yet, and neither do commits on Windows: where
  purlis cannot tell, it leaves the message as written. On macOS a sandboxed chat's commits
  are stamped like any other chat's (#1018, #1407).
- **Provenance trailers follow the commit message they are added to.** A message written with
  CRLF line endings gets its trailer lines with CRLF too, and a `git commit -m` message whose last
  line starts with `#` gets the trailers after that line rather than before it, since git keeps
  such a line when no editor ran (#1021).
- **Purlis light's waiting ring reads as amber.** It was a dark hue laid thin, which read as
  tan-grey. It is now its hue's purest colour at dark's strength, as the washes are (#3182).
- **Purlis light's warning, danger and diff washes now show their colour.** The amber behind a
  waiting count or a pane's warning, the red behind a danger notice, and the diff's red and green
  were drawn as a dark hue laid thin over a light background, so they read as grey. Each one is
  now its hue's purest colour, at the same strength (#2924).
- **A chat on `purlis serve` is recorded as one on this machine is.** A chat that host starts
  writes its run and its sandbox decision in that host's event log; when it ends, its
  sub-agents' runs end with it, and a dispatch it worked that ended with no window there ends as
  one that went without its report (#2494).
- **`purlis serve` tidies the skills folders it lays out** (Skill studio preview, #2879). A
  runner, a Docker host or a Kubernetes pod lays out a folder of skills for each chat it starts,
  and never removed them. Now it removes those no running chat uses as it starts and after each
  chat it hosts ends, as the app does.
- **A question from a task keeps its line breaks.** In a chat's pane, a question a task wrote
  over several lines showed each line break as `⟦U+000A⟧` on one line. It is now drawn over the
  lines the task wrote, in the markdown a chat's text is drawn in, as is the asking chat's note:
  a link opens only when you press it, and raw HTML is dropped (#5213).
- **Questions from tasks sit under the pane's head, in its notices band, and close.** They were
  drawn above the head and took up to half the pane with nothing to close them. Each question
  now has a Close, which puts it away from that pane only: it stays in the Inbox and on ✋ until
  you answer it. The band's Minimise folds the note about where questions go into the bell,
  and its buttons no longer sit over the question's title (#5213).
- **Quiet words can be read in every built-in theme.** Words the window dimmed with an opacity
  are drawn in a quieter text tier instead. In Purlis light, the values in a project's trust ask
  had come to 3.9:1 and an empty list's sentence to 3.4:1, under the 4.5:1 text floor. A pane's
  header words are solid too (#3637, #3790).
- **A chat writes nothing committed to a project this purlis may only read.** In a project
  that requires a feature this purlis lacks, or declares a newer format, a chat's hooks no
  longer log its skill uses into `personas/_skills/`. A session record, memory (a workspace's
  or a persona's), a todo, a workspace's manifest, vision or sections, a new workspace, and a
  handoff's row in the dispatch log are each refused, saying nothing was written and why,
  whichever way the write was asked for. The project is not saved (committed or pushed), by
  auto-save after a chat ends or otherwise, and no extension's program is started at a chat's
  start or told of an event there. Every guard still refuses what it refused before. The window
  says so in the project's tab before a release carries this rule (#826).
- **Removing a pool whose runner is on another Docker engine says what stays there.** It asks in those
  words, touches nothing on the engine Docker reaches now, and names the container and volume to remove
  once Docker points back. A pool whose engine is gone for good can still be removed (#4325).
- **Removing a repo that was never cloned no longer leaves a folder behind unnamed.** When a
  workspace names a repo that is not cloned, but something is at its path (a plain folder, a
  folder whose `.git` is not a real one, a file or a link), removing the repo from the workspace
  is refused, says what is there, and keeps the repo's row (#1249).
- **A renamed workspace's open tabs follow its new name.** A todo, a memory, the workspace's
  changes, its archive, a piece's files and a session record that were open when you renamed the
  workspace kept reading it under the old name, and said there was no such workspace. They now
  read it under the new name, and opening one of them again brings that tab forward instead of
  opening a second. The workspace's settings, changes and repo instructions tabs and a piece's
  files tab come back at the next launch under the new name (#1248).
- **The Notice after a sandbox setting changes hears more.** It asks again when the window comes
  back into focus, which catches a sandbox file written by hand or by another window and the
  policy an administrator sets, and when a task with no tab starts or ends (#1462).
- **Allowing something for a chat while it restarted hung its project.** Pressing **Allow** on
  a sandbox block's Notice while that chat was already restarting left the restart waiting for
  good: the chat never came back, and closing any chat of that project, allowing anything else
  and the list of chats owed a restart all waited behind it until purlis was quit. What is
  allowed meanwhile is now carried to the chat's new run, as it was meant to be (#1428).
- **Restart now on a persona's hosts Notice works again after a restart that was refused.** The
  button used to stay dead once pressed. A refused restart now also says what to do: send the
  chat a message first if it has only just started, or use Start fresh (#1428).
- **Chats of one project put back at a launch no longer fail to start because another started
  beside them.** Each start's write of the project's package-cache settings has a file of its
  own, so a chat is no longer refused with "could not make …/cargo/config.toml … No such file or
  directory" and left for Retry now (#4980).
- **Collecting month-old session files keeps one written to while it was being read.** A
  trace that gained a line, or a file another took the name of, during the sweep is kept for the
  next one (#1027).
- A chat on a pool's runner can ask, note, tell and answer through dispatch again. What it sends is queued on the runner, and the runner now sends it on to the app itself, once and in order, including whatever was queued while the runner's link was down, once the link is back. Before, every such message stayed on the runner and was never delivered.
- **Devices: hours this week no longer count a gap purlis could not see.** When a runner's
  container was stopped and started again outside purlis between two reads, Docker says only
  the newer run's times, and purlis counted everything from the older run's start to the newer
  one's as running. Where Docker does not say when the older run ended, purlis now counts none
  of that gap, so a pool's hours and money are not raised by a time it never saw (#3720).
- **Devices: a pool's hours this week stay whole when the record is full.** When
  `runner-hours.jsonl` is over its size, purlis now drops first the runs that ended before this
  week, which count nothing toward it, then the rest by when they ended, and a run still open
  last. Before, it dropped the runs that started first, so a long run could lose its hours this
  week (#3723).
- **A sign-in on a runner that had to stop says why.** Where a pool or its runner changed under it,
  or another sign-in took its place, the strip says it failed and for what reason, not that it was
  cancelled (#4277).
- **Choose another plan keeps the keyboard in a move's notice**, on the first plan's button, rather
  than dropping it to the page's start (#4278).
- **A dispatch or handoff held because its chat runs on a pool says so.** The chat is told it waits
  for the person's Approve in the window, not that its persona lacks a grant (#4148).
- **A pool's runner is no longer called removed when Docker points at another engine.** purlis now
  keeps which engine made each runner. When another engine answers, the pool's row says so,
  **Make the runner again** is not offered, and the runner's chats come back once Docker points back
  (#4166). This holds for runners made from now on: a runner made before this keeps today's check.
- **A runner made again takes its sign-ins from its own home whatever the clocks say.** purlis
  compares the home's own creation time with the one kept when the runner was made, and a volume made
  again under the same name gives nothing (#4167).
- **A runner's sign-in answer goes only to a socket that login's own programs hold.** Where the
  runner's system can't say who holds a socket, it goes where the login was found listening, as
  before.
- **A runner's keep also clears Codex's `.env`**, which no desktop sends.
- **A page's listed title is left empty when it is as long as a title can be and the page keeps a
  text**, so a cut can't leave part of that text in the list.
- **Signing a profile in on a fresh runner works** (#4007). Settings › Pools › Sign in no longer
  fails with "purlis could not find a program called claude" on a runner where no chat has
  started yet. The runner first fetches the harness version the profile pins, from its vendor's
  release and checked against the SHA-256 the vendor publishes, the same as a chat's first start
  does, and the sign-in shell says it is fetching. A fetch that cannot reach the vendor or does
  not match its checksum says why and signs nothing in. The profile's row stops saying its
  harness cannot say whether it is signed in once that version is on the runner: asking about
  the profile starts the fetch in the background, and Ask again shows the answer.
- **A runner chat's tool reaches the hosts you allowed for the chat since it started.** Allow on
  a block's Notice for a chat on a pool now reaches its declared tool's next run on the runner,
  and taking the Allow back narrows that run again, as for a chat on this machine (#3407).
- **A runner chat's tool Ask goes once its command has gone.** When the link to a pool's runner
  goes down, each command of its that waits on your Allow is let go of: its Ask leaves the Inbox,
  no vault is read for it, and nothing is sent. Values you allowed for a command that went
  meanwhile are not sent once purlis has heard it went (#3408).
- **Keep blocked also ends a host's earlier Allow for this chat** (#3407).
- **Safe remove no longer ends in a refusal.** When a chat runs `purlis workspace remove`
  under the sandbox, purlis now asks you on that chat's tab and in the Inbox: **Remove…** or
  **Keep**. Remove… opens Delete workspace, the same dialog the sidebar opens, with the same
  guard; nothing is removed until you press Delete there. The chat is told what you decided
  on its next turn. Before, the command was refused and you had to find the workspace and
  remove it yourself. Removing a persona or a branch folder from a sandboxed chat is still
  refused.
- **Two dispatches under one task name at once start one task.** The refusal of a task name a
  chat already has open is decided under the lock that reserves the task's slot, so a task that
  was let through and is still starting counts as open (#3795).
- **More sandbox blocks in macOS's per-user folders are shown, and sorted right.** A write
  refused in `/var/folders/…/0` or `…/X` was taken for the chat's own temporary folder and
  dropped. A path written through `/System/Volumes/Data` was sorted as a system folder. swiftc's
  and xcrun's own words for a refused write were not read. Each now shows as a block in macOS's
  per-user folders, and none offers a grant (#1416).
- **Builds work in a sandboxed chat.** With the *toolchains* preset on, a project's sandboxed
  chats download into package caches of the project's own, so `cargo build`, `npm install`,
  `pip install`, `go build`, Gradle, yarn and pnpm no longer fail with "Operation not permitted".
  purlis keeps them in `cache-homes/<project>` under its data home (on macOS,
  `~/Library/Application Support/purlis/cache-homes/`; remove a project's folder there to free
  its space) and points each tool at them; your own caches are only read. The project's cargo home starts with where your crates come from (registries and source
  replacements), never your tokens. Each project downloads once into its own caches, which
  costs disk (#1337).
- **A vendored or local-registry source in your cargo config works in a sandboxed chat.** A
  relative `directory` or `local-registry` under `[source]` in your own cargo config is now
  resolved where cargo resolves it, the folder above your cargo home, before it is copied into
  the project's cargo home, so it no longer points into purlis's cache folder. A path that climbs
  out of that folder with `..`, leads out of it through a link, or names no folder there is left
  out, with its whole `[source]` entry, and the copied file says so. The sandbox grants nothing
  new for it (#1364).
- **Only the certificate check is told as the certificate check.** A sandbox report naming a
  system service that merely has the certificate check's service name inside its own is sorted
  as a system service and shown by its whole name (#1927).
- **Allow on a blocked local socket keeps the socket its Notice named.** If the path leads
  somewhere else by the time you press, nothing is allowed and the Notice shows the block
  again as it stands (#1927).
- **"Not now" to what a project expects is an answer to what was shown.** If a path the
  project declared comes to lead to another socket, the question is asked again (#1927).
- **A sandbox Notice's sentences stand whole.** A block of purlis's own operation now says it was
  purlis's own, and a purlis bug, in a sentence of its own, so it no longer runs on from a block
  sentence that ends in a full stop. A write refused in any of macOS's per-user folders gives the
  chat's own `$TMPDIR` as the way round, and no longer names `mktemp`, whose option fits none of
  the folders that are not a temporary one (#1416).
- **`cargo` is on a chat's PATH.** A chat now also searches `~/.cargo/bin` and the folder that
  Homebrew's rustup uses, so `cargo` and `rustc` resolve as they do in a terminal (#1345).
- **A refused write names the file.** A purlis command used to print only "Operation not
  permitted (os error 1)". It now names the file it was writing. In a chat the app started
  sandboxed, it also says the chat's sandbox refused the write. It still exits non-zero (#1345).
- **Git on the project from a sandboxed workspace chat is explained.** `git add`, `git commit`,
  `git fetch` and other git commands that take a lock on the project's own repository would stop
  on a lock file. They are now refused before they run, with a sentence that the app saves and
  syncs the project, from the Save button or the Saving view where auto-save is off (#1345).
- **The sandbox protects more of the scripts a project's configs run.** A script named
  without a `/` is protected where its program reads it as code: `bash hook.sh`,
  `awk -f sum.awk`, `python3 -m tools.x` and an MCP server's `node server.js`. The same
  holds when a launcher runs it (`uv run server.py`, `npx tsx server.ts`,
  `env node server.js`). A runner's own subcommands (`bun test`, `deno task`) and a Python
  package's folder stay writable. A file named without its extension is protected under
  each name its runner tries (`node -r ./hook` covers `hook.js`, `ruby -r./x` covers
  `x.rb`). Also covered: the value of an assignment (`BASH_ENV=./x.sh`, git's
  `-c core.hooksPath=./h`), each value after a compiler's `-Wl,`, and both readings of
  `-f./a=b.awk`. A folder named only after an `=` (`CARGO_TARGET_DIR=./target`) stays
  writable, unless the variable loads code (`BASH_ENV`, `NODE_OPTIONS`, `LD_PRELOAD`,
  `GIT_SSH_COMMAND` and the like), whose value is always protected. A later-letter value is matched to the project through a link, its data-volume
  name or another letter case. The folder of the socket a chat reports on is protected
  under each of its names. A start whose sandbox profile would be too long to hand over is
  refused with a reason and a way out, not a spawn error (#1418).
- **A sandboxed Claude Code chat can reach purlis again.** A `purlis` command run from a
  sandboxed Claude Code chat could not connect to the app, so a handoff printed a command
  instead of opening its tab, and every write the app makes on a chat's behalf failed. The
  chat's sandbox now allows the one socket its own hooks report on, and no other socket. Codex
  and opencode chats already could. On Linux, Claude Code's sandbox cannot allow a single
  socket, so a sandboxed Claude Code chat there still reaches none (#1328).
- **Saves to a forge on a port of its own sign in with its purlis account.** A project or repo
  whose origin is on a forge declared with a port, such as `git.example.com:8443`, is now that
  forge's, so its saves and fetches use the purlis account signed in on that host and port,
  held to the recorded remote as on any host. Before, they found no forge and did not push
  (#1864).
- A secret ask from a chat purlis started no longer fails with "the app that started this chat
  did not answer in time". The chat took its own harness for an unknown one and stopped waiting
  after 25 seconds, while the app held the ask for 90. It now waits past the app's hold and hears
  pending, filled or declined (#5192).
- **A brokered `purlis secret exec` hands on a variable that is not UTF-8.** A chat's variable
  whose name or value is not UTF-8, such as a path in another encoding, was dropped without a
  word on its way to the command the app runs. It is now handed on as its bytes (#1407).
- **The theme check reads more of what stands on a surface in the tints.** A see-through button
  look on an opaque popover, panel or dialog fill is now read in each workspace tint, and so is a
  look only a set of states draws, such as hovered and pressed at once. A custom theme that fell
  short there now draws the surface's family default, and the check says why (#4607).
- **`purlis persona default` no longer breaks a `charter.toml` it cannot edit cleanly.** When
  `[persona]` is written as an inline table, as a dotted key, or behind a header with a comment,
  setting or clearing the default persona used to add a second `[persona]`, which left a file
  nothing could read. It now refuses, says why, and leaves the file as it was (FD-26, #663).
- **Settings › Project › Dispatch says when the project's grants you accepted are not
  checked.** In the first moments after purlis starts, it has not checked them against the
  project's git history yet: the next dispatch checks first, and where the history reads they
  count as before. Where the history cannot be read, none of them counts: a chat you are at asks
  you on its tab, and one nobody is at is refused and listed under Needs you. Only the arrival
  Notice said any of this; the table now says which at the top, with Read again, and greys
  each such grant with a note (#1543).
- **Not on my machine is no longer offered for a teammate's grant limited to one workspace
  that nobody here accepted.** It already allowed nothing here, and pressing it recorded a
  decline in purlis's event log for a grant this machine never followed. It is refused now
  if asked for, and nothing is recorded (#1543).
- **Settings' list of dispatch grants no longer holds the window while it asks git** who
  committed each of the project's grants. The list, and the list a Revoke answers with, are
  read off the window's thread (#1543).
- **Settings' dispatch table reads again once the first check after a launch lands.** In the
  first moments after a launch it says the project's grants you accepted are not checked
  against the project's history yet. It used to stay that way until you pressed *Read again*;
  it now draws what that first check found on its own, and reads again each time purlis says
  what waits of the project's grants may have moved. A check that cannot read the history is
  said as such, and never draws those grants as counting (#1543).
- **Settings no longer takes the keyboard after you have moved on.** A way into Settings that is
  still waiting for its tab is dropped on your next click or key press, so a tab drawn late
  does not pull the keyboard away from where you went. With two Settings tabs of one level side
  by side, the one in the focused pane takes the keyboard. Escape or Cancel on the start-chat
  dialog puts the keyboard back on the `+` that opened it (#1600).
- **Settings › Repos keeps ticks you have not applied.** Ticking a repo to clone or unticking
  one to remove, then opening another group of the workspace's Settings and coming back, used to
  forget the ticks. They are now kept until you apply them, and a tick the disk already agrees
  with is dropped (#1192).
- **Every way into Settings puts the keyboard there.** The palette's Settings…, ⌘, and the app
  menu's Settings…, the gears, a doctor row's or a notice's "Fix it in Settings", and the level
  switcher now leave the keyboard on the current group in the Settings tab's group list, also
  when the tab was already open and is only brought forward. A dialog or drawer closed by such a
  link no longer hands the keyboard back to the button that opened it (#1206).
- **A link to a setting focuses it in its own Settings tab.** With two Settings tabs of the same
  level split side by side, a link that names a setting could put the focus in the other tab
  (#1292).
- **Settings writes nothing committed to a project this purlis may only read.** In a project
  that requires a feature this purlis lacks, or declares a newer format, a save of the shared
  settings file, a value moved between the shared and the machine's own file, a dispatch grant
  for everyone (given, moved or revoked), a forge added or removed, and a workspace's settings
  are each refused, saying nothing was written and why. The machine's own settings file is
  still written. A shared file that is not valid TOML still makes the project read-only, and
  Edit as TOML is still how it is mended: that one save writes it, and nothing else does
  (#1759).
- **Several hosts refused at once are one sandbox Notice.** A chat refused three hosts in one
  command showed only the newest, so allowing it restarted the chat into the next refusal. Now
  the chat's tab shows one Notice listing every host whole, and one Allow allows each of them,
  every host checked as a single one is, with one restart to take them all. A host refused
  while the answer is on its way joins the Notice and stays up, asking. A task's hosts are held
  the same way, so its session's question for several tasks stays answerable host by host.
- **A sandbox block Notice never ends with Dismiss alone.** A refused certificate check, a
  system service, starting a program, or a write whose folder the sandbox did not name now
  offers Start without the sandbox for this chat, saying why nothing can be allowed. Policy
  still has the last word, and says who set it.
- **Docker's "permission denied" no longer reads as a sandbox block on Linux.** There it means a
  user outside the docker group, which no grant or restart mends. On macOS, where the sandbox
  refuses Docker's socket in those words, it is still a block, and a socket refused with
  "operation not permitted" is one everywhere.
- After you answer a quiz, its box is cleared and Send is held, so a second Enter sends nothing
  (#4566).
- **The Shared settings file refuses `[chat_env]`.** Which variables a chat is started with is
  this machine's, and purlis reads it from the Local file alone. A save or a move in Settings
  that would have put `[chat_env]` in the committed file, where nothing reads it, now says so
  and writes nothing (#1197).
- **Shift+F10 straight after the keyboard reaches a row opens its menu** (#3797). When the arrow
  keys scrolled a list to a row, a Shift+F10 pressed within the same frame opened the row's menu
  and closed it again at once, so the key seemed to do nothing. A scroll closes the menu only
  when it moved the row the menu was opened on.
- **The shipped docs stop denying what this version does.** They said opencode chats, renaming
  a workspace and committing memory were not in this version; each is now described as it
  works. Every line that still says something is not in this version names the ticket that
  plans it (#1383).
- **Show what changed follows the branch.** A file's own tab and the Files tab's preview now
  read what the branch changed again when the branch moves, so *Show what changed* comes and
  goes with the branch instead of waiting for another file to be picked. While a comparison tab
  reads again after a move, the comparison it still draws is marked busy and says *Comparing
  … again…*; its *Open at line N* buttons stay usable (#1189).
- **The sign-in strip's terminal follows your theme** when it changes while the strip is open
  (#4122), and what you type there reaches the runner in order (#4123).
- **A Claude Code chat on a 200k window keeps its skills' descriptions.** Claude Code's own entries used to fill its limit and every plane skill's description was dropped. purlis now hands each chat a limit that holds them (#4610).
- Chats are told to load a skill with `skill_load` when their program says it does not know that skill, so one skill naming another that was not handed to the program no longer has to stop at "Unknown skill".
- `skill_load` no longer starts a skill of this chat when asked for another plugin's skill of the same short name.
- **A chat can no longer start a manual-only skill with `skill_load` by itself.** It loads one only when the person named it, as a harness keeps such a skill to the person (#4529).
- **The keyboard is never left behind a skill's page header.** On a scrolled skill page in the
  Skill studio, what the keyboard reaches under the header (its tabs, a row's button) is scrolled
  clear of the header, which stays in view on the panel's fill (#3944).
- **The Skill studio and other tabs open quicker once the Skills view has been shown.** Opening
  a tab no longer draws every skill's card in it again (#4351).
- **A skill source of more than 50 000 files is always refused whole** (Skill studio preview).
  On a busy machine its listing could be read cut short and refused for the wrong reason, and a
  listing whose read failed was taken as complete (#3115).
- **A skills folder purlis can't read whole is listed once and not read** (Skill studio
  preview, #3133). This applies to a repo's skills folder, your own skills folder and an
  opencode plugin or worktree folder, when one holds more than 2000 names or can't be read.
  The studio and `purlis skill list` name the folder and say why, instead of opening and checking
  every entry. A chat in a repo whose skills folder purlis can't read whole doesn't get the
  project's skills, since the repo might have its own copy of any of them.
- **A skill whose SKILL.md purlis doesn't read is listed, with the reason** (Skill studio
  preview, #3133). In a repo, that is a SKILL.md that is a link, a hard link or larger than
  256 KiB. In your own skills folder, it is a link or larger than 256 KiB. A hard link is read
  there, as the Nix store, `cp -al` and `rsync --link-dest` leave them. Such a skill used to
  vanish from the list.
- **A chat is told which project skills its repo leaves out** (Skill studio preview, #3213).
  On Codex and opencode, a repo's own copy of a skill replaces the project's, and a repo whose
  skills folder purlis can't read whole leaves out all of the project's skills. The chat's tab
  now names each skill it starts without because of its repo, and why. The Skill studio and
  `purlis skill list` list them under each program.
- **A repo skill named like a built-in one is said, not hidden** (Skill studio preview, #3027).
  A clone's own `secrets` skill is loaded by Claude Code and Codex beside purlis's built-in
  `secrets`, and a chat may use the repo's. The Skill studio used to call the repo's copy
  hidden. It now marks the built-in skill with the clash, the repo's row warns that its name
  is a built-in one's, and a chat started in that repo says so on its tab.
- **The Skill studio's chats open again with their prompt typed.** "Ask a chat to write outcome
  evals" never opened a chat: its prompt was longer than the 800 characters Claude Code draws a
  paste whole, so purlis typed nothing. "Improve from runs…", the trigger tests' "Ask a chat to
  write them" and "Ask a chat to draft a skill" ran over too for a long name. Each now types one
  short line, naming the job, the skill's folder and the new built-in `purlis-skill-studio`
  skill, which holds the steps and the formats (#4714).
- **A chat's Skills chip and its "skills changed" mark catch up after you create a workspace or a
  persona, and after a closed chat's record of what it could have made is cleared.** Before, each
  stayed as it was until some unrelated change to the project's instructions (#4884).
- **Every skill purlis ships names only `purlis`.** The smart-close skill still showed the old
  command for writing the session record, and the handoff, persona and update skills named old
  commands, files or variables. They all use the purlis names now, and Smart close's
  pre-allowed command is `purlis session record`, so writing the record does not stop on a
  permission prompt (#1329).
- In the Skills view, pressing a repo skill from a branch folder opens that copy's `SKILL.md`, not the Skill studio's Harness page, which lists only each clone's own folder. Open in Skill studio on that row now says why it cannot show the copy.
- The Skills view reads its repo skills again when the checkout the chat works in adds, deletes or changes one, or checks out a branch that does, so a deleted skill no longer stays listed.
- **The Skills view lists the repo skills of a chat's branch folder** (Skills, #4326). A chat in a
  branch folder listed no repo skills, though its harness has them. The view now lists the ones
  that folder holds, and Show in the Explorer view and Open the file go to the branch folder's copy.
- The Skills view's In this chat lists a Claude Code plugin's skills only when the chat really has the plugin. A plugin that is off, set off by the project, installed for another folder, installed after the chat started, or whose marketplace is gone is folded to one line under Left out, with why and, where a command fixes it, Copy command. Use on a plugin the chat has now types it, and the count of Claude Code's own skills follows.
- **The Skills view says when a workspace's pins aren't used** (Skill studio preview, #3432). Where no chat reads a workspace's pins (more than 64, or an entry that is no skill's name), a row's Unpin from this workspace says "Pinned, not used" and why. Pin to this workspace waits and says how to put the list right.
- **Splits survive a restart.** Two chats split side by side or stacked come back as you left
  them, with the sizes you dragged them to. So does a view beside a chat, and the tab that was
  in front on each workspace. purlis now keeps every tab as a tree of panes in the project's
  reopen record. A record from an earlier version still opens the way it did (#4751).
- **The inside-a-chat check finds an app listening in its fallback folder.** A project whose
  path is too long for a socket beside it has its app listen in a per-user fallback folder; the
  check now finds that app too, as it finds one listening beside the project.
- **A hook socket under a folder with a newline, extra spaces or letters past ASCII is read
  right.** The host check read such a path as another, and refused a real host (#1146).
- **The ssh route folders of chats an app crash left behind are removed.** Each route folder
  names the app process that made it, and opening the project removes those whose process is
  gone; a live chat's route, and anything purlis did not make, stay (#1708).
- **Copies of Docker's settings left by a run that ended outright are swept.** Each one older
  than a day goes as the next run is prepared and as the app starts (#2893).
- **Start a chat names the project's own local settings file.** Where it says git would carry
  the file, or where to declare your own profiles, it named `charter.local.toml` whatever the
  project's file is called. It now names the file purlis read, `purlis.local.toml` or
  `charter.local.toml`, as Settings does (#1719).
- **A busy Undo keeps the keyboard on its line.** While a memory's Undo is on its way, its
  button says it is busy and ignores a second press, instead of being disabled, which dropped
  the keyboard focus to the page (#1190).
- **A task's report says you stepped in only when you sent it a prompt.** A stray key, an
  arrow or a line you typed and never sent in a task's pane no longer counts as stepping in
  (#1463).
- **An older runner's chats' conversations are no longer lost when it had already stopped.** After
  an update or a Replace, a runner that had stopped first, for a suspend or because its container
  was removed outside purlis, was removed with its home and every conversation its chats left
  there. Now purlis looks in that home first: where it holds a conversation, the runner is kept,
  and Devices offers Bring back conversations, which puts them in the pool's runner's home where
  their harness resumes them and then removes the old runner, or Discard…, which asks twice. A home with no conversation goes as before.
  opencode's conversations are kept but not brought back. Replace no longer keeps a runner already
  stopped whose home holds none.
- The Skill studio's Library draws its first screen of rows at once in a project with hundreds of skills, and the rest straight after.
- The Skill studio reads its skills faster: opening it no longer runs `git status` several times to learn that `charter.local.toml` says nothing it needs.
- **A chat's sub-agents end with it in the event log.** When a chat's program exits, or purlis
  stops or closes it, each of its sub-agents still running is now recorded as ending with it,
  in the same end state and for the same cause. Before, the log began a sub-agent's run but
  never ended it unless the sub-agent stopped first (#1084).
- A task question whose asking chat runs on a runner whose link is down reaches you after its wait, as one the chat left unanswered does, instead of waiting until the link is back. A dispatch message a chat on a runner queued there is refused saying nothing was sent, rather than claiming the app holds no record of it.
- **A task with no tab has one name everywhere.** The explorer listed a task that had no tab by
  its number, while the Chats list gave its name (#1484).
- **A report kept for a chat that comes back is not lost on the way.** If purlis quits while the
  chat that asked is starting again, or the report cannot be written for it, the report stays
  owed on its dispatch record and reaches the chat next time. Reopen on a finished task's row
  now also hands it the reports of the tasks it had asked for that were kept while it was gone.
  Try to start again no longer tells a task to carry on once its dispatch has ended, and a
  task is told to carry on after a restart only where it runs on the profile and in the folder
  it was dispatched with. An answer to a question a task asked before a restart says the
  question was not kept and that the task will ask again (#1546).
- **A task whose reporting turn hangs after you answer its prompt is still ended.** The time a
  task is given after its report used to be spent if it passed while the task was showing you a
  prompt, so a turn that then hung kept the task's program for good. It is given that time again
  once you answer. A task whose harness starts a turn of its own after its report is treated as a
  later turn: it is ended when that turn ends (#1525).
- **A task you read beside a view is not ended under you.** In a tab that opened on a view, such
  as a persona card, with chats split beside it, a task any of those chats shows now counts as
  one you are looking at, as it does in any other tab (#1525).
- **Closing a project no longer takes away the hook socket of the same project opened again.** A
  project that stops listening removes only the socket file it made, and stops at once even when
  that file was removed or replaced while it listened (#1525).
- **A task picked from ⌘⇧J's menu stays in the pane it was asked from.** With another of the project's windows used last, it opened in that window, unless it was on screen there (#5224).
- **A task's tab stays on its workspace's strip when the plane is read again before the task ends.** It left the strip at that read, and closed as the task ended (#5224).
- **A runner's device id is compared without case.** Two spellings of one device id that
  differ only in case are one id when purlis keeps a runner (#2741).
- **Reopening the app no longer floods macOS with Keychain questions.** The Vaults panel, which
  every project window draws as it opens, no longer runs the 1Password CLI, so it reads no
  token kept in the keyring and no 1Password app data; a vault's tab still checks it. The app
  also reads each kept token once per run rather than once per request, so several chats that
  reopen after an update ask once per token.
  `purlis persona list` and `persona show` no longer read a kept token to show a persona's
  vault either (#1654).
- **purlis no longer makes macOS ask whether it may "access data from other apps" for a
  1Password vault read through a service-account token.** The 1Password CLI read the
  1Password app's settings from that app's container on every run; purlis now tells it not
  to when the run signs in with a service-account token (#1654).
- **The branch watch backs off when the platform keeps losing track, or no watcher can be
  made.** A build that overflows the file watch's queue no longer has every clone's tree watched
  again on each burst: losses in a row watch the trees again at most once in 2 seconds, and still
  stop vouching for the clones at once. A watcher the system cannot make is tried again after a
  minute, not on every read of a clone's save state (#874).
- **The branch cockpit follows a checkout in its folder.** After another branch was checked out
  in the cockpit's folder, a commit on it that wrote no file was not counted until the focus was
  set again. The cockpit now watches the branch checked out there, as soon as the checkout is
  heard (#1152).
- An agent listing a browser's pages now gets the current title of the page it is on, even when another page is slow to answer.
- **The dev channel no longer loses a build to a run that publishes nothing, or goes back to an
  older commit.** A dev build that was waiting for the one in progress could lose its place to
  a run started by a failed or cancelled check, which then published nothing, so its commit
  stayed unpublished until the next merge. And a build of an older commit could be published
  after a newer one, under a higher number, so machines on the dev channel took it. Now only
  a build that will publish waits, and a build publishes only when its commit comes after the
  one the channel serves. A build in progress is never cancelled. A waiting build can still be
  replaced by another commit's, and then the next green commit's build publishes it
  (`docs/updating.md`, "When a merge reaches the dev channel").
- **A changed path through git's own folder is named as refused, not left out.** A comparison
  and the explorer's change markers now list such a path, and any other path purlis will not
  read, with its mark, and never open it (#704).
- **Comparisons match `git diff` for four more kinds of change.** A file turned into a link,
  or a link into a file, is drawn as git draws it: the old kind out and the new kind in. The
  `diff` attribute decides whether a file is binary before its bytes do (`-diff`, `binary`,
  `diff`, and a named driver's `diff.<driver>.binary`). A working-tree file is compared as
  `git add` would store it, so a file checked out with CRLF line ends shows only the lines you
  edited. A submodule's pointer that moved, came, went or was renamed is listed and drawn as a
  `Subproject commit` line. No filter or diff program a repository names is run for any of them
  (#704).
- **A hook line the host took late is recorded once.** With chats in the session host, a line a
  chat's hook also spooled because the host was slow to take it is no longer recorded twice in the
  event log (#2003).
- **The explorer says when the system would not watch a folder.** When the system refused to
  watch one open folder and watched the rest, that folder looked live but never showed what
  changed on disk. The tree now says so on that folder, in every window that has it open, and
  tries again when you close and open it (#1160).
- **A branch's ahead and behind counts do less work.** Each side is counted from where the two
  branches meet, so a base far ahead of the branch is no longer walked again for the ahead count
  (#1152).
- **The explorer's watch holds every folder to the same check, each time.** A folder an open
  window had expanded was checked when the window asked for it, and its timed retry checked it
  again, but a later watch started by another window did not. Each watch now checks every folder
  it follows, and a folder that fails the check is no longer watched: its window shows that its
  changes are not shown. A folder refused while the retry waited out a long pause is now tried
  again within a few seconds, not after up to a minute (#1160).
- **The explorer's added and deleted marks can be read.** A branch's added files are marked in the
  success colour and its deleted files in the danger colour, on the window, the row under the
  pointer and the selected row alike, and the theme check holds each to a mark's 3:1 in any
  theme. The theme check also measures a see-through colour as it is drawn, over its background
  (#2392).
- **What you type into a combo box stays out of the agent's answers.** While you drive a chat's
  browser, the field kept out is the one that has the page's focus, also where the page marks an
  option of a list as the active one (#2972).
- **The first key you type into a large page is quick too.** While you drive a chat's browser,
  your first key into a field no longer waits for the browser to read the whole page: the field
  is kept out of the agent's answers from a read of the part of the page around it (#2967).
- **The commit and push check names an escaped address once.** An escape written right before
  an email address (`\n`, `\0`) no longer lists the address twice, once as written and once as
  it reads. It is listed once, by the value it spells. Both are still listed when the allowlist
  lets one through and not the other (#1315).
- **The commit and push check stays quick on a long line or a long diff.** A line of many
  different values, or many lines a backslash joins, no longer slows it down with every value
  more (#1315).
- **The First task tab offers only a harness this machine has.** A built-in profile whose program
  is not installed is no longer suggested for the second chat: its row says so (*Codex is not
  installed on this machine.*) and it cannot be started. A profile your project defines runs its
  own command, so it is offered as before (#1698).
- **The First task tab remembers its chats across a relaunch.** It reads which of its branches,
  `first-task-1` and `first-task-2`, are in the repo's copy, and shows each chat that already
  started on its branch instead of offering to start it again. Show its diff is still offered
  only for a chat started since the last launch (#1091).
- **The First task tab shows each chat's diff after a relaunch.** A chat started before purlis
  was relaunched was shown as started, on its branch, but without **Show its diff**. purlis now
  reads back from the clone the commit the branch was cut from, and offers the diff again, or
  says why it cannot (#945).
- **The guided steps come back at the last step you were at.** Each place is kept after the one
  before it, so a quick move through the steps can no longer leave an earlier step kept.
- **A hook call the app was slow to take is recorded within seconds, and only once.** A chat's
  hook keeps a line in the chat's spool when the app does not take it within a quarter of a
  second. That spool used to wait for the chat to close or the project to open again, and a
  line the app took late was recorded twice, once as it came and once from the spool. The app
  now drains a running chat's spool a couple of seconds after it next hears from the chat, and
  a line it already recorded as it came is not recorded again from the spool (#952).
- **Starting a chat, opening a project and closing a chat no longer wait for ever on the hook
  spool.** Each waited, with no limit, for the lock on the spool's keys while another process
  held it. Now each waits two seconds. A chat whose key could not be recorded in that time still
  starts, and any line it spools is refused at the next drain rather than accepted unchecked. A
  drain that gives up reads nothing, and the next start drains it (#1426).
- **The browser budget holds for every client of the session host** (#2611). The most browsers
  your device runs at once (Settings › This machine › Browsers) is now kept by the session host
  itself, whoever asks it for a browser, so a second window or a runner's host never starts more
