  than its device's budget, and two browsers started at the same moment never both take the last
  place. A browser refused for it says so, as before.
- **The hosts Notices read again when a chat starts.** The Notice that a project's hosts changed
  and the one that a persona's hosts wait for you now read the project again each time a chat
  starts, beside a settings change and the window coming back into focus. A list allowed or
  acknowledged in another window is no longer still offered here (#1407, #1405).
- **The keyboard stays on a file's row while the project loads.** The file tree in a branch's
  cockpit was drawn again as a new tree when the project's read arrived, so the row the
  keyboard was on left the page and took the focus with it. The tree stays the same tree now
  (#3532).
- **`purlis secret exec` reads a kept 1Password token once per run.** It read the token from
  the Keychain once for every value it handed on, so one run with three values asked you three
  times (#1638).
- **`purlis vault list` no longer reads a kept 1Password token.** Its status for such a vault
  says the token is kept in the keyring and that `purlis vault verify` reads it, so listing
  vaults never makes the Keychain ask (#1180).
- **A tamper with the kill switch is journaled even when its marker cannot be put back.** The
  app used to journal a tamper only after restoring the stop marker; the journal line, which
  alone keeps the stop, is now written either way (#1375).
- **A long line of `cd`s no longer makes the leak guard slow.** The guard follows every `cd`
  on a line, since what a later command reads is read from where the shell then stands, and
  it spelt the whole way there again for each one: a 64 KB line of them took it 2.8 seconds
  in a test build, the square of its length. It now carries where the shell stands from one
  `cd` to the next. What it answers is unchanged.
- **A hook no longer waits without limit to spool its line.** When the app does not take a hook's
  line and another process holds that chat's spool, the hook gives up after a quarter of a second,
  says on stderr that the line is lost, and answers its harness on time (#1412).
- **Words in a state's colour can be read on a view in the light theme.** The light theme's
  running, waiting, success and unreadable colours are a little darker, so the words a view says
  in them, such as a blocked row in the Saving view, clear the contrast body text needs (#1457).
- **A sandboxed chat starts in this machine's local project, and so does the First task.** The
  local project the first run makes was kept in purlis's config home, which a chat's sandbox
  keeps it from writing because it holds your approvals, so every sandboxed chat there was
  refused before it started. It is made in purlis's data home now (`local-project`, beside the
  event log), and the config home stays out of every chat's reach (#1670).
- **The local project's layout follows it to the data home.** When purlis moves the local
  project out of the config home, its own arrangement and the Notices you dismissed there are
  kept under its new path. Another project's are never moved or mixed in, and an entry already
  at the new path is kept as it is (#1698).
- **The ✋ list holds still while it is open.** A chat or a permission prompt that arrives while
  the list is open no longer moves the rows under the pointer, so a one-click answer lands on
  the row you aimed at. The list keeps the rows it opened on, in their order; one answered or
  withdrawn elsewhere meanwhile stays in its place, dimmed, with nothing on it to press; one you
  ignore from the list leaves it; and new ones show the next time it opens. The count on the
  hand still goes up at once (#1146).
- **The network log says what the forge answered a failed `gh` or `glab` call.** It lists the
  HTTP status the CLI reported, such as 404, where it said only that the call failed. A call
  that succeeded still lists no status, because the CLI does not report one. An update check
  that the server answered with a 404 is now listed as answered, not as a request that got no
  answer (#1022).
- **A connection is no longer held a minute when nobody can be asked.** In the first instant of
  a chat's start, or while the project's hooks are not listening yet, a connection to a host
  nothing lists is refused at once, as before purlis asked live (#1709).
- **The network record says how a host was allowed.** A host allowed for everyone in the
  project and taken live by a running chat is recorded as `project`, not `open`; a brokered
  command's connections are recorded by the layer that lists the host for the chat (persona,
  you, this chat), as the chat's own are (#1709, #1708).
- **The open-file limit is raised as far as the Mac allows.** When macOS is set to allow a
  process fewer than 10 240 open files, purlis used to stay at the 256 it was started with. It
  now raises the limit to the most the system accepts. On Windows, the launch log no longer says
  the open-file limit is unlimited: it says the platform has none to raise (#824).
- **A pane's bell is the size of the buttons beside it.** Its count is a small pill on its
  corner, and its hint opens below the pane's head, where it no longer hides Split right. The
  head's buttons stand a small gap apart, so a hovered one never touches the next (#5189).
- **Typing into a page with a rotating advert keeps every key.** While you drive a chat's
  browser, a key goes to the field that has the focus, and a click to what is under it, even
  while another frame of the page (an advert, a widget) loads something new. Input is still held
  back where what it would reach changed since the browser last showed it to you (#2638).
- **The project-root git guard follows an alias the command defines for itself.** Besides
  `-c alias.*` and the config files, an alias set through `GIT_CONFIG_COUNT` with
  `GIT_CONFIG_KEY_n`/`GIT_CONFIG_VALUE_n`, `--config-env` or `GIT_CONFIG_PARAMETERS`, on the
  command or earlier on the same line, is now followed to the branch move or reset it runs. When
  the command points git at a config file of its own (`GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL`, `GIT_CONFIG_SYSTEM`,
  `HOME`, `XDG_CONFIG_HOME`, an `include.path`), or sets a value only the shell fills in, a
  possible alias after it is refused with a sentence that says why. git's own commands still
  run (#1358).
- **A long line of `export`s no longer slows the git guards down.** Each segment used to get
  its own copy of every earlier export, so the cost grew with the square of the line; a long
  enough line could outlast the hook's deadline. It now grows with the line (#1358).
- **A command substitution in git's options no longer hides the command from the project-root
  guard.** In `git -C $(git rev-parse --show-toplevel) checkout -b x`, and the same with
  backticks, `--git-dir`, `--work-tree`, `GIT_DIR=$(…)` or `env -C $(…)`, the guard used to
  read the substitution's words as git's own and miss the branch move or reset after them. It
  now refuses those, an alias in their place included, saying it cannot tell which repository
  the command acts on and asking for the path spelled out. So does a branch move or reset run
  through a program held in a variable (`$G checkout -b x`) (#1354).
- **An alias chain longer than the project-root guard follows is refused.** A chain still on
  an alias after four hops used to be read as ending there and allowed; its end may move HEAD,
  so it is now refused, with a sentence that says so (#1354).
- **The project-root branch guard reads `~` where git is sent.** `git -C ~/clone switch -c x`
  and the same `~` in `--git-dir`, `--work-tree`, `GIT_DIR`, `GIT_WORK_TREE` or `env -C` now
  act in the home directory, as the shell sends them, instead of being refused as the project
  root. A `~` the shell leaves alone (quoted, or in an attached option) is still read as a
  directory named `~` (#1323).
- **A directory the guard cannot name gets its own refusal.** When git is sent to a directory
  only the shell can name (`git -C "$DIR"`, `cd "$DIR" && git …`, a glob, `cd -`), the refusal
  now says so and asks for the path spelled out, instead of claiming what the command would do
  in the project root. That case is refused from any directory, including a workspace clone
  (#1323).
- **Naming the project root's own git directory is the project root.** For a root whose git
  directory lives beside it, `--git-dir=<it>` or `GIT_DIR=<it>` is now refused like the root
  itself (#1323).
- **Quitting waits for a project still being opened or closed.** A project closed or opened just
  before the quit is let go of with the rest, its last record and the window's tabs written, for
  up to ten seconds (#1949).
- **Send reply keeps the keyboard in the Inbox.** Pressing it put the keyboard on the page, since
  the button is disabled while it sends. It now goes back to the reply box (#1700).
- **An untracked folder the change markers cannot open costs only itself.** It is marked as one
  entry, and the rest of the branch's changes are still shown (#1130).
- **A long command with many `git` calls is judged in time on macOS.** The guards that keep the
  project root on its branch and its unpushed commits safe asked git the same question again for
  every `git` on the line, each a git process. A long line of resets and restores could take them
  past the hook's two seconds, and the command was refused for running out of time. Each question
  is now asked once per command, and the answers are the same as before (#2619).
- **A refusal by purlis's egress proxy is answered at once.** The proxy kept telling the app
  about a refused host before it answered the client, so a slow listener held up the client's
  refusal and one of the proxy's few connection slots. It is now kept in the proxy's record
  first, answered, and told by a thread of its own (#1353).
- **A chat's skills chip follows a restart and a skill change.** After a chat restarts, its chip shows the new run's set. After a skill or a workspace's skill settings change on disk, its budget matches the Skills view's header again, without reopening the window (#4094).
- **The handle between split panes has a name.** A screen reader now reads it as "Resize the
  split", the way it reads the region and file tree handles, instead of a bare separator (#629).
- **One chat's held hook spool no longer holds up the drain of every other chat.** When a
  project opens, purlis waits up to a second for each chat's spool. A chat still held after that
  is left as it is, with its keys, and drained at the next start. The file an older build left
  is read only up to the most that build could write. A spool folder whose first sync ran out of
  time is synced again by the next line written to it (#1419).
- **A new project's steward no longer says it has no other personas to route to.** A project
  made from a stack template has that template's personas, but the steward `init` wrote still
  said there were none. Its routing section now points at them instead: `purlis persona list`
  names them and each lives in `personas/<name>/persona.md`. A steward already on disk is yours
  and is left as it is (#882).
- **The Skill studio marks a skill hidden by the router only where a chat really hides it**
  (Skill studio preview, #4215). The marks now preview a chat at the workspace's root. Such a
  chat counts no clone's repo skills, so a workspace with skills in several clones no longer
  shows plane skills as hidden when that chat lists them. The Routing page's new **Preview** line
  names the chat the marks preview. Where an extension router is chosen, it says that the marks
  are the built-in router's choice, because the extension is asked only at each chat's start.
- **`purlis skill grade`'s plan names an outcome eval's file that isn't text**, as the Skill
  studio's plan does: purlis couldn't check it for characters no reader would see, and a judge
  may not be able to read it (#4922).
- **A long message opened in a short pane stays in the waiting strip's room.** It scrolls inside
  the strip, so the terminal below keeps its share of the pane (#4843).
- **A chat waiting on you still says what it said after purlis starts again.** Its last message,
  and the few before it, come back to the waiting strip, the Inbox card and the quiz once the
  window holds the project again, still masked, where they used to read "No message to show"
  until the chat's next turn (#4709).
- **The window catches up when macOS's file events are late.** On a busy Mac the file-event
  service can hand purlis a change seconds or minutes late, and a todo closed or a memory saved
  in a terminal stayed on the panels until then. While a window is shown, purlis now also looks
  at the project's folders every 5 seconds, and at once when you come back to the window, and
  tells the panels and the sidebar what the events had not. It stops looking while every window
  is hidden. The doctor's new **file events** row says when the events were late in the last
  10 minutes (#756).
- **The window's page is titled purlis.** The page inside the window still said `charter`,
  while the window itself said `purlis` (#1253).
- **A screen reader names the handles between the window's regions.** The handles beside each
  sidebar, above the Panel and between the Panel's halves were said as "separator" alone; each
  now says what moving it resizes, such as "Resize the left sidebar" (#629).
- **Save in the window pushes commits the remote does not have yet.** A project with no saving
  mode set no longer answers "Nothing to save" while it has commits its remote lacks; the
  window's Save pushes them.
- **`purlis theme check` reads a pair between the named tints** (#4308). A workspace's own colour
  can be any hue, so a pair a tint can move is now read at every whole degree. A new finding,
  `contrast-between-tints`, names a pair that falls only between the named tints, at the degree it
  is lowest.
- **A panel, popover or dialog a theme fills holds the buttons drawn on it.** When a theme's
  parts give one of these surfaces a fill of its own, the buttons on it, and a menu's rows in a
  popover, are measured on that fill in every workspace tint: their words, Allow's accent edge
  and the danger answers. A surface they would not read on draws its own fill, and
  `purlis theme check` names it (#3099).
- **The theme check holds a state's colour drawn as words to 4.5:1.** The warning-soft button's
  words, the rail's waiting badge and a title-bar chip's waiting count were held at the 3:1 a
  mark takes; a theme that draws them fainter than 4.5:1 now gets a finding, and the window draws
  purlis's own waiting colour instead. Purlis Classic light's waiting amber is a shade darker so
  its count reads on the amber wash (#3041).
- **`purlis theme check` reads the selected row, a card row and a notice's way between the named
  tints** (#4406). Each is now read across every hue a workspace's own colour can be, and said once
  where it falls only between the named tints. New findings: `selected-between-tints`,
  `card-between-tints` and `notice-way-between-tints`.
- **A see-through count on a tab is measured over its counts button** (#4406), so its words are no
  longer judged on the tab's fill, a colour they are never drawn on.
- **The theme check holds only what the window draws.** A look purlis never shows, like a danger
  button pressed as a toggle or a danger menu row open, no longer brings a finding or takes a
  panel's, popover's or dialog's fill away. A field's error is measured only on the grounds a
  field that can refuse stands on (#3384).
- **The theme check measures a see-through part fill where it is drawn.** A part's fill with
  alpha, such as `rail.badge.fill`, is now laid over its root's own fill and then the grounds
  under that, so words that can't be read there draw the defaults back, and words that can
  are kept (#3303).
- **The theme check reads every part's words on the fill under them.** A popover's key, a tab's
  count, a title-bar crumb and a switcher's row are each measured on their own pill or surface,
  in the colour the window draws them in, so a theme can no longer pass by setting a part's
  words to the colour of its own cap. A tab's ×, the title bar's ⌄ and a row's pin are held as
  marks, at 3:1 (#3099).
- **The theme check reads a pane's warning buttons on the warning wash.** A pane's warning and a
  consent's Allow are drawn on `wash.warning` over the terminal's fill, but the check never read
  a control there, so a theme with a heavy warning wash could hide a warning's ways out and still
  pass. Their looks are now held on that wash as they are on the danger wash. No built-in theme
  changes (#4795).
- **A theme that sets only a field's error colour keeps it, over Purlis and over Purlis
  Classic.** The theme check read a field's default help on grounds no help is drawn on: on the
  danger wash, over an active tab, on a line's colour. Purlis's quiet words fall short of 4.5:1
  there, so the field's look fell and took the theme's error colour with it. A field's help is
  now read only where the window draws one, in a dialog and on a view's page, and a wash only
  over the grounds the window draws it on (#4648).
- **Checking a staged import leaves no font registered**: the stage is read only to check, so
  nothing of it is served after it moves into place or is removed (#2587).
- **Settings › You › This machine shows a workspace pin made on the workspace strip at once.**
  Pinning or unpinning a workspace, from its menu, the palette or by dragging its tab across the
  pins, now reads the group's pins again while it is on screen, as a project pin already did
  (#1240).
- **Unpinning a project in Settings › You › This machine keeps it in your recents**, so its Undo
  pins it back; the oldest other recent goes instead when the list is full. And a Forget or Revoke
  that changed nothing now says so, where it used to look done (#1240).
- **This tab keeps a task's row until its finished row arrives.** A task that ended dropped out
  of the Chats view's This tab at once, while Workspace and All kept its row until the finished
  row replaced it. And going to a row outside This tab no longer widens the list to Workspace
  when the step that asked for the row brings its tab forward too (#1696).
- **A theme's title-bar crumb, ⌄, switcher rows and pins now draw** (#3656). A theme's
  `titlebar.crumb.*`, `titlebar.all.*`, `titlebar.row.*` and `titlebar.pin.*` keys were accepted
  but reached nothing, because they were written as parts inside a workspace chip. Each now
  reaches its own element, at rest and in the states it is marked in: under the pointer, open
  or pinned, and the keyboard's focus. A key that names one of them in a chip's variant
  (`titlebar.crumb.pinned.fill`), or in a state it is never in (`titlebar.row.focused.fill`),
  reaches nothing: the schema no longer offers it, and a theme that writes it is told so. Such a
  key that also set a size inside a state, or had a value of the wrong kind, used to refuse the
  whole theme; it is now only left out.
- **The title bar keeps its states readable under any theme** (#4000). A pinned workspace's pin
  and the row Enter would go to are checked under the pointer too. A switcher row's count is
  checked on the row colour a theme sets, and on a switcher popover a theme fills. An unavailable
  row keeps its faint look whatever the rows' colours. A workspace chip whose colours a theme set
  too faint no longer loses its hover and current-workspace fills when it draws its default back.
- **Todo, memory and session tabs come back at launch.** A todo, a memory, a memory archive, a
  file of a branch, a file's comparison and a session record's tab were dropped from the saved
  record and were missing after every relaunch. Each one now comes back, and its saved key is
  held to the one shape charter writes for that tab (#1297).
- **A panel's, the Changes view's and a file tree's lines about something that went wrong are
  drawn in the danger colour**, as the Explorer's already are, and no longer in the colour of a
  failed check's mark (#3938).
- **Typing into a chat no longer freezes the window while its session host is slow.** A pane's
  keys, paste, mouse, resizes and its view going on and off screen used to wait for the session
  host's answer before the window could draw again, for up to 30 seconds on a host that was busy
  or coming up. Each chat now has a queue of its own: what you send goes in at once, reaches the
  chat in the order you sent it, and other chats and the window carry on meanwhile. When it
  cannot reach the chat, because its runner is reconnecting or the host refused it, the chat's
  pane says so with the reason (#4734).
- **Typing into a large page while you drive stays quick.** After the first key into a field,
  a chat's browser no longer reads the whole page before each key: it asks the page only
  whether the same field still has the focus, and reads the page again when the focus moves.
  What you type stays out of the agent's answers as before (#2295).
- **Removing a persona asks about its unsaved skill text first** (Skill studio preview, #4029).
  A persona-level skill being edited in the Skill studio goes with the persona, so Delete
  persona now asks Keep editing, Discard and leave, or Save and leave before its own question,
  as a workspace's removal already did.
- **Unsaved skill text is asked about before any close can lose it** (Skill studio preview, #3929). The Skill studio's editor already asked Keep editing, Discard and leave, or Save and leave when its tab closed. It now asks the same question before a project closes, before the project moves to another window, before a quit, and before the removal of the workspace the skill is saved into. Discard and leave lets the text go only once the close is carried out, so cancelling what the close asks next keeps the text.
- **Unsaved skill text goes with its project to another window** (Skill studio preview, #4028).
  Moving a project to another window no longer asks about the text being edited: the window it
  moves to opens the Skill studio on it as it was. Closing a split window hands the text back to
  the main window with its projects. A quit asks about unsaved text in every window, in the
  window that holds it, rather than only in the main window.
- **A save's rebase that failed is called a conflict only when it is one.** A file git could
  not write, a full disk or a git that died used to be reported as a conflict, and `git rebase
  --abort` ran where no rebase had started, which could leave the project half-updated. Such a
  failure is now said in git's words, and what the failed checkout wrote is put back.
- **Use skill… offers a chat the skills it was started with.** A chat started while the Skill
  studio's flag was off was handed the built-in skills alone, but Use skill… listed the project's
  skills too. It now lists the built-in ones alone, and once the flag is on, the chat's tab offers
  the restart that hands it the project's skills (#3445).
- **A chat at the default sandbox level can make its tools' folders on a home without `~/.local`
  or `~/.config`.** `mkdir -p ~/.config/sometool` and `mkdir -p ~/.local/share/sometool` used to be refused
  when those folders were missing. Purlis now makes `~/.local`, `~/.local/share` and `~/.config`
  as a chat starts, where they are missing.
- **A vault file named by its full path in the project's state folder follows the folder too.**
  A plain-file or reference vault whose `file` is an absolute path in `.charter/` (a hand-edited
  or older record) now reads and writes where the folder is now, after `rename-local` moved it
  or an undo put it back, as a relative record already did (#1321).
- **A refused vault Notice for a chat not on screen no longer says "this chat".** On a session's
  tab, the Notice for one of its tasks starts with the task's path and then says "it" and "that
  chat", the way the dispatch question does, so it never reads as the chat on screen (#1538).
- **A chat that stays on a draining runner is asked about as the runner it runs on.** Once a pool
  moved on to a new runner, a chat still on its older runner had its tools' values, its browser
  logins and the person's Ask bound to the pool's new runner. The session host now tells the
  window which runner a link reached, and such a chat is judged by its pool and that runner as
  they are kept. With a session host from before this, such a chat is sent no value until it
  moves (#3417).
- **A file made and removed at once is no longer missed by the project's watch, a branch's
  change markers or the kill switch.** Each folded the platform's events through a debouncer
  that took a removal arriving while the file's creation was still queued as the file never
  having been there, so a todo drawn in that moment could stay drawn, and a stop marker made
  and taken away inside a tenth of a second was not looked at. They now fold events the way
  the explorer's watch does, and a watch that loses track reads everything again (#1139).
- **The Inbox says "This project expects it."** for a blocked socket or system service the
  project's settings declare, as the chat's own Notice does (#1888).
- **An Allow on this machine shows wherever the question is open.** Settings › Sandbox and the
  project's "This project expects more than this machine allows" Notice read what waits again
  when the other one allows it, so neither offers the same Allow a second time (#1888).
- **A chat owed a restart says the restart waits for its turn as soon as it is mid-turn.** Before,
  a chat whose state was not known yet kept saying to restart it by hand after it started a turn
  (#1888).
- **What changed in a file, to a screen reader.** The comparison tab's "Comparing…", its
  refusals and its "no line differs" sentences are announced as a status, and the side-by-side
  view is named after the file and what it is compared against (#1189).
- **What you type into a browser is kept out of the agent's answers as you typed it, not word by
  word on the way.** While you drive a chat's browser, purlis keeps each field's latest value,
  each run of keys you typed and what you pasted out of every answer the agent gets. A short word
  you passed through on the way to a longer value is no longer blanked on every page. The site
  where you typed, whose pictures and canvases a screenshot paints over, is the site of the page
  you typed on as it shows, even while it is loading another (#2311).
- **The window's line says the newest answer.** A sentence of the window's own, such as which
  forge opening a repo added to the project, is no longer hidden by an older answer of the
  project in front; a newer answer of the project's still replaces it (#1669).
- **A see-through surface keeps the words of what stands on it readable in every workspace tint.**
  A popover, panel or dialog whose fill has alpha now draws its default when a button's or a menu's
  words on it would fall in a tint, and says so in the theme check (#4310).
- **Every change to a workspace's `workspace.json` waits for the one before it.** Saving the
  Workspace settings or Edit as JSON, `purlis workspace snapshot`, `fork`, `rename` and `reinit`,
  and the first manifest purlis writes for a new workspace, now take the same turn that clone and
  removal take, so none of them writes over a change made while it was reading the file (#1292).
- **`workspace remove` clears git's record of each linked worktree it held.** A workspace
  holding a checkout of a repository kept elsewhere left that repository listing the deleted
  folder as a worktree until someone pruned it. Now each such folder's record is removed with
  `git worktree remove`, one folder at a time and never a blanket prune. Where git refuses, a
  locked worktree for one, the removal says which `git -C <repository> worktree prune` clears it
  (#998).
- **`purlis workspace remove` clears the exclude lines it left in a repository kept
  elsewhere.** When a checkout in the workspace is a linked worktree of a repository outside
  the project, the removal now takes out of purlis's block in that repository's
  `info/exclude` only the lines no other checkout purlis wires there still needs, and the whole
  block when none does. Your own lines in that file are never touched. When purlis cannot
  account for every line in the block, it leaves the block whole and names it, as before
  (#998).
- **A renamed workspace's memory header and Log line name it by its new name.** `purlis
  workspace rename` now also rewrites the `-w <name>` purlis wrote into the workspace's
  `memory/MEMORY.md` header and the Log line of its `workspace.md`, so a chat that follows them
  reaches the workspace instead of being told there is none. Lines a person wrote are left as
  they are (#3965).
- **`workspace_section`'s refusal also offers to ask you.** When the app cannot take a section
  entry for a chat, the tool says to edit `workspace.md` to add it, or to ask you to, since a
  chat in a clone cannot edit that file. The harness guide no longer tells Codex chats to run
  `purlis workspace vision`, `purlis persona remember` or `purlis persona where` instead of the
  tools: they reach the app like every other harness's (#1598).
- **A memory whose index line cannot be written is no longer left on disk.** When the line could
  not be added to `MEMORY.md`, the memory file stayed behind with nothing listing it. It is now
  removed again, for `purlis`'s commands, the app and the MCP tools alike (#1058).
- **`purlis workspace use` no longer removes a returning chat's workspace pointer.** Its 30-day
  clean-up of the per-session and per-terminal pointers in the project's state folder now
  follows the rule the app uses when it opens a project: a chat the app will reopen keeps its
  month-old pointer and lock, the tool gate's files are left to the gate, and nothing is
  removed through a link (#1027).
- **`purlis worktree commit` takes paths as git does in the branch folder it runs in.** Run
  inside a branch folder, or with `env -C <branch folder>`, its paths are relative to where it
  runs there, even when the chat was started in the workspace above it. Paths spelled from the
  workspace still work, and a path it cannot place is refused with the spelling that works. A
  message that starts with `--` no longer needs `--message=` (#3927).
- A chat can remove a finished branch folder whose squash merge the base has since changed again, or whose base branch is gone. Commits made after the merge still refuse it. Folders only the harness or a build writes, such as `.claude/.cc-writes/`, `node_modules/` and Tauri's generated schemas, no longer refuse it; other ignored files, such as `.env`, still do.
- **A skill's description written as YAML reads as its words, not `>`.** A folded (`>`), literal
  (`|`), quoted or multi-line `description:` in a `SKILL.md` is read as YAML reads it in the
  Skill studio, the Skills panel, the skills listed to a chat and the skill budget, so such a skill
  is listed by what it says. A rename or copy keeps it whole, and the studio says when a
  description cannot be read (#5182).
- **An editor that fails at once is said, not dropped.** With `$VISUAL` or `$EDITOR` chosen as
  your editor, a terminal editor such as vi or nano has no terminal to open in and exits at
  once, and *Open in your editor* used to do nothing. It now says that the editor exited, and
  the first line of what it printed, such as `emacsclient` saying it found no server. An editor
  that printed nothing is said to need a terminal. What the editor prints is kept in a file
  with no name, so an editor that stays open after purlis quits can go on printing. A file whose
  name is not UTF-8 is also handed to the editor as it is, rather than with its name rewritten
  (#1044).
- **A chat on a pool's runner has its hooks recorded.** Each line a runner chat's hook sends
  is now written once, in the runner's own event log, and the hook is told it was taken. Before,
  the runner refused the line, so it was recorded in no event log and the hook kept a copy
  (#3304).
- **`purlis doctor` names `purlis persona optimize` for a persona's memory.** Its memory
  indexes row said curating a persona's memory from the CLI was "not in this version yet",
  although `purlis persona optimize` has shipped. It now names that command, as it names
  `purlis workspace optimize` for a workspace (HY-12).
- **A memory or session record written by an agent shows up in its panel straight away.**
  Before, a workspace's or persona's `memory/`, and the session records in `sessions/`, reached
  the Memory, Personas and Sessions panels only when something else in the project changed.
  Each panel now reads again only for the kind of change it draws, so a todo closed in one
  workspace no longer re-reads another workspace's panels. Saving a memory re-reads only the
  panels and views that show it. When auto-save commits, pushes or fetches, only the save state
  and the alerts read again, where the whole window used to. A fetch or save that brings
  others' changes into your files still reads everything again (FD-10, #933).
- **`purlis guard ask` never turns a command opencode denies into one it asks about.** opencode
  goes by the last rule that matches a command, so a rule added after `"*": "deny"` used to win
  over it, and a rule for a command that was denied exactly used to replace the deny. Now a
  denied command stays denied, and the command says so. Claude Code was never affected: there a
  deny always wins.
- **The first run checks `glab` as well as `gh`.** Under **On this machine**, the first window
  now says whether GitLab's `glab` is installed and signed in, beside GitHub's `gh`. If it is
  installed but not signed in, **Sign in to GitLab** opens a shell tab running `glab auth login`.
- **purlis opened from the Finder or the Dock can hold two hundred chats.** macOS starts such
  an app with room for only 256 open files, and each chat needs several, so the app could run
  out well short of two hundred. It now raises its own limit as it starts, to 10,240 or the
  system's hard limit if that is lower, and never lowers a limit it was given (#683).
- **`charter statusline --watch` says it cannot watch instead of drawing one frame.** It has
  no repaint yet, and one frame followed by exit 0 looked like a watch that had stopped. It now
  exits 1 with the reason and points you to `charter statusline` run once per turn (#574).
- **Two GitLab pipeline states are no longer read as unknown.** A pipeline that is
  `waiting_for_callback` now shows as pending and counts as running, and auto-merge waits for it
  instead of saying there is nothing to wait for. A pipeline that is `canceling` shows as
  canceled and did not pass. GitLab lists both in its pipelines API (#711).
- **The status line no longer shows a GitLab fork's merge request as the branch's own.** When a
  fork had an open merge request from a branch of the same name, the status line could name it.
  It now names only a merge request from the project itself, as `purlis change show` already
  did (#711).
- **Linux no longer waits half a minute for a desktop portal that cannot start.** Before GTK
  starts, purlis asks the session bus to start the portal and gives it 300 ms. If the bus is
  still silent, purlis restarts itself without the session bus, and the window comes up in
  under 2 s where it used to take 26–31 s. For that run there is no tray icon and no desktop
  notifications, and a second launch is refused rather than handed over. A per-user lock keeps
  that refusal in place without the bus. Cold start is now measured in CI on X and on i3, and
  every launch is held to the limit (#24).
- **A run without the session bus says so in the window, and chats keep the bus.** The line at
  the top names what is off (the tray icon, notifications, a keyring vault from the window,
  handing a second launch over). purlis asks the bus again after 5, 15 and 45 s, and when the
  portal answers the line offers **Restart with the full desktop integration**, asking first
  about any chat that could be mid-turn; purlis never restarts by itself. Chats, and the
  programs purlis starts itself, get the session bus purlis was given rather than the one it
  turned off, so a keyring that git or a CLI uses through D-Bus keeps working. On i3 and other
  X11 sessions with no session bus, purlis now starts on the bus the X display holds, as GTK
  would, so notifications reach a notification daemon started from the window manager's config
  (#746).
- **The guard that stops a live substitution in `purlis change create` or `drop` no longer
  says `purlis change` is missing.** It has shipped since 0.4.0; what is not in this version
  yet is `purlis change push`, which will write the `why` into request bodies (#571).
- **A heredoc `cat` reads inside a quoted command substitution is read as data.**
  `x="$(cat <<'EOF' … EOF)"` no longer has `purlis handoff` in its body refused as a handoff a
  shell runs. The guard now reads the program that opens a heredoc inside `"$( … )"` as the
  command in the substitution, and still refuses the body when either that command or the one
  the substitution stands in runs it: a shell (anywhere in that command's words), `ssh`, `su`,
  `runuser`, `script`, `source` or `.`, a program it cannot name, or the substitution standing
  in the program's place, prefixes included. A live substitution in a body two shells read
  differently is searched too (#488).

## Security

- **The Inbox says when a file that can run later appears in a chat's folder.** When a sandboxed
  chat's turn ends, purlis looks for what a later program loads, such as a repository's hooks, an
  editor's tasks or a harness's project config, in the folders that chat may write. Anything new
  gets one Notice a chat, naming the chat and the paths, with Put away. purlis never changes the
  files. A look that stopped at its limit says the check was incomplete.
- **A token kept in the keyring is handed only to a 1Password CLI purlis can vouch for.** Every
  read holds the `op` it pinned to more than the pin says: on macOS it must carry 1Password's own
  signature, verified against the file. A token is not stored beside an `op` that does not
  (#1542).
- **`purlis vault add --token-stdin` recognises more of the app's chats, and fewer of your own
  processes as one.** On macOS a process below the app that started a chat is refused, whatever
  project it belongs to, and a process number a crashed app left in its record no longer makes a
  later process count as a chat (#1542).
- **`purlis vault add --account` takes a sign-in address only.** It is held to the same rule as
  the guided set-up: a letter or a digit, then letters, digits, `.`, `_` and `-`. A pasted
  `https://…/` link is stored as the address it names (#1542).
- **A 1Password token stored before the guided set-up is held to its item.** Records made since
  then already named the 1Password item a vault's secrets are kept in, so a commit that changed
  the item stopped the token being used. Older records named none. When the item is this
  machine's own (or the default), the next read now writes it into the record; when a commit
  chose it, the token is not used until you give it again from the vault's tab (#1542).
- **`purlis vault add --token-stdin` is refused in a chat of any project this machine opened.**
  It read only the open chats of the project the command named, so a chat of another project
  that named this one was not recognised as a chat. The projects are read from the machine store
  under your account's own home as well as where the environment points (#1542).
- **A blanked field inside a frame the page turns, scales or zooms is painted over.** In a
  screenshot the agent gets, a field inside a frame from another site that the page turns, scales
  or zooms is painted over with the whole frame, and when purlis cannot tell where a frame is
  drawn the screenshot is withheld (#2143).
- **What you allow on this machine is kept outside the project.** The sandbox record (folders,
  hosts, sockets and services you allowed, and which project grants you accepted) moves from the
  project's `app/sandbox.json` to `~/.config/purlis/sandbox-grants/`, where no repository or
  copy of a project can bring one. After this update, purlis asks again once for each project's
  sandbox grants (ADR 0093).
- **A brokered tool runs with an environment of its own.** A tool a chat runs with a vault's
  value starts from only the chat's language, terminal, time zone, ssh agent, certificate
  bundles and the plain values a client reads for where it connects (a database's host, port and
  name, a cloud's region). Its `HOME` and `XDG_*` folders are in the run's own temp folder. A
  setting the tool read from another variable of the chat, or from your home folder, is now
  given as one of its arguments. A persona's approved credentialed MCP server starts the same
  way, with the variables its approved entry sets (#2047).
- **A brokered run serves only chats of this machine.** A vault's tool is run on this machine
  only for a chat this machine runs (#2047).
- **A browser-login tool's keys are quoted where you allow them.** The line an Allow of a
  persona's tools is bound to now quotes a browser login's user and password keys, so two
  different logins never read as the same line. A persona with a browser-login tool asks for
  its Allow once more after this update; a persona whose tools are all programs keeps its
  Allow (#1828).
- **Every chat is of the project it was opened in.** A chat that is not on a profile now takes
  its project, and so its sandbox, from the open project, as a chat on a profile does, and no
  longer from the folder it stands in. Its hooks are told that project too. In a project that
  runs chats sandboxed, such a chat in a folder that is a link, has a link above it, or is
  outside the project is refused, and is never started without the sandbox instead; the refusal
  says how to move on. The environment a chat is given and the vault names stripped from it are
  read from the open project too. A project whose own manifest has gone no longer reads as one
  that leaves the sandbox off: its chats are refused until it is restored. "Start without the
  sandbox" is still yours to pick for one chat (#1410).
- **A chat's confinement in the session host answers only the window it belongs to.** The host
  changes a chat's network, reads its live asks and ends its proxy only for the window link
  that made that confinement or took its chat back, and tells only that window what the proxy
  refused, carried and asks about, on this machine and on a runner (#2444).
- **What a chat's harness says its session has cost is kept where no sandboxed chat can
  write it.** The token and cost figures purlis shows (a dispatch's *Cost (reported)*, a tab's
  tasks' tokens, a session's tokens against its limit) are now kept by each chat's own id in
  the app's folder of the project's state, which every harness's sandbox denies a chat writing.
  Claude Code's status line, which runs outside the sandbox, is the one writer. Before, the
  figure sat in a folder a chat writes, so a chat could change its own figure or another's
  (#1457).
- **A checkout's withdrawn agent or skill goes through the folders held on the way down too.**
  When a project stops offering an agent or skill purlis mirrored into a checkout of a
  repository kept elsewhere, the copy is withdrawn the way a workspace's generated file is: it
  is unlinked inside the folders the walk down holds, so a folder swapped for a link in the
  meantime cannot carry the removal outside the checkout (#1583).
- **A commit message is read whole, as git may store it.** A chat's commit is refused for a
  credential anywhere git keeps in its message, and a `git commit -v` still commits. The
  project-root guard also keeps what a line makes after a `cd` it cannot follow as a directory
  it cannot name.
- **A harness declaration's `env` namespace refuses more.** Beside the variables that change
  what a process loads or runs, a namespace that reaches a TLS-trust, proxy, SSH-agent or
  program-runner variable (a pager, an editor, a browser, a compiler or its wrapper) is now
  refused, with one sentence that says so. A harness's own look-alikes, such as
  `AIDER_PROXY_MODE`, still pass (#1013).
- **Approving a harness a project declares shows the variables it would pass.** The approval
  line now ends with the declaration's `env` names and prefixes ("it passes `MYTOOL_*` from your
  environment"), beside the words it runs and the bytes it types. An approval is tied to the
  declaration's exact contents, which already covered `env`, so one you gave before still holds
  (#969).
- **The approval dialog for a declared harness shows the newline it types.** A declaration's
  `[terminal] newline` is typed into the program's terminal, so the dialog now shows its bytes
  with the program and its words, and you approve them together (#1119).
- **A declared tool runs only where the repository's settings are yours.** A tool run with a
  vault's value from a chat now starts only in a folder whose repository keeps its git settings,
  the settings they include and its hooks where no chat can write them (your project's own
  clones and branch folders, or a folder outside any repository); glab also only where the
  repository holds no glab settings of its own. Elsewhere the run is refused with a sentence
  naming the file (#3868).
- **`gh` and `glab` never run their credential or settings commands with a vault's value from a
  chat.** `auth`, `config`, `alias`, `extension`, `ssh-key`, `gpg-key` (and `glab token` and
  `deploy-key`, `gh repo deploy-key`), and `api` against another host, are refused in a chat
  whatever the tool declares; run them in your own terminal (#3421).
- **A dispatched chat is held to its profile's rules each time it is started again.** When
  purlis is opened again, and on Restart chat, the restart a grant owes and Start fresh, a chat
  that another chat dispatched is no longer started on a profile whose command has come to
  switch the harness's permission prompts off since, or on one the project has stopped listing
  for its persona. Its row says why and what to do (#1509).
- **A Codex profile that sets its approval policy to never as a configuration override is
  treated as one that asks nobody**, as `--ask-for-approval never` already was, and so is a
  short flag written with its value attached. This holds for the chats that may be dispatched
  on such a profile and for the asking chat's own dispatches: a chat on one dispatches under
  standing grants only (#1509).
- **What that item can and cannot do.** Nothing is asked of a chat nobody is at, and what
  such a chat may do at the time is unchanged. Allow from now on grants one named pair, for
  you, on this machine, for work in one workspace: the one the refused task would have worked
  in (in any workspace only where that was the project's root, and the item says so). Before
  you press, the item says what that reaches: a chat nobody is at, and what the other persona
  works with, in the words the dispatch question uses, which name whom its own chats may
  dispatch to. No grant is kept for a workspace that is no longer there.
  It never offers a grant for everyone in the project or for any persona. It is checked again
  when you press: a pair you said never to, or one a policy locks, is not granted, and such an
  item is gone by the time you look. The grant is recorded in purlis's event log as yours,
  with where it came from. Only a refusal a grant would mend is kept: not one for a never, a
  policy lock, a limit or a loop.
- **A refused chat cannot steer it.** The item shows nothing a chat wrote: two personas, a
  workspace, a count and a time, and neither the brief nor the task's name is kept. A chat
  asking over and over raises one item's count and moves no row: the list is in the order
  pairs were first refused, and it holds still while it is open. The keyboard arrives on
  Dismiss, never on the grant. The list has a cap, items go after 30 days, and its commands
  are the window's alone (#1507).
- **In a sandboxed project, only you make a dispatch grant.** Nothing a chat sends creates,
  widens or revokes one: the asking persona is the one purlis's own record says the chat runs
  with, never the request's, the brief is shown as plain text apart from purlis's words, and a
  write purlis makes for a chat never changes `[dispatch]` in the project's file. A chat that
  still runs on another chat's hosts until you allow its own dispatches to no one. Where the
  project's sandbox is off, or you started a chat without it, that chat runs as you and can
  write the files the grants are kept in, so nothing here holds it. An administrator's policy
  can lock a pair, or all dispatch, in `/etc/purlis/policy.json` (`dispatch.locked`,
  `dispatch.allow`): a locked dispatch is refused with the policy's sentence and who set it,
  and offers no Allow (#1437).
- **A filled field takes no keys from the chat.** While the page purlis filled a secret into is
  open, the chat presses no key in it and types or chooses nothing in it; it sends the form by
  clicking its button (#5115).
- **After purlis fills a secret into a page, that browser reaches only the page's site until the
  page is left or closed.** A route change inside the page keeps the hold, and the filled field
  can't be copied, cut or dragged out meanwhile. Going back to the page brings it back empty
  (#5117).
- **purlis reads a folder's git link itself before it runs git there.** A branch folder's
  `.git` is a small file that names the repository it belongs to. Git that purlis runs in such
  a folder (the explorer's state, Changes, saves, removing or merging a branch folder) no longer
  follows that file wherever it points: purlis reads it and tells git exactly which repository
  to use. A folder purlis cut is read only as a worktree of the clone it was cut from. A link
  that names a git directory inside the folder itself is never followed. Elsewhere below a
  workspace a link must name a worktree of a clone, or a submodule of the repository around
  the folder. A folder whose link names anything else is not read, and says "this folder's git
  link was changed, so purlis is not reading it"; one whose link names a git directory that
  is gone says so. This narrows what a rewritten link can reach; where a sandbox cannot keep
  a prepared folder from being moved into a `.git` (#1065), that gap is still open for a
  folder purlis did not cut (#1055).
- **A grant for one workspace is never read as a grant for all of them.** The project's file
  writes it as `{ to = "devops", in = "runners" }` in the persona's list, and your own are kept
  under their own keys, so an older purlis reads no grant there, and an entry that does not
  read grants nothing. A teammate's limited grant waits in Settings for your Accept. A grant
  counts only while its workspace is there, and a workspace made later under the name of one
  purlis saw removed inherits none: Settings shows the grant as covering nothing, with
  **Remove**, and **Count it again** for the workspace that is there now. `purlis workspace
  remove` and `purlis workspace rename` count the old name gone themselves. **A grant does not
  follow a rename**: after `purlis workspace rename runners ci` the grants "in runners" cover
  nothing until you set each one's workspace again in Settings, and the rename says how many
  it left. No grant is kept for a workspace that is not there yet: allowing a handoff that
  makes its workspace starts that one dispatch, and the next one asks. **What this does not
  catch:** a workspace's folder removed and made again by hand, or by a pull, with no
  dispatch and no look at Settings in between is not noticed. Every grant, revoke and change of a grant's workspace is recorded in
  purlis's event log with the workspace it holds in (#1505).
- **An Allow that starts one dispatch is for the dispatch you read.** Where an Allow starts a
  dispatch no grant covers (the list of pairs you said never to does not read, or the
  workspace is not there yet), it starts that dispatch with that brief and no other, and
  nothing of it is left once that dispatch has returned, or once you revoke the grant, say
  never, or change its workspace (#1505).
- **If you run two versions of purlis on one project:** a version from before this change that
  rewrites this machine's record (`app/sandbox.json`) drops the grants you limited to a
  workspace and what you accepted of the project's. Nothing widens: those dispatches ask
  again (#1505).
- **Every tool-call guard decides within its own time budget, and refuses when it cannot.** A
  harness runs the tool when a hook times out, on Claude Code and Codex, so a guard made slow by
  a crafted command could let the call through. Every `PreToolUse` hook (Bash, Read, Edit and
  the dispatch ask) now reads its payload and decides within two seconds, well inside every
  harness's timeout, and refuses with one sentence when it runs out: the command is too long or
  too deeply nested, so split it. A payload that does not arrive in time is refused rather than
  judged as empty. Before any guard reads a command, three caps refuse the shapes that made the
  guards slow: more than 128 KB, substitutions nested more than 8 deep (in the command or in
  any string a guard derives from it), or more than 64 wrapper programs in front of one
  program. Commit messages and ASCII pull request bodies at a forge's largest still pass; a
  longer body goes in a file with `--body-file`, as the refusal says. `docs/hooks.md` records
  what each harness does when a hook times out, and that the budget starts when the hook does,
  not when the process does (#1355).
- **A handoff from a chat nobody is at is no longer refused outright; the app decides it.**
  purlis's hook used to refuse every handoff from a run with its harness's permission prompts
  off. What stands in its place: the app marks such a chat from its harness's reports, its
  profile's command and its own arguments, and never asks anyone on its behalf. It hands off to
  another persona only under a grant you made for yourself or the project, and only from inside
  a sandbox. To its own persona it hands off unasked, which is new, and is bounded: each handoff
  it opened that still works counts toward its running-per-chat limit, the lineage and depth
  limits hold, and it cannot create a workspace (`--create` is refused) (#1444).
- **A pre-allowed dispatch or handoff carries no rider.** A Claude Code chat is handed an
  `allow` for `purlis dispatch` and `purlis handoff`. Where a call runs one of them beside any
  other command, purlis's hook now answers `ask` for the whole call and names the other
  command, and it asks where it cannot read the call. This holds for the dispatch rules that
  were already there as well. Whether Claude Code would have asked by itself is not measured
  (#1444).
- **A host of yours taken out of your local settings file by hand must be confirmed again.**
  Settings now forgets your confirmation of every host the file no longer lists whenever it
  reads or saves the file, so a host written back later reaches nothing until you confirm it
  (#1405).
- **A launch brings a generated or mirrored file up to date only when purlis can confirm it
  wrote the one there.** In a workspace folder and in a checkout, purlis used to overwrite a
  settings file, agent or skill with the project's newer text on the word of a record kept
  beside it, which a chat might be able to write. Now the project's app state, which no chat
  can write, must also note offering that very text at that path. A file only the record
  vouches for is left as it is, and `purlis workspace reinit` says so and what replaces it
  (#1583).
- **A skill folder that is a link is never read** (Skill studio preview, #3017). purlis leaves out of every chat any skill whose folder is a link, whose `SKILL.md` is a link or a hard link, or whose skills folder, workspace or persona is a link. The Skill studio lists each one as "a link, so purlis doesn't read it". A chat that loads one of its skills is never shown a file a link leads to, even when a folder is swapped for a link after the chat's skills were read. A `SKILL.md` larger than purlis reads (256 KiB) is also left out, and the studio says so. An empty choice of chat program now means the same to every part of purlis: the chat is Claude Code's, as when none is named.
- **On Linux, a sandboxed chat's socket listens only where it was bound.** The wrap's supervisor
  now makes a chat's `listen` itself, on the calling thread's own socket: an internet socket the
  chat never bound is refused, and any other socket listens as before. A refused listen is told
  as a blocked bind. A runner in a Docker pool is given the one call this needs, in a seccomp
  profile of its own: Docker's default and `pidfd_getfd` besides.
- **A Docker pool runner made before this version keeps working, but its chats' servers do not
  listen** (unix sockets included) until you remove the runner and add it again. A Kubernetes
  runner's chats listen nowhere yet (#3413).
- **A login purlis performs runs its page scripts in purlis's own world.** The scripts that find,
  focus, check and clear a login's fields run apart from the page's own scripts, as every other
  script purlis runs on a page does, so a page that redefines them cannot steer which field gets
  a value. A login whose world is gone fills nothing more and says so (#2613).
- **A persona's profile is a name that is looked up, never a command that is run.** A name in
  a persona's definition that is not a built-in, a declared harness or a local profile on this
  machine starts nothing of its own. A profile whose command nobody on this machine has been
  shown and approved is not started by a handoff either; the new-chat picker shows it and asks
  (#1445).
- **What a persona wants is an offer, never a grant.** A chat can write persona definitions,
  so nothing that decides a dispatch reads `wants`: a persona that names another there, or
  `*`, is asked exactly as before, and a chat nobody is at is refused as before. A box is
  unticked until you tick it. Only finished personas of the project are offered, never the
  persona itself, a name purlis keeps for itself or "any persona", no more than six, and in
  alphabetical order. A pair you kept blocked in a chat is not offered to that chat again as
  a box. If what is offered changes while the question is on screen, the Notice says so and
  every box is unticked. What the question says a persona
  works with comes from records no chat writes (the vault registry, your own vault grants and
  the project's file), never from the persona's own file or from what the chat sent, and
  never names a secret. The definition is read again when you answer: a name no longer
  offered is not granted, and if anything the question said has changed since it was shown,
  nothing is allowed and you are shown it again. Each pair allowed is recorded in purlis's
  event log as its own grant (#1502).
- **A persona's forge CLI asks before more irreversible acts.** A persona that declares `gh` or
  `glab` no longer runs these without a prompt: a raw `api` call that may write, revoking or
  rotating a credential, transferring ownership, or changing a repository's visibility (#1096).
- **A pinned provider program is checked like a found one at every read.** The `op` a
  keyring-held token was pinned to is held to the same checks as an `op` purlis looks up, and a
  refusal says where purlis looks for `op` rather than asking for purlis to be started from a
  shell (#1517).
- **A profile's sign-in is kept from its chats' commands where its harness allows it.** A
  sandboxed Claude Code chat's commands and its Read and Edit tools are denied the sign-in file in
  its profile's folder. Where a harness keeps its sign-in somewhere its commands can still reach
  (Codex and opencode, which run with their commands, and Claude Code on macOS), Settings › You ›
  Profiles says plainly that the commands its chats run can read it (#2037).
- **A project's `purlis.toml` is read only as a plain file.** When the Settings tab reads or
  saves it, a file that is a link, or a FIFO, is refused at once with a sentence. Before, a
  link's target was shown and rewritten in its place, and a FIFO held the read until something
  wrote into it (#1100).
- **A provider's program a chat could have written is never run.** `op` and `vault` are handed
  a vault's identity, so purlis now refuses one that lies where a chat may write: the project, a
  folder you let chats write, the project's cache home, a harness's own folders, a temp
  directory, or the asking chat's own folder. The file is judged by where it really is, so a
  link to such a file is refused too. A copy elsewhere in the search is used; with none, the
  refusal names the file, nothing is run, and no pin is stored for it. The directories searched
  are those of the process that reads the vault, which for a sandboxed chat is the app, never
  the chat's (#1516).
- **A chat's permission mode is taken only from the hook purlis armed for it.** The mode a chat
  reports, which decides whether its tasks start in auto, is now believed only from a report
  that carries a key purlis gives that chat's hook alone. Any other report's mode is read as
  the default, asking mode, so it can never raise the level a task starts at (#3822).
- **A Resume holds a wider persona's grants while the sandbox is off too.** A session record
  resumed as a persona that reaches past the default persona's hosts or tools holds the
  default's whether or not the project sandboxes its chats at that moment, so turning the
  sandbox on later never hands the resumed chat more than the default persona's until you allow
  its own on its tab (#1407).
- **A runner that answers with this desktop's own link key is not kept.** Pairing a runner now
  refuses a runner whose key is the one this desktop links with, as it refuses one with this
  desktop's device id (#2683).
- **A runner starts a chat's confinement only from a plan that fits it.** A plan the desktop
  relays must put the chat's ssh route in the runner's own folder for the project. It may give
  the chat only the services on the runner that the runner's own sandbox for the project gives.
  The chat reaches an internal address only where the runner's machine policy lists it under
  the new `sandbox.relayed-internal` key. An internal address is a private, cluster or
  link-local one, the runner's own, or one on a network the runner is on. That holds whether
  the plan names the address or a name that resolves to it, and it is checked again at every
  connection. Any other plan is refused with a sentence saying what does not fit, and nothing
  starts (#2445).
- **A runner's log never names a vault.** When a runner's host answers a brokered
  `secret exec`, its log names the program that ran, never the vault it used (#2838).
- **A signed-in browser is handed over only to a chat with that very login** (#2699). Handing a
  browser that holds a login, or one opened from a kept login, to another chat now checks the
  login's whole identity, its persona, project and declaration, not only its name, for every
  login the browser was signed in with: a chat whose login of the same name is declared
  otherwise is refused, and the browser stays with no chat.
- **A name that hides or reorders its own characters can no longer disguise a row.** The tables
  of `purlis skill list`, `purlis skill runs`, `purlis recall`, `purlis status`, `purlis worktree
  list` and `purlis worktree history` show a name's control, bidi and zero-width characters as
  `⟦U+XXXX⟧`, the way the install review does, in every column, the last one too, and line their
  columns up on what they show. purlis's own colours still show (#3150).
- **A task never starts with its permission prompts off.** A chat running with them off starts
  its tasks in auto mode, where Claude Code's classifier still judges every tool call, and
  purlis's sandbox and guards still apply (#3787).
- **Your yes to a project grant is bound to what you accepted.** purlis keeps the commit your
  acceptances were last checked through and reads the history of the project's settings
  since. A grant that a commit took out is no longer accepted on your machine, so one that is
  taken out and put back waits for a new yes, also when both commits arrive in one pull,
  through a merge, or with the settings file renamed; the Notice says why it asks again.
  Where that history cannot be read, every acceptance is asked again. Where it cannot be
  asked at all, no accepted project grant counts until it can. A grant that is only missing
  from the file on disk, as after a branch switch, is not in force and nothing is dropped. A
  history rewritten so that no commit you have took the grant out is not detected. A late
  answer to the Notice answers only what is still exactly as it was shown, putting the Notice
  away accepts nothing, no Notice accepts "any persona", accepting never writes the project's
  file, and a grant naming a persona the project does not define is never accepted. Accept
  and Not on my machine are recorded in purlis's event log, and each is a press in the
  window: no command and nothing a chat sends reaches them (#1506).
- **A 1Password token is not stored while the only `op` found is where a chat can write.** The
  token used to be stored with no program pinned, and every read was refused until it was given
  again. Storing it from a vault's tab, moving it from the environment, or setting up a vault
  with a token is now refused with nothing written, and the message says where `op` was found
  (#1517).
- **A typed `/smart-close` is read from your own keys.** purlis now gives a chat its smart-close
  pass only when you typed `/smart-close` or `/purlis:smart-close` into its pane, with or
  without words after it, or typed at least `/sm` and pressed Enter on the picker. A report from
  inside the chat can no longer give it a pass on its own. If you reach Smart close another way,
  such as an arrow key in the picker or a recalled line, the chat still saves its session record,
  and the tab stays open with a notice that says the record was saved and offers **Close tab**. The tab's **Smart close** works
  as before (#1361).
- **A permission ask is read by the harness purlis started the chat as.** The window read a
  chat's permission prompt in the terms its environment named. It now reads it by the app's own
  record of the chat's harness, and leaves a prompt that names another to the chat's own pane
  (#1703).
- **A generated file is withdrawn through the folders held open on the way down.** When a
  project stops declaring a file purlis generated in a workspace folder, the file is unlinked
  inside the folder the walk down holds, and the folders it leaves empty go the same way, so a
  folder swapped for a link in the meantime can no longer carry the removal outside the project
  (#1583).
- **A workspace folder gives back only a settings file purlis itself offered there.** When the
  project stops declaring settings, purlis removes the settings it generated in each workspace
  folder. It used to go by a record kept in that folder, which a chat might be able to write.
  Now a file goes only when purlis noted offering that very text at that path, in app state no
  chat can write. When nothing was noted, nothing is removed (#1583).
- **Activity leaves out a message that holds a vault value, whatever it looks like.** Before,
  only text shaped like a credential was left out. A value purlis read from a vault or stored in
  one since it started, or a forge token it holds, now keeps the message's line in Activity and
  says its text was left out (#1520).
- **"Allow always" is never offered for an ask from an ACP agent or a harness's own server.**
  Some keep it in the worktree's harness settings, where a later chat reads it as standing
  permission. A client that sends its id anyway is refused with a sentence saying why (#1059).
- **An Allow for one chat is audited only when it is kept, and takes effect only once its audit
  is written.** A block's Notice or Settings' port form allowing something for a chat that
  closed in the meantime is refused before anything is audited, where the audit used to record
  an Allow that was never kept. An Allow for one chat whose audit cannot be written keeps
  nothing, and allowing for the chat what was allowed once is now audited too (#2454).
- **An ask no longer shows a vault value purlis knows.** A value the app read or stored since
  it started (one you revealed or stored in its window, or one it handed a sandboxed chat's
  command) is masked as `[vault value]` in an ask's line, whatever it looks like, and an edit
  that would write one is not drawn. Such an ask offers no Allow in the Inbox: allow it in its
  pane, which shows it whole. A value the app has not read, one a chat read itself for
  instance, is not known to it and is still shown (#1047).
- **Your own ask and deny rules hold under every spelling of the program they name.** A harness
  matches `purlis guard ask` rules against the command as written, so another spelling of the
  same program could run with no prompt. purlis's guard now refuses those spellings, with the
  same reading it uses for its own consent rules, and a rule on the command line holds under
  both of its names (#1286).
- **An edit's Allow, and an answer to a chat's question, are given from purlis's window only.**
  Another client still sees the ask waiting and can deny it, but no longer receives the change
  an edit would write (#1146).
- **A chat from an older version is refused less often, and never on a shorter chain.** Before
  refusing a chat whose chain began under an older version and has a closed chat in it, purlis
  reads who dispatched whom from its own dispatch records; where they show the whole chain, up
  to the chat the person started as the chat's own record names it, and as deep as that
  record says, it is held as a kept chain is. A chain whose records stop anywhere else is
  still refused. A chain the chats still
  open show longer than the chat's recorded depth is kept whole, and the depth raised to it
  (#1548).
- **An unattended chat dispatches only under a grant that already stands.** A chat whose
  harness runs with its permission prompts off has nobody to answer a dispatch grant's Notice,
  so it is never shown one. Its dispatch to another persona starts only when a grant covers the
  pair for you on this machine or for everyone in this project; a grant made for one chat never
  counts for it. Without one the dispatch is refused in a sentence that names the missing pair
  and says how a person grants it, nothing is kept waiting, and no grant can be made from the
  ask. An unattended chat that was started with no sandbox dispatches to no other persona at
  all, since nothing would keep it from changing who it may dispatch to. The persona chat an
  unattended chat starts takes none of this: it starts as the project and this machine declare
  it, with its own persona's hosts and vault, no opt-out and no permission mode of the asking
  chat's, and it waits in its own tab, shown as needing you, when it asks. A persona chat is
  not started on the asking chat's profile where that profile's own command switches the
  prompts off (#1446).
- **Only you answer a chat's ask, and only for that chat.** An answer comes from the app's window
  and lands only on the ask of the chat it names, once. The permission hook believes a reply
  only from the app that started its chat, checked by the operating system's record of who is
  listening, so nothing a chat runs can answer in the app's place. The session protocol refuses
  its `answer` command, and the link's UI RPC never serves the window's answer, until client
  scopes are checked (#664) (HP-6, #672).
- **A command's answer marks the hidden characters in the names it prints.** `persona default`,
  `persona show`, `persona dedupe`, `persona log` and `persona optimize` show a control, bidi or
  zero-width character in a name, a title or a path read from a file as `⟦U+XXXX⟧`, as their
  other lines already did. An ordinary name prints as before, and a persona's charter is printed
  as it is (#3287).
- **Approving a profile shows its whole command, one way only.** The new-chat picker, the
  first-task tab and a waiting chat's *Review and approve…* used to clip a long command at the
  display limit, so the end of it was never on screen when you approved it. Every word of the
  command and its environment, and the profile's kind, is now shown, escaped and quoted as a
  shell would need it typed, and the approval is checked against that whole line. A profile
  whose `env` names a variable a shell could not set (anything but letters, digits and `_`,
  not starting with a digit) is now refused (#1014).
- **The explorer reads a branch's changes without starting git.** It reads them by itself as
  agents write, so it no longer starts git in a branch's folder for them, and nothing that
  folder's git config names can run from that read. The read runs in a short-lived copy of
  purlis itself, which is stopped if it runs too long or uses too much memory, so a branch built
  to hang or swell the read costs that copy and not the app (FM-4, #1107).
- **A git read through purlis's git runner no longer fetches an object the repository
  lacks.** Such a read now fails instead of fetching the object on its own (FM-4, #1107).
- **A secret in a dispatch's brief or report is masked wherever the window shows it.** Activity,
  Dispatches, a finished task's row, a task's changes and the brief reader replace each vault
  value purlis read or stored, each credential-shaped stretch and each forge token it holds with
  `***`, checked every time the text is shown, so a value purlis learns later is masked too. A
  brief or report the store cut short also has the end of what it kept masked. The record keeps
  the text as written (#1872).
- **The app log leaves out an event that holds a vault value purlis read or stored**, whatever
  the value looks like, as it already did for forge tokens (#1872).
- **Git the app runs for a chat can no longer be pointed at a configuration the chat wrote.**
  A sandboxed chat's writes to `.git/commondir`, `.git/objects/info/alternates` and
  `.git/info/attributes`, in any clone, worktree or submodule, are now refused, as its writes
  to `.git/config` and hooks already were (#1335).
- **A brokered commit, clone or branch folder refuses more of a repository's own config.**
  The app already refused to run git for a sandboxed chat in a repository whose own config
  names a program. That list now also covers a trailer's command and a hook defined in config
  rather than in the hooks folder. A brokered commit also refuses a repository whose own config
  names a signer, and says so: such a repository means its commits to be signed, and the app
  never signs for a chat, so commit those from your own terminal. A signer you set for
  yourself alone is not read. The commit itself is told never to open an editor (#1476).
- **`git worktree repair` is let through only where a folder was moved.** purlis's own git
  lets that one command past the check of a folder's git link, so a rename can repair the
  folders it moved. It now covers only the plain command in a folder whose old place is gone,
  and nothing that would repair another folder's link (#1476).
- **A live line on the hook channel is read only from inside the chat it names.** A chat's token
  can be read by any process of the same user on macOS, so the token alone no longer identifies
  a chat. The app records each chat's program as it starts and forgets it when it ends. It reads
  a line only from that program or from a process in its session or below it. A line from
  outside the chat (tmux, `nohup` after its shell ended, `docker exec`) is refused with a
  sentence saying so. Reports a hook spools while the app is away are not covered yet: they are
  still checked by the token's key alone (#1407).
- **A browser login follows the rules of any secret fill.** Its fields give nothing to a copy, a cut or
  a drag, the chat copies and drags nothing in that browser from then on, a user name goes only into a
  one-line field, and only the page purlis opened for the login is filled. A login you allow on its notice starts clean on
  its own site, and other sites in that browser are left as they are (#5121).
- **Certificate checks reject the distrusted emSign intermediates.** purlis's own HTTPS (engine
  updates, the updater) uses `rustls-webpki` 0.103.16 and `webpki-roots` /
  `webpki-root-certs` 1.0.10 (RUSTSEC-2026-0381, -0382, -0383).
- **Each client of `purlisd` may do only what its scope grants.** One table, checked before any
  host hears of a command, says what the window, a terminal client, the fleet MCP, an approvals
  client, the editor and a runner's link may each call. Only the window and an approvals client
  answer an ask, and an ask for a secret only the window. Vault values and settings writes stay
  the window's alone. A process started inside a chat is refused every one of these scopes, even
  when it holds a credential, and a chat's sandbox now denies it the directory those credentials
  live in, also when that directory is reached through a link (FD-27, #664).
- A filter that purlis's git runs never downloads a Git LFS file and asks none of your credential
  helpers, in any repository rather than only in a clone purlis wired. A file purlis's git checks
  out there is its pointer until `git lfs pull`, even where its object is here.
- `purlis worktree add` is refused in a repository whose own config has an `includeIf`, or an
  include in a worktree config: its checkout could read a config purlis never saw.
- **Each person's runners on a cluster pool are theirs alone to reach.** Each person's runner
  namespace binds only them to `purlis-runner-owner`, and the new admission policy
  `purlis-runner-namespaces` lets only the operator make a runner namespace, and the operator bind
  only that role, only there, only to that person (#2055, docs/cluster-operator.md).
- **The cluster operator acts only on Claims admitted under its policy, however it was
  installed.** A Claim made before the policy was in force, or in the 30 seconds after, says
  `MadeBeforePolicy`: delete it and make it again (#2237).
- **A cluster runner's statement names the cluster it was made in.** Every Pool names its
  cluster as `status.cluster`, the uid of its `kube-system` namespace; a desktop pins it with
  the operator's key and refuses a statement of any other cluster. The statement is now v3, so
  a desktop and an operator of this release go together (#3305).
- **The cluster operator's pinned upstream agent-sandbox controller is installed by digest.**
  Step 1 of the install is now
  `kubectl apply --server-side -k operator/vendor/agent-sandbox/v1.0.6`, which applies the
  vendored release with its controller named by the release's digest. On a cluster where the
  release was installed by its tag, doctor now reports it as missing until it is applied again
  this way (#2261, docs/cluster-operator.md).
